CustomStartPointSet.description: A set of start points for MultiStart given by the rows of a matrix; list(pts) returns them.

ExhaustiveSearcher.description: Nearest-neighbour searcher that works with every distance; use knnsearch(ns, Y, ...) and rangesearch(ns, Y, r).

GlobalSearch.description: A solver object that runs a local solver from many scattered start points and keeps the best result. Use it with run(gs, problem), where problem comes from createOptimProblem.

H5A.close.description: Closes an attribute identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: attr_id = H5A.create(loc_id, name, type_id, space_id, acpl)
attr_id = H5A.create(loc_id, name, type_id, space_id, acpl, aapl)
H5A.create.description: Creates an attribute on a file, group or dataset, with a datatype and a dataspace (H5S.create('H5S_SCALAR') for a single value). Write its value with H5A.write. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5A.open.description: Opens an attribute of a file (its root group), group or dataset. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5A.read.description: Reads the value of an attribute, converted as H5D.read converts data. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5A.write.description: Writes the value of an attribute; mem_type 'H5ML_DEFAULT' uses the attribute's type. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5D.close.description: Closes a dataset identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: dset_id = H5D.create(loc_id, name, type_id, space_id, dcpl)
dset_id = H5D.create(loc_id, name, type_id, space_id, lcpl, dcpl, dapl)
H5D.create.description: Creates a dataset with the given datatype (an identifier or a predefined name such as 'H5T_NATIVE_DOUBLE') and dataspace. Without creation property lists the layout is contiguous, so the dataspace cannot have unlimited dimensions. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5D.get_space.description: Returns a copy of a dataset's dataspace, which can be inspected or given a hyperslab selection for H5D.read and H5D.write. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5D.get_type.description: Returns a copy of a dataset's datatype. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5D.open.description: Opens a dataset, given by a path relative to a file or group identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: data = H5D.read(dset_id, mem_type, mem_space, file_space, dxpl)
H5D.read.description: Reads a dataset. mem_type 'H5ML_DEFAULT' keeps the stored type; a predefined type name converts to it. 'H5S_ALL' for both spaces reads everything; a file dataspace with a hyperslab selection (H5S.select_hyperslab) reads that block. Numbers come back in their class, fixed-length strings as columns of a char array and variable-length strings as a cell array. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: H5D.write(dset_id, mem_type, mem_space, file_space, dxpl, data)
H5D.write.description: Writes data to a dataset, all of it with 'H5S_ALL', 'H5S_ALL', or the block selected in the file dataspace. The data is converted to mem_type ('H5ML_DEFAULT': the dataset's type) and must have as many elements as the selection. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5F.close.description: Closes a file identifier. The file itself is closed once the datasets, groups and attributes opened in it are closed too. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5F.create.description: Creates an HDF5 file and returns its identifier. With 'H5F_ACC_TRUNC' an existing file is overwritten; with 'H5F_ACC_EXCL' (the default) creating it fails if it exists. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5F.open.description: Opens an existing HDF5 file and returns its identifier. flags is 'H5F_ACC_RDONLY' (the default) or 'H5F_ACC_RDWR' for writing. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5G.close.description: Closes a group identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: gid = H5G.create(loc_id, name, lcpl, gcpl, gapl)
H5G.create.description: Creates a group in a file or group and returns its identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5G.open.description: Opens a group, given by a path relative to a file or group identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5ML.get_constant_value.description: Returns the number that stands for a named HDF5 constant such as 'H5F_ACC_RDWR' or 'H5S_UNLIMITED'. The low-level functions also accept the names themselves. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5S.close.description: Closes a dataspace identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5S.create.description: Creates a dataspace of type 'H5S_SCALAR' (one element, for example for an attribute), 'H5S_SIMPLE' or 'H5S_NULL'. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5S.create_simple.description: Creates a simple dataspace of rank dimensions. maxdims is [] (the same as dims) or has one value per dimension, where -1 or Inf means unlimited. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5S.get_simple_extent_dims.description: Returns the number of dimensions, the current dimensions and the maximum dimensions of a dataspace; an unlimited maximum is returned as -1. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

usage: H5S.select_hyperslab(space_id, op, start, stride, count, block)
H5S.select_hyperslab.description: Selects a regular block pattern in a dataspace: count blocks of size block, spaced stride apart, from start (zero-based). [] for stride or block means ones. op is 'H5S_SELECT_SET' to replace the selection, or 'H5S_SELECT_OR', 'H5S_SELECT_AND', 'H5S_SELECT_XOR', 'H5S_SELECT_NOTB' or 'H5S_SELECT_NOTA' to combine it with the current one. Dimensions are in the C library's order, slowest first, and offsets start at 0; the MATLAB array that goes with a dataspace of dimensions [a b] is b-by-a. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5T.close.description: Closes a datatype identifier. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5T.copy.description: Copies a datatype, given as an identifier, a dataset identifier or a predefined name: 'H5T_NATIVE_DOUBLE', 'H5T_NATIVE_FLOAT', 'H5T_NATIVE_INT', 'H5T_NATIVE_UINT8' and the other native integer types, 'H5T_IEEE_F64LE' and the other standard types, or 'H5T_C_S1' for text. The copy can be changed, for example with H5T.set_size. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

H5T.set_size.description: Sets the size in bytes of a datatype; for a string type copied from 'H5T_C_S1' this is the length of the strings, or 'H5T_VARIABLE' for variable-length strings. Identifiers are H5ML.id handles; constants are given by name, and 'H5P_DEFAULT' is the only property list accepted. Runs on the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab.

Inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

KDTreeSearcher.description: Nearest-neighbour searcher for the points X; use knnsearch(ns, Y, ...) and rangesearch(ns, Y, r).

MException.description: Creates an error value with identifier, formatted message and an empty stack field, ready to pass to throw. In mylab it is a plain struct, not an object.

MException.last.description: The MException of the error that was caught most recently by try/catch in this session (an MException with empty identifier and message if there was none). 'reset' forgets it. In MATLAB the function reports the last uncaught error at the prompt; mylab also counts errors that were caught.

MultiStart.description: A solver object that runs a local solver from k start points: [x, fval] = run(ms, problem, k). The problem comes from createOptimProblem.

NA.description: Octave's marker for a missing value. In mylab it is NaN. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

NaN.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

NaT.description: Not-a-Time: the missing value for datetime arrays, as a scalar or an array of the given size. It compares unequal to everything; test for it with isnat.

RandStream.description: Creates a random number stream. Use it with rand(s, ...), randn(s, ...), randi(s, ...) and randperm(s, n), or make it the source for rand/randn/randi with RandStream.setGlobalStream(s). reset(s) starts the sequence again. Properties: Type, Seed, State. Every generator type ('mt19937ar', 'mlfg6331_64', ...) is accepted, but all of them use NumPy's default generator, so the numbers differ from MATLAB's. 'Seed' may be 'shuffle'.

RandStream.create.description: Creates a random number stream; the same as RandStream(type, 'Seed', seed).

RandStream.getGlobalStream.description: Returns the stream that rand, randn and randi currently draw from.

RandStream.list.description: Lists the generator type names RandStream accepts. They all use the same generator in mylab.

RandStream.setGlobalStream.description: Makes s the stream that rand, randn, randi and randperm draw from, and returns the previous one. Example: RandStream.setGlobalStream(RandStream('mt19937ar', 'Seed', 1)).

RandomStartPointSet.description: A set of n random start points for MultiStart, drawn inside the problem's bounds; list(pts, problem) returns them.

RespConfig.description: Options for step and impulse under their newer name: Amplitude is the step size and Bias the input level before the step. Delay and InitialState are not supported.

Simulink.Variant.description: A variant control for imported block diagrams: a struct with the field Condition. A variant subsystem whose choice names v as its control runs that choice when the condition is true in the workspace.

TreeBagger.description: Bagged decision trees (random forest). Options: 'Method' ('classification' or 'regression'), 'OOBPrediction', 'MinLeafSize', 'NumPredictorsToSample', 'InBagFraction'. predict returns class labels as a cell array of text (with scores) or regression values; oobError and oobPredict use the out-of-bag observations.

TriScatteredInterp.description: Older form of scatteredInterpolant. vq = F(xq, yq) interpolates linearly and returns NaN outside the convex hull of the samples.

VideoReader.description: Opens a video file for reading. readFrame returns the next frame as a height-by-width-by-3 uint8 array (height-by-width for grayscale video) and hasFrame tells whether one is left; read returns frame k, a range of frames (last may be Inf) or all of them, stacked along the fourth dimension. Properties: Name, Path, Duration, CurrentTime (can be set, to jump), NumFrames, FrameRate, Height, Width, BitsPerPixel, VideoFormat, Tag and UserData. AVI files with Motion JPEG or uncompressed frames, which is what VideoWriter writes, are decoded by mylab itself; other formats (MP4 and so on) are decoded with the ffmpeg program when it is installed, otherwise an error says so.

VideoWriter.description: Creates an object that writes frames to a video file. Typical use: open(v); writeVideo(v, getframe(gcf)) in a loop; close(v), which produces the file. Properties: FrameRate (default 30), Quality (0-100), and read-only Filename, Path, FrameCount, Width, Height, Duration. Profiles: 'Motion JPEG AVI' (the default for .avi), 'Uncompressed AVI', 'Grayscale AVI' and 'MPEG-4' (.mp4). AVI files are written by mylab itself and can be read back with VideoReader. MPEG-4 needs the ffmpeg program; when it is missing an animated GIF with the same base name is written and a warning says so. A file name ending in .gif always writes an animated GIF.

abs.description: Absolute value of each element; for complex x, the magnitude. Example: abs(3 - 4i) is 5.

absorbDelay.description: Turns the delays of a discrete-time model into poles at z = 0 (a delay of d samples becomes z^-d in the model itself). For continuous time use pade to approximate delays.

usage: A = accumarray(subs, vals, sz, fun, fillval)
accumarray.description: Groups the values vals by the subscripts in subs and combines each group. Each row of subs is one subscript (a column of indices for a vector result, two columns for a matrix, or a cell of index vectors). sz fixes the output size ([] lets the largest subscript decide). fun is called with each group's values as a column and must return a scalar (default: sum); if it returns a cell such as @(x) {x}, the result is a cell array. Positions that receive no values hold fillval (default 0, or [] for cells). Example: accumarray([1; 2; 1], [10; 20; 30], [], @max) is [30; 20].

acker.description: Pole placement for a single-input system with Ackermann's formula; repeated poles are allowed. It is less accurate than place for systems of higher order.

acos.description: Inverse cosine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

acosh.description: Inverse hyperbolic cosine. Inputs below 1 give complex results.

adapthisteq.description: Contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalisation: the image is cut into tiles ('NumTiles', default [8 8]), each tile is equalised with its histogram clipped at 'ClipLimit' (0 to 1, default 0.01) so that noise is not amplified too much, and the tile mappings are blended to hide the seams. 'NBins' (default 256), 'Range' ('full' or 'original') and 'Distribution' ('uniform', 'rayleigh' or 'exponential', with 'Alpha') are also available.

adaptthresh.description: Locally adaptive threshold for imbinarize: a fraction of the local average brightness. sensitivity (0 to 1, default 0.5) turns more pixels into foreground as it grows. 'NeighborhoodSize' (default about one eighth of the image), 'Statistic' ('mean', 'median' or 'gaussian') and 'ForegroundPolarity' ('bright' or 'dark') are available.

addOptional.description: Adds an optional positional argument with a default value to the inputParser p. Optional arguments come after the required ones, in the order they were added. Positional reading stops at text that names a parameter, a switch or an optional argument not yet given, when the rest reads as name-value pairs; at text the optional argument's validator rejects; and at any text when it has no validator (so give text arguments a validator). An optional argument not given by position can be given by name, like a parameter: f(x, 'w', 2) sets w.

addParamValue.description: Older name of addParameter: adds a name-value argument with a default value to the inputParser p.

addParameter.description: Adds a name-value argument with a default value to the inputParser p. Callers pass it as 'Name', value after the positional arguments, or as a field of a struct. Names match without regard to case (unless CaseSensitive) and, with PartialMatching, may be shortened as long as they stay unique; when a short name fits several, the one with the lowest PartialMatchPriority (default 1) wins. Struct field names must match in full. A name given twice keeps its last value.

addRequired.description: Adds a required positional argument to the inputParser p. validator is a function handle that must return true (or not raise an error) for acceptable values, e.g. @isnumeric or @(x) x > 0.

addSwitch.description: Adds a switch to the inputParser p: p.Results.name is true when the caller passes the name on its own, and false otherwise.

addTeardown.description: Registers a function to run when the test finishes, whether it passed or not. Functions run in the reverse order of registration. In a setupOnce function or TestClassSetup method the function runs after the last test of the file or class.

add_block.description: Adds a block to a model. source names a block type in the library, destination is the path of the new block, and the remaining pairs set its parameters. Parameter values are text holding a MATLAB expression ('2*K'); numbers are accepted too. source may also be the path of an existing block to copy. Blocks are named by path: 'model/Block', or 'model/Subsystem/Block' inside a subsystem. Library names such as 'blocks/Gain' work, and so do the familiar ones like 'simulink/Continuous/Integrator' and 'built-in/Gain'. Example: add_block('blocks/Gain', 'm/K', 'Gain', '2.5').

add_line.description: Connects an output port to an input port of blocks in the same system. Ports are written as 'BlockName/number', or given as the handles from get_param(block, 'PortHandles'). The control inputs of conditionally run subsystems are 'Name/Enable' and 'Name/Trigger'. One output may feed several inputs (call add_line again, or pass a cell array of destinations); an input takes one line. 'autorouting' is accepted: the editor always routes lines by itself.

addboundary.description: p with more boundaries; the result is simplified again unless Simplify is false, so a boundary inside a region becomes a hole. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.addboundary(...).

addcats.description: Adds categories to a categorical array, at the end or next to an existing category. No element changes.

addedge.description: Adds edges. Nodes that do not exist yet are created. A weighted graph needs a weight for each new edge.

addevent.description: Attaches events to a timeseries: tsdata.event objects, or names (a cell array for several) with their times.

addlistener.description: Calls callback(source, eventData) whenever obj fires the event with notify. The second form runs the callback after ('PostSet') or before ('PreSet') the property is assigned; eventData.AffectedObject is the object. Set L.Enabled = false or call delete(L) to stop listening.

addnode.description: Adds n isolated nodes, or nodes with the given names or table rows.

addpath.description: Adds folders to the search path used to find .m files and data files. Each argument may hold several folders separated by the path separator (':' or ';'), as genpath returns them. Folders go to the front of the path in the order given, or to the back with '-end'; a folder that is already on the path is moved.

addpoints.description: Appends points to the animated line h and grows the axes limits to include them.

addpref.description: Same as setpref in mylab (an existing preference is replaced).

addprop.description: Adds a property called name to one object of a class derived from dynamicprops. Other objects of the class are not changed. The result is a meta.DynamicProperty whose attributes can be set (SetAccess, GetAccess, Hidden, Transient, GetMethod, SetMethod, SetObservable, NonCopyable); delete(p) removes the property from the object again.

usage: ts = addsample(ts, 'Data', d, 'Time', t, 'Quality', q, 'OverwriteFlag', tf)
addsample.description: Adds samples (one per time in t) and keeps the samples in time order. With OverwriteFlag true a new sample replaces an old one at the same time. s can be a struct with fields Data, Time, Quality and OverwriteFlag. Times are numbers in TimeInfo.Units; when TimeInfo.StartDate is set they may also be given as date text or datetime values.

addtarget.description: Add a graphics object to a property link made by linkprop, so its linked properties follow the others.

addtodate.description: Adds a quantity of 'year', 'month', 'week', 'day', 'hour', 'minute', 'second' or 'millisecond' to serial date numbers. Months and years move by calendar, keeping the day of the month where it exists.

addvars.description: Appends variables (columns) to the right of a table.

adjacency.description: Sparse adjacency matrix. A(i, j) counts the edges from i to j; 'weighted' or a weight vector puts edge weights there instead.

adjoint.description: Classical adjoint (adjugate) of a square symbolic matrix: A*adjoint(A) is det(A)*I.

adtest.description: Anderson-Darling goodness-of-fit test for the 'norm' (default), 'exp', 'ev', 'logn' or 'weibull' family with estimated parameters, or for a fully specified distribution object.

affine2d.description: Affine transformation with the 3-by-3 matrix T used as [x y 1] = [u v 1] * T (the last column must be [0; 0; 1]). Methods: transformPointsForward, transformPointsInverse, invert, outputLimits, isRigid, isSimilarity and isTranslation.

affinetform2d.description: Affine transformation with the 3-by-3 matrix A used as [x; y; 1] = A * [u; v; 1] (the last row must be [0 0 1]).

airy.description: Airy functions: k = 0 gives Ai (default), 1 its derivative, 2 Bi, 3 the derivative of Bi. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version.

alignsignals.description: Lines up two signals by putting zeros in front of the one that is ahead; d is the delay found by finddelay. 'truncate' keeps the original lengths.

all.description: True if every element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix, along dim, or over 'all' elements. all([]) is true.

allchild.description: The objects directly inside the figure, axes or other graphics object h.

allfinite.description: True if no element of A is NaN or infinite. A is numeric, logical or char.

allmargin.description: All crossover frequencies and margins of an open loop as a struct: GainMargin with GMFrequency, PhaseMargin with PMFrequency, DelayMargin with DMFrequency (seconds, or sample periods for a discrete-time model) and Stable, which tells whether the unity-feedback loop is stable.

allpaths.description: All paths from s to t that visit no node twice, as a cell array of node lists.

alpha.description: Sets the transparency of the surfaces, patches and images in the current axes, or of the object h: 0 is clear, 1 is opaque. Per-point modes ('flat', 'interp') are ignored.

alphanumericBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: a place where a letter or digit meets another kind of character. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

alphanumericsPattern.description: A pattern that matches letters and digits. With no argument it matches one or more of them, with N exactly N, and with (min, max) between min and max (max may be Inf). Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

amd.description: Minimum-degree style ordering of a symmetric pattern: factorizing A(p, p) usually creates fewer new nonzeros than factorizing A.

ancestor.description: Walks up from h through its parents and returns the first object of the given type, such as 'axes' or 'figure' (h itself when it has that type), or [] when there is none. 'toplevel' returns the highest match instead.

and.description: Same as A & B (element-wise logical AND).

angdiff.description: Difference b - a between angles in radians, wrapped to the range from -pi to pi. With one input, the differences between neighbouring elements of a vector.

angle.description: Phase angle of each complex element in radians, between -pi and pi.

animatedline.description: Creates a line that grows as points are added with addpoints, without clearing the axes. Options: Color, LineWidth, LineStyle, Marker, MaximumNumPoints (older points are dropped beyond this number). Example: h = animatedline; for k = 1:50, addpoints(h, k, sin(k/5)); drawnow; end

annotation.description: Draws a shape on the figure (not tied to axes) in normalized figure units from 0 to 1. x = [x1 x2] and y = [y1 y2] give the start and end points; pos = [left bottom width height].

anova1.description: One-way analysis of variance: tests whether several groups share the same mean. Groups are the columns of y, or are given by labels in group (numbers, a char matrix or a cell array). tbl is the ANOVA table as a cell array; stats holds the group names, sizes and means. No figure is shown.

anova2.description: Two-way analysis of variance for balanced data: columns of y are the levels of one factor and each block of reps rows a level of the other. p holds the p-values for columns, rows and (when reps > 1) the interaction.

usage: [p, tbl, stats, terms] = anovan(y, group, 'Name', value, ...)
anovan.description: N-way analysis of variance. group is a cell array of grouping variables. Options: 'model' ('linear', 'interaction', 'full', an order or a terms matrix), 'sstype' (1, 2 or 3, default 3), 'varnames', 'continuous' and 'display'.

any.description: True if at least one element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix (a row of results), along dim, or over 'all' elements. any([]) is false.

anynan.description: True if any element of A is NaN. A is numeric, logical or char.

appcoef.description: Approximation coefficients at level n (default the coarsest level) of a wavedec decomposition; level 0 gives the signal.

appcoef2.description: Approximation coefficients at level n (default the coarsest) of a wavedec2 decomposition.

appdesigner.description: Not available. .mlapp files are binary and cannot be opened; export the app to a .m file in MATLAB and run that. The mylab web app has its own app builder (New app).

append.description: Joins text element by element. Unlike strcat it keeps trailing blanks of char vectors. Arrays must have the same size; single texts are repeated. The result is a string array if any input is a string, else a cell array if any input is a cell array, else a char vector.

applyFixture.description: Sets up a fixture such as matlab.unittest.fixtures.TemporaryFolderFixture and undoes it when the test finishes. Returns the fixture, whose properties (for example Folder) can then be read.

applylut.description: Neighbourhood operation on a binary image by table lookup: each pixel's 2-by-2 or 3-by-3 neighbourhood selects an entry of the table made by makelut.

arburg.description: Autoregressive model of order p by Burg's method, which minimises the forward and backward prediction errors and always gives a stable model. The signal is modelled as white noise passed through 1/A(z); a is [1 a1 ... ap], e the variance of the noise and k the reflection coefficients. Each column of a matrix is treated as a signal.

arcov.description: Autoregressive model of order p by the covariance method: least squares on the forward prediction error without windowing the data.

area.description: Plots the curve y and shades the region between it and zero. Only a single vector is supported. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

argnames.description: The arguments of a symbolic function, as a row vector of variables.

armcov.description: Autoregressive model of order p by the modified covariance method: least squares on the forward and backward prediction errors.

array2table.description: Turns each column of the matrix A into a table variable.

array2timetable.description: Makes a timetable whose variables are the columns of the matrix A.

arrayfun.description: Calls f on each element of one or more same-size arrays, the way cellfun does for cells. Elements of a struct array are passed as 1-by-1 structs and elements of a cell array as 1-by-1 cells. Example: arrayfun(@(k) k^2, 1:3) is [1 4 9].

aryule.description: Autoregressive model of order p from the Yule-Walker equations (biased autocorrelation). The signal is modelled as white noise passed through 1/A(z); a is [1 a1 ... ap], e the variance of the noise and k the reflection coefficients. Each column of a matrix is treated as a signal.

asFewOfPattern.description: A pattern that matches p repeated as few times as possible, at least min times (default 0) and at most max times. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

asManyOfPattern.description: A pattern that matches p repeated as many times as possible, at least min times (default 1) and at most max times. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

asin.description: Inverse sine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

asinh.description: Inverse hyperbolic sine of each element.

assert.description: Throws an error if cond is false (or not all true). The default message is 'Assertion failed.'; a custom message and identifier follow the same rules as error.

assertClass.description: Checks that the class of actual is exactly className. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertClass(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertEmpty.description: Checks that actual has no elements. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertEmpty(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertEqual.description: Checks that actual equals expected in class, size and value (NaN equals NaN; cell arrays and structs are compared element by element). 'AbsTol', t and 'RelTol', t allow numeric differences up to t, or t times the expected value. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertError.description: Checks that calling the function raises an error with that identifier, for example testCase.verifyError(@() myFun(-1), 'myFun:negative'). ?MException accepts any error. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertError(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertFail.description: Fails unconditionally, for code paths that must not be reached. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertFail(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertFalse.description: Checks that actual is the logical scalar false. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertFalse(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assertGreaterThan.description: Checks that every element of actual is greater than bound. A failure stops the current test at once (Failed and Incomplete); later tests still run. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertGreaterThan(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

A method of the test case, also written testCase.assertInstanceOf(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assignin.description: Assigns value to the variable name in another workspace: 'base' (the top-level workspace) or 'caller' (the function that called the current one).

assume.description: Sets an assumption on a symbolic variable, replacing earlier ones. Later simplifications and solutions use it. Sets: 'real', 'positive', 'integer', 'rational'; 'clear' removes assumptions.

assumeAlso.description: Adds an assumption on a symbolic variable and keeps the ones already set.

assumeClass.description: Checks that the class of actual is exactly className. A failure stops the current test and marks it Incomplete (filtered) without failing it: use it for conditions the test needs but does not check. A method of the test case, also written testCase.assumeClass(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

assumptions.description: The assumptions set on a variable (or on all variables), as a vector of conditions.

atan.description: Inverse tangent in radians, between -pi/2 and pi/2. See atan2 for the full circle.

atan2.description: Four-quadrant angle in radians, between -pi and pi, of the point (x, y). Note that y comes first. Inputs expand against each other. Example: atan2(1, -1) is 3*pi/4.

atan2d.description: Four-quadrant inverse tangent like atan2, but the result is in degrees.

atanh.description: Inverse hyperbolic tangent. Inputs outside (-1, 1) give complex or infinite results.

audioinfo.description: Describes a sound file: Filename, CompressionMethod, NumChannels, SampleRate, TotalSamples, Duration and BitsPerSample (BitRate for OGG and MP3). The formats are those of audioread.

audioplayer.description: Creates a player object for the samples y. play(p), playblocking(p), pause(p), resume(p) and stop(p) are accepted but play nothing: mylab has no audio device. Properties: SampleRate, TotalSamples, NumChannels, BitsPerSample.

audioread.description: Reads a sound file: samples as doubles between -1 and 1, one column per channel, and the sample rate. [first last] reads part of the file; 'native' returns the file's own integer type. WAV and FLAC files are read by mylab itself; OGG, MP3, AIFF and AU files need the optional Python package soundfile (which also makes FLAC faster).

audiowrite.description: Writes samples (one column per channel, doubles between -1 and 1 or integers) to a sound file whose format follows the extension. WAV (8, 16, 24, 32 or 64 bits per sample) and FLAC (8, 16 or 24) are written by mylab itself; OGG, MP3, AIFF and AU need the optional Python package soundfile. 'Quality' (0 to 100) and 'BitRate' apply to OGG and MP3. Values outside -1..1 are clipped with a warning.

autumn.description: n-by-3 colormap from red through orange to yellow.

axang2rotm.description: Rotation matrix for a turn by angle (radians) about the axis [x y z]. The axis need not have length 1.

axes.description: Creates new axes in the current figure and makes them current; Position is given as fractions of the figure (use it for insets), and other axes properties can follow as name/value pairs. axes(ax) makes existing axes current. A figure handle as first input or 'Parent' chooses the figure.

usage: axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax zmin zmax])
axis.description: Sets axis limits or appearance. An Inf or -Inf limit keeps that end automatic, e.g. axis([0 Inf 0 Inf]). 'equal' makes units the same length on both axes, 'image' does that and fits the data tightly, 'square' makes the plot box square, 'tight' fits the limits to the data, 'off' hides the axes, 'auto' restores automatic limits, 'normal' also undoes 'equal' and 'square', 'ij' puts the y origin at the top and 'xy' back at the bottom. With an output and no input, returns the current limits.

backgroundPool.description: A stand-in for MATLAB's background pool, accepted as the first argument of parfeval. Work given to it runs at once in this session.

balance.description: Scales (and permutes) a square matrix so that its rows and columns have similar norms, which makes eigenvalue computations more accurate: B = T\A*T. With three outputs the scaling vector S and the permutation P are returned separately (T(:,P) = diag(S)). 'noperm' scales without permuting.

balreal.description: Balanced realization: a state transformation that makes the controllability and observability gramians equal and diagonal. g holds their diagonal, the Hankel singular values, in decreasing order; T maps the old state to the new one (xb = T*x) and Ti is its inverse. Unstable modes are kept apart, come first and get g = Inf. The model must be minimal.

balred.description: Reduced-order approximation with the given number of states, obtained by balancing the model and dropping the states with the smallest Hankel singular values. By default the DC gain is preserved ('MatchDC'); 'Truncate' simply deletes the states, which matches better at high frequency. The option is also accepted under its older name 'StateElimMethod' or in a balredOptions structure. Unstable poles are always kept. The result has the type of sys.

balredOptions.description: Options for balred: how the discarded states are removed, 'MatchDC' (default) or 'Truncate'.

bandpass.description: Filters x with a bandpass filter that keeps the range wpass = [low high] and removes the filter delay. The options are those of lowpass; 'Steepness' may have one value per edge.

bandpower.description: Average power of a signal (the mean of its squared magnitude), or the power in the frequency range [low high], found by summing a periodogram. A spectrum pxx with its frequencies f may be given instead of the signal.

bandstop.description: Filters x with a bandstop filter that removes the range wpass = [low high] and compensates for the filter delay. The options are those of lowpass.

bandwidth.description: For a matrix, the number of nonzero diagonals below (lower) and above (upper) the main diagonal. For a SISO control-system model, the first frequency (rad per time unit) where the gain has dropped 3 dB below its DC value, or by dbdrop dB (a negative number).

bar.description: Vertical bar chart of y, at positions x or 1..n. A matrix y draws groups of bars, one group per row and one colour per column, or stacks them with 'stacked'. width is the fraction of the space each group fills (default 0.8). Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, LineWidth, FaceAlpha, DisplayName. b is a Bar handle (a row array of them for a matrix y).

bar3.description: Draw the values of a matrix as 3-D bars, one row of bars per column of Z.

bar3h.description: Draw the values of a matrix as horizontal 3-D bars.

barh.description: Horizontal bar chart; takes the same inputs and options as bar.

barthannwin.description: Modified Bartlett-Hann window of length n. The result is a column vector.

bartlett.description: Triangular window of length n with zeros at both ends. The result is a column vector.

barttest.description: Bartlett's test for the number of dimensions needed to explain the non-random variation of the data: for k = 0, 1, ... it tests whether the remaining eigenvalues of the covariance are equal.

barycentricToCartesian.description: Cartesian coordinates of points given by barycentric coordinates B (one row per ID) relative to the triangles or tetrahedra ID. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.barycentricToCartesian(...).

base2dec.description: Number written by the text s in the given base (2 to 36). A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers; text that is not a valid number gives NaN.

bdIsLoaded.description: True when a model with this name is in memory.

bdclose.description: Closes block-diagram models; the same as close_system.

bdroot.description: Name of the current model, or of the model that a block path or handle belongs to.

beep.description: Accepted for compatibility; makes no sound.

besselap.description: Analog Bessel lowpass prototype of order n, scaled so that its magnitude approaches that of a Butterworth filter of the same order at high and low frequencies.

besself.description: Analog Bessel filter of order n, which has a nearly constant group delay up to about Wo (rad/s). ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'; a two-element Wn gives a bandpass filter of order 2n unless 'stop' is asked for. There is no digital version; use bilinear to convert it.

besselh.description: Hankel function (Bessel function of the third kind) of order nu. K is 1 (default) for J + i*Y or 2 for J - i*Y. scale = 1 multiplies by exp(-i*Z) for K = 1 and exp(i*Z) for K = 2.

besseli.description: Modified Bessel function of the first kind I_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

besselj.description: Bessel function of the first kind J_nu(z), element by element. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version. Results may be complex for negative z.

besselk.description: Modified Bessel function of the second kind K_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

bessely.description: Bessel function of the second kind Y_nu(z). Negative z gives complex results; 1 scales.

beta.description: Beta function, gamma(a).*gamma(b)./gamma(a+b), element by element.

betacdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the beta distribution with shape parameters a and b: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

betafit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [a, b] of the beta distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

betainc.description: Regularized incomplete beta function for x in [0, 1], lower tail by default or upper tail with 'upper'.

betaincinv.description: Inverse of the incomplete beta function: the x with betainc(x, z, w) = y. 'upper' inverts the upper tail.

betainv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the beta distribution with shape parameters a and b: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

betalike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the beta distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

betaln.description: Logarithm of the beta function, log(beta(z, w)), without overflow.

betapdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the beta distribution with shape parameters a and b, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

betarnd.description: Random numbers from the beta distribution with shape parameters a and b. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

betastat.description: Mean m and variance v of the beta distribution with shape parameters a and b.

between.description: The calendar duration from t1 to t2, as whole months, then days, then the remaining time, so that t1 + c equals t2.

bfsearch.description: Breadth-first search from node s: the nodes in the order they are discovered. events is 'discovernode', 'finishnode', 'startnode', 'edgetonew', 'edgetodiscovered', 'edgetofinished', 'allevents' or a cell array of several; several events give a table.

bicg.description: Solves A*x = b with the biconjugate gradient method. A must be a matrix (the method also needs A'), and preconditioners are not used. tol defaults to 1e-6 and maxit to min(n, 20).

usage: x = bicgstab(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
bicgstab.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the stabilized biconjugate gradient method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

usage: x = bicgstabl(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
bicgstabl.description: Solves A*x = b with the stabilized biconjugate gradient method BiCGstab(2). A can be a matrix or a function handle that returns A*x. flag is 0 when the relative residual tol (default 1e-6) was reached within maxit iterations.

usage: [zd, pd, kd] = bilinear(z, p, k, fs)
[Ad, Bd, Cd, Dd] = bilinear(A, B, C, D, fs)
bilinear.description: Converts an analog filter to a digital one with the substitution s = 2 fs (z-1)/(z+1). Row vectors are taken as numerator and denominator, column vectors as zeros and poles. With fp (Hz) the frequency axis is pre-warped so that the responses agree exactly at fp.

bin2dec.description: Value of a binary digit string; spaces are ignored. A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers, and text that is not binary gives NaN. A 0b prefix is allowed, and a suffix s8, s16, s32 or s64 (u8 ... u64) reads the digits as a signed (unsigned) integer of that size, so bin2dec('11111011s8') is -5. Example: bin2dec('101') is 5.

binocdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the binomial distribution with n trials with success probability p: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

binofit.description: Estimate of the success probability from x successes in n trials, with the exact (Clopper-Pearson) confidence interval. x and n may be arrays; pci has one row per element.

binoinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the binomial distribution with n trials with success probability p: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

binopdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the binomial distribution with n trials with success probability p, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

binornd.description: Random numbers from the binomial distribution with n trials with success probability p. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

binostat.description: Mean m and variance v of the binomial distribution with n trials with success probability p.

bitand.description: Bitwise AND of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitcmp.description: Bitwise complement of non-negative integers within the width of the integer class (8, 16, 32 or 64 bits).

bitget.description: Value (0 or 1) of bit number bit (1 = least significant) of each non-negative integer in a. Example: bitget(6, 1:3) is [0 1 1].

bitor.description: Bitwise OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitset.description: Sets bit number bit of a to 1 (or to value, 0 or 1). Example: bitset(8, 1) is 9.

bitshift.description: Shifts the bits of integer values left by n places (right when n is negative). n must be a scalar. Example: bitshift(1, 3) is 8.

bitxor.description: Bitwise exclusive OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

blackman.description: Blackman window of length n as a column vector.

blackmanharris.description: Four-term Blackman-Harris window with very low sidelobes (about -92 dB). The result is a column vector. A second input 'periodic' gives the window used for spectral analysis (one period of n+1 samples).

blkdiag.description: Block-diagonal matrix with A1, A2, ... along the diagonal and zeros elsewhere. The result is sparse when any input is sparse.

usage: B = blockproc(A, [m n], fun, Name, Value)
blockproc.description: Applies fun to each m-by-n block of A and joins the results. fun gets a struct with the fields data, location ([row col] of the block), blockSize, imageSize and border. Options: 'BorderSize' [v h] adds pixels around each block, 'TrimBorder' (default true) removes them from the result, 'PadPartialBlocks' fills up the blocks at the right and bottom edges, and 'PadMethod' is a number, 'replicate' or 'symmetric'.

bode.description: Bode frequency response. mag is the gain (absolute, not dB) and phase the phase in degrees; both are ny-by-nu-by-nf arrays (use squeeze for a SISO model) and wout is a column of frequencies. The phase is continuous: it is assembled from the phase of each zero and pole, so integrators start at -90 degrees each and delays keep adding lag without wrapping. The optional second argument is a vector of frequencies in rad per time unit, or a range {wmin, wmax}; without it the frequencies are chosen from the poles and zeros (up to the Nyquist frequency pi/Ts for a discrete-time model). Without output arguments the plot is drawn; several models can be given, each with a line style.

bodemag.description: Bode magnitude plot only (in dB against frequency on a logarithmic axis).

bodeplot.description: Draws the Bode diagram; same arguments as bode.

bohmanwin.description: Bohman window of length n (zero at both ends). The result is a column vector.

bone.description: n-by-3 greyscale colormap with a slight blue tint.

bootci.description: Bootstrap confidence interval for the statistic computed by bootfun. 'Type' is 'bca' (default), 'norm', 'per', 'cper' or 'stud'; 'Alpha' sets the level (default 0.05).

bootstrp.description: Bootstrap: draw nboot samples with replacement from the rows of the data and apply bootfun to each. Every row of bootstat is one result; bootsam holds the row numbers used.

boundary.description: Coordinates of the boundaries of p (or of the boundaries I) as column vectors, each closed by repeating its first vertex and separated by NaN. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.boundary(...).

boundingbox.description: Smallest and largest x and y of the vertices of p (of all elements of an array), or of the boundaries I. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.boundingbox(...).

bounds.description: Smallest and largest elements of x in one call, ignoring NaN. mylab always looks at all elements; a dimension argument is not supported.

box.description: Shows or hides the top and right edges of the current axes' frame; box alone toggles. The axes property Box does the same.

boxchart.description: Box-and-whisker plot; drawn like boxplot in mylab.

boxplot.description: Box-and-whisker plot. Each column of x is one box, or the values of a vector x are split by the grouping variable. Options: 'Labels', 'Notch', 'Whisker', 'Widths', 'Positions', 'Orientation' ('horizontal').

brush.description: Turns data brushing on or off for the current figure. The state is recorded on the figure and returned by s = brush; selecting data needs a mouse, so nothing can be brushed.

bsxfun.description: Expands singleton dimensions of A and B so their sizes match, then calls the binary function f once with the expanded arrays. Plain operators already expand like this, e.g. A - mean(A).

bubblechart.description: A scatter plot whose marker sizes show a third value. bubblesize and bubblelim control how values map to sizes.

bubblechart3.description: A 3-D scatter plot whose marker sizes show a fourth value.

bubblelegend.description: A legend that shows what bubble sizes mean.

bubblelim.description: The data values shown with the smallest and the largest bubble.

bubblesize.description: Diameters in points of the smallest and largest bubbles of an axes.

bucky.description: The graph of the buckminsterfullerene molecule C60, the pattern of a soccer ball: B is the 60-by-60 sparse adjacency matrix (each atom has three neighbours, 90 edges in all) and V the 60-by-3 coordinates of the atoms, on the unit sphere. The atoms are numbered in another order than MATLAB's (by height, then around), so the same graph has a permuted B.

buffer.description: Cuts a signal into frames of n samples, one per column, overlapping by p samples (or skipping -p samples when p is negative). The first frame starts with p zeros unless opt is 'nodelay' or a vector of p starting samples. The last frame is padded with zeros; with two outputs only full frames are returned and z holds the samples left over.

builtin.description: Calls the built-in function with that name, even when a file or class method with the same name exists.

buttap.description: Analog Butterworth lowpass prototype of order n with cutoff 1 rad/s: no zeros, poles on the unit circle in the left half plane, gain 1.

butter.description: Butterworth filter of order n with the -3 dB frequency Wn. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'; a two-element Wn gives a bandpass filter of order 2n unless 'stop' is asked for. With three outputs the zeros, poles and gain are returned, with four a state-space model [A, B, C, D]. A trailing 's' designs an analog filter, whose frequencies are in rad/s.

buttord.description: Lowest Butterworth order that loses at most Rp dB up to Wp and at least Rs dB from Ws, with the cutoff Wn to pass to butter. Scalars describe a lowpass (Wp < Ws) or highpass filter, two-element vectors a bandpass or bandstop filter. The stopband requirement is met exactly.

bvp4c.description: Solves the two-point boundary value problem y' = odefun(x, y), bcfun(ya, yb) = 0 by 4th-order collocation with residual control. With unknown parameters the functions are odefun(x, y, p) and bcfun(ya, yb, p), and bcfun returns one extra condition per parameter. The result has fields x, y, yp, parameters and stats; evaluate it with deval. Options come from bvpset.

bvp5c.description: Solves a two-point boundary value problem like bvp4c (same arguments and result). mylab uses the same collocation method for both.

bvpget.description: Value of one option from an options structure; default (or []) when the option is not set.

bvpinit.description: Initial guess for bvp4c and bvp5c: the mesh x and a guess for the solution, either a vector (the same at every mesh point) or a function y = yinit(x). params is a guess for unknown parameters. The last form extends a solution to a wider interval.

bvpset.description: Options for bvp4c and bvp5c: RelTol (1e-3), AbsTol (1e-6), NMax (largest number of mesh points), Stats, Vectorized, FJacobian, BCJacobian and SingularTerm.

bwarea.description: Area of the foreground with a weighting of the 2-by-2 pixel patterns that allows for the slanted edges of objects; close to, but not the same as, the pixel count.

bwareafilt.description: Keeps the objects whose area lies in [low high], or the n largest (or 'smallest') objects.

bwareaopen.description: Removes connected groups with fewer than p pixels from a binary image.

bwboundaries.description: Traces the outer boundary of each object in a binary image (8-connected). B is a cell array with one k-by-2 matrix of [row column] points per object, going clockwise and ending at its starting point; L is the label matrix and n the number of objects. Boundaries of holes inside objects are not traced, with or without 'noholes'.

bwconncomp.description: Connected components of a 2-D binary image as a struct with fields Connectivity, ImageSize, NumObjects and PixelIdxList (a cell with the linear indices of each component).

bwconvhull.description: Convex hull image: the smallest convex region that covers all foreground pixels ('union', the default) or one hull per object ('objects').

bwdist.description: Distance from every pixel to the nearest true pixel, as single. method is 'euclidean' (default), 'cityblock', 'chessboard' or 'quasi-euclidean'. idx is the linear index of that nearest pixel.

bweuler.description: Euler number: the number of objects minus the number of holes (8-connected objects by default).

bwhitmiss.description: Hit-or-miss transform: keeps the pixels whose neighbourhood contains SE1 in the foreground and SE2 in the background. An interval is a matrix of 1 (foreground), -1 (background) and 0 (either).

bwlabel.description: Labels the connected groups of true pixels in a binary image with 1, 2, ..., n (0 is background). conn is 8 (default; diagonal neighbours touch) or 4. Groups are numbered in the order their first pixel appears going down the columns.

bwlabeln.description: Labels the connected components of a binary array of any dimension (8-connected in 2-D and 26-connected in 3-D by default).

bwmorph.description: Applies a binary morphological operation n times (once by default; Inf repeats until nothing changes). Operations: 'thin' and 'skel' (reduce shapes to one-pixel-wide lines, both by Zhang-Suen thinning), 'remove' (keep outlines), 'clean' (drop isolated pixels), 'fill' (fill isolated holes), 'majority', 'bridge', 'diag', 'spur', 'hbreak', 'endpoints', 'branchpoints', 'dilate', 'erode', 'open', 'close', 'tophat', 'bothat', 'perim4' and 'perim8'. Thinned shapes can differ by a few pixels from other implementations.

bwperim.description: Outline of the objects in a binary image: true pixels that touch a false pixel or the image border (4-connected by default).

bwpropfilt.description: Keeps the objects whose regionprops property lies in [low high], or the n objects with the 'largest' (default) or 'smallest' values.

bwselect.description: Keeps the objects that contain the pixels at columns c and rows r (n-connected, default 8).

bwskel.description: Skeleton of a binary image: objects are thinned to lines one pixel wide that keep their connectivity.

usage: B = bwtraceboundary(BW, P, fstep, conn, N, dir)
bwtraceboundary.description: Follows the boundary of an object from the pixel P = [row col], looking first in the compass direction fstep ('N', 'NE', 'E', ...). B lists the [row col] of at most N boundary pixels, going 'clockwise' (default) or 'counterclockwise'.

bwulterode.description: Ultimate erosion: the regional maxima of the distance to the background, one spot for each rounded part of an object.

c2d.description: Discretizes a continuous-time model with sample time Ts. Methods: 'zoh' (zero-order hold on the input, the default; exact for inputs that are constant between samples), 'foh' (first-order hold: straight lines between samples), 'impulse' (impulse invariant), 'tustin' (bilinear transformation; add a critical frequency to match the response there exactly, as in c2d(sys, Ts, 'prewarp', w0)) and 'matched' (poles and zeros mapped with z = exp(s*Ts), SISO only). Delays become whole sample delays; with 'zoh' a delay that is not a multiple of Ts is treated exactly (the model gets extra states), with the other methods it is rounded and a warning is given. For a state-space model and 'zoh' or 'foh', G maps the continuous initial conditions [x0; u0] to the discrete initial state.

c2dOptions.description: Options for c2d: the method and, for 'tustin', the frequency at which the response is matched.

caldays.description: A calendar duration of n calendar days (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

caldiff.description: Calendar durations between successive elements of a datetime vector.

calendar.description: Shows the calendar of a month (the current one by default), or returns it as a 6-by-7 matrix with weeks as rows starting on Sunday and zeros for days outside the month.

calmonths.description: A calendar duration of n calendar months (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calquarters.description: A calendar duration of n calendar quarters (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calweeks.description: A calendar duration of n calendar weeks (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

calyears.description: A calendar duration of n calendar years (whole numbers). Added to a datetime it moves by calendar units, so the clock time is kept and month ends are respected: datetime(2024,1,31) + calmonths(1) is 29-Feb-2024.

camdolly.description: Move the camera and its target sideways, up and toward the scene.

camlight.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. An output, if requested, is [].

camlookat.description: Fit the view to the objects h (or to everything in the axes).

camorbit.description: Move the camera around its target, horizontally and vertically, in degrees.

campos.description: campos([x y z]) places the camera; campos returns where it is.

camproj.description: camproj('orthographic' | 'perspective') sets the projection; camproj returns it.

camroll.description: Turn the camera about its viewing axis by dtheta degrees.

camtarget.description: camtarget([x y z]) sets the point the camera looks at; camtarget returns it.

camup.description: camup([x y z]) sets the direction that points up in the picture; camup returns it.

camva.description: camva(angle) sets the camera view angle in degrees (smaller zooms in); camva returns it.

camzoom.description: Zoom in (f > 1) or out (f < 1) by changing the camera view angle.

canUseGPU.description: Always false: mylab does not use GPUs.

canUseParallelPool.description: Always false: mylab runs everything in one process.

canon.description: Canonical state-space forms. 'modal' (default) makes A block diagonal, with real poles on the diagonal and a 2-by-2 block [re im; -im re] per complex pair; 'companion' puts the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial in the last column of A. T is the state transformation xc = T*x. The modal form needs a full set of eigenvectors and the companion form controllability from the first input.

usage: [A, B, r, U, V, stats] = canoncorr(X, Y)
canoncorr.description: Canonical correlation analysis: coefficients A and B, canonical correlations r, canonical variables U and V, and tests of the number of non-zero correlations.

usage: X = care(A, B, Q, R, S, E)
care.description: Stabilizing solution of the continuous algebraic Riccati equation A'*X*E + E'*X*A - (E'*X*B + S)*inv(R)*(B'*X*E + S') + Q = 0. R defaults to the identity, S to zero and E to the identity. G = inv(R)*(B'*X*E + S') is the feedback gain and L the closed-loop poles of A - B*G.

cart2pol.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to polar (or cylindrical): theta is the angle in radians and rho the distance from the origin. A single matrix with 2 or 3 columns may be given and, with one output, a matrix of the same layout is returned.

cart2sph.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to spherical: azimuth in the x-y plane, elevation from that plane (both in radians) and radius.

cartesianToBarycentric.description: Barycentric coordinates of the points C (one row per ID) relative to the triangles or tetrahedra ID; the rows of B sum to 1. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.cartesianToBarycentric(...).

caseInsensitivePattern.description: A pattern that matches p without regard to upper and lower case. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

caseSensitivePattern.description: A pattern that matches p with the exact case, even in a function that is called with 'IgnoreCase', true. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

cast.description: Converts x to the named class: 'double', 'single', 'logical', 'char' or an integer class. cast(x, 'like', p) converts to the class of p.

cat.description: Joins arrays along dimension dim: 1 stacks them vertically, 2 side by side, 3 stacks them as pages of an N-D array, and so on. Sizes must agree in every other dimension.

categorical.description: Creates a categorical array: each element is one of a fixed list of named categories. values can be numbers, logical values, a cell array of text or a string array. Without valueset the categories are the sorted distinct values; empty text and NaN become <undefined>. names gives the category name for each allowed value. Compare with text (c == 'red'), count with countcats, list with categories. Ordinal arrays also support < and >. Assigning a new name adds a category. Works as a table variable and as a grouping variable for groupsummary, findgroups and grp2idx. Example: c = categorical({'red', 'blue', 'red'})

categories.description: Returns the category names of a categorical array as a cell array (a column), in category order. Example: c = categorical({'red', 'blue', 'red'}); categories(c) gives {'blue'; 'red'}.

category.description: Model category: 'library', 'custom', 'interpolant' or 'spline'. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

caxis.description: Sets the data values mapped to the first and last colormap colours of the current axes (surfaces, images, filled contours and scatter colours); 'auto' returns to the data range, and with no input the current limits are returned. clim is the newer name. Call it after plotting.

cbrt.description: Real cube root of each element.

cceps.description: Complex cepstrum: the inverse FFT of the complex logarithm of the spectrum, with the phase unwrapped and its linear part (a delay of nd samples) removed.

cconv.description: Circular convolution modulo n: the ordinary convolution wrapped onto n samples. Without n the result is the ordinary convolution.

cd.description: Changes the current working folder (a leading ~ means your home folder). With no input, prints or returns the current folder.

cdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of a distribution given by name and parameters, or of a probability distribution object. 'upper' returns the upper tail probability.

cdfplot.description: Plot the empirical cumulative distribution function of x. stats holds the minimum, maximum, mean, median and standard deviation of the sample.

ceil.description: Rounds each element up, toward +Inf. Example: ceil(2.1) is 3.

cell.description: Cell array whose cells all hold the empty matrix []. cell(n) is n-by-n.

cell2mat.description: Concatenates the contents of a cell array into one array, joining each row of cells side by side and then stacking the rows. The pieces must fit together. Example: cell2mat({1 2; 3 4}) is [1 2; 3 4].

cell2struct.description: Builds a scalar struct whose fields, named by a cell array (or a single name), take their values from the cells of C in order. A dimension argument and struct-array results are not supported.

cell2table.description: Makes a table with one variable per column of the cell array C. Columns holding only numeric scalars become numeric variables; others stay cell columns.

celldisp.description: Prints the contents of every cell, labelled like C{1} or C{2,3}, descending into nested cell arrays. name replaces the label 'C'.

cellfun.description: Calls f on the contents of each cell (on matching cells of several same-size inputs). By default every call must return a scalar and the results form an array the size of C; with 'UniformOutput' false they are collected in a cell array. f may be a handle or a function name; the names 'isempty', 'length', 'numel', 'isreal', 'islogical' and 'ndims' are handled directly. An error handler h is called with an error struct and the inputs. Example: cellfun(@numel, {'ab', 'c'}) is [2 1].

cellstr.description: Converts text to a cell array of char vectors: each row of a char matrix becomes one cell (trailing blanks removed), giving a column; a string array gives a cell array of the same size (<missing> becomes ''); a cell array is returned as is.

centrality.description: Importance of each node. For a graph: 'degree', 'closeness', 'betweenness', 'pagerank', 'eigenvector'. For a digraph: 'indegree', 'outdegree', 'incloseness', 'outcloseness', 'betweenness', 'pagerank', 'hubs', 'authorities'. Tolerance and MaxIterations control the iterative types.

centroid.description: Center of mass of the filled area of p (holes subtracted), or of each boundary I taken as a solid. NaN for an empty polyshape. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.centroid(...).

cfit.description: Curve fit object with the given coefficient values (fit returns cfit objects too). f(x) and feval(f, x) evaluate it. Methods: coeffvalues, coeffnames, confint, predint, differentiate, integrate, formula, numcoeffs, argnames, dependnames, indepnames, probnames, probvalues, type, category, islinear and plot. Coefficients are read as f.a, f.p1 and so on.

usage: x = cgs(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
cgs.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the conjugate gradient squared method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

char.description: Makes a char array. Numbers are taken as character codes. A cell array, a string array or several text inputs become rows of a char matrix, padded with spaces to equal length. Example: char(72, 105) is a two-row char array; char([72 105]) is 'Hi'. For a datetime array, char(t, fmt) and char(t, fmt, locale) write the dates in format fmt, with month and day names in the language of locale (for example 'fr_FR'; [] for fmt keeps the array's format).

characterListPattern.description: A pattern that matches one character out of the given ones, or one character in the range from first to last. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

charpoly.description: Characteristic polynomial of a square symbolic matrix: its coefficients (highest power first), or the polynomial in x.

cheb1ap.description: Analog Chebyshev type I lowpass prototype with Rp dB of passband ripple and passband edge 1 rad/s.

cheb1ord.description: Lowest Chebyshev type I order that meets the passband ripple Rp and stopband attenuation Rs (dB), with the passband edge to pass to cheby1.

cheb2ap.description: Analog Chebyshev type II lowpass prototype with a stopband Rs dB down that starts at 1 rad/s.

cheb2ord.description: Lowest Chebyshev type II order that meets the passband ripple Rp and stopband attenuation Rs (dB), with the stopband edge to pass to cheby2.

chebwin.description: Chebyshev window whose sidelobes are all r dB (default 100) below the main lobe. The result is a column vector.

cheby1.description: Chebyshev type I filter of order n with Rp dB of ripple in the passband, which ends at Wp. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'; a two-element Wn gives a bandpass filter of order 2n unless 'stop' is asked for. With three outputs the zeros, poles and gain are returned, with four a state-space model [A, B, C, D]. A trailing 's' designs an analog filter, whose frequencies are in rad/s.

cheby2.description: Chebyshev type II filter of order n: flat passband and a stopband that starts at Ws and stays Rs dB down. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'; a two-element Wn gives a bandpass filter of order 2n unless 'stop' is asked for. With three outputs the zeros, poles and gain are returned, with four a state-space model [A, B, C, D]. A trailing 's' designs an analog filter, whose frequencies are in rad/s.

checkerboard.description: Checkerboard image with squares of n pixels (default 10), 2p rows and 2q columns of squares (default p = q = 4). The light squares are white in the left half and gray (0.7) in the right half.

chi2cdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

chi2gof.description: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test. By default the data are tested against a normal distribution with estimated mean and standard deviation, using 10 bins and pooling the end bins until the expected counts reach 5. Options: 'NBins', 'Ctrs', 'Edges', 'CDF', 'Expected', 'NParams', 'EMin', 'Frequency', 'Alpha'. p is NaN when no degrees of freedom are left. stats has chi2stat, df, edges, O and E.

chi2inv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

chi2pdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

chi2rnd.description: Random numbers from the chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

chi2stat.description: Mean m and variance v of the chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom.

children.description: The parts of a symbolic expression (terms of a sum, factors of a product, arguments of a function) as a cell array.

usage: y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method)
y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method, phi)
chirp.description: Swept-frequency cosine whose frequency moves from f0 at time 0 to f1 at time t1 (defaults 0, 1 and 100 Hz). method is 'linear' (default), 'quadratic' or 'logarithmic'; phi is the initial phase in degrees.

chol.description: Cholesky factor of a symmetric positive definite matrix: upper triangular R with R'*R = A, or lower triangular L with L*L' = A. If A is not positive definite it is an error, unless p is requested: then p is nonzero and R is empty (mylab does not return a partial factor).

cholupdate.description: Rank-one update of a Cholesky factor. If R = chol(A), R1 is the upper triangular factor of A + x*x' ('+', the default) or of A - x*x' ('-'). With two outputs a failed downdate returns p = 1 instead of an error (p = 2: R is not a valid factor).
