circshift.description: Shifts elements circularly by k places, wrapping the ones that fall off the end back to the start. Without dim the shift follows the first dimension whose size is not 1; a two-element shift moves rows and columns. Example: circshift([1 2 3], 1) is [3 1 2].

circumcenter.description: Centers (and radii) of the circumscribed circles or spheres of the triangles or tetrahedra. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.circumcenter(...).

cla.description: Removes everything drawn in the current axes, keeping the figure and any other axes.

clabel.description: Writes the level values on the lines of a contour plot, where [C, h] came from contour or contourf. With C alone the most recent contour plot of the current axes is labelled.

class.description: Name of the type of x as a char vector, for example 'double', 'char', 'logical', 'int8', 'cell', 'struct', 'string' or 'function_handle'. Objects report their class name, such as 'table', 'containers.Map' or the name of a classdef class.

usage: [class, err, posterior, logp, coeff] = classify(sample, training, group, type, prior)
classify.description: Discriminant analysis in one call: classify the rows of sample using the training rows and their groups. type is 'linear' (default), 'diaglinear', 'quadratic', 'diagquadratic' or 'mahalanobis'. err is the apparent error rate on the training data.

clc.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

clear.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clearAllMemoizedCaches.description: Empties the cache of every memoized function made with memoize.

clearpoints.description: Removes all points from the animated line h.

clearvars.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clf.description: Clears everything from the current figure, or from figure handle f.

clim.description: Sets the data values mapped to the first and last colormap colours of the current axes (surfaces, images, filled contours and scatter colours); 'auto' returns to the data range, and with no input the current limits are returned. clim is the newer name. Call it after plotting.

clock.description: The current local date and time as [year month day hour minute seconds].

close.description: Closes the current figure, figure number n, the figure with handle f or with that Name, or all figures. close(v) finishes the file of a VideoWriter, and close(h) dismisses a waitbar or message box.

close_system.description: Removes a model from memory. Changes are discarded unless the second argument is 1, which saves the model first. bdclose('all') closes every model.

closereq.description: Deletes the window whose callback is running (the default CloseRequestFcn).

cluster.description: Cut a linkage tree into clusters: at most n clusters, or by a threshold on the inconsistency coefficient (default) or on the linkage distance. Clusters are numbered in order of first appearance.

clusterdata.description: Hierarchical clustering of data in one step (pdist, linkage and cluster).

cmdscale.description: Classical multidimensional scaling: a configuration of points whose distances reproduce the dissimilarities D (a square matrix or a pdist vector). e holds the eigenvalues.

coder.ceval.description: Calls compiled C code, which mylab cannot do: it raises an error. Guard it with if ~coder.target('MATLAB').

coder.cinclude.description: A code-generation directive; does nothing in mylab.

coder.columnMajor.description: A code-generation directive; does nothing in mylab.

coder.const.description: Returns x. (For code generation it marks a value as constant.)

coder.extrinsic.description: A code-generation directive. mylab runs code directly, so this does nothing.

coder.inline.description: A code-generation directive; does nothing in mylab.

coder.nullcopy.description: Returns x. (For code generation it skips an initialization.)

coder.target.description: True for 'MATLAB' (the code is being run, not turned into C) and false for every other target name. Without an input: ''.

coder.updateBuildInfo.description: A code-generation directive; does nothing in mylab.

coder.varsize.description: A code-generation directive; does nothing in mylab.

coeffnames.description: Column cell array of the coefficient names. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

coeffs.description: Coefficients of a polynomial. One output lists the nonzero coefficients from the lowest power up. With two outputs, c and the matching terms t run from the highest power down. 'All' also returns zero coefficients, highest power first.

coeffvalues.description: Row vector of the coefficient values of a fit (a cell holding the piecewise-polynomial structure for interpolants and smoothing splines). f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.coeffvalues(...).

col2im.description: Rearranges columns back into an image: the reverse of im2col.

colamd.description: Column ordering that reduces fill-in when A(:, p) is factorized.

colfilt.description: Neighbourhood operation on columns: every m-by-n neighbourhood becomes one column of a temporary matrix that is passed to fun. For 'sliding', fun returns one value per column; for 'distinct' blocks it returns a matrix of the same size.

collect.description: Groups the terms of an expression by powers of x (or of the default variable).

colon.description: Function form of the a:b and a:step:b range operators. Returns a row vector, empty when the range runs the wrong way or the step is 0.

colorbar.description: Adds a colour scale beside the current axes for the most recent image, surface or contour plot (or for the colormap alone). location is 'eastoutside' (default), 'westoutside', 'northoutside' or 'southoutside'. c is a ColorBar handle: c.Label.String sets its label, and Limits, Ticks, TickLabels and FontSize can be read and set. colorbar off removes it.

colormap.description: Sets the colour map of the current figure, recolouring its images and surfaces and those drawn later. name is a colormap name such as 'parula' (the default, drawn with matplotlib's viridis), 'jet', 'hot', 'gray' or any matplotlib colormap; map is an m-by-3 matrix of RGB values in [0, 1], e.g. jet(16). target may be an axes or figure handle. With an output, returns the current map as a matrix (256 rows for named maps).

colororder.description: Query or change the colours that successive plots in an axes or figure get.

colperm.description: Column permutation that orders the columns by increasing number of nonzeros.

colspace.description: Basis of the column space of a symbolic matrix, one basis vector per column.

columns.description: Number of columns of a, the same as size(a, 2). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

combine.description: Combines terms of the same kind: powers with the same base, logarithms, or products of sines and cosines. With datastores, combine(ds1, ds2, ...) returns a datastore that reads them side by side: each read returns a cell array with one column per datastore (a value that is not a cell array is put in one), and readall stacks the reads. The datastores are copied and start from the beginning.

comet.description: Draws the curve as an ordinary line plot; the moving-head animation is not reproduced.

comet3.description: Draws the 3-D curve as an ordinary plot3 line, without the animation.

compan.description: Companion matrix of the polynomial with coefficients p (highest power first). Its eigenvalues are the roots of the polynomial.

compass.description: Arrows from the origin, drawn in polar axes.

complex.description: Builds a complex array a + b*i. With one input the imaginary part is zero but the result is still stored as complex, so isreal reports false.

compose.description: Formats data into text with sprintf-style conversions, giving one piece of text per row rather than one long result. With a single array, each row is fed to the format, using as many columns per piece as the format has conversions; with several arrays, matching elements are formatted together. Returns a cell array of char vectors, or a string array when fmt is a string. Example: compose('%d-%d', [1 2; 3 4]) is {'1-2'; '3-4'}.

computer.description: The kind of computer: 'GLNXA64', 'PCWIN64', 'MACI64' or 'MACA64' (in the browser 'WASM32'); with 'arch' the lower-case architecture name such as 'glnxa64'. maxsize is the largest number of elements an array may have and endian is 'L' or 'B'.

cond.description: 2-norm condition number, the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value. Large values mean that solving with A loses accuracy. Other norms are not supported.

condeig.description: How sensitive each eigenvalue of A is to small changes in A. For eigenvalue k, with unit left eigenvector y and unit right eigenvector x, the value is 1/|y'*x|: 1 for a normal matrix, and large when the eigenvalue is ill-conditioned. The three-output form also returns the eigenvectors V and the eigenvalues D.

condensation.description: The digraph whose nodes are the strongly connected components of G (numbered as by conncomp), with an edge where G has an edge between two components.

condest.description: Estimate of the 1-norm condition number of a square matrix, computed from a sparse LU factorization. A singular matrix gives Inf.

usage: coneplot(X, Y, Z, U, V, W, Cx, Cy, Cz, s)
coneplot.description: Velocity vectors drawn as cones at the given points.

configureDictionary.description: An empty dictionary whose key and value types are fixed before any entry is added, e.g. configureDictionary("string", "double").

confint.description: Confidence bounds of the coefficients (2-by-p, lower bounds in the first row), from the t distribution with the fit's degrees of freedom; level defaults to 0.95. f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.confint(...).

confusionchart.description: Draw a confusion matrix as a coloured grid with counts. 'Normalization' may be 'row-normalized', 'column-normalized' or 'total-normalized'.

confusionmat.description: Confusion matrix: C(i, j) counts the observations of true class i predicted as class j.

conj.description: Complex conjugate of each element: the sign of the imaginary part is flipped.

conncomp.description: Connected components: bins(k) is the component number of node k. For a digraph the default is strongly connected components, numbered in topological order; 'weak' ignores edge directions.

connect.description: Builds a model from a block diagram. In the first form every block has InputName and OutputName set, and blocks are wired wherever an input name equals an output name; inputs and outputs name the external signals of the result (summing junctions come from sumblk). In the second form blksys is an appended model and each row of Q is [input, outputs feeding it], with a minus sign for a subtracted output; inputs and outputs are index vectors. The result is a state-space model.

containers.Map.description: Creates a map from keys (char vectors or numbers) to values. Read and write entries with m(key) and m(key) = value; use keys(m), values(m), isKey(m, k), remove(m, k) and m.Count. A map is a handle: copying the variable shares the same map.

contains.description: True if s contains pattern anywhere. pattern may be a cell or string array, meaning any of them. s may be a cell or string array, giving a logical array.

contour.description: Draws contour lines (lines of equal height) of Z, optionally over the grid X, Y, with n levels or at the given level values (also 'LevelList'). 'ShowText', 'on' labels the lines; 'LineColor' and 'LineWidth' style them. Replaces the current axes unless hold is on. With two outputs, C is the contour matrix (for each line a column [level; count] followed by the x and y coordinates) and h the Contour handle.

usage: contour3(Z) or contour3(X, Y, Z, levels)
contour3.description: Contour lines drawn at their heights in 3-D axes.

usage: C = contourc(Z, levels) or contourc(x, y, Z, levels)

contourf.description: Like contour, but fills the regions between the contour lines with colour.

contourslice.description: Contour lines of volume data in slice planes.

contrast.description: A gray colormap that spreads the intensities of an image evenly.

controlSystemDesigner.description: Control system design app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

conv.description: Convolution of two vectors, which is also polynomial multiplication. shape is 'full' (default, length numel(u)+numel(v)-1), 'same' (central part the size of u) or 'valid'. The result is a column if u is a column. Example: conv([1 1], [1 -1]) is [1 0 -1].

conv2.description: Two-dimensional convolution. shape 'full' (default) returns the whole result, 'same' the central part with the size of A, and 'valid' only the part computed without zero padding. With two vectors u and v, A is convolved with column u and then with row v.

convertCharsToStrings.description: Converts char arrays to string scalars and cell arrays of char vectors to string arrays. Other values are returned unchanged.

convertStringsToChars.description: Converts string scalars to char vectors and string arrays to cell arrays of char vectors. Other values are returned unchanged.

convertTo.description: Converts a datetime array to numbers: kind is 'datenum', 'posixtime', 'excel', 'juliandate', 'modifiedjuliandate' or 'yyyymmdd'.

convertvars.description: Converts the selected variables of a table with a conversion function given by name ('string', 'double', 'categorical', ...) or as a function handle. Variables are selected by name, by number, with a logical vector, with vartype(...) or with a function handle such as @isnumeric.

convexHull.description: Convex hull of a delaunayTriangulation: in 2-D a closed counterclockwise list of vertex IDs, in 3-D a triangle list with outward normals; AV is the area or volume. Also DT.convexHull().

convhull.description: Convex hull. In 2-D, k lists the corner points counterclockwise, starting from the leftmost point and ending where it starts, so plot(x(k), y(k)) draws the hull; v is the area. In 3-D, each row of k is a triangle of the hull surface and v the volume. Points that are all on one line (or plane) raise an error.

convhulln.description: Convex hull of the points in the rows of P in any dimension: each row of K is a facet, v the enclosed volume.

convn.description: N-dimensional convolution. shape is 'full' (default), 'same' (the central part, the size of A) or 'valid' (only where B fits completely inside A).

cool.description: n-by-3 colormap from cyan to magenta.

cophenet.description: Cophenetic correlation between the tree Z and the distances Y it was built from; d holds the cophenetic distances.

copper.description: n-by-3 colormap from black to a light copper colour.

copularnd.description: Random points in the unit cube from a copula: Gaussian or t with correlation matrix rho (a scalar means a 2-by-2 matrix), or the bivariate 'Clayton', 'Frank' or 'Gumbel' copula with parameter alpha.

copyElement.description: The method a class derived from matlab.mixin.Copyable overrides (in a methods (Access = protected) block) to change what copy(obj) does, for example to copy the objects its properties refer to. Call copyElement@matlab.mixin.Copyable(obj) inside it for the standard shallow copy, in which NonCopyable properties get their default values.

copyfile.description: Copies a file or a whole folder. source may contain wildcards (*), and destination may be a folder; existing files are overwritten. With outputs, [status, message, messageId] report success (true) or the reason for failure instead of raising an error.

copyobj.description: Copies 2-D line objects into the axes ax and returns the copies. Other kinds of object cannot be copied in mylab.

corner.description: Corner points as [x y] rows, strongest first, at most N (default 200). The method is 'Harris' (default) or 'MinimumEigenvalue'; 'QualityLevel' (default 0.01), 'SensitivityFactor' (default 0.04) and 'FilterCoefficients' are available.

corr.description: Linear (Pearson, default) or rank (Spearman) correlation between the columns of X, or between each column of X and each column of Y. Kendall's tau is not supported.

corr2.description: Correlation coefficient between two arrays of the same size.

corrcoef.description: Pearson correlation coefficients between the columns of X (or between x and y), with ones on the diagonal. P holds p-values for testing zero correlation. Name-value options are ignored.

corrcov.description: Correlation matrix R and standard deviations sigma from a covariance matrix C.

cos.description: Cosine of each element, with x in radians.

cosd.description: Cosine of angles given in degrees. Odd multiples of 90 give exactly 0.

cospi.description: cos(pi*x), exact for integers and half-integers (cospi(0.5) is 0).

cotd.description: Cotangent of an angle in degrees.

count.description: Number of non-overlapping occurrences of pattern (or of any pattern in a list) in s. A cell array of text gives an array of counts. Example: count('banana', 'an') is 2.

countEachLabel.description: Table with one row per label of an image datastore: the variable Label (categorical) and the variable Count, the number of files that have that label. For categorical labels every category is listed, in category order. Also callable as ds.countEachLabel().

countcats.description: Number of elements in each category of a categorical array, in category order.

cov.description: Covariance. For a vector, the variance; for a matrix whose columns are variables, the covariance matrix; for two vectors, their 2-by-2 covariance matrix. w = 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1. 'omitrows' drops rows containing NaN.

covar.description: Output covariance P and state covariance Q of a stable model driven by white noise of intensity W. A continuous-time model with direct feedthrough has an infinite output covariance.

cp2tform.description: Fits a transformation to pairs of control points and returns a maketform struct. The type is 'nonreflective similarity', 'similarity', 'affine' or 'projective'.

usage: [pxy, f] = cpsd(x, y, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
cpsd.description: Cross power spectral density of x and y by Welch's method: the average of conj(X) .* Y over the segments, so its phase is the phase by which y lags x. The inputs are those of pwelch.

cputime.description: Processor time used by mylab so far, in seconds. Differences between two calls time code.

createCallbackFcn.description: Part of the code App Designer exports: returns a callback that calls method(app, event), or method(app) when passEvent is false.

usage: problem = createOptimProblem('fmincon', 'objective', fun, 'x0', x0, 'lb', lb, 'ub', ub)
createOptimProblem.description: Bundle an objective, a start point, bounds and constraints into a problem structure for GlobalSearch and MultiStart.

createns.description: Create a KDTreeSearcher or an ExhaustiveSearcher for the points X.

cross.description: Cross product of two 3-element vectors, shaped like a. Matrix inputs are not supported. Example: cross([1 0 0], [0 1 0]) is [0 0 1].

crosstab.description: Cross-tabulation: counts of every combination of the values of the grouping variables. chi2 and p test independence; labels is a cell array with the value names of each variable in its own column.

crossval.description: Cross-validation. fun(XTRAIN, ..., XTEST, ...) is called once per fold (10 folds by default) and its results are stacked in rows. The 'mse' and 'mcr' forms return the cross-validated mean squared error or misclassification rate of predfun(XTRAIN, ytrain, XTEST). Options: 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout', 'Partition', 'Stratify' and 'MCReps'.

cscd.description: Cosecant of an angle in degrees.

csvread.description: Reads a comma-separated numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based row and column offsets of the first value to read.

csvwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix as comma-separated values with five significant digits; r and c shift the data down and right, padding with zeros.

ctranspose.description: Same as A' : swaps rows and columns and conjugates complex values.

ctrb.description: Controllability matrix [B, A*B, A^2*B, ...]. The system is controllable when its rank equals the number of states.

usage: [Abar, Bbar, Cbar, T, k] = ctrbf(A, B, C)
ctrbf.description: Controllability staircase form: an orthogonal T with Abar = T*A*T' = [Auc 0; A21 Ac] and Bbar = T*B = [0; Bc], where (Ac, Bc) is controllable and Auc holds the uncontrollable modes. k lists how many controllable states each step found, so sum(k) is the controllable dimension.

cummax.description: Running maximum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: cummax([1 3 2 5]) is [1 3 3 5].

cummin.description: Running minimum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumprod.description: Running product along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumsum.description: Running total along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. 'reverse' accumulates from the end. Integer inputs keep their class and saturate. NaN flags are accepted but have no effect. Example: cumsum([1 2 3]) is [1 3 6].

cumtrapz.description: Running trapezoid-rule integral, same size as y and starting at 0. Uses unit spacing or the points in x, along the first dimension whose size is not 1.

curl.description: Curl of a symbolic vector field V with three components, for the variables X.

cvpartition.description: Random partition of n observations for cross-validation. With a grouping variable the partition is stratified (each class is spread evenly) unless 'Stratify' is false. Use training(c, i) and test(c, i) for the logical masks of fold i; properties: NumTestSets, TrainSize, TestSize, NumObservations and Type.

cwt.description: Continuous wavelet transform with an analytic wavelet: 'morse' (the default, with symmetry 3 and time-bandwidth product 60), 'amor' (Morlet) or 'bump'. wt has one row per scale and one column per sample; f lists the centre frequency of each row from high to low (cycles per sample, or Hz with fs), with 10 scales per octave. The wavelets are scaled so that a sine wave of amplitude A gives |wt| near A. coi marks, for every sample, the frequency below which end effects matter. Options: 'VoicesPerOctave', 'TimeBandwidth', 'WaveletParameters', 'FrequencyLimits', 'NumOctaves' and 'ExtendSignal'.

cylinder.description: Coordinates of a cylinder of height 1 with n points around (default 20). r is the radius, or a vector of radii along the height for a surface of revolution. Without outputs it draws the surface.

czt.description: Chirp z-transform: the z-transform of x at the m points a * w.^-(0:m-1). The defaults give the ordinary DFT; other values zoom in on part of the spectrum.

d2c.description: Continuous-time model whose discretization is sysd. Methods: 'zoh' (default; uses a matrix logarithm and fails for poles at z = 0 or on the negative real axis), 'tustin' and 'matched'.

d2cOptions.description: Options for d2c: the method and, for 'tustin', the prewarp frequency.

d2d.description: Changes the sample time of a discrete-time model, with the 'zoh' (default) or 'tustin' method. When the new sample time is a multiple of the old one and the method is 'zoh', the result is exact for inputs held over the longer period.

d2dOptions.description: Options for d2d: the method and, for 'tustin', the prewarp frequency.

damp.description: Natural frequency, damping ratio and time constant of each pole, sorted by natural frequency. For a discrete-time model the poles are first mapped to the s-plane with log(z)/Ts. Without outputs a table is printed.

usage: X = dare(A, B, Q, R, S, E)
dare.description: Stabilizing solution of the discrete algebraic Riccati equation A'*X*A - E'*X*E - (A'*X*B + S)*inv(B'*X*B + R)*(B'*X*A + S') + Q = 0, with the gain G = inv(B'*X*B + R)*(B'*X*A + S') and the closed-loop poles L.

daspect.description: Sets the relative length of one data unit along x, y and z; daspect([1 1 1]) draws circles as circles, like axis equal. In 3-D only equal ratios have an effect.

datacursormode.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

datasample.description: Picks k random elements of a vector, or k random rows of a matrix or table (columns with dim = 2). Sampling is with replacement unless 'Replace', false. idx are the positions that were picked.

datastore.description: Creates a datastore for a collection of files. The default kind is the tabular text datastore (see tabularTextDatastore); 'Type', 'image' makes an image datastore (see imageDatastore) and takes its options. Another 'Type' is an error.

date.description: Today's date as text in the form '15-Mar-2024'.

usage: n = datenum(Y, M, D, H, MI, S)
n = datenum([Y M D H MI S])
datenum.description: Converts dates to serial date numbers. A serial date number counts days from year 0, with the time of day as the fraction. Input can be a datetime array, date text (optionally with a datestr-style format), separate components, or a matrix of date vectors.

dateshift.description: Moves each datetime to the start or end of the unit of time that contains it: 'year', 'quarter', 'month', 'week' (weeks start on Sunday), 'day', 'hour', 'minute' or 'second'. The end of a year, quarter, month or week is its last day; the end of a shorter unit is the instant the next one begins. rule is 'current' (default), 'next', 'previous', 'nearest' or a whole number of units to move. With 'dayofweek', moves to the given weekday (a name or 1-7 with 1 = Sunday) on or after t ('next', default), on or before t ('previous') or closest to t ('nearest').

datestr.description: Formats dates as text. t can be serial date numbers, date vectors, datetimes or date text; several dates give one row of text each. The default is 'dd-mmm-yyyy HH:MM:SS', or just the date when every time is midnight. Format numbers 0 to 31 select standard layouts (for example 1 is 'dd-mmm-yyyy', 13 is 'HH:MM:SS', 29 is 'yyyy-mm-dd' and 31 is 'yyyy-mm-dd HH:MM:SS'). A free format uses yyyy, yy, mmmm, mmm, mm (month), dddd, ddd, dd, HH, MM (minute), SS, FFF (milliseconds) and AM or PM for a 12-hour clock.

datetick.description: Label an axis that holds serial date numbers with dates.

usage: t = datetime(Y, M, D, H, MI, S)
datetime.description: Creates an array of points in time. Numeric inputs give the year, month, day and optionally the hour, minute and second (scalars or arrays of one size; out-of-range values roll over). Text (a char vector, string array or cell array of text) is parsed: ISO forms such as '2024-03-15 10:30:00' and common forms such as '15-Mar-2024', '03/15/2024' or 'March 15, 2024' are recognized automatically, and 'InputFormat' states the layout explicitly. 'ConvertFrom' accepts 'datenum', 'posixtime', 'excel', 'juliandate', 'modifiedjuliandate', 'yyyymmdd' and 'epochtime'. 'Format' sets how values are shown, using the letters y (year), M (month: MM number, MMM short name, MMMM full name), d (day), e (weekday: eee short, eeee full), H (hour 0-23), h (hour 1-12), m (minute), s (second), S (fraction of a second), a (AM/PM), with literal text in single quotes. 'TimeZone' may be 'UTC', 'local', '' (none) or an IANA zone name such as 'Europe/Paris'. 'Locale' (such as 'fr_FR', 'de_DE', 'es_ES', 'it_IT', 'pt_BR', 'nl_NL', 'sv_SE', 'pl_PL', 'ru_RU', 'ja_JP' or 'zh_CN'; default 'en_US') is the language of month names, weekday names and the AM/PM marker in the text read; values are shown in English, and char(t, fmt, locale) shows them in another language. Properties Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Format and TimeZone can be read and set. Datetimes support subtraction (giving a duration), adding durations and calendar durations, comparison, sorting, indexing and concatenation; NaT marks a missing value.

datetime.empty.description: An empty datetime array (0-by-0 by default).

usage: [Y, M, D, H, MI, S] = datevec(t)
datevec.description: Splits dates into components. Each row of v is [year month day hour minute second]. t can be serial date numbers, date text or datetimes.

day.description: Day of the month of each element of a datetime array. Options give the day of the year, the day of the week (1 is Sunday) or the English weekday names ('name' or 'shortname'; char(t, 'eeee', locale) gives them in another language).

days.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many 24-hour days. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of 24-hour days.

dbcont.description: At the K>> prompt: continue running until the next breakpoint.

dbdown.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

usage: q = dblquad(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
q = dblquad(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, tol, method)
dblquad.description: Double integral over a rectangle. f(x, y) is called with a vector x and a scalar y. method is @quad (default), @quadl, @quadgk or @integral.

dbquit.description: At the K>> prompt: stop the program.

dbscan.description: Density-based clustering: points with at least minpts neighbours within epsilon are core points; clusters are numbered from 1 and noise points get -1. A distance matrix can be given with 'Distance', 'precomputed'.

dbstack.description: The functions that are running, innermost first. As an output it is a struct array with the fields file, name and line (the line each function is at); n leaves out the first n entries and '-completenames' gives full file paths. k is the index of the current workspace (1).

dbstatus.description: Lists the breakpoints, or returns them as a struct array.

dbstep.description: At the K>> prompt: run the next line (stepping over calls), step into a function, or run until the current function returns.

dbstop.description: Sets a breakpoint: the program pauses with a K>> prompt when it reaches that line. Needs an interactive terminal. In the web app, use Step through instead.

dbup.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

dcgain.description: Steady-state gain: the transfer matrix at s = 0 (continuous time) or z = 1 (discrete time). A channel with an integrator has an infinite DC gain.

dct.description: Discrete cosine transform, scaled so that it is orthogonal. Type 2 is the default; types 1, 3 and 4 are available. x is padded or cut to n samples; matrices are transformed column by column.

dct2.description: Two-dimensional discrete cosine transform of a matrix, padded or cut to m-by-n first.

usage: sol = dde23(ddefun, lags, history, tspan, options)
dde23.description: Solves delay differential equations y'(t) = ddefun(t, y, Z) with constant lags: column j of Z is y(t - lags(j)). history is a vector, a function y = history(t) for t <= t0, or an earlier solution to continue. Discontinuities are tracked and stepped onto. The result has fields x, y, yp, discont and stats (and xe, ye, ie with events, called as events(t, y, Z)); evaluate it with deval.

ddeget.description: Value of one option from an options structure; default (or []) when the option is not set.

ddencmp.description: Default values for denoising ('den') or compression ('cmp') of x with wdencmp: a threshold, soft or hard thresholding, and whether to keep the approximation.

usage: sol = ddesd(ddefun, delays, history, tspan, options)
ddesd.description: Solves delay differential equations with general delays. delays is a function d = delays(t, y) returning the delayed times (not the lags), a cell array of such functions, or a vector of constant lags. Column j of Z is y(d(j)).

ddeset.description: Options for dde23 and ddesd: RelTol (1e-3), AbsTol (1e-6), NormControl, InitialStep, MaxStep, InitialY, Jumps, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Refine and Stats.

deal.description: Copies inputs to outputs: one input is copied to every output; otherwise there must be as many inputs as outputs and each goes to its own output.

deblank.description: Removes trailing whitespace and null characters only.

dec2base.description: Text for the non-negative integer d in the given base (2 to 36), with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. A char vector of symbols can be given instead of the base.

dec2bin.description: Binary digits of the integer d as text, with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. A fraction is dropped; a negative number is written in two's complement with the fewest bits (8, 16, 32 or 64) that hold every value, so dec2bin(-5) is '11111011'. Example: dec2bin(5) is '101'.

dec2hex.description: Hexadecimal digits (upper case) of the integer d as text, with at least n digits. An array gives a char matrix with one row per number. Negative numbers are written in two's complement as for dec2bin, so dec2hex(-1) is 'FF'. Example: dec2hex(255) is 'FF'.

usage: [y0, yp0] = decic(f, t0, y0guess, fixed_y0, yp0guess, fixed_yp0)
[y0, yp0, resnrm] = decic(f, t0, y0guess, fixed_y0, yp0guess, fixed_yp0, options)
decic.description: Consistent initial conditions for ode15i: changes the guesses so that f(t0, y0, yp0) = 0. fixed_y0 and fixed_yp0 are vectors with 1 for the components that must keep their guessed value (or [] for none). The slopes are adjusted first; the free components of y0 only when that is not enough. resnrm is the norm of the remaining residual.

decimate.description: Lowers the sample rate of a vector by the integer r after lowpass filtering. The default filter is a Chebyshev type I filter of order n (default 8) run forwards and backwards; the kept samples are r apart and end with the last one. 'fir' uses a Hamming-window FIR filter of order n (default 30) and keeps the first sample.

decomposition.description: Factorizes A once and stores the result, so that many systems can be solved quickly with dA\b and b/dA (also dA'\b). type is 'auto', 'qr', 'cod', 'lu', 'ldl', 'chol', 'triangular', 'permutedTriangular', 'banded', 'hessenberg' or 'diagonal'. Properties: Type, MatrixSize, IsReal, IsSparse, IsConjugateTransposed, ScaleFactor, CheckCondition, Datatype. Functions: isIllConditioned(dA), rcond(dA), rank(dA) for 'qr' and 'cod'.

deconv.description: Polynomial division: b = conv(a, q) + r. r has the same length as b, padded with leading zeros.

deconvlucy.description: Removes a known blur with the Richardson-Lucy algorithm, which keeps the image non-negative. iter (default 10) is the number of iterations; dampar damps changes smaller than the noise. The plain algorithm is used, without acceleration.

usage: [J, lagra] = deconvreg(I, psf, np, lrange, regop)
deconvreg.description: Removes a known blur with a regularised filter that favours smooth results. np is the noise power; the multiplier lagra is searched in lrange (default [1e-9 1e9]) so that the blurred result differs from I by that amount. regop defaults to the Laplacian.

deconvwnr.description: Removes a known blur (the point-spread function psf) with a Wiener filter. nsr is the noise-to-signal power ratio (default 0, a plain inverse filter).

deg2rad.description: Converts angles from degrees to radians (multiplies by pi/180).

degree.description: Number of edges at each node of an undirected graph. A self-loop counts twice.

del2.description: Discrete Laplacian. For a vector it is one quarter of the second difference; for a matrix it is (d2U/dx2 + d2U/dy2)/4. Values on the edges are extrapolated from the interior. h, hx and hy are scalar spacings between points (default 1).

delaunay.description: Delaunay triangulation. Each row of T holds the point numbers of one triangle (counterclockwise), or of one tetrahedron in 3-D. Draw it with triplot(T, x, y) or trisurf(T, x, y, z).

delaunayTriangulation.description: Delaunay triangulation of 2-D or 3-D points (counterclockwise triangles in 2-D). Duplicate points are removed with a warning. C (k-by-2 point indices) gives 2-D edge constraints, which are recovered by edge flips; constraints that cross each other are not supported. DT is a triangulation (all its methods work) with the extra methods convexHull, voronoiDiagram and isInterior, and the property Constraints. Assigning DT.Points or DT.Constraints retriangulates.

delaunayn.description: Delaunay triangulation of the points in the rows of P, in any dimension.

delete.description: Deletes the named file(s), or, for a handle object, runs the class's delete method (if any) and marks the object invalid so later use raises an error. For graphics handles (from plot, figure, legend, ...) the object is removed from its plot; deleting a figure closes it.

delete_block.description: Removes a block and the lines attached to it.

delete_line.description: Removes the line between two ports (or the line with handle h).

delevent.description: Removes the events with the given name (or names), or only the n-th event with that name.

delimitedTextImportOptions.description: Creates import options for delimited text by hand instead of detecting them from a file. Give 'NumVariables' or 'VariableNames' (and 'VariableTypes', which default to 'char'), then 'Delimiter', 'DataLines', 'VariableNamesLine' and the other properties listed under detectImportOptions. Use the result with readtable(filename, opts).

delsample.description: Removes the samples at the given indices, or at the given times.

demosaic.description: Turns a Bayer-pattern sensor image into an RGB image by gradient-corrected interpolation. The alignment names the colours of the top-left 2-by-2 pixels: 'gbrg', 'grbg', 'bggr' or 'rggb'.

dendrogram.description: Draw a linkage tree. At most P leaves are shown (default 30; 0 shows all). Options: 'Orientation', 'Labels', 'ColorThreshold'.

dependnames.description: Cell array holding the dependent variable name. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

designfilt.description: Designs a digital filter and returns a digitalFilter object. The response is 'lowpassfir', 'highpassfir', 'bandpassfir', 'bandstopfir', 'lowpassiir', 'highpassiir', 'bandpassiir', 'bandstopiir', 'differentiatorfir', 'hilbertfir' or 'arbmagfir'. Describe the filter with 'FilterOrder' and cutoff frequencies ('CutoffFrequency', 'HalfPowerFrequency', or 'PassbandFrequency' and 'StopbandFrequency', with a 1 or 2 suffix for band filters), or leave the order out and give the band edges with 'PassbandRipple' and 'StopbandAttenuation' (dB) for the smallest filter that meets them. 'DesignMethod' picks 'window', 'equiripple', 'ls', 'kaiserwin', 'butter', 'cheby1', 'cheby2' or 'ellip'; 'SampleRate' gives frequencies in Hz. The object has the properties Coefficients (a row of FIR taps or a matrix of second-order sections) and the design values, and works with filter, filtfilt, freqz, grpdelay, phasez, impz, stepz, zplane, filtord, tf, zpk, ss, isstable and islinphase.

det.description: Determinant of a square matrix. Example: det([1 2; 3 4]) is -2.

detcoef.description: Detail coefficients at level n (default the coarsest level) of a wavedec decomposition. Several levels come back as several outputs, or as a cell array with one output.

usage: [H, V, D] = detcoef2('all', C, S, n)
detcoef2.description: Detail coefficients at level n of a wavedec2 decomposition: o is 'h', 'v' or 'd' for one orientation, 'all' for the three, or 'compact' for one row vector.

detectImportOptions.description: Looks at a delimited text file and returns an options object that says how readtable, readmatrix or readcell will read it: Delimiter, VariableNames, VariableTypes ('double', 'char', 'string', 'datetime', 'duration', 'categorical', 'logical' and the integer and single classes), SelectedVariableNames, DataLines, VariableNamesLine, RowNamesColumn and the rules MissingRule, ImportErrorRule ('fill', 'error', 'omitrow', 'omitvar'), EmptyLineRule, ExtraColumnsRule, ConsecutiveDelimitersRule and LeadingDelimitersRule. Change a property with opts.Name = value. setvartype changes the type of some or all variables; setvaropts sets per-variable options (FillValue, TreatAsMissing, DecimalSeparator, ThousandsSeparator, TrimNonNumeric, InputFormat, DatetimeFormat, TimeZone, Categories, Ordinal, TrueSymbols, FalseSymbols, Prefixes, Suffixes); getvaropts returns them as a struct; preview reads the first eight rows. The name-value arguments are those of readtable, for example 'Delimiter', 'NumHeaderLines', 'DecimalSeparator', 'TextType' and 'VariableNamingRule'. Spreadsheet files are not supported here: pass their Sheet and Range to readtable directly.

detrend.description: Removes the best-fit straight line (default), mean ('constant') or polynomial of degree n from a vector or from each column of a matrix. Breakpoints are not supported.

deval.description: Evaluates a solution structure from an ODE, DDE or BVP solver at the times t, using the solver's own continuous extension. Each column of y is the solution at one time; idx picks components. yp is the derivative of the interpolating polynomial. Times outside the solution interval raise an error.

dfsearch.description: Depth-first search from node s. The events are the same as for bfsearch.

diag.description: For a vector v, builds a square matrix with v on the k-th diagonal (k = 0 main, k > 0 above, k < 0 below). For a matrix A, extracts the k-th diagonal as a column vector. Example: diag([1 2]) is [1 0; 0 2].

dialog.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

diary.description: Records everything printed in the command window in a text file. diary on appends to the file named 'diary' in the current folder (or the name set earlier), diary(filename) switches to that file and turns recording on, diary off stops, and diary alone toggles. Typed commands are not recorded, only output.

dicominfo.description: Reads the header of a DICOM file into a struct with one field per data element (and Width and Height). Needs the optional pydicom package.

dicomread.description: Reads the pixel data of a DICOM file. Needs the optional pydicom package.

dictionary.description: A map from keys to values that remembers the order in which entries were added. All keys have one type and all values have one type; text is stored as strings. keys and values are arrays of the same size (or one value for all the keys). Look up with d(keys), set with d(keys) = values, delete with d(keys) = [] or remove. For values of any kind use cells: d(key) = {value} and d{key}. A dictionary is a value, so d2 = d makes an independent copy. Functions: keys, values, entries, numEntries, isKey, insert, remove, lookup, types, isConfigured. Example: d = dictionary(["a" "b"], [1 2]); d("c") = 3; d("b")

diff.description: Differences between neighbouring elements, x(2)-x(1), x(3)-x(2), ..., along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. n repeats the operation n times, so the result is n elements shorter. Example: diff([1 4 9]) is [3 5].

usage: [fx, fy, fxx, fxy, fyy] = differentiate(sfit, x, y)
differentiate.description: Derivatives of a fit at the points x (analytic for polynomials and piecewise polynomials, numerical otherwise). f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.differentiate(...).

digitBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: a place where a digit meets a character that is not a digit. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

digits.description: Sets or returns the number of significant digits used by vpa and vpasolve (32 by default).

digitsPattern.description: A pattern that matches digit characters 0-9. With no argument it matches one or more of them, with N exactly N, and with (min, max) between min and max (max may be Inf). Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind. Example: extract("abc123def45", digitsPattern) gives ["123"; "45"].

usage: G = digraph(s, t, weights, nodenames | num | NodeTable)
digraph.description: Directed graph. A(i, j) nonzero is an edge from node i to node j; in the list form each edge goes from s(k) to t(k). See graph for the tables G.Edges and G.Nodes.

dir.description: Lists a folder, the files matching a wildcard pattern such as '*.csv', or a single file. With an output, returns a column struct array with fields name, folder, date, bytes, isdir and datenum. A folder listing includes '.' and '..'.

dirac.description: Dirac delta function (or its n-th derivative). For numbers: Inf at 0 and 0 elsewhere.

diric.description: Dirichlet (periodic sinc) function sin(n x/2) / (n sin(x/2)), with its limit at multiples of 2 pi.

discretize.description: Puts the values of X into bins and returns the bin number of each value (NaN outside the edges). A bin includes its left edge, and the last bin also its right edge; with 'IncludedEdge', 'right' it is the other way round. With values the result holds the value of each bin instead of its number; with 'categorical' it is an ordinal categorical array whose categories are named after the bins, e.g. '[0, 4)'. N asks for N bins of equal width. X and edges can be datetime or duration arrays.

disp.description: Print the value of x without showing a variable name. An empty char prints a blank line; other empty values print nothing. Example: disp('hello') prints hello.

display.description: Prints x the way an unterminated statement would, with an 'ans =' header.

distances.description: Shortest-path distances between all pairs of nodes, or from the nodes s to the nodes t. Unreachable pairs are Inf.

divergence.description: Divergence of the symbolic vector field V with respect to the variables X.

dlmread.description: Reads a delimited numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based offsets.

dlmwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix to a delimited text file (comma by default; '\t' or 'tab' for tabs). precision is a number of significant digits or a format such as '%.3f' (default five significant digits).

usage: [M, P, Z, E] = dlqe(A, G, C, Q, R)
dlqe.description: Discrete Kalman estimator: the innovation gain M, the prediction error covariance P, the error covariance after the measurement update Z and the estimator poles E.

usage: K = dlqr(A, B, Q, R, N)
dlqr.description: Discrete-time linear-quadratic regulator: u[k] = -K*x[k] minimizes the sum of x'*Q*x + u'*R*u + 2*x'*N*u for x[k+1] = A*x[k] + B*u[k].

dlyap.description: Solves the discrete Lyapunov equation A*X*A' - X + Q = 0, the Sylvester equation A*X*B - X + C = 0, or A*X*A' - E*X*E' + Q = 0.

dlyapchol.description: Cholesky factor R of the solution X = R'*R of A*X*A' - X + B*B' = 0 for a stable A.

usage: [p, q, r, s, cc, rr] = dmperm(A)
dmperm.description: Dulmage-Mendelsohn decomposition. With one output, p is a maximum matching: p(j) is the row matched to column j (0 if none). With more outputs A(p, q) is block upper triangular; r and s mark the block boundaries, cc and rr the coarse (under-, well- and over-determined) parts.

do_string_escapes.description: Replaces escape sequences such as \n and \t in s by the characters they stand for. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

doc.description: Same as help: prints the help text in the command window (no browser is opened).

donutchart.description: A pie chart with a hole in the middle; InnerRadius sets the size of the hole.

dos.description: Same as system, kept for code written for Windows.

dot.description: Dot product. For two vectors with the same number of elements, sum(conj(a).*b); for matrices, the dot products of matching columns as a row vector. A dim argument is not supported.

double.description: Converts to double precision. Char input gives character codes; a string or string array is parsed as numbers element by element (NaN where the text is not a number or is <missing>). Cells and structs cannot be converted. Example: double('A') is 65; double("2.5") is 2.5.

downsample.description: Keeps every n-th sample of x, starting with the first (or after skipping phase samples).

drawnow.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. Options such as limitrate are accepted. Where there is no live window (browser app, Jupyter, MCP, --no-plots) each call records a snapshot of the current figure, and the snapshots of a run are returned as an animated GIF. shg and refresh do the same.

dsearchn.description: For each row of Q, the row number of the nearest point in X and the distance to it.

dsolve.description: Solves ordinary differential equations. Declare the unknown with 'syms y(t)', write derivatives with diff(y, t), and give conditions such as y(0) == 1. For a condition on a derivative use Dy = diff(y, t); Dy(0) == 0. Constants of integration are named C1, C2, ... Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

usage: sys = dss(A, B, C, D, E)
sys = dss(A, B, C, D, E, Ts)
dss.description: State-space model given in descriptor form E dx/dt = A x + B u, y = C x + D u. E must be nonsingular; the model is stored in the ordinary form with E\A and E\B.

usage: [A, B, C, D, E, Ts] = dssdata(sys)
dssdata.description: State-space matrices in descriptor form. Models are stored with E equal to the identity, which is what is returned.

dtw.description: Dynamic time warping: the smallest total distance between x and y when samples may be repeated to stretch either signal. ix and iy are the matched sample numbers. maxsamp limits how far the two indices may drift apart; metric is 'euclidean', 'absolute' or 'squared'. Columns of matrices are samples of a multichannel signal.

dummyvar.description: Indicator (0/1) columns for a grouping variable of positive integers or a categorical array; several grouping columns give several blocks of indicator columns.

duration.description: Creates an array of lengths of time from hours, minutes and seconds (and optionally milliseconds), or from text such as '01:30:00' or '2:12:00:00' (days:hours:minutes:seconds). The Format property controls the display: 'hh:mm:ss' (default), 'dd:hh:mm:ss', 'mm:ss', 'hh:mm', fractional seconds as in 'hh:mm:ss.SSS', or a single unit 'y', 'd', 'h', 'm' or 's'. Durations can be added, subtracted, compared, scaled by numbers and divided by each other (giving a number). In arithmetic with a duration, a plain number counts as days.

duration.empty.description: An empty duration array (0-by-0 by default).

dwt.description: One level of the discrete wavelet transform: approximation coefficients cA (low-pass filtered) and detail coefficients cD (high-pass filtered), each kept at every second sample. Each has floor((n + f - 1)/2) elements for a signal of n samples and filters of f taps. The wavelet is 'haar', 'dbN' (Daubechies, N vanishing moments), 'symN' (symlets) or 'coifN' (coiflets, N = 1..5); two filter vectors may be given instead of a name. The signal is extended at its ends with the current extension mode (see dwtmode); 'mode', m overrides it for one call.

usage: [cA, cH, cV, cD] = dwt2(X, LoD, HiD)
dwt2.description: One level of the two-dimensional wavelet transform: the approximation and the horizontal, vertical and diagonal details. cH is low-pass along the rows and high-pass along the columns, so it responds to horizontal edges. The signal is extended at its ends with the current extension mode (see dwtmode); 'mode', m overrides it for one call.

dwtmode.description: Sets or shows the way signals are extended at their ends by the wavelet transforms: 'sym' (mirror, repeating the end sample; the default), 'symw' (mirror about the end sample), 'asym' and 'asymw' (the same with a sign change), 'zpd' (zeros), 'sp0' (repeat the end value), 'sp1' (continue the end slope), 'ppd' (periodic) and 'per' (periodic, giving half as many coefficients as samples).

dyaddown.description: Keeps every second element: the even-numbered ones by default, the odd-numbered ones when evenodd is odd. For a matrix type is 'c' (columns), 'r' (rows) or 'm' (both).

dyadup.description: Inserts zeros between elements. By default the samples go to the even positions (a zero comes first and last); with an even evenodd they go to the odd positions.

e.description: The base of the natural logarithm, 2.71828..., the same as exp(1). A variable called e takes precedence, as for every function. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

ecdf.description: Empirical cumulative distribution function (Kaplan-Meier estimate). f starts at 0 and x repeats the smallest value first, so stairs(x, f) draws the step function. Options: 'Censoring', 'Frequency', 'Alpha', 'Function' ('cdf', 'survivor' or 'cumulative hazard') and 'Bounds'. flo and fup are Greenwood confidence bounds. Without outputs the function is plotted.

echo.description: Show the lines of scripts as they run. echo on and echo off turn it on and off for scripts, and echo alone switches it. echo fname on shows the lines of the function fname, echo on all those of every function, and echo off all turns all of it off.

edge.description: Finds edges in a grayscale image and returns them as a binary image. Methods: 'sobel' (default), 'prewitt' and 'roberts' threshold the gradient magnitude and thin the result ('nothinning' skips that; direction 'horizontal' or 'vertical' limits the search), and can also return the two gradient images; 'log' and 'zerocross' mark zero crossings after a Laplacian-of-Gaussian filter (sigma 2); 'canny' and 'approxcanny' smooth (sigma sqrt(2)), keep ridges of the gradient and link weak edges to strong ones, with thresholds [low high]. Thresholds are chosen automatically when omitted and returned as the second output. Edge maps agree closely with other implementations but individual pixels may differ.

edgeAttachments.description: Column cell array of the IDs of the triangles (tetrahedra) attached to each edge. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.edgeAttachments(...).

edgecount.description: Number of edges between the node pairs (s, t).

edges.description: The edges of the triangulation, as an m-by-2 matrix of vertex IDs with the smaller ID first, unique and sorted by rows. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.edges(...).

ei.description: Exponential integral Ei(x): the principal value integral of exp(t)/t up to x.

eig.description: Eigenvalues of a square matrix as a column vector, or eigenvector matrix V and diagonal eigenvalue matrix D with A*V = V*D. With B, solves the generalized problem A*V = B*V*D. Symmetric (Hermitian) input gets real eigenvalues in ascending order; for other matrices the order and eigenvector scaling may differ from other implementations.

eigs.description: A few eigenvalues of a large (usually sparse) square matrix: the k largest in magnitude by default (k = 6). sigma chooses which ones: 'largestabs' ('lm'), 'smallestabs' ('sm'), 'largestreal', 'smallestreal', 'bothendsreal', or a number to get the eigenvalues closest to it. With two outputs the columns of V are eigenvectors and D is a diagonal matrix. A second matrix B solves the generalized problem A*v = lambda*B*v. Function-handle operators are not supported.

usage: [b, a] = ellip(n, Rp, Rs, Wp, ftype)
ellip.description: Elliptic (Cauer) filter of order n with Rp dB of passband ripple and Rs dB of stopband attenuation; Wp is the passband edge. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'; a two-element Wn gives a bandpass filter of order 2n unless 'stop' is asked for. With three outputs the zeros, poles and gain are returned, with four a state-space model [A, B, C, D]. A trailing 's' designs an analog filter, whose frequencies are in rad/s.

ellipap.description: Analog elliptic lowpass prototype with Rp dB of passband ripple, Rs dB of stopband attenuation and passband edge 1 rad/s.

ellipj.description: Jacobi elliptic functions with argument u and parameter m (0 <= m <= 1). They satisfy sn.^2 + cn.^2 = 1 and dn.^2 + m*sn.^2 = 1.

ellipke.description: Complete elliptic integrals of the first (K) and second (E) kind for parameter m in [0, 1]. A tolerance argument is not supported.

ellipord.description: Lowest elliptic filter order that meets the passband ripple Rp and stopband attenuation Rs (dB), with the passband edge to pass to ellip.

usage: [X, Y, Z] = ellipsoid(xc, yc, zc, xr, yr, zr)
ellipsoid.description: Coordinates of an ellipsoid with center (xc, yc, zc) and semi-axes xr, yr, zr, as (n+1)-by-(n+1) matrices (n = 20 by default). Without outputs it draws the surface.

enbw.description: Equivalent noise bandwidth of a window, in frequency bins or in Hz with a sample rate.

endsWith.description: True if s ends with pattern (or any pattern in a cell array). Works element-wise on a cell array s.

entries.description: The key-value pairs of the dictionary d: a table with the variables Key and Value, or with format "struct" a struct array with those fields, or with "cell" an N-by-2 cell array.

entropy.description: Entropy of a grayscale image in bits, -sum(p .* log2(p)) over its 256-bin histogram.

entropyfilt.description: Entropy of the gray levels in the neighbourhood of each pixel (9-by-9 by default), computed on 256 levels.

enumeration.description: Lists the members of an enumeration class (a classdef with an enumeration block), or returns them as an object array together with their names.

envelope.description: Upper and lower envelopes of a signal. The default uses the magnitude of the analytic signal (the mean is removed first and added back). 'analytic' with fl uses an FIR Hilbert filter of that length, 'rms' a moving root-mean-square over wl samples, and 'peak' a spline through the local maxima (and minima) that are at least np samples apart.

eomday.description: Last day of the given month, taking leap years into account: eomday(2024, 2) is 29.

eps.description: With no input, the gap between 1 and the next larger double, about 2.2204e-16. eps(x) gives that gap at the magnitude of each element of x. eps('single') gives the single-precision gap.

eqnproblem.description: Create a problem that asks for values satisfying a set of equations; solve(prob, x0) finds them.

erase.description: Deletes every occurrence of pattern (or of each pattern in a list) from the text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output. Example: erase('a-b-c', '-') is 'abc'.

eraseBetween.description: Removes the text between a start and an end marker. Markers are text or patterns (the markers stay) or character positions (the characters at the positions are removed too). 'Boundaries' is 'inclusive' or 'exclusive' and overrides that default.

erfc.description: Complementary error function, 1 - erf(x), accurate for large x.

erfcinv.description: Inverse complementary error function; defined for y in [0, 2].

erfcx.description: Scaled complementary error function exp(x.^2) .* erfc(x), computed without overflow or loss of accuracy for large x.

erfinv.description: Inverse error function; defined for y in [-1, 1].

error.description: Throws an error that stops the program unless caught by try/catch. The message is formatted like sprintf when extra arguments or escapes are present. A first argument such as 'pkg:name' (with a colon and no spaces) followed by more text is taken as the identifier. A struct with message and identifier fields can be passed instead. error([]) does nothing.

errorbar.description: Plots y with vertical error bars, of half-length err or with separate lower and upper lengths neg and pos. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

errordlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Error' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines. The script continues; use error to stop it.

estim.description: State estimator with a given gain L: its inputs are the known inputs and the measured outputs of sys, its outputs the estimated outputs followed by the estimated states.

etime.description: Seconds elapsed from date vector t0 to date vector t1 ([year month day hour minute seconds], as returned by clock).

etree.description: Elimination tree of a symmetric sparse matrix (or of A'*A with 'col', A*A' with 'row'): p(k) is the parent of column k, 0 for a root. post is a postorder of the tree.

etreeplot.description: Draws the elimination tree of a sparse matrix.

eul2quat.description: Quaternion from Euler angles. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first. seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors.

eul2rotm.description: Rotation matrix from Euler angles (one row of three). seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors.

eul2tform.description: 4-by-4 transform with the rotation given by Euler angles and no translation. seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors.

eval.description: Runs text as code in the current workspace. If it fails and catchcode is given, that is run instead. With outputs, code must be a single expression whose values are returned. Building variable names with eval is error-prone; prefer arrays, cells or structs.

evalc.description: Runs text as code and returns everything it would have printed, as a char vector.

evalclusters.description: Choose the number of clusters. clust is 'kmeans', 'linkage', 'gmdistribution', a function handle or a matrix of solutions; criterion is 'CalinskiHarabasz', 'DaviesBouldin', 'silhouette' or 'gap'. The result has OptimalK, OptimalY, CriterionValues and InspectedK.

evalfr.description: The transfer matrix at one complex number x, a point of the s-plane or z-plane, e.g. evalfr(sys, 2i).

evalin.description: Runs code or evaluates an expression in the 'base' or 'caller' workspace, so it sees and changes the variables there. A third argument is run if the first raises an error.

evcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with location mu and scale sigma (defaults 0 and 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

event.EventData.description: Creates an empty event data object with the properties Source and EventName. Classes that carry extra data with an event derive from it: classdef MyData < event.EventData.

event.hasListener.description: True when at least one enabled listener is attached to the event of the handle object obj.

events.description: Lists the events of a class (those declared in events blocks of the class and its superclasses, plus ObjectBeingDestroyed for handle classes).

evfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [location, scale] of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05). censoring marks right-censored observations with 1 and freq gives the count of each observation.

evinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with location mu and scale sigma (defaults 0 and 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

evlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

evpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with location mu and scale sigma (defaults 0 and 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

evrnd.description: Random numbers from the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with location mu and scale sigma (defaults 0 and 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

evstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the extreme value (type 1, for minima) distribution with location mu and scale sigma (defaults 0 and 1).

exceltime.description: Spreadsheet serial day numbers (day 1 is January 1, 1900) for each datetime.

exist.description: Tells what a name refers to: 1 for a variable, 2 for a file or a function defined in a .m file or in the session, 5 for a built-in function, 7 for a folder, 0 if not found. kind ('var', 'file', 'dir' or 'builtin') limits the search.

exit.description: Ends the mylab session, optionally with a numeric exit status for the operating system.

exp.description: e raised to the power of each element. Example: exp(0) is 1.

expand.description: Multiplies out products and powers, and expands sin and cos of sums, e.g. (x + 1)^2 becomes x^2 + 2*x + 1. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

expcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the exponential distribution with mean mu (default 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

expfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of the mean of the exponential distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05). censoring marks right-censored observations with 1 and freq gives the count of each observation.

expint.description: Exponential integral E1(x), the integral of exp(-t)/t from x to Inf. Negative real x gives complex results.

expinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the exponential distribution with mean mu (default 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

explike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the exponential distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

expm.description: Matrix exponential of a square matrix (not the element-wise exp).

expm1.description: exp(x) - 1 computed accurately when x is tiny.

exportgraphics.description: Saves the figure containing obj (a figure or axes handle, e.g. gcf or gca) to an image file, with the format taken from the extension. The whole figure is saved, even for an axes. Other options are accepted and ignored.

exppdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the exponential distribution with mean mu (default 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

exprnd.description: Random numbers from the exponential distribution with mean mu (default 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

expstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the exponential distribution with mean mu (default 1).

extract.description: All the pieces of str that match the pattern (or text) pat. For one text the result is an N-by-1 string array, or cell array of char vectors when str is a char vector. For an array of texts every element must have the same number of matches.

extractAfter.description: Text after the first occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBefore.description: Text before the first occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBetween.description: Text between start and end markers (excluded unless 'Boundaries' is 'inclusive'), or between two character positions (both included). For a char vector every match is returned as a column cell array; for a cell array each element must contain exactly one match. Example: extractBetween('a[b]c[d]', '[', ']') is {'b'; 'd'}.

eye.description: Identity matrix: ones on the main diagonal, zeros elsewhere. A non-square size puts ones on the diagonal starting at the top-left. N-D sizes are not supported. Example: eye(2) is [1 0; 0 1].

ezcontour.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y), a handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default. ezcontourf fills the areas between the lines.

ezcontourf.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y), a handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default. ezcontourf fills the areas between the lines.

ezmesh.description: Like ezsurf, but draws a wireframe mesh.

ezplot.description: Plots a function given as a handle or as an expression in quotes over [-2*pi, 2*pi] or the given interval. A function of two variables, or an equation, is drawn as the curve where it is zero; two functions give the parametric curve (fx(t), fy(t)). Expressions in quotes need no dots before *, / and ^.

ezplot3.description: Plot the space curve x = fx(t), y = fy(t), z = fz(t). The older form of fplot3.

ezpolar.description: The polar curve rho = f(theta), by default for 0 <= theta <= 2*pi.

ezsurf.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) for a function handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default, and titles the plot with the expression. ezsurfc draws the same plot.

ezsurfc.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) for a function handle or an expression in quotes, over [-2*pi, 2*pi] by default, and titles the plot with the expression. ezsurfc draws the same plot.

faceNormal.description: Unit normals of the triangles of a 3-D surface triangulation, one row per triangle. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.faceNormal(...).

factor.description: Row vector of the prime factors of the scalar n in ascending order, with repeats. Example: factor(12) is [2 2 3].

usage: [lambda, psi, T, stats, F] = factoran(X, m, 'Name', value, ...)
factoran.description: Maximum-likelihood factor analysis with m common factors on standardised variables: loadings lambda, specific variances psi, rotation matrix T, fit statistics and factor scores F. Options: 'rotate' ('varimax', 'quartimax', 'none'), 'scores', 'start', 'xtype', 'nobs'.

factorial.description: n! for each element of n, e.g. factorial(5) is 120. Returned as double.

falltime.description: Time each falling edge of a two-level waveform takes to go from the upper to the lower reference level; the options are those of risetime.

false.description: Logical 0, or a logical array of zeros. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array.

fatalAssertClass.description: Checks that the class of actual is exactly className. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertClass(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertEmpty.description: Checks that actual has no elements. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertEmpty(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertEqual.description: Checks that actual equals expected in class, size and value (NaN equals NaN; cell arrays and structs are compared element by element). 'AbsTol', t and 'RelTol', t allow numeric differences up to t, or t times the expected value. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertError.description: Checks that calling the function raises an error with that identifier, for example testCase.verifyError(@() myFun(-1), 'myFun:negative'). ?MException accepts any error. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertError(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertFail.description: Fails unconditionally, for code paths that must not be reached. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertFail(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertFalse.description: Checks that actual is the logical scalar false. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertFalse(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertGreaterThan.description: Checks that every element of actual is greater than bound. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertGreaterThan(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Checks that every element of actual is at least bound. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertInstanceOf.description: Checks that isa(actual, className) is true (subclasses count). A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertInstanceOf(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertLength.description: Checks that length(actual) equals expectedLength. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertLength(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertLessThan.description: Checks that every element of actual is less than bound. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertLessThan(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertLessThanOrEqual.description: Checks that every element of actual is at most bound. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertLessThanOrEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertMatches.description: Checks that the text actual matches the regular expression. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertMatches(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertNotEmpty.description: Checks that actual has at least one element. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertNotEmpty(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertNotEqual.description: Checks that the two values differ. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertNotEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertNotSameHandle.description: Checks that the two are different handle objects. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertNotSameHandle(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertNumElements.description: Checks that numel(actual) equals expectedCount. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertNumElements(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertReturnsTrue.description: Checks that the function returns the logical scalar true. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertReturnsTrue(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertSameHandle.description: Checks that both are the same handle object. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertSameHandle(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.
