fatalAssertSize.description: Checks that size(actual) equals expectedSize. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertSize(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertSubstring.description: Checks that the text actual contains substring. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertSubstring(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertThat.description: Checks actual against a constraint object from matlab.unittest.constraints, for example IsEqualTo(5, 'Within', AbsoluteTolerance(0.1)) or IsGreaterThan(3) & IsLessThan(9). A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertThat(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertTrue.description: Checks that actual is the logical scalar true. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertTrue(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertWarning.description: Checks that calling the function issues a warning with that identifier. The function's outputs are returned. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertWarning(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fatalAssertWarningFree.description: Checks that calling the function issues no warning. The function's outputs are returned. A failure stops the whole test run: use it when later tests cannot be trusted. A method of the test case, also written testCase.fatalAssertWarningFree(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

fcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the F distribution with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom nu1 and nu2: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

fclose.description: Closes a file opened with fopen, or all of them. status is 0. An id that is not open is an error.

fcn2optimexpr.description: Turn a function of optimisation variables into an optimisation expression, for functions that cannot be written with the supported operators.

fcontour.description: Draws contour lines of f(x, y) over [-5, 5] in x and y, or over the given ranges.

fdisp.description: Writes what disp(x) shows to the file with identifier fid (1 and 2 mean the command window). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

feather.description: Arrows starting at equally spaced points along the x-axis.

feature.description: Reads an internal setting. 'numcores' gives the number of processor cores, 'getpid' the process number, 'DefaultCharacterSet' is 'UTF-8'. Other names return 0.

featureEdges.description: Sharp edges of a triangle mesh: edges whose two triangles' normals differ by more than filterangle (radians), plus edges shared by one triangle or by more than two. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.featureEdges(...).

usage: T = feedback(sys1, sys2, feedin, feedout, sign)
feedback.description: Closed loop of sys1 with sys2 in the return path: T = sys1/(1 + sys1*sys2) for negative feedback (the default) and sys1/(1 - sys1*sys2) for sign = +1. feedback(L, 1) closes a unity-feedback loop. feedin and feedout select which inputs and outputs of sys1 take part in the loop; the result keeps all inputs and outputs of sys1. Continuous-time delays inside the loop are not supported: approximate them first with pade.

feof.description: True when there is nothing left to read from the file. Unlike some implementations this is already true right after the last byte has been read, without a further failed read.

ferror.description: Message of the most recent file error, such as a failed fseek, or '' when there was none (errnum is then 0). 'clear' resets it. mylab keeps one message for all files.

fetchNext.description: The outputs of a future that has not been read yet, with its index (1). An error if the future was already read.

fetchOutputs.description: The outputs of the function a future from parfeval ran. If that function failed, its error is raised here.

feval.description: Calls the function f, given as a handle or a name, with the remaining arguments. Example: feval('max', [3 8 1]) is 8.

fflush.description: Writes any buffered output of a file to disk. Accepted with any argument, including stdout, so that Octave-style code runs.

fft.description: Fast Fourier transform (discrete Fourier transform) along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim; each column of a matrix is transformed. n zero-pads or truncates to n points. The result is always complex; abs(Y) is the amplitude spectrum. Example: fft([1 0 0 0]) is [1 1 1 1].

fft2.description: Two-dimensional fast Fourier transform of a matrix, optionally padded or cropped to m-by-n.

fftfilt.description: FIR filtering of x with the coefficients b; the result equals filter(b, 1, x). The block length n is accepted for compatibility.

fftn.description: N-dimensional discrete Fourier transform: the FFT along every dimension of X. siz pads or cuts X to that size first.

fftshift.description: Swaps the halves of a spectrum so the zero-frequency term sits in the middle, which suits plotting fft output against centred frequencies.

fgetl.description: Reads the next line of a file as text, without its line ending. Returns the number -1 at the end of the file, so test the result with ischar.

fgets.description: Reads the next line of a file as text, keeping its line ending; nchar limits how many characters are returned. Returns -1 at the end of the file.

usage: [x, fval, attainfactor] = fgoalattain(fun, x0, goal, weight, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
fgoalattain.description: Bring several objectives as close as possible to goal values, with weights that say how much each may miss its goal.

fieldnames.description: Field names of a struct as a column cell array of char vectors, in creation order. For an object, its public properties (the same list as properties(obj)).

fields.description: The same as fieldnames: the field names of a structure, as a column cell array. An old name MATLAB still accepts, used by some existing code.

figure.description: Opens a new figure, or makes figure n (or figure handle f) current, creating it if needed. Later plots go to the current figure. f is a Figure handle with properties such as Number, Name, Color and Position, which may also be given as Name/Value options; other common window options (e.g. 'NumberTitle', 'Visible', 'Units') are accepted.

figurepalette.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

fileparts.description: Splits a file path into its folder, base name and extension (with the dot). Example: fileparts('a/b.txt') gives 'a', 'b' and '.txt'.

fileread.description: Entire contents of a text file (read as UTF-8) as one char vector.

filesep.description: Separator between folders in a path: '/' on Linux and macOS, '\' on Windows.

fill.description: Draws a filled polygon with corners (x(k), y(k)); c is a colour name or RGB triplet, and matrix x, y draw one polygon per column. fill replaces the plot unless hold is on; patch always adds to the current axes. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

fill3.description: Draws filled polygons in 3-D with corners (x(k), y(k), z(k)); matrix inputs draw one polygon per column. c is a colour name, an RGB triplet, or numbers mapped through the colormap. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth.

fillmissing.description: Replaces missing entries. Methods: 'constant' (the value v), 'previous', 'next', 'nearest' and, for numeric data, 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip' and 'makima'. Matrices are filled column by column (or along dim); tables variable by variable. Leading or trailing gaps are extrapolated by the interpolating methods unless 'EndValues' is 'none', 'nearest' or a constant. TF marks the entries that were filled. Example: fillmissing([1 NaN 3], 'linear') is [1 2 3].

filloutliers.description: Replaces outliers. fillmethod is a number, 'center', 'clip', 'previous', 'next', 'nearest', 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip' or 'makima'. The detection options are those of isoutlier.

filt.description: Discrete-time transfer function written the way digital filters are: num and den hold coefficients in ascending powers of z^-1, so filt([1 2], [1 0.5]) is (1 + 2 z^-1)/(1 + 0.5 z^-1). The sample time is unspecified (-1) unless Ts is given. The result is a tf model whose Variable is 'z^-1'.

filter.description: Applies the rational digital filter with numerator b and denominator a to the data x, along a row vector or down the columns of a matrix. Initial conditions are not supported. Example: filter(1, [1 -0.5], [1 1 1]) is [1 1.5 1.75].

filter2.description: Two-dimensional correlation of the matrix X with the kernel h (convolution with h turned by 180 degrees); both may be complex, and the result is single when either is single. shape is 'same' (default), 'full' or 'valid'.

filtfilt.description: Zero-phase digital filtering: runs the filter forward and then backward, so the output has no phase delay and the filter's effect is squared. Works along a row vector or down columns. The data must be longer than three times the filter order.

filtic.description: Initial conditions for filter(b, a, ..., z) that continue a signal whose past outputs were y = [y(-1), y(-2), ...] and past inputs x = [x(-1), x(-2), ...].

filtord.description: Order of a digital filter: the highest delay with a nonzero coefficient.

fimplicit.description: Draws the curve where f(x, y) equals zero, over [-5, 5] in both directions by default. Example: fimplicit(@(x, y) x.^2 + y.^2 - 4)

find.description: Linear indices of the nonzero elements of x, in column-major order. n limits the result to the first (or 'last') n hits. With two or three outputs, returns row and column subscripts and the values. The result is a row for row-vector input, otherwise a column. Example: find([0 5 0 7]) is [2 4].

find_system.description: Lists the model and the paths of its blocks as a cell array, including blocks inside subsystems. Name, value pairs keep only blocks whose parameter has that value (BlockType, Name, Parent or any block parameter); 'SearchDepth', n limits how deep subsystems are searched.

findall.description: Returns the graphics objects whose properties have the given values, searching all figures or only parent and the objects inside it. Several name/value pairs must all match; '-or' and '-not' combine conditions, '-regexp' matches text with a regular expression, '-property' tests that a property exists, and '-depth' limits how deep the search goes ('flat' is depth 0). The result is empty when nothing matches. findall does the same. Example: set(findobj(gca, 'Type', 'line'), 'LineWidth', 2)

findchangepts.description: Indices at which a signal changes most abruptly: x(ipt) is the first sample of a new segment. 'Statistic' is 'mean' (default), 'rms', 'std' or 'linear'; 'MaxNumChanges' allows more than one change, 'MinThreshold' keeps every change that lowers the residual by more than the threshold, and 'MinDistance' sets the shortest segment.

finddelay.description: Delay of y relative to x in samples, taken from the peak of their cross-correlation: positive when y is a delayed copy of x.

findedge.description: Edge index of the edge between s and t (0 if there is none), or the end nodes of the edges with the given indices. With two outputs and node pairs it lists every matching edge of a multigraph and the pair each one belongs to.

findgroups.description: Numbers the groups formed by the unique values (or unique combinations of values) of the grouping vectors, in sorted order of those values. G gives the group number of each element (NaN when a value is missing); ID holds each group's value. Works for numeric, logical, cell arrays of text and string vectors, and for all variables of a table. Example: findgroups([5 3 5]) is [2 1 2].

findnode.description: Numeric index of each node given by name or number; 0 for a node that is not in the graph.

findobj.description: Returns the graphics objects whose properties have the given values, searching all figures or only parent and the objects inside it. Several name/value pairs must all match; '-or' and '-not' combine conditions, '-regexp' matches text with a regular expression, '-property' tests that a property exists, and '-depth' limits how deep the search goes ('flat' is depth 0). The result is empty when nothing matches. findall does the same. Example: set(findobj(gca, 'Type', 'line'), 'LineWidth', 2)

findpeaks.description: Local maxima of a vector: samples larger than both neighbours (a flat top counts once, at its first sample; the end points never count). locs are indices, or the matching values of x. w are the widths and p the prominences (how far a peak stands above the higher of the two valleys that separate it from taller peaks). Options: 'MinPeakHeight', 'MinPeakProminence', 'Threshold' (height above both neighbours), 'MinPeakDistance' (peaks closer than or exactly this far from a taller peak are dropped), 'MinPeakWidth', 'MaxPeakWidth', 'WidthReference' ('halfprom' or 'halfheight'), 'SortStr' ('ascend' or 'descend') and 'NPeaks'. Without outputs the peaks are plotted.

findprop.description: Describes a property of an object of a classdef class: a struct with Name, GetAccess, SetAccess, Dependent, Constant and more. Returns [] when there is no such property.

findstr.description: Starting positions where the shorter of the two texts occurs in the longer one. An old function; strfind is preferred.

finv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the F distribution with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom nu1 and nu2: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

finverse.description: Inverse function of the symbolic expression f(x).

fir1.description: Window-method FIR filter of order n (n+1 coefficients, linear phase). Wn is the cutoff as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency; two values give a bandpass filter and more give several bands. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass', 'stop', 'DC-0' (first band stops) or 'DC-1' (first band passes). The window is a vector of n+1 values (default Hamming). The response is scaled to one in the middle of the first passband unless 'noscale' is given. A filter that passes the Nyquist frequency needs an even order, so an odd n is raised by one.

usage: b = fir2(n, f, m, npt, lap, window)
fir2.description: FIR filter of order n whose magnitude response follows the points (f, m): f runs from 0 to 1 (the Nyquist frequency) and repeated values mark jumps. The wanted response is sampled on npt points (default 512), jumps are smoothed over lap points, and the impulse response is windowed (default Hamming).

firls.description: Linear-phase FIR filter of order n that minimises the weighted squared error. f lists band edges in pairs (fractions of Nyquist), a the wanted amplitude at each edge, and w one weight per band. 'hilbert' and 'differentiator' give odd-symmetric filters; for a differentiator the error is weighted by 1/f^2.

firpm.description: Parks-McClellan equiripple FIR filter of order n: the largest weighted error is as small as possible. f lists band edges in pairs, a the wanted amplitude at each edge and w one weight per band. err is the weighted ripple. A cell {density} as last input changes the density of the frequency grid (default 16).

fishertest.description: Fisher's exact test of no association in a 2-by-2 table of counts. stats has the odds ratio and its confidence interval. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

usage: fitobject = fit(x, y, fitType, Name, Value)
fit.description: Fit a curve (x a column vector) or a surface (x a two-column matrix) to the column vector y. fitType is a library model name ('poly1'-'poly9', 'exp1', 'exp2', 'power1', 'power2', 'gauss1'-'gauss8', 'sin1'-'sin8', 'fourier1'-'fourier8', 'rat01'-'rat55', 'weibull', 'linearinterp', 'nearestinterp', 'cubicinterp', 'pchipinterp', 'smoothingspline'; for surfaces 'poly11'-'poly55', 'lowess', 'loess', 'linearinterp', 'nearestinterp', 'cubicinterp', 'biharmonicinterp' and 'thinplateinterp'), an equation such as 'a*exp(-b*x)+c', a cell array of linear terms or a fittype. Options (as a fitoptions object or Name,Value pairs): Normalize, Exclude, Weights, StartPoint, Lower, Upper, Robust ('off', 'LAR', 'Bisquare'), Algorithm ('Trust-Region', 'Levenberg-Marquardt'), MaxIter, MaxFunEvals, TolFun, TolX, Display, SmoothingParam, Span (lowess and loess: the fraction of the points in each local fit, default 0.25) and 'problem' for the values of problem parameters. lowess and loess fit, around each point, a weighted linear or quadratic surface to the nearest Span share of the data with tricube distance weights (Robust 'Bisquare' or 'LAR' refits with weights that play down outliers). Surface interpolants pass through the data: linear, nearest and cubic over a Delaunay triangulation (NaN outside the data's convex hull), thin-plate and biharmonic splines everywhere; repeated (x, y) points are averaged. Linear models are solved by least squares; nonlinear ones start from data-driven starting points (a random one, with a warning, for custom equations without StartPoint). gof has sse, rsquare, dfe, adjrsquare and rmse; output has numobs, numparam, residuals, Jacobian, exitflag, algorithm and, for nonlinear fits, iterations, funcCount and firstorderopt. Data with NaN or Inf is an error: remove it with prepareCurveData or exclude it.

fitcdiscr.description: Discriminant analysis classifier: 'linear' (default), 'quadratic', 'diaglinear', 'diagquadratic', 'pseudolinear' or 'pseudoquadratic'; 'Gamma' regularises the covariance. Properties: Mu, Sigma, Coeffs, Prior. Scores are posterior probabilities. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcecoc.description: Multiclass model built from binary learners (error-correcting output codes). 'Coding' is 'onevsone' (default), 'onevsall', 'ordinal', 'binarycomplete', 'ternarycomplete' or a matrix; 'Learners' is 'svm' (default), 'linear', 'knn', 'tree', 'discriminant', 'naivebayes' or a template. predict returns the labels, the negated average binary losses and the binary learner scores. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcensemble.description: Ensemble of classification trees: 'Bag' (random forest), 'AdaBoostM1', 'AdaBoostM2', 'LogitBoost' or 'GentleBoost' (default LogitBoost for two classes, AdaBoostM2 otherwise; 100 cycles). Options: 'Learners' (templateTree), 'LearnRate'. Extra methods: oobLoss and oobPredict (bagging), predictorImportance. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcknn.description: k-nearest-neighbour classifier (k = 1 by default). Options: 'Distance', 'DistanceWeight', 'Standardize', 'BreakTies', 'IncludeTies', 'Exponent', 'Cov', 'Scale'. Scores are the class fractions among the neighbours. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitclinear.description: Two-class linear classifier: 'Learner' 'svm' (default) or 'logistic', 'Regularization' 'ridge' or 'lasso', 'Lambda' (default 1/n). Properties: Beta, Bias, Lambda. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcnb.description: Naive Bayes classifier. Each predictor is modelled within each class by a 'normal' (default), 'kernel', 'mvmn' (categorical) or 'mn' (multinomial counts) distribution; DistributionParameters holds the fitted values. A normal predictor that is constant within a class is an error. Scores are posterior probabilities. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcnet.description: Small fully connected neural network classifier (softmax output). Options: 'LayerSizes' (10), 'Activations' ('relu', 'tanh', 'sigmoid', 'none'), 'Lambda', 'IterationLimit', 'Standardize'. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitcsvm.description: Two-class support vector machine. Options: 'KernelFunction' ('linear', 'gaussian'/'rbf', 'polynomial'), 'BoxConstraint' (1), 'KernelScale' (1 or 'auto'), 'Standardize', 'PolynomialOrder'. Properties: Alpha, Bias, Beta (linear kernel), SupportVectors, IsSupportVector. The second column of the score is the signed distance from the boundary. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitctree.description: Classification tree (CART). Options: 'MinParentSize' (10), 'MinLeafSize' (1), 'MaxNumSplits', 'SplitCriterion' ('gdi', 'deviance', 'twoing'), 'MergeLeaves', 'NumVariablesToSample'. Extra methods: view, prune and predictorImportance; properties such as NumNodes, Children, CutPredictor, CutPoint, NodeClass and ClassProbability describe the tree. Text and categorical predictors of a table are used through their category numbers. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName) / (tbl, 'y ~ x1 + x2'). Labels may be numeric, logical, text or categorical and are returned by predict in the same type. Shared options: 'ClassNames', 'Prior', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames', 'ResponseName', 'ScoreTransform' and, to get a cross-validated model, 'CrossVal', 'KFold', 'Holdout', 'Leaveout' or 'CVPartition'. Methods: predict (labels, scores), resubPredict, loss, resubLoss, margin, edge and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitdist.description: Fit a distribution to the data vector x by maximum likelihood and return a probability distribution object (for 'Normal' the standard deviation is the unbiased sample one). paramci(pd) gives confidence intervals and negloglik(pd) the negative log-likelihood. Options: 'Censoring', 'Frequency', 'NTrials' (binomial), 'Theta' (generalized Pareto), 'By' (one fit per group, returned in a cell array). name 'Kernel' gives a kernel density estimate with the options 'Kernel', 'Width' and 'Support'.

usage: mdl = fitensemble(X, Y, method, nlearn, learners, ...)
fitensemble.description: The older form of fitcensemble and fitrensemble.

fitgeotform2d.description: Fits a transformation that takes the moving points onto the fixed points: 'similarity', 'reflectivesimilarity', 'affine' or 'projective'. Returns a simtform2d, affinetform2d or projtform2d object.

fitgeotrans.description: Fits a transformation that takes the moving points onto the fixed points (n-by-2 matrices of [x y]) in the least-squares sense: 'nonreflectivesimilarity' (2 pairs or more), 'similarity' (3), 'affine' (3) or 'projective' (4). Returns an affine2d or projective2d object.

usage: mdl = fitglm(X, y, modelspec, 'Distribution', distr, 'Name', value, ...)
fitglm.description: Fit a generalized linear model: 'Distribution' is 'normal', 'binomial', 'poisson', 'gamma' or 'inverse gaussian', with its canonical 'Link' unless another is given ('identity', 'log', 'logit', 'probit', 'comploglog', 'loglog', 'reciprocal' or a power). Other options: 'Offset', 'Weights', 'BinomialSize', 'DispersionFlag', 'Intercept', 'CategoricalVars'. The model has Coefficients, Deviance, Dispersion, Fitted, Residuals, LogLikelihood and the methods predict, feval, random, coefCI, coefTest and devianceTest.

fitgmdist.description: Fit a Gaussian mixture with k components by expectation-maximisation. Options: 'CovarianceType', 'SharedCovariance', 'RegularizationValue', 'Replicates', 'Start', 'Options'. The model has mu, Sigma, ComponentProportion, NumComponents, AIC, BIC, NegativeLogLikelihood, Converged and the methods cluster, posterior, pdf, cdf, random and mahal.

fitlm.description: Fit a linear regression model. modelspec is 'constant', 'linear' (default), 'interactions', 'purequadratic', 'quadratic', 'polyIJK', a terms matrix or a formula such as 'y ~ x1 + x2*x3' (a*b means a + b + a:b, x^2 includes x, -1 removes the intercept). Text and categorical table variables become indicator variables. The model has Coefficients (a table with Estimate, SE, tStat, pValue), Rsquared, RMSE, MSE, Residuals, Fitted and more, and the methods predict, feval, random, anova, coefCI, coefTest, plot, plotResiduals, addTerms and removeTerms. Options: 'CategoricalVars', 'Exclude', 'Intercept', 'PredictorVars', 'ResponseVar', 'RobustOpts', 'VarNames', 'Weights'.

fitnlm.description: Fit a nonlinear regression model. The model is a function handle modelfun(b, X) or a formula whose unknown names are the coefficients. The result has Coefficients, RMSE, Rsquared, Fitted, Residuals and the methods predict (with intervals), feval, coefCI and coefTest.

fitoptions.description: Fit options object for fit. Methods: 'NonlinearLeastSquares' (StartPoint, Lower, Upper, Algorithm, DiffMinChange, DiffMaxChange, Display, MaxFunEvals, MaxIter, TolFun, TolX, Robust), 'LinearLeastSquares' (Robust, Lower, Upper), 'SmoothingSpline' (SmoothingParam), the interpolant methods and 'None'; all have Normalize, Exclude, Weights and Method. Options of a library model include its default bounds (for example c >= 0 for Gaussian widths). Properties can also be set with opts.Name = value.

fitrensemble.description: Ensemble of regression trees: 'LSBoost' (default) or 'Bag'. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitrgp.description: Gaussian process regression. The kernel ('squaredexponential' by default, 'exponential', 'matern32', 'matern52', 'rationalquadratic' and their 'ard' forms), the noise 'Sigma' and the 'BasisFunction' coefficients are fitted by maximising the marginal likelihood. [ypred, ysd, yint] = predict(mdl, Xnew) gives predictions with standard deviations and intervals. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitrlinear.description: Linear regression for wide data: 'Learner' 'svm' (default) or 'leastsquares', 'Regularization' 'ridge' or 'lasso', 'Lambda' (default 1/n), 'Epsilon'. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitrnet.description: Small fully connected neural network for regression. Options as for fitcnet. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitrsvm.description: Support vector regression with an epsilon-insensitive loss. Options: 'KernelFunction', 'BoxConstraint', 'Epsilon' (default iqr(Y)/13.49), 'KernelScale', 'Standardize'. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fitrtree.description: Regression tree (CART, splits chosen to reduce the mean squared error). Options: 'MinParentSize', 'MinLeafSize', 'MaxNumSplits', 'MergeLeaves'. Extra methods: view, prune and predictorImportance. The data are (X, Y) or (tbl, ResponseVarName). Methods: predict, resubPredict, loss, resubLoss and crossval (then kfoldLoss and kfoldPredict).

fittype.description: Model for fit. A string that is not a library model is a custom equation; its coefficients are the variables other than the independent variable (alphabetically), and the operators are made element-wise. Options: 'independent' (default 'x'; {'x','y'} for surfaces), 'dependent', 'coefficients', 'problem' (fixed parameters given to fit with 'problem') and 'options'. For an anonymous function the last input is the independent variable. A cell array such as {'x','sin(x)','1'} is a linear model with coefficients a, b, c. ft(a, b, x) and feval(ft, a, b, x) evaluate it; formula, coeffnames, argnames, numcoeffs, type, category and islinear describe it.

fix.description: Rounds each element toward zero, dropping the fractional part. Example: fix(-2.7) is -2.

flattopwin.description: Flat-top window: a five-term cosine sum with a very flat main lobe, used to measure amplitudes. It takes small negative values. The result is a column vector. A second input 'periodic' gives the window used for spectral analysis (one period of n+1 samples).

flintmax.description: 2^53, the largest value up to which every integer is exactly representable as a double. A class argument is not supported.

flip.description: Reverses the order of elements along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: flip([1 2 3]) is [3 2 1].

flipdim.description: Old name of flip(A, dim): reverses the order of elements along dimension dim.

flipedge.description: Reverses the direction of all edges of a digraph, or of the chosen ones.

fliplr.description: Reverses the order of the columns (left-right mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

flipud.description: Reverses the order of the rows (up-down mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

floor.description: Rounds each element down, toward -Inf. Example: floor(-2.5) is -3.

fmesh.description: Like fsurf, but draws a wireframe mesh of z = f(x, y).

fminbnd.description: Minimizes a function of one variable on the interval [a, b] (golden section search with parabolic steps). output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon)
fmincon.description: Constrained nonlinear optimization: minimizes fun(x) from the start x0 subject to linear constraints, bounds and nonlinear constraints, where nonlcon returns [c, ceq] with c <= 0 and ceq = 0 required. Uses sequential quadratic programming with numerical gradients and finds a local minimum. Only the MaxIterations (or MaxIter) option is read. exitflag is 1 on success, -2 if the result is infeasible.

usage: [x, fval, maxfval, exitflag] = fminimax(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
fminimax.description: Minimise the largest value of a vector-valued function, subject to constraints.

fminsearch.description: Minimizes a function of several variables without derivatives (Nelder-Mead simplex), starting at x0. Options TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals are read. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output, grad, hessian] = fminunc(...)
fminunc.description: Minimizes a smooth function of several variables without constraints (quasi-Newton BFGS). grad is the gradient and hessian an approximation of the Hessian at the solution.

fontname.description: Set the font of all text in a figure, axes or other object.

fontsize.description: Set or scale the font size of all text in a figure, axes or other object.

fopen.description: Opens a file and returns a file id (3 or higher) for the reading and writing functions, or -1 on failure with the reason in msg. permission is 'r' (read, the default), 'w' (create or empty, then write), 'a' (append), or 'r+', 'w+', 'a+' for reading and writing; a 'b' or 't' suffix is accepted and makes no difference, since line endings are never translated. machinefmt sets the default byte order for fread and fwrite: The byte order is 'l' or 'ieee-le' (little-endian), 'b' or 'ieee-be' (big-endian) or 'n' (native). encoding (default 'UTF-8') is used when text is read or written. A file opened for reading is also looked for on the search path. File ids 1 and 2 always mean the command window. Given a file id, fopen returns the file's name and settings; fopen('all') lists the open ids.

format.description: Chooses how many digits numbers display with: long shows about 15 significant digits, short (the default) about 5. 'compact' and 'loose' are accepted but change nothing.

formula.description: The expression that defines a symbolic function, as a plain sym.

fourier.description: Fourier transform of f(x): the integral of f(x)*exp(-i*w*x) over all x. A transform that cannot be found is returned unevaluated. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

fpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the F distribution with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom nu1 and nu2, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

fplot.description: Plots the function handle f over the interval [a b] (default [-5 5]) by sampling it at many points; f is called with a vector and, if that fails, one point at a time. With two handles draws the parametric curve (fx(t), fy(t)).

fplot3.description: The space curve x = fx(t), y = fy(t), z = fz(t).

fprintf.description: Formats data like sprintf and writes it out. Without a file id, or with fid 1 or 2, the text goes to the command window; otherwise to a file opened with fopen. No newline is added automatically. The optional output is the number of bytes written.

fputs.description: Writes text, exactly as given, to the file with identifier fid (1 and 2 mean the command window). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

frame2im.description: Returns the image stored in a movie frame (its cdata), and the frame's colormap as a second output.

frd.description: Frequency-response data model: complex response samples at the frequencies freq (rad per time unit unless FrequencyUnit says otherwise). response is a vector for one input and one output, or an ny-by-nu-by-nf array. frd(othersys, freq) samples another model. frd models can be added, multiplied, inverted and put in feedback loops point by point (the frequencies must agree), and bode, nyquist, nichols, sigma, margin and getPeakGain work on the samples. Properties: Frequency, ResponseData, FrequencyUnit, Ts.

frdata.description: Response samples and frequencies of an frd model. response is ny-by-nu-by-nf; with 'v' and a SISO model it is a column vector.

usage: A = fread(fid, size, precision, skip, machinefmt)
fread.description: Reads binary data. size is n, Inf or [m n] (n may be Inf). precision names the type in the file: 'uint8' (the default), 'int8', 'uint16', 'int16', 'uint32', 'int32', 'uint64', 'int64', 'single', 'double', 'char' and C-style names such as 'short', 'long' and 'float', or a bit field 'ubitN' or 'bitN' (N from 1 to 64; signed for bitN). The result is double unless the precision says otherwise: '*uint8' keeps the file's type and 'uint8=>char' converts. 'N*type' with skip reads N values, then passes over skip bytes (bits for a bit field). Bit fields are packed from the least significant bit of each byte ('ieee-le'), or from the most significant with the 'ieee-be' byte order. count is the number of values read.

freeBoundary.description: Facets referenced by only one triangle (edges, chained into loops, in 2-D) or tetrahedron (triangles with outward normals). With two outputs F indexes the boundary points P instead of TR.Points. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.freeBoundary(...).

freqresp.description: Complex frequency response as an ny-by-nu-by-nf array: sys evaluated at s = j*w (or z = exp(j*w*Ts)), delays included. units is 'rad/TimeUnit' (default), 'Hz', 'kHz', 'rpm' and so on.

freqs.description: Frequency response of the analog filter b(s)/a(s) at the angular frequencies w (rad/s), or at n (default 200) logarithmically spaced frequencies chosen from the poles and zeros.

freqz.description: Frequency response of a digital filter at n points (default 512) from 0 to pi, or round the whole circle with 'whole'. A vector in place of n gives the frequencies to use (rad/sample, or Hz with fs). The filter is given as b and a, as a matrix of second-order sections with six columns, or as a digitalFilter object from designfilt. Without outputs the magnitude in dB and the phase are plotted.

frewind.description: Moves the position of a file back to its start.

friedman.description: Friedman's test: a non-parametric two-way analysis of variance that tests for column effects after adjusting for row effects.

frnd.description: Random numbers from the F distribution with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom nu1 and nu2. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

fscanf.description: Reads formatted data from the rest of an open file, like sscanf: conversions such as %d, %f, %g and %s are applied repeatedly. size may be n, Inf or [m n] (with n possibly Inf) and fills the result column by column.

fseek.description: Moves the read/write position of a file by offset bytes from origin: 'bof' or -1 (start of file, the default), 'cof' or 0 (current position), 'eof' or 1 (end of file). Returns 0, or -1 (leaving the position unchanged) when the target lies outside the file.

usage: [x, fval] = fseminf(fun, x0, ntheta, seminfcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, options)
fseminf.description: Minimise a function subject to constraints that must hold for every value of a parameter over an interval.

fsolve.description: Solves the system of equations f(x) = 0, starting from x0. f returns a vector of residuals. Options are ignored.

fspecial.description: Ready-made filter kernels for imfilter. 'average' is a box of equal weights (3-by-3 by default); 'gaussian' a bell of size hsize (3) and standard deviation sigma (0.5); 'disk' a circular average of the given radius (5) with partly covered pixels weighted by area; 'laplacian' the 3-by-3 Laplacian with shape alpha (0.2); 'log' a Laplacian of Gaussian (5, 0.5); 'motion' a line of length len (9) at theta degrees (0) that imitates camera motion; 'sobel' and 'prewitt' emphasise horizontal edges (transpose for vertical); 'unsharp' sharpens. The 'motion' weights are an approximation and can differ in the last digits from other implementations.

fstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the F distribution with numerator and denominator degrees of freedom nu1 and nu2.

usage: fsurf(fx, fy, fz, [umin umax vmin vmax])
fsurf.description: Draws the surface z = f(x, y) over [-5, 5] in x and y, or over the given ranges; three functions give a parametric surface. 'MeshDensity', n sets the number of grid points per direction.

ftell.description: Current position in a file, in bytes from its start.

full.description: Converts a sparse matrix to an ordinary full matrix. A full input is returned unchanged.

fullfile.description: Joins folder and file names with the operating system's separator. Example: fullfile('data', 'run1.csv') is 'data/run1.csv' on Linux.

func2str.description: Text form of a function handle: the function name, or the full expression starting with @ for an anonymous function.

functions.description: Describes a function handle as a struct: function (the name, or the text of an anonymous function), type ('simple', 'anonymous', 'scopedfunction' for a local function, 'nested') and file. For an anonymous function, workspace{1} is a struct of the variables it captured when it was created.

functiontests.description: Builds a test suite from the local functions of a test file. Functions whose names start or end with 'test' are tests and take one input, the test case. Functions named setupOnce and teardownOnce run once for the file, setup and teardown around every test; they share data through testCase.TestData. Write the file as: function tests = myTest; tests = functiontests(localfunctions); end

funm.description: Evaluates a function of a square matrix by the Schur-Parlett method. fun is @exp, @log, @sin, @cos, @sinh, @cosh, or a handle fun(x, k) that returns the k-th derivative of the function at x. options is a struct with TolBlk, TolTay, MaxTerms and Display. exitflag is 0 on success and 1 when a Taylor series did not converge.

fwrite.description: Writes the elements of A, column by column, as binary data of the given precision ('uint8' by default; the names are those of fread, including the bit fields 'ubitN' and 'bitN'). Values out of range are set to the nearest limit. skip leaves that many bytes (bits for a bit field) before each value. Bit fields written one after another share bytes; the last byte is filled with zero bits when something else is written or the file is closed.

fzero.description: Finds a zero of a function of one variable, starting from x0 (a sign change is searched for around it) or inside the interval [a b] whose ends have opposite signs. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output] = ga(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, intcon, options)
ga.description: Minimise a function with a genetic algorithm. Useful when the function has many local minima or no usable derivative. Results vary from run to run unless you set the random seed first.

gallery.description: Test matrices. Families: binomial, cauchy, chebspec, chebvand, chow, circul, clement, condex, cycol, dorr, dramadah, fiedler, forsythe, frank, gcdmat, gearmat, grcar, hanowa, house, integerdata, invhess, invol, ipjfact, jordbloc, kahan, kms, krylov, lauchli, lehmer, lesp, lotkin, minij, moler, neumann, normaldata, orthog, parter, pei, poisson, prolate, qmult, randcolu, randcorr, randhess, randjorth, rando, randsvd, redheff, riemann, ris, smoke, toeppd, toeppen, tridiag, triw, uniformdata, wathen, wilk. 'poisson', 'tridiag', 'toeppen', 'neumann', 'dorr' and 'wathen' return sparse matrices. The random families use the current random stream; integerdata, normaldata and uniformdata are repeatable for a given seed, but their values differ from other systems.

gamcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the gamma distribution with shape a and scale b (b defaults to 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

gamfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [shape, scale] of the gamma distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05). censoring marks right-censored observations with 1 and freq gives the count of each observation.

gaminv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the gamma distribution with shape a and scale b (b defaults to 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

gamlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the gamma distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

gamma.description: Gamma function of each element; gamma(n) equals factorial(n-1) for positive integers.

gammainc.description: Regularized incomplete gamma function: the lower tail P(a, x) by default, or the upper tail 1 - P with 'upper'. Note that x comes first. a must be non-negative.

gammaincinv.description: Inverse of the incomplete gamma function: the x with gammainc(x, a) = y. 'upper' inverts the upper tail.

gammaln.description: Natural log of the gamma function, useful when gamma itself would overflow.

gampdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the gamma distribution with shape a and scale b (b defaults to 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

gamrnd.description: Random numbers from the gamma distribution with shape a and scale b (b defaults to 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

gamstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the gamma distribution with shape a and scale b (b defaults to 1).

usage: [x, fval] = gamultiobj(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, options)
gamultiobj.description: Find a set of trade-off (Pareto) points for several objectives at once with a genetic algorithm. Each row of x is one solution and the matching row of fval holds its objective values.

usage: [yi, yq, ye] = gauspuls(t, fc, bw, bwr)
tc = gauspuls('cutoff', fc, bw, bwr, tpe)
gauspuls.description: Gaussian-modulated sinusoid with centre frequency fc (default 1000 Hz) and fractional bandwidth bw (default 0.5) measured bwr dB (default -6) down. yq is the quadrature pulse and ye the envelope. The 'cutoff' form returns the time at which the envelope has fallen by tpe dB (default -60).

gausswin.description: Gaussian window of length n. alpha (default 2.5) is the reciprocal of the standard deviation measured in half window lengths, so a larger alpha gives a narrower window. The result is a column vector.

gca.description: Handle to the current axes, creating a figure and axes if needed. Its properties (XLim, YLim, Title, XLabel, FontSize, XScale, Box, XGrid, XTick, XTickLabel, ...) can be read and set with dot syntax or get/set, and most plotting functions accept it as their first input.

gcb.description: Path of the block most recently added with add_block.

gcbf.description: The window that holds the component whose callback is running; empty outside callbacks.

gcbo.description: The component whose callback is running, and its window; empty outside callbacks.

gcd.description: Greatest common divisor of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

gcf.description: Handle to the current figure, creating one if none exists. f.Number is its figure number; the handle works with get, set, saveas, print and close.

gcp.description: The current parallel pool: a struct with NumWorkers 1, or [] with 'nocreate' because no pool is ever running.

gcs.description: Name of the current model: the one most recently created, loaded or changed.

genpath.description: The folder and all folders below it, joined with the path separator, for use with addpath. Folders named private or resources, and those whose names start with '@', '+' or '.', are left out. Returns '' if the folder does not exist.

gensig.description: Test signal for lsim: 'sine', 'square' or 'pulse' with period tau, lasting Tf (default 5 periods) and sampled every Ts (default tau/64).

geoaxes.description: Axes for latitude and longitude data (a Mercator grid; no map imagery is drawn).

geobasemap.description: geobasemap(name) chooses the basemap of geographic axes (it sets the background; no imagery).

usage: geobubble(lat, lon, sizedata, colordata) or geobubble(tbl, latvar, lonvar)

geocdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the geometric distribution with success probability p (the value counts the failures before the first success): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

geoinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the geometric distribution with success probability p (the value counts the failures before the first success): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

geolimits.description: geolimits(latlim, lonlim) sets, and [latlim, lonlim] = geolimits returns, the limits of a map.

geomean.description: Geometric mean: the n-th root of the product of n values. Negative values give NaN. nanflag 'omitnan' leaves NaN values out ('includenan', the default, keeps them).

geopdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the geometric distribution with success probability p (the value counts the failures before the first success), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

geoplot.description: A line through points given by latitude and longitude.

geornd.description: Random numbers from the geometric distribution with success probability p (the value counts the failures before the first success). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

geoscatter.description: Markers at points given by latitude and longitude.

geostat.description: Mean m and variance v of the geometric distribution with success probability p (the value counts the failures before the first success).

get.description: Reads a property of a graphics handle h (from gcf, gca, plot, title, ...). Property names ignore case. When h holds several handles (e.g. all lines returned by one plot call) the result is a cell array with one row per handle. get(h) returns a struct of the common properties. A figure number or 0 (the graphics root) also works as h. Dot syntax, e.g. h.LineWidth, reads the same properties.

getGainCrossover.description: All frequencies where the gain of a SISO model equals gain (1 for the 0 dB crossover).

getPeakGain.description: Largest gain over frequency (the H-infinity norm; the largest singular value for a model with several inputs or outputs) and the frequency where it occurs. fband = [fmin, fmax] restricts the search. For a rational SISO model the peak is found exactly from the derivative of the squared gain.

getReport.description: Returns the text of an error caught with try/catch, including the function and line where it happened. 'basic' gives the message only. Example: try, f(); catch err, disp(getReport(err)), end

getString.description: Returns the text of a message object created with message.

get_param.description: Reads a parameter of a block or a setting of a model, as text. Also available for blocks: Name, BlockType, Parent, Position, Orientation, Ports ([inputs outputs]), Handle, PortHandles (a struct with the fields Inport and Outport for add_line) and DialogParameters; for models and subsystems: Blocks and Lines.

getabstime.description: The times of a timeseries as date text (a cell column), counted from TimeInfo.StartDate and shown in TimeInfo.Format (default 'dd-mmm-yyyy HH:MM:SS').

getappdata.description: Returns the value stored on h under name by setappdata, or [] when there is none. With one input, returns everything stored on h as a struct.

getdatasamples.description: The data of the samples at the indices ind (numbers or a logical mask), laid out like ts.Data.

getdatasamplesize.description: The size of one data sample: [1 n] for samples in rows of n values, or the leading dimensions when time runs along the last dimension.

getenv.description: Value of an operating-system environment variable, or '' if it is not set.

getfield.description: Value of a field, the same as s.name. Several names follow nested structs (s.a.b), and a cell array of subscripts indexes the value before it, so getfield(s, {2}, 'a', {3}) is s(2).a(3).

getframe.description: Captures the current axes (or the given axes or whole figure) as a movie frame: a struct with cdata, a height-by-width-by-3 uint8 image, and an empty colormap. rect = [left bottom width height] in pixels keeps part of the picture. Example: F(k) = getframe(gcf) inside a loop collects frames for movie or writeVideo.

getinterpmethod.description: The name of the interpolation method resample uses: 'linear' or 'zoh'.

getnhood.description: Neighbourhood of a structuring element as a logical matrix.

getpixelposition.description: Position of a figure or axes in pixels, [left bottom width height].

getpoints.description: Returns the points currently stored in the animated line h as row vectors.

getpref.description: Value of a stored preference. If it does not exist the default is stored and returned, or an error is raised when no default is given. With only a group, all its preferences are returned as a struct.

getqualitydesc.description: The description (from QualityInfo.Code and QualityInfo.Description) of the quality code of each sample, as a cell column.

getsamples.description: A timeseries with only the samples at the indices ind (numbers or a logical mask).

getsampleusingtime.description: A timeseries with the samples at time t, or at the times from tstart to tend (both included). Times are numbers in TimeInfo.Units; when TimeInfo.StartDate is set they may also be given as date text or datetime values.

gettsafteratevent.description: The samples at or after an event.

gettsafterevent.description: The samples after an event (a tsdata.event, or the n-th event with that name).

gettsatevent.description: The samples at the time of an event.

gettsbeforeatevent.description: The samples before or at an event.

usage: ts2 = gettsbetweenevents(ts, name1, name2, n1, n2)
gettsbetweenevents.description: The samples from the first event to the second (both included).

gevcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the generalized extreme value distribution with shape k, scale sigma and location mu (defaults 0, 1, 0): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

gevfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [shape, scale, location] of the generalized extreme value distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

gevinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the generalized extreme value distribution with shape k, scale sigma and location mu (defaults 0, 1, 0): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

gevlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the generalized extreme value distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

gevpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the generalized extreme value distribution with shape k, scale sigma and location mu (defaults 0, 1, 0), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

usage: r = gevrnd(k, sigma, mu, m, n, ...)
gevrnd.description: Random numbers from the generalized extreme value distribution with shape k, scale sigma and location mu (defaults 0, 1, 0). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

gevstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the generalized extreme value distribution with shape k, scale sigma and location mu (defaults 0, 1, 0).

ginput.description: Reads n mouse clicks (or clicks until Enter) from the current figure window and returns their data coordinates as column vectors. It needs a live plot window; elsewhere it raises an error.

givens.description: 2-by-2 rotation G = [c s; -s' c] that maps [x; y] to [r; 0]. With two outputs it returns the cosine and sine instead of the matrix.

usage: [b, dev, stats] = glmfit(X, y, distr, 'Name', value, ...)
glmfit.description: Coefficients of a generalized linear model (a constant term is added first). For 'binomial' y is a 0/1 vector or [successes trials]. Options: 'link', 'constant', 'offset', 'weights', 'estdisp'. stats holds se, t, p, covb, dfe, s and the residuals.

usage: [yhat, dylo, dyhi] = glmval(b, X, link, stats, 'Name', value, ...)
glmval.description: Predictions of a generalized linear model with coefficients b, and confidence bounds yhat - dylo and yhat + dyhi when stats from glmfit is given. Options: 'confidence', 'size', 'offset', 'constant'.

gmdistribution.description: Gaussian mixture distribution with the component means in the rows of mu, covariances sigma and mixing proportions p.

gmonopuls.description: Gaussian monopulse (the derivative of a Gaussian) with centre frequency fc (default 1000 Hz) and unit peak. The 'cutoff' form returns the time between its two extremes.

usage: x = gmres(A, b, restart, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
gmres.description: Solves A*x = b for a general square A with the generalized minimum residual method, restarted every `restart` iterations ([] for no restart). A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed. iter is [outer inner].

gobjects.description: Creates an array that holds graphics handles, to fill in a loop: h = gobjects(1, 3); h(k) = plot(...).

goertzel.description: Discrete Fourier transform of x at the bins idx only (one-based, as in fft; they need not be integers).

gpcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the generalized Pareto distribution with shape k, scale sigma and threshold theta (defaults 0, 1, 0): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

gpfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [shape, scale] (threshold 0) of the generalized Pareto distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

gpinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the generalized Pareto distribution with shape k, scale sigma and threshold theta (defaults 0, 1, 0): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

gplike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the generalized Pareto distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

gplot.description: Draws the graph with adjacency matrix A and node coordinates xy (one row per node). With outputs it returns the line coordinates instead, separated by NaN.

usage: gplotmatrix(X, Y, group, clr, sym, siz, doleg, dispopt, xnam, ynam)

gppdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the generalized Pareto distribution with shape k, scale sigma and threshold theta (defaults 0, 1, 0), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

usage: r = gprnd(k, sigma, theta, m, n, ...)
gprnd.description: Random numbers from the generalized Pareto distribution with shape k, scale sigma and threshold theta (defaults 0, 1, 0). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

gpstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the generalized Pareto distribution with shape k, scale sigma and threshold theta (defaults 0, 1, 0).

gpuArray.description: Returns A unchanged. mylab has no GPU arrays, so all calculations run on the CPU; this exists so that GPU-enabled code runs without edits.

gpuDevice.description: Describes the GPU in use. mylab has none, so the struct reports DeviceAvailable false and no memory; selecting or resetting a device does nothing.

gpuDeviceCount.description: Always 0: mylab does not use GPUs.

gradient.description: Numerical derivative: central differences in the interior and one-sided differences at the ends. Spacing may be a scalar step or a vector of coordinates. For a matrix, gx differentiates along each row (across columns) and gy along each column. Example: gradient([1 4 9 16]) is [3 4 6 7].

gram.description: Controllability or observability gramian of a stable model: the solution of A*Wc + Wc*A' + B*B' = 0 (or A'*Wo + Wo*A + C'*C = 0), and of the corresponding discrete equations for a discrete-time model. 'cf' and 'of' return the Cholesky factor R with W = R'*R.

usage: G = graph(s, t, weights, nodenames | num | NodeTable)
graph.description: Undirected graph. Build it from a symmetric adjacency matrix A (nonzeros are edges and their weights), from lists of end nodes s and t (numbers or names), or from tables. G.Edges is a table with EndNodes (and Weight); G.Nodes is a table with one row per node (variable Name when the nodes are named). Both tables can take extra variables.

gray.description: n-by-3 colormap of greys from black to white (default 256 rows).

gray2ind.description: Converts a grayscale image to an indexed image with an n-level gray colormap (64 by default, 2 for a binary image).

graythresh.description: Threshold between 0 and 1 chosen by Otsu's method, which splits a 256-bin histogram into two groups with the smallest spread inside the groups. em (0..1) says how well the two groups separate.

grid.description: Shows or hides grid lines on the current axes; grid alone toggles.

usage: vq = griddata(x, y, v, xq, yq)
vq = griddata(x, y, v, xq, yq, method)
vq = griddata(x, y, z, v, xq, yq, zq)
griddata.description: Interpolates scattered samples v at (x, y) onto the query points, usually a grid from meshgrid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'natural', 'cubic' and 'v4'. Query points outside the convex hull of the samples give NaN (except 'nearest' and 'v4'). 'natural' uses linear interpolation in mylab. Repeated sample points are averaged, with a warning.

griddedInterpolant.description: Interpolant on a full grid (ndgrid format, strictly increasing grid vectors). Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'next', 'previous', 'pchip', 'cubic' (cubic convolution on a uniform grid, otherwise a spline), 'spline' and 'makima', applied dimension by dimension. Extrapolation uses the interpolation method unless extrapMethod is given; 'none' gives NaN outside the grid. F(Xq) takes one query point per row (or any array for 1-D data); F({xq1, ...}) evaluates on the grid of query vectors. V can have one extra trailing dimension for several values per grid point. The properties GridVectors, Values, Method and ExtrapolationMethod can be read and assigned.

groot.description: Handle to the graphics root, the parent of all figures (the same as handle 0). Its properties include CurrentFigure and ScreenSize.

groupcounts.description: Counts the rows of each group. For a table the result has the grouping variables, GroupCount and Percent. For an array the counts, the groups and the percentages are returned separately; the columns of a matrix, or the vectors in a cell array, are separate grouping variables, and then BG is a cell array with one column per variable. groupvars names the grouping variables. An optional groupbins argument puts a grouping variable into bins first: bin edges, a number of bins, or for datetimes a unit such as 'month', 'day', 'hourofday', 'dayname'. 'IncludeMissingGroups', false leaves out the groups of missing values.

groupfilter.description: Keeps the rows of a table that pass a test made group by group. method is a function handle that gets the data of one variable for one group and returns true or false for the whole group, or one logical value per row. groupvars names the grouping variables. An optional groupbins argument puts a grouping variable into bins first: bin edges, a number of bins, or for datetimes a unit such as 'month', 'day', 'hourofday', 'dayname'.

groupsummary.description: Summary statistics for each group of table rows. The result has one row per group with the grouping values, a GroupCount column and one column per method and data variable, named like mean_Height. Methods: 'mean', 'sum', 'min', 'max', 'median', 'mode', 'std', 'var', 'range', 'numel', 'nnz', 'nummissing', 'all', or a function handle; NaN values are left out of the statistics. datavars defaults to all other numeric variables.

grouptransform.description: Transforms the data of each group separately: 'zscore', 'norm', 'meancenter', 'rescale', 'meanfill', 'linearfill' or a function handle that returns one row per row of the group (or one row for all). The transformed values replace the data variables, or with 'ReplaceValues', false are added as new variables named method_variable. groupvars names the grouping variables. An optional groupbins argument puts a grouping variable into bins first: bin edges, a number of bins, or for datetimes a unit such as 'month', 'day', 'hourofday', 'dayname'.

grp2idx.description: Turns a grouping variable into group numbers 1, 2, .... Numbers are grouped in sorted order, text in order of first appearance and categorical arrays in category order. names is a cell array of the group names. Missing values get NaN.

grpdelay.description: Group delay of a digital filter in samples: minus the slope of the phase. The inputs are those of freqz. Points where the response is zero get a delay of 0.

grpstats.description: Summary statistics by group. whichstats is a name or a cell array of names and function handles: 'mean', 'sem', 'numel', 'gname', 'std', 'var', 'min', 'max', 'range', 'median', 'mode', 'meanci' and 'predci'; one output is returned per statistic, with one row per group. group may be a cell array of several grouping variables. For a table the result is a table with the group variables, GroupCount and one variable per statistic and data variable.

usage: gscatter(x, y, g, clr, sym, siz, doleg, xnam, ynam)
gscatter.description: Scatter plot of y against x with one colour (and marker) per group of g, and a legend. g can be a cell array of grouping variables (one group per combination). clr is colour letters or an RGB matrix, sym marker letters, siz marker sizes, doleg 'on' or 'off'; xnam and ynam label the axes. h holds one line per group.

gtext.description: Places text where the mouse is clicked in a plot window. Without a live window the text is put in the middle of the axes and a warning suggests text(x, y, str).

guidata.description: Stores one value (usually a struct) with the window that h belongs to, or returns it. h can be the window or any component in it, so callbacks use it to share data: handles = guidata(hObject); handles.count = handles.count + 1; guidata(hObject, handles);

guide.description: Not available: GUIDE and its .fig files are not supported. Build the window in code with figure and uicontrol, or with uifigure.

guihandles.description: A struct with one field per Tag in the window of h; each field holds the component with that tag (several components when they share a tag). Tags that are not valid field names are skipped.

gunzip.description: Decompresses .gz files (or an http(s) address) next to the originals, or into outputfolder.

gzip.description: Compresses each file into a .gz file next to it, or in outputfolder. The originals are kept.

usage: h5create(..., 'ChunkSize', chunk, 'Deflate', level, 'Shuffle', tf, 'Fletcher32', tf, 'FillValue', v)
h5create.description: Creates a dataset in an HDF5 file (and the file and the groups on the way, if needed). dataset is a full name such as '/group/data'. size may contain Inf for a dimension that can grow, which needs a ChunkSize; compression with Deflate (0 to 9) and the Shuffle and Fletcher32 filters need one too. Datatype is 'double' (the default), 'single', an integer class or 'string'. Sizes and positions are given the MATLAB way, first dimension first; in the file the dimensions are stored in the opposite order, as MATLAB also does. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

h5disp.description: Prints the groups, datasets and attributes of an HDF5 file, or of one group or dataset. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

h5info.description: Describes an HDF5 file, group or dataset. A group gives Filename, Name, Groups, Datasets and Attributes; a dataset gives Name, Datatype (Class, Type, Size), Dataspace (Size, MaxSize), ChunkSize, FillValue, Filters and Attributes. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

usage: data = h5read(filename, dataset, start, count, stride)
h5read.description: Reads a dataset of an HDF5 file, or part of it. Numbers keep their class, strings come back as a string array, and a compound dataset as a struct with one field per member. A dataset with one dimension is returned as a column. Sizes and positions are given the MATLAB way, first dimension first; in the file the dimensions are stored in the opposite order, as MATLAB also does. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

h5readatt.description: Reads an attribute of a group or dataset of an HDF5 file ('/' is the file itself). Text is returned as a character vector. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

usage: h5write(filename, dataset, data, start, count, stride)
h5write.description: Writes data to an existing dataset of an HDF5 file: all of it, or the block that starts at start and has count elements per dimension. Writing beyond the current size of a dimension created with Inf makes the dataset larger. Sizes and positions are given the MATLAB way, first dimension first; in the file the dimensions are stored in the opposite order, as MATLAB also does. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

h5writeatt.description: Creates or replaces an attribute of an existing group or dataset of an HDF5 file. The value is numeric or text. HDF5 files are read and written with the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab; the browser app loads it the first time a program uses HDF5.

hadamard.description: Hadamard matrix of order n: entries +1 and -1 with H'*H = n*eye(n). n must be a power of 2, or 12 or 20 times a power of 2.

hamming.description: Hamming window of length n as a column vector.

hampel.description: Outlier removal: a sample that differs from the median of its 2k+1 neighbours (k defaults to 3) by more than nsigma (default 3) scaled median absolute deviations is replaced by that median. j marks the replaced samples.

handle.description: The graphics object a numeric handle stands for. double(h) gives the number of any graphics object (a figure's is its figure number), and storing an object into a double array stores that number, as in h = zeros(1, 2); h(1) = plot(x, y); handle turns such numbers back into objects. A handle object is returned unchanged.

hankel.description: Hankel matrix: constant along the anti-diagonals. hankel(c) has first column c and zeros below the main anti-diagonal; hankel(c, r) has first column c and last row r.

hann.description: Hann (raised-cosine) window of length n as a column vector; the end points are zero.

hanning.description: Hann window variant without the zero end points, as a column vector.

harmmean.description: Harmonic mean: n divided by the sum of the reciprocals. nanflag 'omitnan' leaves NaN values out ('includenan', the default, keeps them).

has.description: True where a symbolic expression contains the variable or subexpression sub.

hasFrame.description: True while a VideoReader object has frames that readFrame has not returned yet.

hascycles.description: True if the graph contains a cycle.

hasdata.description: True while a datastore has data left to read. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.hasdata(...).

hasdelay.description: True when the model has an input, output or input/output delay.

head.description: First k rows of a table or array (default 8).

usage: heatmap(C), heatmap(x, y, C) or heatmap(tbl, xvar, yvar)
heatmap.description: A grid of coloured, labelled cells.

heaviside.description: Step function: 0 for x < 0, 1 for x > 0 and 1/2 at x = 0. Works on numbers and on symbolic expressions.

height.description: Number of rows of a table (or of an array).

help.description: Shows the calling forms and a short description of a function. For functions and classdef classes in your own .m files it shows the comment block at the top of the file. With an output the text is returned instead of printed.

helpdlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Help' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines.

hess.description: Hessenberg form: A = P*H*P' with P unitary and H zero below the first subdiagonal. With two matrices it returns Q*A*Z = AA (upper Hessenberg) and Q*B*Z = BB (upper triangular).

hessian.description: Matrix of second derivatives of the scalar expression f for the variables v.

hex2dec.description: Value of a hexadecimal digit string (either case). A char matrix or cell array gives a column of numbers, and text that is not hexadecimal gives NaN. A 0x prefix is allowed, and a suffix s8 ... s64 or u8 ... u64 reads the digits as an integer of that type, so hex2dec('FFs8') is -1. Example: hex2dec('ff') is 255.

hgexport.description: The older way to save a figure to a file.

hggroup.description: Create a group object. Graphics objects created with 'Parent', g can then be shown, hidden or deleted together.

hgload.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

hgsave.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

hgtransform.description: Create a group whose children are drawn moved, scaled or rotated by the 4-by-4 matrix M (see makehgtform).

hidden.description: hidden on/off: whether a mesh hides what lies behind it (opaque faces) or is see-through.

highpass.description: Filters x with a highpass filter whose passband starts at wpass and removes the filter delay. The options are those of lowpass.

hilb.description: n-by-n Hilbert matrix with entries 1/(i+j-1), a classic badly conditioned example.

hilbert.description: Analytic signal of real data: the real part is x and the imaginary part its Hilbert transform, so abs(z) is the instantaneous amplitude. Works along a row vector or down columns; any imaginary part of x is ignored.

hist.description: Older histogram function using equal-width bins (10 by default) or bins around the given centres. With outputs it returns the bin counts (and centres) without plotting; without outputs it draws the bars. Use histogram for a graphics handle.

histc.description: Counts values falling in each interval edges(k) <= x < edges(k+1); the last count is for values equal to the last edge. bin gives each value's interval (0 if outside). Older function; histcounts is usually more convenient.

histcounts.description: Counts how many values of x fall in each bin; every bin includes its left edge and the last bin also its right edge. Automatic bins use a round width (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten) based on the spread of the data, with edges on multiples of it; integer data over a small range gets unit-width bins centred on the integers. Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'pdf', 'cdf', 'countdensity' or 'cumcount'. bin gives the bin number of each element (0 when outside). Example: histcounts(1:5) is [1 1 1 1 1] with edges 0.5:1:5.5.
