histcounts2.description: Two-dimensional histogram counts: N(i, j) is the number of points with X in bin i and Y in bin j. Options: XBinEdges, YBinEdges, NumBins, BinWidth, XBinLimits, YBinLimits, BinMethod, Normalization.

histeq.description: Histogram equalization: remaps gray levels so that the output uses n levels (64 by default) about equally often, or so that its histogram resembles hgram. T is the mapping applied to the 256 input levels. Results can differ slightly from other implementations in how ties between output levels are resolved.

histfit.description: Histogram of the data with the density of a fitted distribution drawn over it (normal by default; dist is any name fitdist accepts). The number of bins defaults to the square root of the number of values. h holds the bar and the line.

histogram.description: Plots a histogram of the finite values in x. Bins are chosen automatically (unit bins for small integer data) unless a bin count or edges are given, or the options NumBins, BinEdges, BinWidth, BinLimits or BinMethod ('integers'). Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'percentage', 'countdensity', 'pdf', 'cumcount' or 'cdf'. Style options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName, Orientation. h is a Histogram handle: h.Values gives the bar heights, and changing h.NumBins, h.BinEdges, h.BinWidth or h.Normalization redraws the plot.

histogram2.description: Counts of pairs of values in a grid of rectangular bins, drawn as 3-D bars.

hms.description: Hour, minute and second of a datetime array, or the hours, minutes and seconds that make up each element of a duration array.

hold.description: With hold on (or hold all), new plots are added to the current axes instead of replacing them; hold off returns to replacing. hold alone toggles. An axes handle selects other axes. The axes property NextPlot ('add' or 'replace') shows the same state.

holes.description: The holes of p as a column of solid polyshapes. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.holes(...).

home.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

horner.description: Writes a polynomial in nested (Horner) form.

horzcat.description: Joins arrays side by side, the same as [A, B, ...]. They must have the same number of rows.

hot.description: n-by-3 colormap from black through red and yellow to white.

hough.description: Hough transform for lines: every foreground pixel votes for all lines rho = x cos(theta) + y sin(theta) through it (x and y count from 0 at the first column and row). H has one row per rho and one column per theta (degrees, -90 to 89 by default). 'RhoResolution' and 'Theta' change the grid.

houghlines.description: Line segments in BW that belong to the given Hough peaks: a struct array with point1, point2 ([x y]), theta and rho. Gaps shorter than 'FillGap' (default 20) are bridged and segments shorter than 'MinLength' (default 40) are dropped.

houghpeaks.description: Row and column of the largest values of a Hough matrix. After each peak its neighbourhood ('NHoodSize') is cleared; values below 'Threshold' (default half the maximum) are ignored.

hour.description: Hour (0-23) of each element of a datetime array.

hours.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many hours. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of hours.

hsv.description: n-by-3 colormap cycling through the hues of the colour wheel.

hsv2rgb.description: Converts hue-saturation-value colours (each 0..1) to red-green-blue, as double.

hsvd.description: Hankel singular values of a model: large values belong to states that matter for the input/output behaviour, small ones to states that balred can remove. Unstable modes give Inf.

hygecdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the hypergeometric distribution with population size m, k items with the property, n items drawn: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

hygeinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the hypergeometric distribution with population size m, k items with the property, n items drawn: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

hygepdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the hypergeometric distribution with population size m, k items with the property, n items drawn, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

usage: r = hygernd(m, k, n, m, n, ...)
hygernd.description: Random numbers from the hypergeometric distribution with population size m, k items with the property, n items drawn. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

hygestat.description: Mean m and variance v of the hypergeometric distribution with population size m, k items with the property, n items drawn.

hypot.description: sqrt(a.^2 + b.^2) element by element, computed without overflow for large values.

i.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

usage: X = icare(A, B, Q, R, S, E)
icare.description: Stabilizing solution of the continuous algebraic Riccati equation (see care), with the outputs in the order solution, gain K, closed-loop poles L. [] selects a default (R = I, S = 0, E = I). info has Report = 0 on success; a nonzero G term is not supported.

icdf.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantiles) of a distribution given by name and parameters, or of a probability distribution object.

ichol.description: Incomplete Cholesky factor of a sparse symmetric positive definite matrix: a lower-triangular L with L*L' close to A, used to precondition pcg as pcg(A, b, tol, maxit, L, L'). By default L keeps the nonzero pattern of the lower triangle of A. opts.type = 'ict' with opts.droptol allows fill-in; opts.diagcomp adds a diagonal shift. An error is raised if a pivot is not positive.

usage: X = idare(A, B, Q, R, S, E)
idare.description: Stabilizing solution of the discrete algebraic Riccati equation (see dare), with the outputs in the order solution, gain K, closed-loop poles L.

idct.description: Inverse discrete cosine transform: idct(dct(x)) returns x.

idealfilter.description: Keeps ('pass') or removes ('notch') the frequencies in the rows [low high] of interval, in cycles per time unit, by zeroing them in the Fourier transform of each data column (after removing its mean). Needs evenly spaced times; index picks the columns to filter.

idivide.description: Integer division with a chosen rounding: 'fix' (toward zero, the default), 'floor', 'ceil' or 'round'. At least one input must be an integer type (two integer inputs must share a class) and the result has that class. Example: idivide(int32(7), int32(2)) is 3.

idwt.description: One level of the inverse wavelet transform. n keeps the n central samples (use the length of the original signal when it was odd). Either coefficient vector may be [] to rebuild from the other one alone.

usage: X = idwt2(cA, cH, cV, cD, wname)
X = idwt2(cA, cH, cV, cD, LoR, HiR)
idwt2.description: One level of the inverse two-dimensional wavelet transform; the size keeps the central part.

ifelse.description: Another name for merge(mask, tval, fval). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

ifft.description: Inverse fast Fourier transform. The result is returned as real when its imaginary parts are negligible; 'symmetric' always returns the real part.

ifft2.description: Two-dimensional inverse FFT; real output when the imaginary parts are negligible or with 'symmetric'.

ifftn.description: Inverse N-dimensional discrete Fourier transform. The result is real when its imaginary part is only round-off; 'symmetric' always returns the real part.

ifftshift.description: Undoes fftshift (they differ for odd lengths).

ifourier.description: Inverse Fourier transform: 1/(2*pi) times the integral of F(w)*exp(i*w*x) over all w. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

ilaplace.description: Inverse Laplace transform of F(s), as a function of t (for t >= 0). Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

ilu.description: Incomplete LU factorization of a sparse square matrix, for use as a preconditioner: L*U approximates A while staying sparse. setup is a struct; setup.type is 'nofill' (default) or 'ilutp', and setup.droptol sets the drop tolerance for 'ilutp'.

im2bw.description: Binary image that is true where the brightness is above level, a fraction of the class range (default 0.5). RGB and indexed images are converted to grayscale first.

im2col.description: Rearranges m-by-n blocks of a matrix into columns. 'sliding' (default) takes every block position; 'distinct' takes non-overlapping blocks, padding the matrix with zeros.

im2double.description: Converts an image to double, rescaling integer classes to 0..1 (a uint8 255 becomes 1). double input is returned unchanged. With 'indexed' the values are colour numbers, which are only shifted to count from 1.

im2frame.description: Wraps an image in a movie frame struct with the fields cdata and colormap. RGB images given as doubles between 0 and 1 are stored as uint8; an indexed image keeps its colormap.

im2gray.description: Like rgb2gray, and a grayscale image is passed through unchanged.

im2int16.description: Converts an image to int16, rescaling so that the full range of the input class maps to -32768..32767.

im2single.description: Like im2double, but the result is of class single.

im2uint16.description: Converts an image to uint16, rescaling so that the full range of the input class maps to 0..65535.

im2uint8.description: Converts an image to uint8, rescaling as needed: 0..1 floating-point values map to 0..255 (values outside are clipped), uint16 values are divided by 257, and true becomes 255.

imabsdiff.description: Absolute difference of two images in their own class, without the underflow that X - Y would give for unsigned integers.

imadd.description: Adds two images, or a constant to an image, in the class of the image: integer results are rounded and clipped to the class range instead of wrapping.

imadjust.description: Stretches contrast: values from low_in to high_in are mapped to low_out..high_out (0..1 by default), with values outside clipped. Limits are fractions of the class range; [] means [0 1]. With no limits, the darkest and brightest 1% of pixels are saturated. gamma bends the mapping (below 1 brightens). For RGB images give limits, optionally one column per channel.

imag.description: Imaginary part of each element (0 for real input).

image.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

imageDatastore.description: A list of image files that is read one image at a time. location is a folder, a file, a pattern with * or a cell or string array of these; 'IncludeSubfolders' also looks inside subfolders. Only files whose extension is in 'FileExtensions' are kept; by default those are the image formats imread reads. With 'LabelSource', 'foldernames' each file is labelled with the name of the folder that holds it; 'Labels' gives one label per file instead. Properties: Files (a column cell array of full paths), Folders, Labels (categorical for folder names; a column vector), ReadSize, ReadFcn (imread unless you give a function that takes a file name), AlternateFileSystemRoots, SupportedOutputFormats and DefaultOutputFormat. Labels, ReadSize, ReadFcn and Files can be assigned. The datastore is a handle: read moves a position shared by every copy of the variable. Methods: read, readimage, readall, hasdata, reset, preview, progress, countEachLabel, splitEachLabel, shuffle, subset, partition, numpartitions, transform, combine and copy. datastore(location, 'Type', 'image', ...) makes the same object.

imagesc.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

imbilatfilt.description: Bilateral filter: smooths while keeping edges, because a neighbour counts less the more its value differs. degreeOfSmoothing is the variance allowed in value (default 1% of the squared range of the class) and spatialSigma the width of the Gaussian in space (default 1). 'NeighborhoodSize' and 'Padding' are available.

imbinarize.description: Binary image from a grayscale image. With no threshold Otsu's method picks one for the whole image (see graythresh). T is a threshold between 0 and 1, or a matrix of them. 'adaptive' compares each pixel with the mean of its neighbourhood (about one eighth of the image size), which copes with uneven lighting: a pixel is false when it is clearly darker than its surroundings (15% at the default 'Sensitivity' of 0.5), so evenly lit areas come out true. Its results are close to, but not identical with, other implementations.

imbothat.description: The closing minus the image: keeps small dark details.

imboxfilt.description: Mean filter with a box of odd size (default 3). 'Padding' is 'replicate' (default), 'symmetric', 'circular' or a number; 'NormalizationFactor' replaces the division by the number of pixels. The result has the class of the input.

imclearborder.description: Removes the objects that touch the edge of a binary image, or in a gray image the structures that are lighter than their surroundings and connected to the edge.

imclose.description: Closing, a dilation followed by an erosion: fills dark gaps and holes smaller than the structuring element.

imcomplement.description: Negative of an image: 255 - A for uint8, 1 - A for floating point, and logical NOT for a binary image.

imcrop.description: Cuts a rectangle out of an image. The rectangle is in pixel coordinates, so with whole numbers the result has height+1 rows and width+1 columns; a BoundingBox from regionprops gives exactly the region. Choosing the rectangle with the mouse is not supported.

imdilate.description: Dilation: each pixel becomes the largest value under the structuring element, which grows bright regions (and true regions of a binary image). The structuring element is a strel object or a matrix of zeros and ones; its centre is element floor((size+1)/2).

imdivide.description: Divides images element by element, rounding and saturating integer classes.

imerode.description: Erosion: each pixel becomes the smallest value under the structuring element, which shrinks bright regions. The structuring element is a strel object or a matrix of zeros and ones; its centre is element floor((size+1)/2).

imextendedmax.description: Regional maxima after peaks lower than h have been removed (the maxima of imhmax).

imextendedmin.description: Regional minima after valleys shallower than h have been removed (the minima of imhmin).

imfill.description: Fills holes in a binary image (background regions that cannot be reached from the border), or flood-fills the background starting from the given linear indices or [row col] rows. Grayscale images and interactive use are not supported.

imfilter.description: Filters an image with the kernel h. By default this is correlation, the result has the size of A and pixels outside the image count as 0. padding may be a number, 'replicate' (repeat the border), 'symmetric' (mirror) or 'circular' (wrap around). 'conv' rotates the kernel by 180 degrees, 'full' returns the larger full result. The output has the class of A, so integer images are rounded and clipped; convert with im2double to keep fractions and negative values. A 2-D kernel is applied to each colour channel.

imfinfo.description: Describes an image file without loading the pixels: a struct with Filename, FileModDate, FileSize, Format, Width, Height, BitDepth, ColorType ('grayscale', 'truecolor' or 'indexed'), NumberOfFrames, DelayTime (hundredths of a second, GIF) and Colormap. A file with several frames gives one struct per frame.

imfuse.description: Combines two images into one uint8 picture for comparison: 'falsecolor' (default; A in green and B in magenta, so equal areas look gray), 'blend', 'diff' (absolute difference), 'checkerboard' or 'montage' (side by side). 'Scaling' is 'independent' (default), 'joint' or 'none'; 'ColorChannels' is 'green-magenta', 'red-cyan' or [R G B] with 1 for A, 2 for B and 0 for none. The smaller image is padded with zeros.

imgaussfilt.description: Gaussian blur with standard deviation sigma (0.5 by default; [sy sx] for different amounts down and across). The kernel is 2*ceil(2*sigma)+1 wide unless 'FilterSize' is given, and the border is repeated unless 'Padding' says 'symmetric', 'circular' or a number.

imgradient.description: Magnitude and direction (degrees, counter-clockwise from the positive x axis) of the image gradient. The method is 'sobel' (default), 'prewitt', 'central', 'intermediate' or 'roberts'.

imgradientxy.description: Gradient of an image along x (left to right) and y (top to bottom). The method is 'sobel' (default), 'prewitt', 'central' or 'intermediate'.

imguidedfilter.description: Edge-preserving smoothing guided by the image G (A itself by default): locally B is a linear function of G. 'NeighborhoodSize' defaults to [5 5] and 'DegreeOfSmoothing' to 1% of the squared range of the class.

imhist.description: Histogram of a grayscale image with n bins (256 by default, 2 for a binary image) spread over the range of the image's class. With outputs it returns the counts and bin centres as columns; with none it draws the histogram as a bar chart. For an indexed image the counts are per colormap entry.

imhistmatch.description: Adjusts the gray levels of I so that its histogram resembles that of ref, using nbins (default 64) bins. The channels of an RGB image are matched one by one.

imhmax.description: Lowers every peak by h and removes the maxima that are less than h high.

imhmin.description: Raises every valley by h and removes the minima that are less than h deep.

imimposemin.description: Changes I so that its only regional minima are where BW is true; used to place the seeds of a watershed.

imlincomb.description: Linear combination K1*A1 + K2*A2 + ... (+ K) of images, computed in double and rounded and saturated only once at the end. The result has the class of the first image unless another class is named.

immse.description: Mean squared error between two arrays of the same size, computed in double.

immultiply.description: Multiplies images element by element, saturating integer classes.

imnoise.description: Adds noise to an image. Mean and variance refer to a 0..1 intensity scale (defaults 0 and 0.01); density is the fraction of pixels set to black or white (0.05); speckle noise is multiplicative (0.05). Uses the generator controlled by rng.

imodwt.description: Rebuilds a signal from its maximal-overlap wavelet transform.

imopen.description: Opening, an erosion followed by a dilation: removes bright details smaller than the structuring element while keeping larger shapes.

impinvar.description: Digital filter whose impulse response is the analog filter's impulse response sampled at fs (default 1 Hz) and scaled by 1/fs. tol (default 0.001) decides when two poles count as repeated.

import.description: Lets later code call functions and classes of a +pkg folder without the package name: after import geom.* (or import geom.area), area(x) means geom.area(x). Unlike in MATLAB the import stays in effect for the rest of the session, in every function. Imports of packages that do not exist (Java packages, for example) are ignored.

importdata.description: Loads numeric text data. Without header lines the result is a matrix. With header lines it is a structure with data (the matrix), textdata (the header text) and, when the last header line names the columns, colheaders. The delimiter and number of header lines are detected when not given. .mat files are loaded as with load.

improfile.description: Values of an image along the line (or polyline) through the points (xi, yi), at n evenly spaced points (about one per pixel by default). The method is 'nearest' (default), 'bilinear' or 'bicubic'. Choosing the line with the mouse is not supported.

impulse.description: Impulse response. y has one row per time, one column per output and one page per input; x holds the states of a state-space model. For a discrete-time model the input is a pulse of height 1/Ts lasting one sample. A direct feedthrough term (an impulse at t = 0) is not shown. The optional time argument is either a final time or a vector of increasing times such as 0:0.01:5 (for a discrete-time model its step must equal Ts). The response of a continuous-time model is exact at the given times, which need not be evenly spaced, so the time vector of a simulation can be used. Without a time argument a duration and step are chosen from the poles so that the transient is shown until it has settled. Without output arguments the response is plotted; several models, each optionally followed by a line style such as 'r--', are drawn in the same axes.

impulseplot.description: Plots the impulse response; same arguments as impulse.

impyramid.description: One step of a Gaussian pyramid: 'reduce' smooths and halves the size (rounding up), 'expand' interpolates to 2n-1 pixels each way.

impz.description: Impulse response of a digital filter. n is the number of samples (chosen from the poles when left out) or a vector of sample numbers; t holds the times (samples, or seconds with fs). Without outputs a stem plot is drawn.

imquantize.description: Replaces each element by the number of its interval: 1 up to and including levels(1), 2 up to levels(2), and so on. With values the result takes values(k) for interval k.

imread.description: Reads an image file (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, TIFF and the other formats Pillow knows) or an http(s) address. Grayscale images come back as an H-by-W array and colour images as H-by-W-by-3, of class uint8 (uint16 for 16-bit grayscale files, logical for 1-bit files). For an indexed file the first output holds zero-based uint8 colour numbers and map is the N-by-3 colormap; use ind2rgb to get colours. alpha is the transparency channel, or empty. A frame number (or 'Frames', k or 'all') picks frames of an animated GIF or multi-page TIFF; several frames are stacked along the fourth dimension. Files are also looked for on the search path. 16-bit RGB files are read with 8 bits per channel. The sample pictures that ship with MATLAB are not included.

imreconstruct.description: Morphological reconstruction: the marker is grown by repeated dilation but never above the mask. For binary images this keeps the objects of the mask that contain a marker pixel. conn is 4 or 8 (the default) for images and 6, 18 or 26 for volumes, or a 3-by-3 matrix of neighbours.

imref2d.description: Describes where an image lies in world coordinates. Properties: ImageSize, XWorldLimits, YWorldLimits, PixelExtentInWorldX, PixelExtentInWorldY, ImageExtentInWorldX, ImageExtentInWorldY, XIntrinsicLimits and YIntrinsicLimits. Methods: worldToIntrinsic, intrinsicToWorld, worldToSubscript, contains and sizesMatch.

imregionalmax.description: Regional maxima: connected groups of equal pixels all of whose neighbours are lower. conn is 4 or 8 (the default) for images and 6, 18 or 26 for volumes, or a 3-by-3 matrix of neighbours.

imregionalmin.description: Regional minima: connected groups of equal pixels all of whose neighbours are higher. conn is 4 or 8 (the default) for images and 6, 18 or 26 for volumes, or a 3-by-3 matrix of neighbours.

imresize.description: Resizes an image by a scale factor or to a given size; one of rows and cols may be NaN to keep the aspect ratio. method is 'bicubic' (default), 'bilinear', 'nearest', 'box', 'lanczos2' or 'lanczos3'. When shrinking, the kernel is widened so that fine detail is averaged rather than aliased (not for 'nearest'; switch off with 'Antialiasing', false). The result has the class of A. Resizing an indexed image together with its colormap is not supported. Value ranges follow the class: 0..255 for uint8, 0..65535 for uint16, -32768..32767 for int16 and 0..1 for double and single.

imresize3.description: Resizes a volume. The method is 'cubic' (default), 'linear', 'nearest', 'box', 'triangle', 'lanczos2' or 'lanczos3'; shrinking is anti-aliased unless 'Antialiasing' is false.

imrotate.description: Rotates an image counter-clockwise by angle degrees about its centre. method is 'nearest' (default), 'bilinear' or 'bicubic'. The result is large enough to hold the whole rotated image ('loose') unless 'crop' keeps the original size; uncovered corners are 0. Multiples of 90 degrees are exact. 'bicubic' uses a cubic spline, so values differ slightly from other implementations.

imsharpen.description: Sharpens by unsharp masking: adds back 'Amount' (default 0.8) times the difference between the image and a Gaussian blur of standard deviation 'Radius' (default 1). 'Threshold' (0 to 1) leaves low-contrast detail alone. Only the lightness of an RGB image is sharpened.

imshow.description: Shows an image with square pixels and no axis ticks. Grayscale images use the gray colormap over the range of their class (0 to 255 for uint8, 0 to 1 for double; black and white for logical); [low high] sets the range and [] uses the image's own minimum and maximum. M-by-N-by-3 arrays are shown as colour, X with a colormap as an indexed image, and a file name is read first.

imshowpair.description: Shows two images together to compare them; the methods and options are those of imfuse.

imsubtract.description: Subtracts images (or a constant) in the class of the image; unsigned results below 0 become 0.

imtile.description: Arranges several images (a cell array, or a stack along the third or fourth dimension) in a grid and returns one image. 'GridSize' [rows cols], 'BorderSize', 'BackgroundColor' and 'ThumbnailSize' are available; images of other sizes are resized to the first one.

imtophat.description: The image minus its opening: keeps small bright details.

imtransform.description: Applies a transformation made by maketform to an image. The result covers the transformed image unless 'XData' and 'YData' give the range to show; 'XYScale', 'Size' and 'FillValues' are available. interp is 'bilinear' (default), 'nearest' or 'bicubic'.

imtranslate.description: Shifts an image tx pixels to the right and ty pixels down, keeping its size. Uncovered pixels are 0 or the fill value; fractional shifts are interpolated ('linear' by default, or 'nearest' or 'cubic').

imwarp.description: Applies a geometric transformation to an image. The result is just large enough to hold the whole transformed image unless 'OutputView' gives an imref2d to draw into; RB tells where the result lies. interp is 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'cubic'; pixels that come from outside the image get 'FillValues' (default 0). A geometric transformation is an object made by affine2d, projective2d, affinetform2d, rigidtform2d, simtform2d, transltform2d, projtform2d, fitgeotrans or fitgeotform2d.

imwrite.description: Writes an image to a file; the format comes from the extension or from fmt ('png', 'jpg', 'bmp', 'gif', 'tif', ...). uint8 data is written as is, double and single data is taken to span 0..1, logical data becomes a 1-bit image and 16-bit grayscale is kept in PNG and TIFF files. With a colormap the first input is an indexed image. 'Quality' (0-100, default 75) applies to JPEG and 'Alpha' adds transparency to a PNG. For GIF files 'WriteMode', 'append' adds a frame to an existing file, 'DelayTime' is the time each frame is shown in seconds, and 'LoopCount', Inf makes the animation repeat forever; a 4-D array writes several frames at once. Other options are accepted and ignored.

incenter.description: Centers (and radii) of the circles or spheres inscribed in the triangles or tetrahedra. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.incenter(...).

incidence.description: Sparse node-by-edge incidence matrix: column j has -1 at the source node and +1 at the target node of edge j.

inconsistent.description: Inconsistency of each link of a tree: mean and standard deviation of the heights of the links up to depth levels below (default 2), their number, and the coefficient.

ind2gray.description: Grayscale image from an indexed image and its colormap.

ind2rgb.description: Turns an indexed image into a double RGB image by looking every colour number up in the colormap. Integer-class indices count from 0, double indices from 1.

ind2sub.description: Converts linear indices into subscripts for an array of size sz. With fewer outputs than dimensions, the last output counts through the remaining dimensions. Example: [r, c] = ind2sub([3 4], 8) gives r = 2, c = 3.

indegree.description: Number of edges entering each node of a digraph.

indepnames.description: Column cell array of the independent variable names. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

index.description: Position of the first (or, with 'last', the last) occurrence of the text t in s, or 0 when t does not occur. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

inedges.description: Indices of the edges entering a node of a digraph, and the nodes they come from.

inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

inferiorto.description: Called in the constructor of a class kept in an @folder: the named classes take precedence over this class when their objects appear together in a call.

initial.description: Response of a state-space model to the initial state x0 with zero input. The optional time argument is either a final time or a vector of increasing times such as 0:0.01:5 (for a discrete-time model its step must equal Ts). The response of a continuous-time model is exact at the given times, which need not be evenly spaced, so the time vector of a simulation can be used. Without a time argument a duration and step are chosen from the poles so that the transient is shown until it has settled. Without output arguments the response is plotted; several models, each optionally followed by a line style such as 'r--', are drawn in the same axes.

initialplot.description: Plots the response to an initial state; same arguments as initial.

inline.description: Creates a function from text, e.g. f = inline('x.^2 + 1'); f(3). Without argument names the variables in the expression are used in alphabetical order. The result is an anonymous function; new code should write @(x) x.^2 + 1.

inner2outer.description: Reorganizes a table whose variables are nested tables: the inner variable names become the outer variables, each one a nested table with the former outer names.

innerjoin.description: Combines rows of two tables that have equal key values (by default all variables with the same name). Every matching pair of rows gives one output row; the result is sorted by key. Non-key variables of the right table are appended; names used in both tables get _left and _right suffixes. 'LeftVariables' and 'RightVariables' choose the variables to keep.

inpolygon.description: True for the query points (xq, yq) that lie inside or on the edge of the polygon with corners (xv, yv). on is true for points exactly on the edge. Separate several loops with NaN; a loop inside another makes a hole.

input.description: Shows prompt and reads a line from the user. The reply is evaluated as an expression, so typing 2*3 gives 6; an empty reply gives []. With 's' the raw text is returned instead.

inputParser.description: Creates an object that describes and checks the inputs of a function. Declare arguments with addRequired, addOptional and addParameter, then call parse(p, varargin{:}). Afterwards p.Results is a struct with one field per argument (fields in alphabetical order), p.UsingDefaults lists the arguments that were not given and p.Unmatched holds unknown name-value pairs when p.KeepUnmatched is true. Other settings: FunctionName (used in error messages), CaseSensitive (default false), PartialMatching (default true), StructExpand (default true). Example: p = inputParser; addRequired(p, 'n'); addParameter(p, 'Tol', 1e-3); parse(p, varargin{:}); p.Results

inputdlg.description: Asks for one line of text per prompt (prompts is text or a cell array) and returns the answers as a column cell array of character vectors; use str2double for numbers. An empty reply keeps that prompt's default. In a terminal or notebook the question is asked as text; when nobody can answer (for example in a batch run) the default is used and a note is printed. A front end that cancels returns {}.

inputname.description: Inside a function: the name of the caller's variable that was passed as argument k, or '' when the argument was an expression or a constant (an error instead when the second argument is true). It is known for functions called by name with arguments in parentheses; at the prompt, outside any function, it returns ''.

insert.description: Adds entries to the dictionary d and returns it. With 'Overwrite', false it is an error if a key is already there.

insertAfter.description: Inserts new after every occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

insertBefore.description: Inserts new before every occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

int.description: Symbolic integral. Without limits it returns an antiderivative (without the constant); with limits a and b the definite integral. The variable defaults to x, or the one closest to x. An integral that cannot be found is returned unevaluated. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

int16.description: Converts to the int16 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -32768..32767, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int16(2.5) is 3.

int2str.description: Rounds x to integers and converts the result to text like num2str.

int32.description: Converts to the int32 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -2147483648..2147483647, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int32(2.5) is 3.

int64.description: Converts to the int64 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range about -9.2e18..9.2e18, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int64(2.5) is 3.

int8.description: Converts to the int8 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -128..127, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int8(2.5) is 3.

usage: q = integral(f, a, b, 'RelTol', rt, 'AbsTol', at)
integral.description: Integrates f from a to b by adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature. f must accept a vector and return a vector of the same size (use .*, ./ and .^). Limits may be infinite, and integrable singularities at the end points are handled. With 'ArrayValued' f is called with scalars and may return an array. 'Waypoints' are points the path goes through: real ones mark discontinuities, complex ones define a piecewise-linear contour. Defaults: RelTol 1e-6, AbsTol 1e-10.

usage: q = integral2(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
q = integral2(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, 'Method', m, 'RelTol', rt, 'AbsTol', at)
integral2.description: Double integral of f(x, y) over xmin <= x <= xmax, ymin(x) <= y <= ymax(x). f takes arrays and returns an array of the same size; ymin and ymax may be numbers or function handles of x. Method is 'tiled' (rectangles, finite regions), 'iterated' (nested 1-D integrals, needed for infinite limits) or 'auto'.

usage: q = integral3(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax)
integral3.description: Triple integral of f(x, y, z). ymin and ymax may be functions of x; zmin and zmax may be functions of (x, y). f takes arrays of equal size.

integralBoxFilter.description: Box filter computed from an integral image: the mean over every window that fits inside the image, so the result is smaller than the image by the filter size minus one.

integralImage.description: Summed-area table: J(r+1, c+1) is the sum of I(1:r, 1:c). The result is one row and one column larger than I, with zeros in its first row and column.

integrate.description: Integral of a curve fit from x0 to each element of x. f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.integrate(...).

interp.description: Raises the sample rate of a vector by the integer r. The original samples are kept and the new ones are computed from the 2n nearest samples (n defaults to 4), assuming the signal contains no frequencies above cutoff (default 0.5) times the original Nyquist frequency. b is the interpolation filter.

interp1.description: One-dimensional interpolation of the samples (x, y) at the points xq. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'previous', 'next', 'spline' (not-a-knot cubic spline), 'pchip' and 'cubic' (shape-preserving piecewise cubic) and 'makima' (modified Akima). Outside the range of x the result is NaN for the first four methods and extrapolated for the cubic ones, unless 'extrap' or a fill value is given. If y is a matrix, each column is interpolated. Example: interp1([1 2 3], [10 20 30], 2.5) is 25.

usage: Zq = interp2(X, Y, Z, Xq, Yq)
interp2.description: Interpolation on a 2-D grid. X and Y are grid vectors or meshgrid matrices (default 1:n and 1:m). A row vector Xq with a column vector Yq is expanded to a grid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline' and 'makima'. Points outside the grid give NaN or extrapval. interp2(Z, k) refines the grid by halving the spacing k times (once if k is omitted).

usage: Vq = interp3(X, Y, Z, V, Xq, Yq, Zq)
interp3.description: Interpolates values on a 3-D grid made with meshgrid (X varies along the columns). Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline'. Points outside the grid give NaN, or extrapval.

interpft.description: Resamples periodic data to n points by zero-padding (or trimming) its Fourier transform.

usage: Vq = interpn(X1, X2, ..., V, Xq1, Xq2, ...)
interpn.description: Interpolates values on an N-dimensional grid made with ndgrid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline'. Points outside the grid give NaN, or extrapval.

intersect.description: Values found in both a and b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given; c = a(ia) = b(ib). The result is a row unless a is a column. Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored. Example: intersect([3 1 2], [2 3 4]) is [2 3].

intfilt.description: Interpolation FIR filter for a signal with l-1 zeros inserted between samples: the least-squares filter that uses the 2p nearest samples of a signal band-limited to alpha times Nyquist, or the filter for Lagrange polynomial interpolation of order n.

usage: x = intlinprog(f, intcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
intlinprog.description: Mixed-integer linear programming: like linprog, but the variables listed in intcon must take integer values. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. Options are ignored.

intmax.description: Largest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmax('uint8') is 255.

intmin.description: Smallest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmin('int8') is -128.

inv.description: Inverse of a square matrix, so that A*Y is the identity. A warning is printed when A is singular or nearly so, and the result is then unreliable (possibly Inf). For solving A*x = b, A\b is faster and more accurate.

invhilb.description: The exact inverse of the n-by-n Hilbert matrix hilb(n). All its entries are integers.

iopzmap.description: Pole-zero map of a model; for a SISO model the same as pzmap.

ipermute.description: Undoes permute: ipermute(permute(A, order), order) gives back A.

iqr.description: Interquartile range: the 75th minus the 25th percentile, a spread measure robust to outliers.

usage: I = iradon(R, theta, interp, filter, frequency_scaling, output_size)
iradon.description: Rebuilds an image from its projections by filtered back-projection. interp is 'linear' (default) or 'nearest'; the filter is 'Ram-Lak' (default), 'Shepp-Logan', 'Cosine', 'Hamming', 'Hann' or 'none'.

isAlways.description: True if a symbolic condition such as sin(x)^2 + cos(x)^2 == 1 holds for all values of its variables. False when it does not hold or cannot be decided.

isConfigured.description: True when the dictionary d has key and value types, which it gets from configureDictionary or from its first entry.

isConnected.description: True where the two vertices are joined by an edge of the triangulation (column vector). TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.isConnected(...).

isInterior.description: For a 2-D delaunayTriangulation with edge constraints: true for the triangles inside the region bounded by the constraints (inside and outside alternate across nested boundaries). Column vector, one element per triangle. Also DT.isInterior().

isKey.description: True when the containers.Map m has the key. With a cell array of keys, returns a logical array. The same as m.isKey(key).

isMATLABReleaseOlderThan.description: True if the MATLAB release mylab reports itself as (see version) is older than the given release, written like 'R2021b'. stage is 'release' (the default) or 'prerelease', and update an update number; mylab counts as the general release without updates.

isStringScalar.description: True if x is a string array with exactly one element.

isSymType.description: True if a symbolic value is of the given kind: 'variable', 'number', 'integer', 'rational', 'constant', 'expression', 'equation', 'function', 'plus', 'times' or 'power'.

is_function_handle.description: True if x is a function handle such as @sin or @(t) t.^2.

isa.description: True if class(x) equals classname. Also accepts the group names 'numeric' (double, single or integer), 'float' (double or single) and 'integer' (any integer class). For objects of a classdef class it is also true for any superclass, e.g. isa(dog, 'Animal').

isalnum.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a letter or a digit. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isalpha.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a letter (the same as isletter). A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isappdata.description: True when setappdata stored something under name on h.

isargout.description: True when output number k of the running function was requested by the caller. Outputs skipped with ~ are not tracked, so they count as requested. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isascii.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is an ASCII character (code below 128). A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isbanded.description: True when A has no nonzeros beyond the given lower and upper bandwidths.

isbetween.description: True where lower <= t <= upper. The bounds may be datetimes or date text. intervalType is 'closed' (default), 'open', 'openleft' or 'openright'.

iscalendarduration.description: True when x is a calendar duration array.

iscategorical.description: True when x is a categorical array.

iscategory.description: True for each name that is a category of c.

iscell.description: True if x is a cell array.

iscellstr.description: True if C is a cell array in which every cell holds a char vector (or empty char).

ischar.description: True if x is a char array, e.g. text in single quotes.

iscntrl.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a control character (code below 32, or 127). A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

iscolumn.description: True if A has exactly one column (a 0-by-1 array counts).

isct.description: True for a continuous-time model (sample time 0).

isdag.description: True if a digraph has no cycles.

isdatetime.description: True when x is a datetime array.

isdeployed.description: Always false: mylab code never runs as a compiled standalone application.

isdiag.description: True if every entry of the numeric matrix A off the main diagonal is zero.

isdictionary.description: True when x is a dictionary.

isdigit.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is one of the decimal digits 0 to 9. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isdir.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isdst.description: True for the datetimes at which daylight saving time is in effect in their time zone (false for datetimes without a time zone).

isdt.description: True for a discrete-time model (nonzero sample time). A static gain counts as both continuous and discrete.

isduration.description: True when x is a duration array.

isempty.description: True if A has no elements, i.e. at least one dimension is 0.

isenum.description: True when x is a member (or an array of members) of an enumeration class.

isequal.description: True if all inputs have the same size and contents. Numeric type is ignored, so isequal(1, int8(1)) is true. NaN is never equal to NaN; see isequaln.

isequaln.description: Like isequal, but NaN values in matching positions count as equal.

isfield.description: True if s is a struct with a field of that name; a cell array of names gives a logical array. Non-struct input gives false.

isfile.description: True if f names an existing file (not a folder).

isfinite.description: Logical array that is true where x is neither NaN nor infinite.

isfloat.description: True if x is a double or single array.

isfolder.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isglobal.description: True when the variable called name (a char vector or string) is declared global in the current workspace.

isgraph.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a printable character other than a space. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isgraphics.description: True for each element of h that is a valid (not deleted or closed) graphics handle, optionally of the given type such as 'line' or 'figure'. Figure numbers count as handles of open figures. ishandle and ishghandle are the same.

ishandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishermitian.description: True if the square matrix A equals its conjugate transpose A' ('skew': equals -A'). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

ishghandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishold.description: True if hold is on for the current axes.

ishole.description: Column vector, true for the boundaries that are holes. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.ishole(...).

isindex.description: True when v can be used as an index: a logical array, or positive whole numbers (not larger than n when it is given). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isinf.description: Logical array that is true where x is Inf or -Inf.

isinteger.description: True if x has an integer class such as int8 or uint32. A double holding a whole number is not an integer type.

isinterior.description: True for the query points that are in the filled area of p or on its boundary (column vector); TFon marks the points on a boundary. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.isinterior(...).

isjava.description: Whether x is a Java object: always false, because mylab has no Java.

iskeyword.description: True if s is a reserved word of the language such as 'for' or 'end'. With no input, returns all keywords as a column cell array.

isletter.description: True for each alphabetic character in a char array; false for non-char input.

islinear.description: True for models that are linear in their coefficients (polynomials and linear-term models). Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

islogical.description: True if x is a logical (boolean) array.

islower.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a lower-case letter. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

ismatrix.description: True if A has exactly two dimensions (any size, including empty).

ismember.description: True where an element of a is found in s; loc gives the index of the first match in s (0 when absent). Works for numbers, text and cell arrays of text. With 'rows', each row of A is looked up among the rows of B and column vectors are returned. Example: ismember([1 2; 5 6], [5 6; 0 0], 'rows') is [false; true].

ismembertol.description: Set membership within a tolerance: true where an element of A is within tol*max(abs([A(:); B(:)])) of an element of B (default tol 1e-12, 1e-6 for single).

ismethod.description: True if obj has a public method called name.

ismissing.description: True where an element is missing: <missing> in a string array, NaN in a numeric array, or an empty char vector in a cell array. Returns a logical array the size of x.

ismultigraph.description: True if some pair of nodes is joined by more than one edge.

isnan.description: Logical array that is true where x is NaN.

isnat.description: True where the elements of a datetime array are NaT.

isnumeric.description: True for double, single and integer arrays (real or complex). False for logical, char, cell, struct and string values.

isobject.description: True if x is an object: a containers.Map, a table, or an instance of a classdef class.

isocaps.description: The parts of the volume's outer faces where the data lies above the isovalue.

isonormals.description: Normals of an isosurface from the gradient of the volume data.

isordinal.description: True when the categories of c have an order (created with 'Ordinal', true).

usage: isosurface(V, isovalue) or isosurface(X, Y, Z, V, isovalue)
isosurface.description: The surface where V equals isovalue.

isoutlier.description: Marks the outliers of A along its first non-singleton dimension. The default method 'median' flags values more than 3 scaled median absolute deviations from the median; 'mean' uses 3 standard deviations from the mean and 'quartiles' 1.5 interquartile ranges outside the quartiles.

ispattern.description: True when x is a pattern object.

ispref.description: True if the preference group, or the named preference in it, exists.

isprime.description: Logical array that is true where x is a prime number.

isprint.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a printable character, including the space. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isprop.description: True if obj has a public property called name.

isproper.description: True when no channel has more zeros than poles. With 'elem' the result is a logical matrix with one entry per output/input pair.

isprotected.description: True when new categories cannot be added to the categorical array c by assigning values (it was created with 'Protected', true, or it is ordinal).

ispunct.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a punctuation character (printable, and neither a letter, a digit nor a space). A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isreal.description: False only when x is stored as a complex array; a complex array whose imaginary parts are all zero still counts as not real. True for non-numeric values.

isregular.description: True when the row times of a timetable (or a datetime or duration vector) are equally spaced; dt is the step. With timeComponent 'years', 'quarters', 'months', 'weeks' or 'days' the spacing is checked in calendar units, so month starts count as regular.

isrow.description: True if A has exactly one row (a 1-by-0 array counts).

issimplified.description: True when p is well defined: no crossing or repeated boundaries and the orientation convention (solid clockwise, holes counterclockwise) holds. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.issimplified(...).

issiso.description: True for a model with one input and one output.

issorted.description: True if the elements (or rows, with 'rows') are already in order. Other modes: 'strictascend', 'strictdescend' and 'strictmonotonic'. Works on cell arrays of text too.

issortedrows.description: True if the rows of A are in sorted order, as sortrows would leave them. direction may also be 'monotonic', 'strictascend', 'strictdescend' or 'strictmonotonic'.

isspace.description: True for each whitespace character in a char array; false for non-char input.

issparse.description: True when A is stored as a sparse matrix.

issquare.description: True if A has the same number of rows and columns.

isstable.description: True when all poles lie in the open left half-plane (continuous time) or strictly inside the unit circle (discrete time). Delays do not affect the answer.

isstatic.description: True for a model without dynamics or delays (a pure gain).

isstr.description: Old name of ischar: true if x is a char array.

isstring.description: True if x is a string scalar, e.g. text in double quotes.

isstrprop.description: Tests each character of s for a category: 'alpha', 'digit', 'alphanum', 'wspace', 'upper', 'lower', 'punct' or 'cntrl'.

isstruct.description: True if x is a struct or struct array.

issymmetric.description: True if the square matrix A equals its transpose ('skew': equals minus its transpose). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

istable.description: True if x is a table.

istext.description: True if x is either a char array or a string.

istft.description: Inverse short-time Fourier transform by weighted overlap-add. Give the same 'Window', 'OverlapLength', 'FFTLength' and 'FrequencyRange' that were used for stft. 'Method' is 'wola' (default) or 'ola'; 'ConjugateSymmetric', true returns a real signal.

istimetable.description: True when x is a timetable.

istril.description: True if every entry above the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

istriu.description: True if every entry below the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

isundefined.description: True for the elements of a categorical array that have no category.

isunix.description: True when running on a POSIX system (Linux or macOS).

isupper.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is an upper-case letter. A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

isvalid.description: True for a handle object (classdef handle class, containers.Map, ...) that has not been deleted with delete(h). For graphics handles it is false once the object has been deleted or its figure closed; for an array of graphics handles it returns one value per handle.

isvarname.description: True if s is a valid variable name: a letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 63 characters, and not a keyword.

isvector.description: True if A is 1-by-n or n-by-1 with at least one element.

isweekend.description: True for the datetimes that fall on a Saturday or Sunday.

isxdigit.description: Logical array of the size of the char array s that is true where a character is a hexadecimal digit (0-9, a-f, A-F). A cell array gives a cell array of results; a value that is not text gives false. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

iwishrnd.description: A random matrix from the inverse Wishart distribution with parameter matrix Tau and df degrees of freedom.

iztrans.description: Inverse Z-transform of a rational function F(z), as a sequence in n. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

j.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

jackknife.description: Jackknife: apply jackfun to the data with each row left out in turn; one result per row.

jacobian.description: Jacobian matrix: the derivative of each element of the vector f with respect to each variable in v. Row i, column j holds diff(f(i), v(j)).

java.*.description: Java classes cannot be used. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaArray.description: Would create a Java array. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaMethod.description: Would call a Java method. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaMethodEDT.description: Would call a Java method. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaObject.description: Would create a Java object. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaObjectEDT.description: Would create a Java object. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javaaddpath.description: Would add to the Java class path. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javachk.description: Returns a struct with a message saying that Java is not available in mylab.

javaclasspath.description: Would return the Java class path. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javarmpath.description: Would remove from the Java class path. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

javax.*.description: Java classes cannot be used. mylab runs on Python and has no Java virtual machine, so this function always stops with an error that says so. Use MATLAB-language types (string, containers.Map, cell arrays, datetime) or a Python library through py.name(...) instead.

jbtest.description: Jarque-Bera test of normality based on skewness and kurtosis. For fewer than 2000 values the null distribution is found by simulation, and p is limited to the range 0.001 to 0.5.

jet.description: n-by-3 rainbow colormap (default 256 rows) from dark blue to dark red.

join.description: Text: joins the strings in C with a delimiter (default a space) along the last dimension, or along dim. Tables: adds to each row of Tleft the variables of the row of Tright with the same key values (by default the variables with the same name); every left row must match exactly one right row, and the left row order is kept.

jsondecode.description: Converts JSON text to a value. Objects become structs, arrays of numbers become column vectors or matrices (null becomes NaN), arrays of objects with the same fields become struct arrays, other arrays become cell arrays, true/false become logical values and a lone null becomes []. Field names that are not valid identifiers are changed (other characters become _). To read a file: jsondecode(fileread('data.json')).

jsonencode.description: Converts a value to JSON text. Structs and containers.Map become objects, vectors and cell arrays become arrays, matrices become arrays of rows, tables become an array with one object per row. NaN and Inf become null unless 'ConvertInfAndNaN' is false. 'PrettyPrint' adds line breaks and two-space indentation.

juliandate.description: Julian date (days since noon on November 24, 4714 BC in the proleptic Gregorian calendar), or the modified Julian date.

kaiser.description: Kaiser window of length n as a column; larger beta (default 0.5) gives lower side lobes.

usage: [n, Wn, beta, ftype] = kaiserord(f, a, dev)
kaiserord.description: Estimates the order, cutoff frequencies and Kaiser window parameter of a window-method FIR filter. f holds the band edges, a the amplitude of each band and dev the allowed deviation in each band. Use the result as fir1(n, Wn, ftype, kaiser(n+1, beta), 'noscale'); the 'cell' form returns those arguments in a cell array.

usage: [kest, L, P] = kalman(sys, Qn, Rn, Nn)
[kest, L, P] = kalman(sys, Qn, Rn, Nn, sensors, known)
kalman.description: Kalman estimator for a state-space plant. The last inputs of sys are the process noise w (as many as Qn has rows) unless known lists the deterministic inputs; sensors lists the measured outputs. Qn, Rn and Nn are the covariances of w, of the measurement noise v and between them. kest takes [known inputs; measurements] and returns [output estimates; state estimates]. L is the estimator gain and P the error covariance; for a discrete-time plant M and Z are the innovation gain and the updated covariance, and a last argument 'current' (default) or 'delayed' chooses whether the estimate uses the newest measurement.

keyboard.description: Pauses the program at this point and opens the K>> debugger prompt, where you can inspect variables, step (n, s) or continue (c). Only works in an interactive terminal; elsewhere it does nothing.

keys.description: Returns the keys of the containers.Map m as a cell array, in sorted order.

kmeans.description: k-means clustering of the rows of X into k groups. idx gives each row's cluster number, C the cluster centres, sumd the within-cluster sums of distances and D the distance from every point to every centre. Options: 'Distance' ('sqeuclidean' default or 'cityblock'), 'Replicates' (keep the best of several runs), 'MaxIter' (default 100) and 'Start' ('plus' k-means++ default, 'sample', 'uniform' or a k-by-p matrix). Rows with NaN get idx NaN. Results are random; set rng for repeatable runs.

usage: [idx, C, sumd, D, midx, info] = kmedoids(X, k, 'Name', value, ...)
kmedoids.description: k-medoids clustering: like k-means but each centre is one of the data points (rows midx). Options: 'Distance', 'Start', 'Replicates', 'Algorithm'.

knnsearch.description: For each row of Y, the k nearest rows of X (default 1) and their distances. With 'IncludeTies' the results are cell arrays that also hold points tied with the k-th.

kron.description: Kronecker product: every element A(i,j) is replaced by the block A(i,j)*B.

kroneckerDelta.description: 1 if m equals n (or 0 when n is left out), otherwise 0.

kruskalwallis.description: Kruskal-Wallis test: a one-way analysis of variance on ranks, testing that the groups come from the same distribution.

ksdensity.description: Kernel density estimate of the sample x: f is the estimated density at the points xi (100 points covering the data by default). Options: 'Bandwidth', 'Kernel' ('normal', 'box', 'triangle', 'epanechnikov'), 'Function' ('pdf', 'cdf', 'survivor'), 'NumPoints', 'Support' ('positive'), 'Weights'.

kstest.description: One-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test against the standard normal distribution, or against a distribution object, a function handle or a two-column table [x, F(x)] given as 'CDF'. 'Tail' is 'unequal', 'larger' or 'smaller'.

kstest2.description: Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test that both samples come from the same continuous distribution (asymptotic p-value).

kurtosis.description: Sample kurtosis, a measure of how heavy the tails are; a normal distribution gives 3 (this is not the excess kurtosis). flag 0 applies the bias correction. NaN values are ignored.

lab2rgb.description: Converts L*a*b* colours to RGB. Colours outside the RGB gamut give values outside 0..1 unless 'OutputType' is 'uint8' or 'uint16'. 'WhitePoint' names the reference white ('d65' by default; also 'd50', 'd55', 'a', 'c', 'e', 'icc', 'f2', 'f7', 'f11' or [X Y Z]) and 'ColorSpace' the kind of RGB ('srgb', 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb').

lab2xyz.description: Converts L*a*b* colours to CIE XYZ for the given reference white (default 'd65').

label2rgb.description: Colours a label matrix for display: each label gets a colour from the colormap (a name such as 'jet', the default, or an N-by-3 matrix) and label 0 gets zerocolor (white by default; a letter such as 'k' or an RGB triple). 'shuffle' mixes the colour order. The result is uint8.

labelmatrix.description: Label matrix built from the struct returned by bwconncomp.

lag.description: Shifts the data of a regular timetable forward in time by n time steps (default 1) or by the duration dt, which must be a multiple of the time step. The row times stay; the rows that have no data left are filled with missing values. A negative shift moves the data back.

lambertw.description: Lambert W function: the solution w of w*exp(w) = x, on branch k (default 0).

laplace.description: Laplace transform of f(t), as a function of s. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

laplacian.description: Sum of the second derivatives of f with respect to each variable in X.

lasso.description: Lasso and elastic-net regression. Each column of B holds the coefficients for one value of FitInfo.Lambda (ascending); FitInfo.Intercept has the constant terms. Options: 'Lambda', 'Alpha' (1 = lasso), 'NumLambda', 'LambdaRatio', 'Standardize', 'Intercept', 'CV', 'DFmax', 'RelTol', 'Weights', 'PredictorNames'. With 'CV' the mean squared error is cross-validated and LambdaMinMSE and Lambda1SE are reported.

lassoglm.description: Lasso or elastic-net regularised generalized linear model ('normal', 'binomial', 'poisson', 'gamma', 'inverse gaussian'). FitInfo has Intercept, Lambda, DF and Deviance.

lasterr.description: Message (and identifier) of the most recent error. It is reliable inside a catch block; prefer 'catch err' and err.message in new code.

lasterror.description: Struct with the message, identifier and stack of the most recent error. It is reliable inside a catch block; prefer 'catch err' in new code.

lastwarn.description: Text of the most recent warning, or an empty char if there was none.

latc2tf.description: Transfer function of a lattice filter: FIR by default, all-pole with 'allpole', all-pass with 'allpass', or lattice-ladder when v is given.

latcfilt.description: Filters x with a lattice filter. f is the forward output and g the backward output; with ladder coefficients v the filter is the lattice-ladder (pole-zero) form, with v = 1 all-pole.

latex.description: LaTeX code for a symbolic expression, as text.

lcm.description: Least common multiple of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

ldivide.description: Same as A .\ B, i.e. B ./ A.

ldl.description: Block LDL factorization of a symmetric matrix: A = L*D*L' with D block diagonal (1-by-1 and 2-by-2 blocks). With three outputs L is lower triangular and P'*A*P = L*D*L'.

legend.description: Adds a legend naming the plotted items in drawing order, or only the graphics handles h. Without labels it uses each item's DisplayName, or data1, data2, ... legend off removes it, legend boxoff/boxon hides or shows its frame. Options: Location (a compass name such as 'northeast', 'southwest', 'best', or an outside position like 'eastoutside'), Orientation ('horizontal'), NumColumns, FontSize, Box, TextColor, Title. l is a Legend handle (String, Location, Box, FontSize, ...). With yyaxis, items from both sides are listed.

legendre.description: Associated Legendre functions of degree n and orders 0 to n, one order per row, at the points X in [-1, 1]. 'sch' gives the Schmidt semi-normalized functions and 'norm' the fully normalized ones.

length.description: Size of the longest dimension of A, or 0 if A is empty. Example: length(ones(3, 7)) is 7.

letterBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: a place where a letter meets a character that is not a letter. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

lettersPattern.description: A pattern that matches letters (of any alphabet). With no argument it matches one or more of them, with N exactly N, and with (min, max) between min and max (max may be Inf). Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

levinson.description: Levinson-Durbin recursion: the prediction polynomial of order n (default length(r)-1) from the autocorrelation r, with the prediction error e and the reflection coefficients k.

lft.description: Linear fractional (star) connection: the last nu inputs and ny outputs of sys1 are closed with sys2 in positive feedback. Without nu and ny all channels of the smaller model are used: sys2 closes the lower channels of sys1, or sys1 closes the upper channels of sys2.

lhs.description: Left side of a symbolic equation or inequality.

license.description: Says whether a product is available: true for 'MATLAB' and for the toolboxes mylab covers in part ('image_toolbox', 'signal_toolbox', 'statistics_toolbox', 'optimization_toolbox'), false for everything else. mylab itself is free software under the MIT licence.

light.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. An output, if requested, is [].

lightangle.description: lightangle(az, el) adds a light shining from that direction; lightangle(h, az, el) moves one.

lighting.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. Surfaces keep their flat colormap shading.

lillietest.description: Lilliefors test that the data come from a normal ('normal', default), 'exponential' or 'extreme value' family with estimated parameters. p is limited to the range 0.001 to 0.5 unless 'MCTol' asks for a simulated value.

limit.description: Limit of a symbolic expression as x approaches a (0 when a is left out). 'left' and 'right' give one-sided limits. When the two sides differ the two-sided limit is NaN. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

line.description: Draws a line in the current axes without clearing it, whatever the hold state. A matrix draws one line per column. Accepts the same Name/Value options as plot.

lineBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: the start or the end of a line. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

linearSystemAnalyzer.description: Response viewer app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

usage: [A, B, C, D] = linearize(model, x0, u0)
linearize.description: The same as linmod: the matrices A, B, C, D of the model around an operating point.

lines.description: n-by-3 matrix repeating the default line colour order (default 7 rows).

linkage.description: Agglomerative hierarchical cluster tree from data X or from a distance vector y. method is 'single' (default), 'complete', 'average', 'weighted', 'centroid', 'median' or 'ward'. Each row of Z joins two clusters (new clusters are numbered after the observations) at the height in column 3.

linkaxes.description: Gives the listed axes the same x and/or y limits (the range covering all of them) and keeps them in step when one of them changes. 'off' is accepted but does not unlink.

linkdata.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

linkprop.description: Keeps the named properties of the graphics objects equal: all start from the values of the first object, and setting the property on one sets it on the others. addtarget and removetarget change the linked objects; set Enabled to 'off' to pause the link.

usage: [A, B, C, D] = linmod(model, x0, u0)
linmod.description: Linearizes a model around an operating point: dx/dt = A x + B u, y = C x + D u. The inputs u are the top-level In blocks, the outputs y the top-level Out blocks, and x the continuous states in the order of the blocks. The matrices are computed by central differences at the states x0 (default: the initial values) and inputs u0 (default: zero). Discrete states are held at their initial values. With one output the result is a struct with the fields a, b, c, d and StateName.

usage: [A, B, C, D] = linmod2(model, x0, u0)
linmod2.description: The same as linmod (both use central differences).

usage: x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq)
x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
linprog.description: Linear programming: minimizes f'*x subject to A*x <= b, Aeq*x = beq and lb <= x <= ub, using the HiGHS solver. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. exitflag is 1 when solved, 0 at the iteration limit, -2 when infeasible and -3 when unbounded (then x is []). An options argument is ignored.

linsolve.description: Solves the linear system A*x = b, the same as A\b. An options struct is not supported.

linspace.description: Row vector of n points evenly spaced from a to b, both ends included. n defaults to 100. Example: linspace(0, 1, 5) is [0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1].

listLength.description: How many values the indexing operations indexOp produce when applied to obj. Used inside the parenListLength, dotListLength and braceListLength methods of classes derived from matlab.mixin.indexing.RedefinesParen, RedefinesDot or RedefinesBrace, to pass the question on to a contained value.

listdlg.description: Lets the user choose from a numbered list and returns the chosen item numbers and ok = 1, or [] and ok = 0 after a cancel. The default selection is InitialValue (item 1). In a terminal or notebook the question is asked as text; when nobody can answer (for example in a batch run) the default is used and a note is printed.

listener.description: Like addlistener: calls callback(source, eventData) when obj fires the event. Keep L; delete(L) stops listening.

load.description: Loads variables from a MAT-file into the workspace, or returns them as the fields of a struct. Names (with * and ? wildcards) or -regexp patterns select variables; asking for a name that is not in the file gives a warning. Files of versions 4, 5, 6 and 7 written by MATLAB or Octave are read directly, including big-endian files, objects, function handles and MATLAB string arrays, and so are version 7.3 (HDF5) files, with h5py; objects that MATLAB itself wrote into a version 7.3 file are not read (each loads as an empty array, with a warning). Variables saved as global become global again. An object is rebuilt from the default values of its class (the constructor runs only for a class with ConstructOnLoad); each saved property value then goes through the property's validation and set method, and loadobj runs last when the class defines it. A saved property the class no longer has is dropped; if the class has loadobj, it receives the saved values as a struct instead. When the class is not on the path, the object is loaded as a struct of its saved properties, with a warning. A file that is not a MAT-file (or any file with -ascii) is read as rows of numbers separated by spaces, commas or tabs, with % comments, into one matrix named after the file. .mat is added to a name without extension, and the file is also looked for on the search path.

load_system.description: Loads a model file into memory without showing it. Models are also loaded automatically the first time their name is used, so sim('mymodel') works when mymodel.mlb.json is in the current folder. A .slx file is converted on loading; blocks that have no equivalent are listed in a warning.

localfunctions.description: Returns a cell column of handles to the local functions of the file that calls it (the main function of a function file is not included). Typical use: tests = functiontests(localfunctions).

log.description: Natural logarithm of each element. log(0) is -Inf and negative inputs give complex results.

log10.description: Base-10 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results.
