log1p.description: log(1 + x) computed accurately when x is tiny. Inputs below -1 give NaN.

log2.description: Base-2 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results. The two-output form [f, e] = log2(x) is not supported.

logical.description: Converts to logical: nonzero becomes true, zero becomes false. NaN input is an error.

loglog.description: Like plot, but with logarithmic x and y axes.

logm.description: Matrix logarithm, the inverse of expm. May be complex.

logncdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the lognormal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma of the logarithm (defaults 0 and 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

lognfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [mu, sigma] of the logarithm of the lognormal distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05). censoring marks right-censored observations with 1 and freq gives the count of each observation.

logninv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the lognormal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma of the logarithm (defaults 0 and 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

lognlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the lognormal distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

lognpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the lognormal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma of the logarithm (defaults 0 and 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

lognrnd.description: Random numbers from the lognormal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma of the logarithm (defaults 0 and 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

lognstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the lognormal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma of the logarithm (defaults 0 and 1).

logspace.description: Row vector of n points spaced evenly on a log scale from 10^a to 10^b. n defaults to 50. Example: logspace(0, 2, 3) is [1 10 100].

lookAheadBoundary.description: A pattern that matches the position in front of a match of p without taking the characters of p. Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

lookBehindBoundary.description: A pattern that matches the position right after a match of p without taking its characters. p may have a variable length within limits (a repetition counts up to 16 extra characters). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

lookup.description: The values of the given keys in the dictionary d. With 'FallbackValue' a key that is not in the dictionary gives that value instead of an error.

lower.description: Converts text to lower case, character by character, so the length never changes. Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cells.

lowpass.description: Filters x with a lowpass filter whose passband ends at wpass (a fraction of Nyquist, or Hz with fs) and removes the filter delay. 'Steepness' (0.5 to 1, default 0.85) sets how narrow the transition band is, 'StopbandAttenuation' (default 60 dB) how far the stopband is pushed down and 'ImpulseResponse' ('auto', 'fir' or 'iir') the kind of filter. d is the digitalFilter that was used. Columns of a matrix are filtered separately.

usage: [At, Bt, Ct, Dt] = lp2bp(A, B, C, D, Wo, Bw)
lp2bp.description: Turns an analog lowpass prototype into a bandpass filter centred on Wo with bandwidth Bw (rad/s). The order doubles.

usage: [At, Bt, Ct, Dt] = lp2bs(A, B, C, D, Wo, Bw)
lp2bs.description: Turns an analog lowpass prototype into a bandstop filter centred on Wo with bandwidth Bw (rad/s). The order doubles.

usage: [At, Bt, Ct, Dt] = lp2hp(A, B, C, D, Wo)
lp2hp.description: Turns an analog lowpass prototype into a highpass filter with cutoff Wo rad/s.

usage: [At, Bt, Ct, Dt] = lp2lp(A, B, C, D, Wo)
lp2lp.description: Moves the cutoff of an analog lowpass prototype (cutoff 1 rad/s) to Wo rad/s.

lpc.description: Linear prediction coefficients of order p (default length(x)-1) from the autocorrelation of x; g is the variance of the prediction error.

usage: L = lqe(A, G, C, Q, R)
L = lqe(A, G, C, Q, R, N)
lqe.description: Kalman estimator gain for dx/dt = A*x + B*u + G*w, y = C*x + v with process-noise covariance Q, measurement-noise covariance R and cross-covariance N. P is the error covariance and E the estimator poles of A - L*C.

lqg.description: Linear-quadratic-Gaussian regulator. QXU weights [x; u] in the cost and QWV is the covariance of [w; v] for dx/dt = A*x + B*u + w, y = C*x + D*u + v. The result maps y to u and is connected with positive feedback: feedback(sys, rsys, +1). Options for integral action or two degrees of freedom are not supported.

lqgreg.description: Regulator formed from a Kalman estimator (from kalman) and a state-feedback gain: u = -K*xhat. The result maps the measurements to the controls, for positive feedback.

lqi.description: Linear-quadratic regulator with integral action. The state is extended with the integral xi of r - y, and K = [Kx, Ki] is used as u = -K*[x; xi]. Q weights the extended state, so it has one row per state plus one per output.

usage: K = lqr(A, B, Q, R, N)
lqr.description: Linear-quadratic regulator: the state feedback u = -K*x that minimizes the integral of x'*Q*x + u'*R*u + 2*x'*N*u. S is the Riccati solution and P the closed-loop poles of A - B*K. R must be positive definite and (A, B) stabilizable. For a discrete-time model the discrete problem is solved. A model can be given instead of A and B, as in lqr(sys, Q, R).

usage: K = lqrd(A, B, Q, R, Ts)
K = lqrd(A, B, Q, R, N, Ts)
lqrd.description: Discrete regulator for a continuous plant: the gain for u[k] = -K*x[k] with a zero-order hold that minimizes the continuous-time cost of lqr. The plant and the cost are both discretized exactly.

lqry.description: Linear-quadratic regulator with a weight on the outputs: minimizes y'*Q*y + u'*R*u + 2*y'*N*u.

ls.description: Lists the files in a folder, or those matching a wildcard pattern. With an output the names are returned as the rows of a char matrix, padded with spaces (on every platform).

lscov.description: Least squares with known weights or covariance. w is a vector of weights, one per row; V is the covariance matrix of the errors in b. Also returns the standard errors of x, the mean squared error and the covariance matrix of x. alg is 'chol' (default) or 'orth' (for a semidefinite V).

usage: [y, t, x] = lsim(sys, u, t, x0)
lsim.description: Response to an arbitrary input. u has one row per time sample and one column per input, and t is evenly spaced (it can be left out for a discrete-time model). x0 is the initial state of a state-space model. Between samples the input of a continuous-time model is held constant ('zoh') or joined by straight lines ('foh'); by default 'foh' is used unless the signal is mostly flat with jumps, like a step or a square wave. The state is advanced exactly for that input, so the result does not depend on an integration tolerance. Without outputs the response is plotted over the input.

lsiminfo.description: Characteristics of a response given as data: TransientTime, SettlingTime, Min, MinTime, Max and MaxTime. yfinal defaults to the last sample and the settling band is 2 % unless ST says otherwise.

lsimplot.description: Plots a simulated response; same arguments as lsim.

usage: x = lsqcurvefit(fun, x0, xdata, ydata, lb, ub)
lsqcurvefit.description: Nonlinear curve fitting by least squares: finds parameters x so that fun(x, xdata) matches ydata as closely as possible, starting from x0. Uses Levenberg-Marquardt, or a trust-region method when bounds are given. Options StepTolerance (TolX) and FunctionTolerance (TolFun) are read. Example: lsqcurvefit(@(p, t) p(1)*exp(p(2)*t), [1 -1], t, y).

usage: [x, resnorm, residual, exitflag, output, lambda] = lsqlin(C, d, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, x0, options)
lsqlin.description: Solve a linear least-squares problem, minimising norm(C*x - d)^2, with linear inequality and equality constraints and bounds.

lsqminnorm.description: Least-squares solution of A*x = b that has the smallest norm when the solution is not unique (rank-deficient or underdetermined A). tol is the rank tolerance; 'warn' prints a warning when A is rank deficient.

usage: x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
lsqnonlin.description: Nonlinear least squares: minimizes the sum of squares of the residual vector returned by fun(x), starting from x0, optionally within bounds. Methods and options as in lsqcurvefit.

lsqnonneg.description: Non-negative least squares: minimizes norm(C*x - d) subject to x >= 0. resnorm is the squared residual norm.

lsqr.description: Least-squares solution of A*x = b for a rectangular or square matrix, by an iterative method that only needs products with A and A'. tol defaults to 1e-6.

ltiview.description: Response viewer app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

lu.description: LU factorization with partial pivoting. With three outputs, P*A = L*U where L is unit lower triangular. With two outputs, L already includes the row permutation, so A = L*U.

lyap.description: Solves the continuous Lyapunov equation A*X + X*A' + Q = 0, the Sylvester equation A*X + X*B + C = 0, or the generalized equation A*X*E' + E*X*A' + Q = 0. A unique solution needs that no eigenvalue of A is the negative of another (for example a stable A).

lyapchol.description: Cholesky factor R of the solution X = R'*R of A*X + X*A' + B*B' = 0 for a stable A.

mad.description: Mean absolute deviation from the mean (flag 0, default) or median absolute deviation from the median (flag 1). NaN values are ignored.

mag2db.description: Converts amplitude ratio to decibels: 20*log10(m). Negative values give NaN.

magic.description: n-by-n magic square: every row, column and both main diagonals add up to the same value, n*(n^2+1)/2. Each integer 1..n^2 appears once. magic(2) is returned as [4 3; 1 2] even though no true 2-by-2 magic square exists.

mahal.description: Squared Mahalanobis distance of each row of Y from the sample X.

makedist.description: Create a probability distribution object, for example makedist('Normal', 'mu', 1, 'sigma', 2) or makedist('Weibull', 'A', 2, 'B', 3). The parameters are properties of the object (pd.mu). Use it with pdf, cdf, icdf, random, mean, std, var, median, iqr and truncate. Without inputs it lists the distribution names.

usage: M = makehgtform('translate', [tx ty tz], 'scale', s, 'xrotate', t, ...)

makelut.description: Lookup table for applylut: fun is called with every possible n-by-n (n = 2 or 3) binary neighbourhood and its results are stored.

maketform.description: Older form of a transformation: a struct for imtransform, tformfwd and tforminv. A is used as [x y 1] = [u v 1] * A, or the transformation is found from three (affine) or four (projective) points U and their images X.

makima.description: Modified Akima piecewise cubic interpolation, which avoids most overshoot without flattening the curve as much as pchip. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial.

usage: [Gm, Pm, Wcg, Wcp] = margin(mag, phase, w)
margin.description: Gain and phase margins of the open loop sys. Gm is the factor by which the gain can grow before the closed loop becomes unstable (absolute, not dB) and Wcg the frequency where the phase is -180 degrees; Pm is the phase margin in degrees and Wcp the frequency where the gain is 1. When several crossovers exist the smallest margins are reported; Inf and NaN mean there is no crossover. For rational models the crossovers are roots of polynomials, so the values are exact up to rounding. Without outputs a Bode diagram with the margins in its title is drawn. With mag, phase (degrees) and w the margins are interpolated from data.

mat2cell.description: Cuts a 2-D array into blocks and returns them in a cell array. r lists the block heights and c the block widths; they must add up to the size of A (c defaults to all columns). Example: mat2cell(magic(4), [2 2], [3 1]) gives a 2-by-2 cell.

mat2gray.description: Rescales a matrix to a double image between 0 and 1: low maps to 0 and high to 1, with values outside clipped. Without limits the smallest and largest elements are used.

mat2str.description: Text that rebuilds the matrix A when evaluated, with n significant digits (15 by default). With 'class' the text is wrapped in the class name, e.g. int8([1 2 3]). An empty array is written as zeros(m,n).

matches.description: True for each element of str (a string array, char vector or cell array of char vectors) that matches pat as a whole. pat is text, a list of texts (any one may match) or a pattern.

material.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

matfile.description: Gives access to the variables of a MAT-file as if they were properties of m. Reading m.name loads that variable only; indexing such as m.x(2, :) returns part of it. Assigning m.name = value, or to part of a variable, writes the file at once (the file must have been opened with 'Writable', true, which is the default only for a file that does not exist yet). who(m), whos(m) and size(m, 'name') describe what is stored, and m.Properties holds Source and Writable. In a version 7.3 (HDF5) file, indexing a numeric, char or logical variable reads only the selected elements, and assigning to part of one writes only that part, as long as the variable keeps its size and class; size(m, 'name') and whos(m) read no data. Indices can be scalars, ranges such as a:b and a:step:b, colons and 'end'. Other variables, and every variable of an older version of file, are read as a whole. All MAT-file versions that load reads are accepted; like MATLAB, matfile creates a version 7.3 file when the file does not exist yet.

matlab.automation.Verbosity.Concise.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.automation.Verbosity.Detailed.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.automation.Verbosity.None.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.automation.Verbosity.Terse.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.automation.Verbosity.Verbose.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.indexing.IndexingOperationType.Br.description: The Type of one level of an indexing operation handed to parenReference, dotReference or braceReference (classes derived from matlab.mixin.indexing.RedefinesParen and friends): Paren for (), Dot for .name and Brace for {}. Compare with ==.

matlab.indexing.IndexingOperationType.Do.description: The Type of one level of an indexing operation handed to parenReference, dotReference or braceReference (classes derived from matlab.mixin.indexing.RedefinesParen and friends): Paren for (), Dot for .name and Brace for {}. Compare with ==.

matlab.indexing.IndexingOperationType.Pa.description: The Type of one level of an indexing operation handed to parenReference, dotReference or braceReference (classes derived from matlab.mixin.indexing.RedefinesParen and friends): Paren for (), Dot for .name and Brace for {}. Compare with ==.

matlab.lang.makeUniqueStrings.description: Makes the texts in S different from each other, and from those in excluded, by appending _1, _2 and so on to later duplicates. A logical or index vector instead of excluded says which elements may be changed. maxlength limits the length of the results (63 by default).

matlab.lang.makeValidName.description: Turns text into valid variable names. A letter that follows white space becomes a capital and the white space is removed; other invalid characters become underscores ('underscore', the default), are removed ('delete') or are written as their hexadecimal code ('hex'); a name that does not start with a letter, and a keyword, gets the prefix 'x' (or p). Names are cut to 63 characters. S is a character vector, a string array or a cell array; modified tells which names changed. Example: matlab.lang.makeValidName('1 bad name') is 'x1BadName'.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.convertDimens.description: The size of obj as text such as '2×3', for custom headers of object arrays. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.displayProper.description: Prints the property groups (matlab.mixin.util.PropertyGroup objects) of obj the way the standard display does. Use it in a displayScalarObject method that prints its own header.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getClassNameF.description: The class name of obj as text, for use in a custom header. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getDeletedHan.description: The words 'handle to deleted', for the header of a deleted handle object. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getDetailedFo.description: The standard footer of an object display, which is empty text. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getDetailedHe.description: The standard header of an object display (in mylab the same text as getSimpleHeader). Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getHandleText.description: The word 'handle', for custom headers. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getSimpleFoot.description: The standard footer of an object display, which is empty text. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay.getSimpleHead.description: The standard first line of an object display, such as 'Name with properties:'. Part of the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Call it from a getHeader or getFooter method that you write yourself.

matlab.mixin.util.IndexingContext.Assign.description: One of the values a numArgumentsFromSubscript method receives as its third input. It says where the indexing expression is used: Statement (on its own line), Expression (inside a larger expression or a function call) or Assignment (on the left of =). Compare with ==.

matlab.mixin.util.IndexingContext.Expres.description: One of the values a numArgumentsFromSubscript method receives as its third input. It says where the indexing expression is used: Statement (on its own line), Expression (inside a larger expression or a function call) or Assignment (on the left of =). Compare with ==.

matlab.mixin.util.IndexingContext.Statem.description: One of the values a numArgumentsFromSubscript method receives as its third input. It says where the indexing expression is used: Statement (on its own line), Expression (inside a larger expression or a function call) or Assignment (on the left of =). Compare with ==.

matlab.mixin.util.IndexingContext.Unknow.description: One of the values a numArgumentsFromSubscript method receives as its third input. It says where the indexing expression is used: Statement (on its own line), Expression (inside a larger expression or a function call) or Assignment (on the left of =). Compare with ==.

matlab.mixin.util.PropertyGroup.description: A group of properties for the display of a class derived from matlab.mixin.CustomDisplay. Return one or more groups from a getPropertyGroups method: a cell array of property names shows those properties of the object; a struct shows its own field names and values instead. The optional title is printed above the group.

matlab.unittest.TestCase.forInteractiveU.description: A test case to try qualifications at the prompt: each verify, assert or assume call prints whether it passed, with diagnostics when it failed.

matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withDefaultPl.description: A test runner with the standard text output, the same as TestRunner.withTextOutput.

matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withNoPlugins.description: A silent test runner: results = run(runner, suite) prints nothing and only returns the results.

matlab.unittest.TestRunner.withTextOutpu.description: A test runner that prints progress and failure diagnostics. Run a suite with results = run(runner, suite) or results = runner.run(suite). 'LoggingLevel' sets which logged messages are shown.

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromClass.description: The Test methods of a test class as a suite (one element per method and parameter combination).

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromFile.description: The tests of one test file as a suite. Selection arguments as for selectIf may follow.

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromFolder.description: The tests of every test file in a folder as a suite: test classes, function-based test files, and scripts whose names start or end with 'test'.

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromMethod.description: The tests that one Test method of a test class produces.

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromName.description: The test with the given full name, or the tests of a cell array of names.

matlab.unittest.TestSuite.fromPackage.description: The tests of the test classes and test files inside a package (+name folder).

matlab.unittest.Verbosity.Concise.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.unittest.Verbosity.Detailed.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.unittest.Verbosity.None.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.unittest.Verbosity.Terse.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.unittest.Verbosity.Verbose.description: Verbosity levels for test output and logged messages, from least to most detail: None (0), Terse (1), Concise (2), Detailed (3), Verbose (4). Used with log(testCase, level, message), runtests(..., 'OutputDetail', level) and runtests(..., 'LoggingLevel', level).

matlab.unittest.constraints.AbsoluteTole.description: A tolerance for IsEqualTo: numbers are equal when abs(actual - expected) <= tol. Use as IsEqualTo(expected, 'Within', AbsoluteTolerance(1e-6)). Combine with RelativeTolerance using | (either may hold) or & (both).

matlab.unittest.constraints.ContainsSubs.description: Satisfied when the value is text that contains the given text. Options: 'IgnoringCase', 'IgnoringWhitespace'. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, ContainsSubstring(text)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.EndsWithSubs.description: Satisfied when the value is text that ends with the given text. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, EndsWithSubstring(text)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasElementCo.description: Satisfied when numel(value) equals n. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasElementCount(n)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasField.description: Satisfied when the value is a struct with that field. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasField(name)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasInf.description: Satisfied when the value contains Inf or -Inf. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasInf). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasLength.description: Satisfied when length(value) equals n. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasLength(n)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasNaN.description: Satisfied when the value contains at least one NaN. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasNaN). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.HasSize.description: Satisfied when size(value) equals sz. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, HasSize(sz)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsAnything.description: Satisfied by every value. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsAnything). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsEmpty.description: Satisfied when the value has no elements. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsEmpty). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsEqualTo.description: Satisfied when the value equals expected in class, size and content (NaN equals NaN; cells and structs are compared element by element). Options: 'Within' with a tolerance, 'IgnoringCase', 'IgnoringWhitespace' and 'IgnoringFields'. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsEqualTo(expected)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsFalse.description: Satisfied by the logical scalar false only. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsFalse). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsFile.description: Satisfied when the value is the name of an existing file. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsFile). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsFinite.description: Satisfied when every element is finite. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsFinite). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsFolder.description: Satisfied when the value is the name of an existing folder. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsFolder). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsGreaterTha.description: Satisfied when every element of the value is greater than bound. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsGreaterThan(bound)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

Satisfied when every element of the value is at least bound. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo(bound)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsInstanceOf.description: Satisfied when isa(value, className) is true (subclasses and categories such as 'numeric' count). Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsInstanceOf(className)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsLessThan.description: Satisfied when every element of the value is less than bound. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsLessThan(bound)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsLessThanOr.description: Satisfied when every element of the value is at most bound. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsLessThanOrEqualTo(bound)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsOfClass.description: Satisfied when the class of the value is exactly className. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsOfClass(className)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsReal.description: Satisfied when the value is a real (not complex) array. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsReal). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSameHandle.description: Satisfied when the value is the very same handle object as h. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSameHandleAs(h)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSameSetAs.description: Satisfied when the value and set hold the same elements, in any order. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSameSetAs(set)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsScalar.description: Satisfied when the value has exactly one element. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsScalar). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSparse.description: Satisfied when the value is a sparse matrix. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSparse). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSubsetOf.description: Satisfied when every element of the value is also an element of set. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSubsetOf(set)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSubstringO.description: Satisfied when the value is text found inside the given text. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSubstringOf(text)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsSupersetOf.description: Satisfied when every element of set is also an element of the value. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsSupersetOf(set)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IsTrue.description: Satisfied by the logical scalar true only. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IsTrue). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IssuesNoWarn.description: Satisfied when the value is a function handle that runs without issuing a warning. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IssuesNoWarnings). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.IssuesWarnin.description: Satisfied when the value is a function handle that issues every listed warning identifier. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, IssuesWarnings({'id1', 'id2'})). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.Matches.description: Satisfied when the value is text matched by the regular expression. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, Matches(expression)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.RelativeTole.description: A tolerance for IsEqualTo: numbers are equal when abs(actual - expected) <= tol * abs(expected). Use as IsEqualTo(expected, 'Within', RelativeTolerance(0.01)).

matlab.unittest.constraints.StartsWithSu.description: Satisfied when the value is text that starts with the given text. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, StartsWithSubstring(text)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.constraints.Throws.description: Satisfied when the value is a function handle that, called with no inputs, raises an error with that identifier. Use it with verifyThat, assertThat, assumeThat or fatalAssertThat: testCase.verifyThat(actual, Throws(identifier)). Constraints combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.diagnostics.DisplayDiagn.description: A test diagnostic that shows a value the way disp does when the qualification fails.

matlab.unittest.diagnostics.FunctionHand.description: A test diagnostic that runs a function when the qualification fails and shows what it prints.

matlab.unittest.diagnostics.StringDiagno.description: A test diagnostic made of text, shown when the qualification it is passed to fails. Passing the text itself as the last argument of verifyEqual and friends does the same.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.CurrentFolderFi.description: Changes the current folder to folder and changes back afterwards. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.EnvironmentVari.description: Sets an environment variable and restores its previous value afterwards. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.PathFixture.description: Adds a folder (or a cell array of folders) to the search path and restores the previous path afterwards. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.SuppressedWarni.description: Turns off the display of the given warning identifiers and restores the previous settings afterwards. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.TemporaryFolder.description: Creates a new empty temporary folder, named by f.Folder, and deletes it with everything in it afterwards. Options: 'WithSuffix', text; 'PreservingOnFailure', true keeps the folder. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.fixtures.WorkingFolderFi.description: Creates a temporary folder (f.Folder) and makes it the current folder; afterwards the previous current folder is restored and the temporary one deleted. Apply it with f = testCase.applyFixture(...); it is undone automatically when the test (or, in a TestClassSetup method, the test class) finishes.

matlab.unittest.plugins.DiagnosticsOutpu.description: A runner plugin that prints the diagnostics of failed tests. Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.plugins.FailureDiagnosti.description: A runner plugin that prints the diagnostics of failed tests. Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.plugins.LoggingPlugin.wi.description: A runner plugin that shows messages logged with log(testCase, ...) up to the given verbosity level. Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.plugins.StopOnFailuresPl.description: A runner plugin that ends the run after the first test file or class with a failure (mylab does not open a debugger). Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.plugins.TestRunProgressP.description: A runner plugin that prints progress at the given verbosity level (0 to 4). Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.plugins.XMLPlugin.produc.description: A runner plugin that writes the results to an XML file in JUnit format, as continuous-integration systems read it. Add it to a runner with addPlugin(runner, plugin) before calling run(runner, suite).

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasBaseFolder.description: Selects tests whose file lies in the given folder. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasBaseFolder(folder)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasName.description: Selects tests by full name, such as 'MyTest/testA'. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasName(name)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasParameter.description: Selects parameterized tests by parameter property, value name and value (each option is optional). Use it with selectIf(suite, selector).

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasParameterNa.description: Selects parameterized tests that use a parameter value with that name. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasParameterName(name)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasParameterPr.description: Selects parameterized tests that use the given TestParameter property. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasParameterProperty(name)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasProcedureNa.description: Selects tests by the name of the test function or method. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasProcedureName(name)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasSuperclass.description: Selects tests of classes derived from the given class. Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasSuperclass(className)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlab.unittest.selectors.HasTag.description: Selects tests that carry the tag (the TestTags attribute). Use it with selectIf: suite = selectIf(suite, HasTag(tag)). Text may contain * and ? as wildcards, or be a text constraint such as ContainsSubstring('abc'). Selectors combine with &, | and ~.

matlabFunction.description: Converts a symbolic expression into a function handle that works on numeric arrays. The inputs are the variables in alphabetical order, or the order given by 'Vars'. Writing a file is not supported.

matlabpool.description: Accepted for old code and does nothing; the pool size is 0.

max.description: Largest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first maximum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN; complex values are compared by magnitude. max(A, B) takes the larger of A and B element by element. Example: [m, i] = max([3 9 2]) gives m = 9, i = 2.

maxNumCompThreads.description: The number of computational threads: by default the number of processor cores. Setting a number returns the previous value. mylab records the setting; the threads NumPy uses for linear algebra are chosen by its own libraries.

usage: [mf, GF, cs, ct] = maxflow(G, s, t)
maxflow.description: Maximum flow from s to t, with the edge weights as capacities (1 without weights). GF is a digraph of the edges that carry flow; cs and ct are the two sides of a minimum cut. algorithm is 'searchtrees', 'augmentpath' or 'pushrelabel'.

maxk.description: The k largest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), largest first. NaN values come last. I gives their indices. Example: maxk([3 9 4 7], 2) is [9 7].

mdscale.description: Multidimensional scaling in p dimensions. 'Criterion' is 'stress' (non-metric, default), 'sstress', 'metricstress', 'metricsstress', 'sammon' or 'strain'. Other options: 'Start', 'Replicates', 'Weights'.

mean.description: Arithmetic average, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. 'omitnan' ignores NaN values. The result is double, also for integer input; mean([]) is NaN. Example: mean([1 2; 3 4]) is [2 3].

mean2.description: Mean of all elements of an array, as double.

meanfreq.description: Mean frequency of the power spectrum: the power-weighted average frequency.

medfilt1.description: One-dimensional median filter of order n (default 3): each output is the median of a window around the sample, which removes spikes while keeping edges. padding is 'zeropad' (default) or 'truncate'; 'omitnan' ignores NaN.

medfilt2.description: Median filter: each pixel becomes the median of its m-by-n neighbourhood (3-by-3 by default), which removes salt-and-pepper noise. Outside the image is 0 unless 'symmetric' mirrors the border. Colour images are filtered one channel at a time.

medfreq.description: Median frequency: the frequency that splits the power of the spectrum into two equal halves.

median.description: Middle value after sorting (the average of the two middle values for an even count), along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. Any NaN makes the result NaN unless 'omitnan' is given.

memmapfile.description: Maps a file into memory, so that its bytes are read and changed like an array. With a type name ('uint8' by default, any integer class, 'single' or 'double') m.Data is a column vector of the whole file. With a cell array, each row {type, [rows cols], name} describes one field of a record and m.Data is a struct array with one element per record. Offset skips bytes at the start, Repeat limits the number of elements or records (Inf: as many as fit), and Writable true lets assignments to m.Data, or to parts of it, change the file. The properties Filename, Format, Offset, Repeat and Writable can be changed later. Values are stored in the byte order of the machine.

memoize.description: Returns a version of the function that remembers its results: a call with the same inputs (and the same number of outputs) returns the stored outputs without running the function again. CacheSize (10 by default) is the number of input combinations kept; when it is full the one used longest ago is dropped. Enabled false calls the function every time. clearCache empties the cache, and stats(m) reports its contents and hit counts (Cache, MostHitCachedInput, CacheHitRatePercent, CacheOccupancyPercent). Memoizing the same named function twice gives the same object. Only memoize functions without side effects.

memory.description: Rough memory figures: user has MaxPossibleArrayBytes, MemAvailableAllArrays and MemUsedMATLAB; sys.PhysicalMemory has Available and Total. Values are 0 where the platform does not report them.

menu.description: Shows numbered choices and returns the number picked, or 0 if no valid choice was made. When nobody can answer, the first choice is used.

merge.description: Chooses between two values. With a logical scalar mask the result is tval when it is true and fval otherwise (the values can be of any type). With a logical array mask the result takes elements of tval where mask is true and of fval elsewhere; each value is a scalar or has the size of mask. ifelse is another name for the same function. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

mergecats.description: Combines several categories into one, named newname (or the first of oldnames).

mergevars.description: Combines several variables of a table into one variable with several columns (or into a nested table). The new variable takes the place of the first merged one and is called VarN (N is that position) unless a name is given.

mesh.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshc.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshgrid.description: Builds grid coordinates from vectors: each row of X is a copy of x and each column of Y is a copy of y, so X and Y are numel(y)-by-numel(x). Handy for evaluating a function of two variables over a grid. With three vectors it builds 3-D grids.

meshz.description: A mesh with a curtain around it down to the lowest value.

message.description: Creates a message object from a message identifier such as 'MyPkg:myId'. mylab has no message catalog, so getString(msg) returns the identifier followed by the arguments. error(message(id)) raises an error with that identifier.

meta.class.fromName.description: The meta.class object of the class called name, the same as ?name but with the name given as text. Returns an empty meta.class array when there is no such class.

meta.package.fromName.description: Describes the package name (a +name folder on the path): Name, ClassList, FunctionList, PackageList and ContainingPackage. Empty when the package does not exist.

metaclass.description: Returns the meta.class object that describes the class of obj. Its properties include Name, Abstract, Sealed, Enumeration, HandleCompatible, ContainingPackage, PropertyList (meta.property objects with Name, GetAccess, SetAccess, Dependent, Constant, Hidden, Transient, HasDefault, DefaultValue, DefiningClass, ...), MethodList (Name, Access, Static, Abstract, Sealed, Hidden, InputNames, OutputNames), EventList, EnumerationMemberList and SuperclassList. The same object is written ?ClassName. Meta classes compare with == and with < and > (is a subclass of / superclass of).

methods.description: Lists the public methods of an object or class; with an output, returns them as a cell column.

mex.description: Compiles C or C++ source files into a MEX file, a function written in C that mylab calls like a .m function. The system compiler does the work (cc, gcc or clang; $CC and $CXX override it), and the result is written to the current folder (or -outdir) with the extension mexext returns. The sources include mylab's own mex.h, which provides the usual mx and mex functions; nothing links to MATLAB. Options: -output name, -outdir dir, -I, -L, -l, -D and -U as for a C compiler, -O (optimise, the default), -g (debug build, turns on mxAssert), -v (show the commands), -n (only show them), -silent, -R2018a (interleaved complex data for mxGetData) and CFLAGS=, CXXFLAGS=, LDFLAGS= to replace the default flags. Building replaces a loaded copy of the same MEX file. MEX files compiled for MATLAB cannot be loaded and must be rebuilt from source with this command; MEX files do not work in the browser version of mylab. See docs/MEX.md.

mexext.description: The file extension of MEX files on this computer, without the dot: 'mexa64' on Linux, 'mexmaci64' or 'mexmaca64' on macOS (Intel or Apple silicon) and 'mexw64' on Windows. mexext('all') returns a struct array with the arch and ext of each platform.

mfilename.description: Name of the .m file that is currently running, without folder or extension. 'fullpath' adds the folder, 'fullpathext' the folder and extension. Empty when called from the prompt.

midcross.description: Times at which a two-level waveform crosses the level halfway between its two states.

milliseconds.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many milliseconds. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of milliseconds.

min.description: Smallest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first minimum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN. min(A, B) takes the smaller of A and B element by element.

mink.description: The k smallest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), smallest first. NaN values come last. Example: mink([3 9 4 7], 2) is [3 4].

minreal.description: Minimal realization. For a state-space model the states that cannot be reached from the inputs or seen at the outputs are removed (and the number removed is printed); for a transfer function or zero-pole-gain model every zero that coincides with a pole within tol (default about 1.5e-8, relative) is cancelled with it.

usage: x = minres(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
minres.description: Solves A*x = b for a symmetric (possibly indefinite) A with the minimum residual method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed.

minspantree.description: Minimum spanning tree of an undirected graph (of the component of the root, or of every component with Type 'forest'). pred holds the predecessor of each node.

minute.description: Minute (0-59) of each element of a datetime array.

minutes.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many minutes. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of minutes.

mislocked.description: True if the running function, or the function called name, was locked with mlock.

missing.description: A missing value. Here it is a string scalar holding <missing>; ismissing(m) is true.

mkdir.description: Creates a folder, including any missing parent folders. It is not an error if the folder already exists. The optional output is true.

mkpp.description: Builds a piecewise polynomial. Row k of coefs holds the coefficients of piece k (highest power first) in the local variable x - breaks(k); d is the number of components for a vector-valued polynomial. Example: ppval(mkpp([0 1 2], [1 0; -1 1]), 1.5) is 0.5.

mldivide.description: Same as A \ B, which solves A*X = B (least squares if A is not square).

mle.description: Maximum-likelihood parameter estimates with confidence intervals. The default distribution is normal (here the standard deviation is the maximum-likelihood one, with divisor n). Options: 'Alpha', 'Censoring', 'Frequency', 'NTrials' (binomial), 'Start'; a custom distribution is given with 'pdf' (and 'cdf' for censored data), 'logpdf' (and 'logsf') or 'nloglf', together with 'Start' and optionally 'LowerBound' and 'UpperBound'.

mlock.description: Called inside a function: marks that function as locked. mislocked reports it and munlock removes the mark.

mmfileinfo.description: Describes a video file as a struct with Filename, Path, Duration, Video (Format, Height, Width) and Audio. The audio part is always empty: mylab does not read the sound track of a video file.

mnrfit.description: Multinomial logistic regression. Y holds category numbers, a categorical array or a matrix of counts. 'model' is 'nominal' (default, last category as reference), 'ordinal' (proportional odds) or 'hierarchical'.

mnrval.description: Category probabilities of a multinomial model fitted by mnrfit. 'type' is 'category' (default), 'cumulative' or 'conditional'.

mod.description: Remainder after division, defined as a - floor(a./b).*b, so a nonzero result has the sign of b. mod(a, 0) is a. Example: mod(-1, 3) is 2. See rem for the truncating version.

mode.description: Most frequent value, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. Ties go to the smallest value and NaN is ignored. Only the first output is supported.

modred.description: Removes the states listed in elim from a state-space model, either keeping the DC gain (the default, which assumes the removed states settle instantly) or by plain deletion.

modwt.description: Maximal-overlap discrete wavelet transform (no downsampling, periodic ends): rows 1 to J hold the wavelet coefficients of each level and the last row the scaling coefficients, all with the length of x. The default wavelet is 'sym4' and the default level floor(log2(n)). The energy of x is split between the rows.

modwtmra.description: Multiresolution analysis from a maximal-overlap transform: each row is the part of the signal at one scale, and the rows add up to the signal.

moment.description: Central moment of the given order: the mean of (x - mean(x)).^order.

montage.description: Shows several images side by side in one figure; see imtile for the inputs and options.

month.description: Month numbers (1-12) of a datetime array, or the English month names as a cell array of text (char(t, 'MMMM', locale) gives them in another language). Serial date numbers and date text are also accepted.

more.description: Accepted for compatibility; output is never paged, so it does nothing.

movefile.description: Moves or renames a file or folder. source may contain wildcards, and destination may be an existing folder to move into. With outputs, [status, message, messageId] report success (true) or the reason for failure instead of raising an error.

movegui.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

movevars.description: Moves table variables to a new position, before or after another variable (given by name or number), or to the end.

movfun.description: Applies a function to each sliding window of A; fun takes a column vector and returns a scalar. Endpoints is 'shrink' (default), 'fill', 'periodic', 'same' or a fill value.

movie.description: Plays the frames in F (from getframe or im2frame) n times at fps frames per second in a plot window. Without a live window it returns at once: the frames were already recorded as an animation while they were drawn.

movmad.description: Moving median absolute deviation over a sliding window.

movmax.description: Moving maximum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movmean.description: Moving (rolling, sliding-window) average over windows of k samples centred on each point (for even k, one more sample before than after), or kb before and kf after. Near the ends the window shrinks by default; 'Endpoints' can be 'discard', 'fill' (NaN) or a number. SamplePoints are not supported. Example: movmean([1 2 3 4 5], 3) is [1.5 2 3 4 4.5].

movmedian.description: Moving median over a sliding window, useful for removing spikes; options as in movmean.

movmin.description: Moving minimum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movprod.description: Moving product over a sliding window of k elements (or kb before and kf after).

movstd.description: Moving standard deviation over a sliding window; w = 1 normalizes by the window size instead of size-1. Other options as in movmean.

movsum.description: Moving sum over a sliding window; windows and options work as in movmean.

movvar.description: Moving variance over a sliding window; options as in movstd.

mpoles.description: Finds repeated poles. p(idx) lists the poles with nearly equal ones (within tol, default 0.001) next to each other, largest magnitude first; mults counts 1, 2, ... within each group. reorder = 0 keeps the original order of the groups.

mrdivide.description: Same as B / A, which solves X*A = B.

usage: [cxy, f] = mscohere(x, y, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
mscohere.description: Magnitude-squared coherence |Pxy|^2 / (Pxx Pyy): between 0 and 1, it tells how well y is predicted from x by a linear system at each frequency. The inputs are those of pwelch.

msgbox.description: Prints the message with the label 'Message' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines. icon 'error', 'warn' or 'help' changes the label.

multcompare.description: Pairwise comparisons of group means from the stats output of anova1, anova2, anovan, kruskalwallis or friedman. Each row of c is [group1, group2, lower, difference, upper, p-value]; m has the estimates and standard errors. Options: 'Alpha', 'CriticalValueType' ('tukey-kramer', 'bonferroni', 'dunn-sidak', 'lsd', 'scheffe'), 'Display', 'Dimension' (anovan) and 'Estimate' (anova2).

multithresh.description: n (default 1) thresholds that split the values of A into classes by Otsu's method, which makes the classes as different from each other as possible. metric is between 0 and 1; higher means a cleaner split. Use the thresholds with imquantize.

munlock.description: Removes the lock that mlock put on the running function, or on the function called name.

mustBeA.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value is of one of the named classes (a class name, or a cell/string array of names; subclasses count).

mustBeBetween.description: Checks that every element of x lies between lo and hi. intervalType is 'closed' (default), 'open', 'openleft', 'openright', 'closedleft' or 'closedright'. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeBetween}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeBetween when the check fails.

mustBeColumn.description: Checks that x is N-by-1. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeColumn}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeColumn when the check fails.

mustBeFile.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing file, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFile}.

mustBeFinite.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is Inf or NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFinite}.

mustBeFloat.description: Checks that x is a double or single array. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeFloat}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeFloat when the check fails.

mustBeFolder.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing folder, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFolder}.

mustBeGreaterThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is greater than c.

mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at least c.

mustBeInRange.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element lies between lower and upper (inclusive).

mustBeInteger.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is a finite whole number, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeInteger}.

mustBeLessThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is less than c.

mustBeLessThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at most c.

mustBeMatrix.description: Checks that x has two dimensions. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeMatrix}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeMatrix when the check fails.

mustBeMember.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value (number, text or cell of text) is one of the allowed values.

mustBeNegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is less than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNegative}.

mustBeNonNan.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonNan}.

mustBeNonempty.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is not empty, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonempty}.

mustBeNonmissing.description: Checks that x has no missing element (NaN, NaT, <missing>, <undefined>). Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeNonmissing}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeNonmissing when the check fails.

mustBeNonnegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or greater, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonnegative}.

mustBeNonpositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or less, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonpositive}.

mustBeNonsparse.description: Checks that x is not a sparse matrix. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeNonsparse}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeNonsparse when the check fails.

mustBeNonzero.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzero}.

mustBeNonzeroLengthText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is text with at least one character, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzeroLengthText}.

mustBeNumeric.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a numeric array, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumeric}.

mustBeNumericOrLogical.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is numeric or logical, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumericOrLogical}.

mustBePositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is greater than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBePositive}.

mustBeReal.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value has no imaginary part, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeReal}.

mustBeRow.description: Checks that x is 1-by-N. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeRow}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeRow when the check fails.

mustBeScalarOrEmpty.description: Checks that x has at most one element. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeScalarOrEmpty}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeScalarOrEmpty when the check fails.

mustBeSparse.description: Checks that x is a sparse matrix. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeSparse}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeSparse when the check fails.

mustBeText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a char vector, string, or cell array of char vectors, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeText}.

mustBeTextScalar.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is one piece of text (char row vector or string scalar), and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeTextScalar}.

mustBeUnderlyingType.description: Checks that the class of x is one of the names in types (text or a list). Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeUnderlyingType}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeUnderlyingType when the check fails.

mustBeValidVariableName.description: Checks that name is text that can be used as a variable name. Use it in an arguments block or a property declaration, e.g. x {mustBeValidVariableName}, or call it directly; it returns nothing and raises an error with identifier MATLAB:validators:mustBeValidVariableName when the check fails.

mustBeVector.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a row or column vector, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeVector}.

mvncdf.description: Cumulative probability of the multivariate normal distribution at each row of X, or the probability of the box between the rows of xl and xu.

mvnpdf.description: Density of the multivariate normal distribution at each row of X. mu defaults to zero and Sigma to the identity matrix.

mvnrnd.description: Random vectors from the multivariate normal distribution with mean mu (a row) and covariance matrix Sigma; one sample per row of R.

mvtcdf.description: Cumulative probability of the multivariate t distribution with correlation matrix C and df degrees of freedom, at each row of X or over the box between xl and xu.

mvtpdf.description: Density of the multivariate t distribution with correlation matrix C and df degrees of freedom at each row of X.

mvtrnd.description: Random vectors (one per row) from the multivariate t distribution with correlation matrix C and df degrees of freedom.

mylabMexCall__.description: Internal: runs a MEX file. mylab calls it for each MEX file it finds on the path; it is not meant to be called directly.

namedPattern.description: Gives the pattern p a name, which is shown when the pattern is displayed. It matches what p matches. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

namelengthmax.description: The longest allowed name of a variable or function: 63 characters.

nan.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

nancov.description: Covariance ignoring NaN: by default rows with any NaN are removed; with 'pairwise' each entry uses all rows where both variables are present.

nanmax.description: Maximum that ignores NaN values, like max.

nanmean.description: Mean that ignores NaN values; same as mean(..., 'omitnan').

nanmin.description: Minimum that ignores NaN values, like min.

nanstd.description: Standard deviation that ignores NaN values; flag 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1.

nansum.description: Sum that ignores NaN values; same as sum(..., 'omitnan').

nargchk.description: Returns an error message if n is outside low..high, or an empty value when it is in range; typically used as error(nargchk(1, 3, nargin)). With 'struct' the result is a struct with message and identifier. narginchk is the modern replacement.

nargin.description: Inside a function, the number of inputs the caller passed. nargin(fun), with a function name or handle, is the number of inputs fun declares; it is negative when the list ends in varargin (-3 for f(a, b, varargin)).

narginchk.description: Inside a function, throws an error if the number of inputs passed is below minargs or above maxargs.

nargout.description: Inside a function, the number of outputs the caller asked for. nargout(fun), with a function name or handle, is the number of outputs fun declares; it is negative when the list ends in varargout, and -1 for an anonymous function.

nargoutchk.description: Accepted for compatibility; mylab does not check anything.

native2unicode.description: Converts bytes in the given character encoding (default UTF-8) to text.

nbincdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the negative binomial distribution with r successes with success probability p (the value counts the failures): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

nbinfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [r, p] of the negative binomial distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

nbininv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the negative binomial distribution with r successes with success probability p (the value counts the failures): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

nbinlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the negative binomial distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

nbinpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the negative binomial distribution with r successes with success probability p (the value counts the failures), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

nbinrnd.description: Random numbers from the negative binomial distribution with r successes with success probability p (the value counts the failures). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

nbinstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the negative binomial distribution with r successes with success probability p (the value counts the failures).

nccreate.description: Creates a variable in a NetCDF file, and the file, the groups on its path and the named dimensions if they do not exist yet. A dimension that exists already is given by its name alone; a length of Inf makes the dimension unlimited. Without Dimensions the variable holds one value. Format applies when the file is created: 'classic' (the default), '64bit', 'netcdf4' or 'netcdf4_classic'. Datatype is 'double' (the default), 'single', 'int32', 'int16', 'int8' or 'char'; NetCDF-4 files also take 'uint8', 'uint16', 'uint32', 'int64', 'uint64' and, in the 'netcdf4' format, 'string'. Classic and netcdf4_classic files allow one unlimited dimension, which must be the variable's last; 'netcdf4' files allow several, anywhere, and groups. ChunkSize, DeflateLevel (0 to 9) and Shuffle set the storage of NetCDF-4 variables. A new variable is filled with the fill value ('disable': no filling), which ncread returns as NaN for double and single variables. Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

ncdisp.description: Prints the dimensions, variables, attributes and groups of a NetCDF file, or of one group or variable. Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

ncfcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the noncentral F distribution with degrees of freedom nu1, nu2 and noncentrality delta: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

ncfinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the noncentral F distribution with degrees of freedom nu1, nu2 and noncentrality delta: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

ncfpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the noncentral F distribution with degrees of freedom nu1, nu2 and noncentrality delta, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

usage: r = ncfrnd(nu1, nu2, delta, m, n, ...)
ncfrnd.description: Random numbers from the noncentral F distribution with degrees of freedom nu1, nu2 and noncentrality delta. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

ncfstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the noncentral F distribution with degrees of freedom nu1, nu2 and noncentrality delta.

nchoosek.description: With scalar n, the number of ways to pick k items from n (the binomial coefficient). With a vector v, every k-element combination of its entries, one per row. Example: nchoosek(5, 2) is 10.

ncinfo.description: Describes a NetCDF file as a struct with Filename, Name, Dimensions (Name, Length, Unlimited), Variables (Name, Dimensions, Size, Datatype, Attributes, ChunkSize, FillValue, DeflateLevel, Shuffle), Attributes (Name, Value), Groups (the same fields for each group of a NetCDF-4 file) and Format, or one group or variable of it. Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

usage: data = ncread(filename, varname, start, count, stride)
ncread.description: Reads a variable of a NetCDF file, or the part that starts at start with count elements per dimension (Inf: to the end) taking every stride-th. The result has the variable's class; a variable with one dimension comes back as a column. For double and single variables the fill value becomes NaN, and scale_factor and add_offset attributes are applied (giving double). Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

ncreadatt.description: Reads an attribute of a NetCDF file. location is '/' for the file's own attributes, the path of a group, or the name of a variable. Text comes back as a character vector, NC_STRING values as strings and numbers as a row vector of their class. Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

nctcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the noncentral t distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

nctinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the noncentral t distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

nctpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the noncentral t distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

nctrnd.description: Random numbers from the noncentral t distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

nctstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the noncentral t distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta.

ncwrite.description: Writes data to a variable of a NetCDF file, starting at index 1 of each dimension or at start, taking every stride-th position. Writing past the end of an unlimited dimension makes it longer. The data is converted to the variable's type; if the variable has scale_factor or add_offset attributes they are applied in reverse first, and NaN is stored as the fill value.
