Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

ncwriteatt.description: Creates or replaces an attribute of a NetCDF file ('/'), of a group or of a variable. The value is text or a numeric vector of class double, single, int32, int16 or int8; a 'netcdf4' file also takes the other integer classes and string arrays. Classic files ('classic' and '64bit') are read and written directly; NetCDF-4 files ('netcdf4' and 'netcdf4_classic', which are HDF5 files) through the Python package h5py, which is installed with mylab. The format of a file is detected when it is read. In a NetCDF-4 file a variable or group is named by its path, such as '/grp/var'.

ncx2cdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the noncentral chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

ncx2inv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the noncentral chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

ncx2pdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the noncentral chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

ncx2rnd.description: Random numbers from the noncentral chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

ncx2stat.description: Mean m and variance v of the noncentral chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom and noncentrality delta.

ndgrid.description: Like meshgrid but the first vector runs along dimension 1 (down the rows), the second along dimension 2 and so on: X and Y are numel(x)-by-numel(y).

ndims.description: Number of dimensions of A, never less than 2. Example: ndims(zeros(2, 3, 4)) is 3.

usage: [ids, dist] = nearest(G, s, d, 'Direction', dir, 'Method', m)
nearest.description: Nodes within distance d of node s, nearest first, with their distances.

nearestNeighbor.description: IDs of the triangulation vertices closest to the query points, and the distances. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.nearestNeighbor(...).

nearestvertex.description: For each query point, the row of p.Vertices of the closest vertex, the boundary it is on and its position in that boundary. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.nearestvertex(...).

neighbors.description: Nodes joined to the given node by an edge (undirected graphs).

new_system.description: Creates an empty block-diagram model in memory and makes it the current model. Add blocks with add_block, connect them with add_line, run it with sim, and write it to name.mlb.json with save_system.

newline.description: A char vector holding the line-feed character (code 10).

newplot.description: Prepare the current axes for a new plot, following its hold state; returns the axes.

nextpow2.description: Smallest integer p with 2^p >= abs(n), element by element; handy for choosing an FFT length. Example: nextpow2(100) is 7.

nexttile.description: Creates the next axes of the current tiled layout and makes it current; nexttile(k) goes to tile k (counting along rows) and [r c] makes an axes spanning r rows and c columns. Without a layout a 'flow' layout is started.

nichols.description: Nichols response: gain and phase (degrees) as for bode; the plot shows gain in dB against phase. The optional second argument is a vector of frequencies in rad per time unit, or a range {wmin, wmax}; without it the frequencies are chosen from the poles and zeros (up to the Nyquist frequency pi/Ts for a discrete-time model).

nicholsplot.description: Draws the Nichols chart; same arguments as nichols.

nlfilter.description: Sliding-window operation: B(i, j) is fun applied to the m-by-n neighbourhood of A(i, j), which must return a scalar. The image is padded with zeros.

usage: [beta, R, J, CovB, MSE, ErrorModelInfo] = nlinfit(X, Y, modelfun, beta0, ...)
nlinfit.description: Nonlinear least squares: fit Y = modelfun(beta, X) starting from beta0 (Levenberg-Marquardt). R holds the residuals, J the Jacobian, CovB the coefficient covariance and MSE the error variance estimate. 'Weights' gives observation weights.

nlparci.description: Confidence intervals for the coefficients of a nonlinear fit, from the outputs of nlinfit. 'alpha' sets the level (default 0.05).

usage: [ypred, delta] = nlpredci(modelfun, X, beta, resid, 'Covar', sigma, ...)
nlpredci.description: Predictions of a nonlinear model with confidence half-widths delta. 'PredOpt' is 'curve' (default) or 'observation'; 'SimOpt' 'on' gives simultaneous bounds; the 'Jacobian' can be given instead of 'Covar'.

nnz.description: Number of nonzero elements in x.

nonzeros.description: Column vector of the nonzero elements of A, in column-major order.

norm.description: For a vector, the p-norm (sum(abs(v).^p))^(1/p); p defaults to 2, the Euclidean length, and Inf or -Inf give the largest or smallest magnitude. For a matrix, p may be 1, 2 (default, the largest singular value), Inf or 'fro' (Frobenius). Example: norm([3 4]) is 5.

normalize.description: Rescales data along the first dimension whose size is not 1. method is 'zscore' (default; option 'std' or 'robust'), 'range' (to [0 1] or a given [a b]), 'norm' (divide by the p-norm, default 2), 'center' (subtract the mean, the median or a value) or 'scale' (divide by the std, 'mad', 'first', 'iqr' or a value).

normcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (defaults 0 and 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

normest.description: Estimate of the 2-norm (largest singular value) of a matrix without converting it to full form.

usage: [c, v, w, it] = normest1(A, t, X0)
normest1.description: Estimates the 1-norm of a square matrix from a few products with A and A'. t is the number of columns used per step (default 2). v and w satisfy w = A*v and norm(w,1) = c*norm(v,1); it = [iterations, products]. A function handle is called as afun('dim'), afun('real'), afun('notransp', X) and afun('transp', X).

normfit.description: Estimates of the mean and standard deviation of normal data (the standard deviation is the square root of the unbiased variance estimate) with exact 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals. For a matrix x each column is fitted separately.

norminv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (defaults 0 and 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

normlike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the normal distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

normpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (defaults 0 and 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

normplot.description: Normal probability plot: the sorted data against normal quantiles on a probability scale, with a reference line through the first and third quartiles. Points close to the line indicate normally distributed data.

normrnd.description: Random numbers from the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (defaults 0 and 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

normstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the normal distribution with mean mu and standard deviation sigma (defaults 0 and 1).

normxcorr2.description: Normalised cross-correlation of a template with an image: values from -1 to 1, with a peak of 1 where the image matches the template exactly. C has size(A) + size(template) - 1 elements each way; a peak at (r, c) means the template's lower right corner sits at A(r, c).

notify.description: Fires an event of the handle object obj: every listener added with addlistener is called as callback(obj, eventData). The event must be declared in an events block of the class. Without eventData the callback gets an object with the properties Source and EventName.

now.description: The current local date and time as a serial date number. A serial date number counts days from year 0, with the time of day as the fraction.

nsidedpoly.description: A regular polygon with n sides as a polyshape, with one side horizontal at the bottom. The size is the circumscribed radius (1 by default) or the side length; the center defaults to the origin.

nthargout.description: Calls f with the given inputs and returns only its n-th output. A vector n returns several outputs as a cell array; nout sets how many outputs f is asked for. Example: nthargout(2, @max, [3 9 2]) is 2.

nthroot.description: Real n-th root of each element; for negative x with odd n the real negative root is returned, e.g. nthroot(-8, 3) is -2. Negative x with an even or non-integer n is an error.

ntsc2rgb.description: Converts NTSC (YIQ) colours to RGB, limited to the range 0..1.

null.description: Orthonormal basis for the null space of A: the columns of Z satisfy A*Z = 0.

num2cell.description: Cell array with each element of A in its own cell, keeping its class: A can be numeric, logical, char, a struct array (each cell holds a 1-by-1 struct), a cell array (each cell holds a 1-by-1 cell), a string array (each cell holds a string) or an array of objects. With dims, the listed dimensions are kept together: num2cell(A, 1) puts each column of A in one cell, and num2cell(A, [1 2]) each page.

num2ruler.description: Convert plain numbers to the kind of value an axis ruler shows (dates, durations or categories).

num2str.description: Converts numbers to text. Integers print in full; other values keep four digits after the decimal point (at least five significant digits for small values), with trailing zeros dropped. precision sets the number of significant digits and format is a sprintf format. Matrices give a char matrix with one row per row. Text input is returned as is. Example: num2str(pi) is '3.1416'.

numArgumentsFromSubscript.description: How many values an indexing expression on obj produces where a comma-separated list is expected, for example in [a, b] = obj{1:2}. A class that overloads subsref can define this method to state the count; calling builtin('numArgumentsFromSubscript', obj, s, ctx) gives the standard answer. s is the subscript struct array that subsref receives.

numEntries.description: Number of key-value pairs in the dictionary d.

numargs.description: Number of inputs of the model: coefficients, problem parameters and independent variables. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

numboundaries.description: Number of boundaries (solid ones and holes) of p. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.numboundaries(...).

numcoeffs.description: Number of coefficients of the model. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

numden.description: Numerator and denominator of a symbolic expression after writing it as one fraction.

numedges.description: Number of edges of a graph or digraph.

numel.description: Total number of elements in A, the product of all its dimensions.

numfields.description: Number of fields of the struct s (0 if s is not a struct).

numnodes.description: Number of nodes of a graph or digraph.

numpartitions.description: The largest number of parts partition can divide a datastore into: its number of files. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.numpartitions(...).

numsides.description: Number of edges of p, or of each boundary I. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.numsides(...).

nuttallwin.description: Nuttall's four-term Blackman-Harris window. The result is a column vector. A second input 'periodic' gives the window used for spectral analysis (one period of n+1 samples).

nyquist.description: Nyquist response: real and imaginary parts of the frequency response, each ny-by-nu-by-nf. The plot shows the curve for positive and negative frequencies and marks the critical point -1. The optional second argument is a vector of frequencies in rad per time unit, or a range {wmin, wmax}; without it the frequencies are chosen from the poles and zeros (up to the Nyquist frequency pi/Ts for a discrete-time model).

nyquistplot.description: Draws the Nyquist diagram; same arguments as nyquist.

nzmax.description: Amount of storage allocated for nonzeros: nnz(S) (at least 1) for a sparse matrix and numel(A) for a full one.

obsv.description: Observability matrix [C; C*A; C*A^2; ...]. The system is observable when its rank equals the number of states.

usage: [Abar, Bbar, Cbar, T, k] = obsvf(A, B, C)
obsvf.description: Observability staircase form: an orthogonal T with Abar = T*A*T' = [Ano A12; 0 Ao] and Cbar = C*T' = [0 Co], where (Co, Ao) is observable. sum(k) is the observable dimension.

usage: [bw, flo, fhi, power] = obw(x, fs, freqrange, p)
obw.description: Occupied bandwidth: the width of the band that holds p percent (default 99) of the power, with equal amounts left out below flo and above fhi.

ode.description: An object describing an initial value problem. Properties: ODEFcn, InitialTime, InitialValue, Parameters (passed as the third argument of ODEFcn), Solver ('auto', 'stiff', 'nonstiff' or a solver name), SelectedSolver, RelativeTolerance, AbsoluteTolerance, MassMatrix (odeMassMatrix), Jacobian (odeJacobian), EventDefinition (odeEvent), NonNegativeVariables, InitialSlope and SolverOptions (a structure of odeset options such as MaxStep). S = solve(F, t0, tf) or solve(F, t) returns Time and Solution (one column per time); fh = solutionFcn(F, t0, tf) returns a function that evaluates the solution anywhere in the interval.

ode113.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). ode113 is meant for stringent tolerances and expensive functions; mylab integrates with a high-order (8th) explicit pair and a 7th-order continuous extension.

usage: [t, y] = ode15i(f, tspan, y0, yp0, options)
ode15i.description: Solves the fully implicit problem f(t, y, y') = 0 with a variable-order backward differentiation method. y0 and yp0 must be consistent, f(t0, y0, yp0) = 0; use decic to compute such values. The Jacobian option is a function [dfdy, dfdyp] = jac(t, y, yp) or a cell {dfdy, dfdyp}; JPattern is a cell of two sparsity patterns. An Events function is called as events(t, y, yp).

ode15s.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). This is an implicit solver for stiff problems; it also uses Jacobian (matrix or function), JPattern and Vectorized. ode15s is a variable-order method (numerical differentiation formulas of orders 1 to 5; BDF 'on' selects the backward differentiation formulas, MaxOrder limits the order). It solves index-1 differential-algebraic problems given by a singular mass matrix (MassSingular, InitialSlope); inconsistent initial values of the algebraic variables are corrected.

ode23.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). ode23 is a low-order explicit Runge-Kutta (2,3) pair, good for crude tolerances.

ode23s.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). This is an implicit solver for stiff problems; it also uses Jacobian (matrix or function), JPattern and Vectorized. ode23s is a one-step Rosenbrock method of order 2. The mass matrix must be constant and nonsingular; NonNegative is not available.

ode23t.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). This is an implicit solver for stiff problems; it also uses Jacobian (matrix or function), JPattern and Vectorized. ode23t is the trapezoidal rule, which adds no numerical damping; it also solves index-1 differential-algebraic problems with a singular mass matrix.

ode23tb.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). This is an implicit solver for stiff problems; it also uses Jacobian (matrix or function), JPattern and Vectorized. ode23tb is the TR-BDF2 method: a trapezoidal stage followed by a backward differentiation stage of order 2.

usage: [t, y, te, ye, ie] = ode45(f, tspan, y0, options)
ode45.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). ode45 is the general-purpose explicit Runge-Kutta (4,5) pair; with two entries in tspan it returns four output points per step (Refine 4).

ode78.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). ode78 is a high-order explicit solver for smooth problems and tight tolerances (an 8th-order pair with a 7th-order continuous extension).

ode89.description: Solves y' = f(t, y) from tspan(1) to tspan(end) with initial value y0. With two entries in tspan the output holds every solver step; with more than two it holds exactly those times. [t, y, te, ye, ie] also returns the event times, states and indices when an Events function is set. sol = solver(...) returns a structure for deval and odextend. Extra arguments after options are passed on to f and to the option functions. Options (odeset): RelTol, AbsTol (scalar or vector), NormControl, MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine, NonNegative, Events, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Stats and Mass with MStateDependence. A mass matrix M (constant, M(t) or M(t, y)) solves M*y' = f(t, y). ode89 is a high-order explicit solver for smooth problems and very tight tolerances (mylab uses the same 8th-order pair as ode78).

usage: E = odeEvent(EventFcn = g, Direction = dir, Response = r, CallbackFcn = cb)
odeEvent.description: Event definition for an ode object: g(t, y) is watched for zero crossings. Direction is 'both', 'ascending' or 'descending'. Response is 'proceed' (record and continue), 'stop', or 'callback', which calls [stop, y] = cb(t, y) and restarts from the returned state.

odeJacobian.description: Jacobian for an ode object: a matrix or a function of (t, y), and optionally its sparsity pattern.

usage: M = odeMassMatrix(MassMatrix = m, Singular = s, StateDependence = d)
odeMassMatrix.description: Mass matrix for an ode object: a matrix or a function of (t) or (t, y). Singular is 'yes', 'no' or 'maybe'; StateDependence is 'none', 'weak' or 'strong'.

odeSolutionValue__.description: Internal helper behind the function returned by solutionFcn: evaluates stored solution structures at the times t.

odeget.description: Value of one option from an options structure; default (or []) when the option is not set.

odephas2.description: Output function that draws a phase-plane plot of the first two selected components.

odephas3.description: Output function that draws a 3-D phase plot of the first three selected components.

odeplot.description: Output function that plots the solution components against time when the integration finishes. Use it as odeset('OutputFcn', @odeplot).

odeprint.description: Output function that prints the time and the solution at every step.

odeset.description: Creates or changes an options structure for the ODE solvers. Names are not case sensitive and may be shortened while they stay unique. The result has one field per option; unset options are []. With no arguments, lists every option. Options: RelTol (1e-3), AbsTol (1e-6), NormControl, NonNegative, OutputFcn, OutputSel, Refine, Stats, InitialStep, MaxStep, Events, Jacobian, JConstant, JPattern, Vectorized, Mass, MStateDependence ('none', 'weak', 'strong'), MvPattern, MassSingular ('yes', 'no', 'maybe'), InitialSlope, MaxOrder and BDF.

usage: solext = odextend(sol, f, tfinal, y0, options)
odextend.description: Continues a solution structure to tfinal with the same solver and options. An empty f reuses the function stored in sol; y0 restarts from a different state; options are merged over the stored ones. The result covers the whole interval.

onCleanup.description: Runs the given function (no inputs) when the variable c goes away: when the function that created it returns or stops with an error, or when c is cleared. Typical use: fid = fopen(name); c = onCleanup(@() fclose(fid)); The function does not run when c is merely overwritten, and objects stored inside cells or structs are not tracked. An error inside the cleanup function is reported as a warning.

ones.description: An array of ones. The class is double unless a class name is given; 'like', p takes the class and complexity from the value p.

open.description: open(v) starts a VideoWriter file so that writeVideo can add frames. open(filename) loads a .mat file; other files are not opened because mylab has no editor windows, and .fig files are not supported.

open_system.description: Loads a model (from name.mlb.json or name.slx in the current folder or on the path) and makes it the current model. In the mylab web app the model also opens in the diagram editor; elsewhere a note is printed once and the model can be used from code.

openfig.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

optimProblemShim__.description: Internal helper of the problem-based optimisation functions. Not meant to be called directly.

optimalleaforder.description: Leaf order of a tree that maximises the similarity of neighbouring leaves.

optimconstr.description: An empty array of optimisation constraints to fill in element by element.

optimeq.description: An empty array of equations for an equation problem.

optimexpr.description: An empty array of optimisation expressions to fill in element by element.

optimget.description: Read one setting from an options structure made by optimset; the default is returned when the setting is empty.

optimineq.description: An empty array of inequality constraints.

optimoptions.description: Same as optimset; the solver name is accepted and ignored. Returns a plain struct.

optimproblem.description: Create an optimisation problem. Set prob.Objective and prob.Constraints from expressions in optimisation variables, then call solve(prob) or solve(prob, x0); a suitable linear, quadratic, integer or nonlinear solver is chosen.

optimset.description: Builds an options struct from name/value pairs for fzero, fminsearch and similar solvers. mylab reads TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals where they apply and ignores other names.

usage: x = optimvar('x', n, m, 'LowerBound', lb, 'UpperBound', ub, 'Type', 'integer')
optimvar.description: Create an optimisation variable (a scalar or an array) to build objectives and constraints from with ordinary arithmetic.

optionalPattern.description: A pattern that matches p if it is there, and nothing otherwise. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

or.description: Same as A | B (element-wise logical OR).

ordeig.description: Eigenvalues of a Schur form T, or of a QZ pair (AA, BB), in the order in which they appear on the diagonal. Use it to build a selection for ordschur and ordqz.

order.description: Order of a model: the number of states of a state-space model, the number of poles of a SISO transfer function or zero-pole-gain model, and the number of states of its realization for a model with several inputs or outputs.

orderfields.description: Reorders the fields of a struct: alphabetically, in the order of a cell array of names, by a permutation vector, or like the fields of another struct. p is the permutation that was applied.

ordfilt2.description: Order-statistic filter: each pixel becomes the order-th smallest value among the neighbours marked by the nonzero elements of domain. order 1 is a minimum filter.

usage: [AAS, BBS, QS, ZS] = ordqz(AA, BB, Q, Z, select)
ordqz.description: Reorders a QZ factorization so that the chosen generalized eigenvalues come first. The selection works as in ordschur: a logical vector, one of 'lhp', 'rhp', 'udi', 'udo', or a vector of cluster numbers.

ordschur.description: Reorders a Schur form so that the chosen eigenvalues come first, with US*TS*US' still equal to U*T*U'. select is a logical vector with one entry per eigenvalue; keyword is 'lhp', 'rhp', 'udi' or 'udo' (left/right half plane, inside/outside the unit disk); clusters is a vector of cluster numbers, and the largest number ends up first.

orient.description: Paper orientation used when a figure is printed: 'portrait', 'landscape' or 'tall'.

orth.description: Orthonormal basis for the column space (range) of A.

orthfilt.description: The four filters of the orthogonal wavelet whose scaling filter is w. w is first scaled so that the low-pass filters sum to sqrt(2).

ostrsplit.description: Splits s at every character that occurs in seps and returns the pieces in a cell array. With true as third argument empty pieces are left out. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

otsuthresh.description: Otsu's threshold computed from histogram counts; level is the chosen bin as a fraction of the bin range.

outdegree.description: Number of edges leaving each node of a digraph.

outedges.description: Indices of the edges leaving a node (all its edges in an undirected graph), and the nodes at their other ends.

outerjoin.description: Like innerjoin but also keeps rows without a match ('Type' 'full', 'left' or 'right'), filling the missing side with NaN, empty text or <missing>. Without 'MergeKeys' the key variables of both tables are kept (with _left and _right suffixes); with it they are merged into one.

overlaps.description: True when two polyshapes share area or touch. For an array P, the symmetric matrix of all pairs. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.overlaps(...).

overshoot.description: Overshoot of each transition of a two-level waveform as a percentage of the difference between the state levels: how far the signal goes beyond the level it settles to, looked for just after the transition.

pad.description: Pads text with spaces (or the single character ch) to length n. side is 'right' (default), 'left' or 'both'. Without n, the elements of a cell or string array are padded to the length of the longest one. Text already longer than n is left alone. Example: pad('ab', 5, 'left', '*') is '***ab'.

padarray.description: Enlarges an array by padsize(k) elements along dimension k. The new elements are 0, padval, or come from the array itself: 'replicate' repeats the border, 'symmetric' mirrors it and 'circular' wraps around. direction is 'both' (default), 'pre' or 'post'.

pade.description: Pade approximation of a time delay. [num, den] = pade(T, N) gives the order-N rational approximation of exp(-T*s). pade(sys, N) replaces every delay of a continuous-time model by such an approximation, so that functions that need a rational model (feedback, rlocus, ss conversions) can be used; NU, NY and NINT set separate orders for input, output and input/output delays, and Inf keeps a delay as it is. For a discrete-time model the delays become poles at z = 0.

pagectranspose.description: Complex conjugate transpose of every page of an N-D array.

pageeig.description: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of every page of an N-D array; each page must be square. The options of eig ('vector', 'matrix', 'balance', 'nobalance') are accepted.

pageinv.description: Inverse of every page of an N-D array; each page must be square.

pagelsqminnorm.description: Minimum-norm least-squares solution of A(:,:,k)*X = B(:,:,k) for every page.

pagemldivide.description: Solves A(:,:,k) \ B(:,:,k) for every page. Page dimensions of size 1 expand.

pagemrdivide.description: Computes B(:,:,k) / A(:,:,k) for every page. Page dimensions of size 1 expand.

pagemtimes.description: Matrix multiplication applied page by page: each 2-D slice X(:,:,k) is multiplied by the matching slice Y(:,:,k). The inner dimensions of each pair of pages must agree.

pagenorm.description: Matrix norm of every page, as a 1-by-1-by-pages array. p is 1, 2 (default), Inf or 'fro'.

pagepinv.description: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of every page of an N-D array.

pagesvd.description: Singular value decomposition of every page of an N-D array.

pagetranspose.description: Transposes every page (2-D slice along the first two dimensions) of an N-D array.

pan.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

usage: sys = parallel(sys1, sys2, inp1, inp2, out1, out2)
parallel.description: Parallel connection: both models receive the same input and their outputs are added, which is sys1 + sys2. With index vectors only the listed inputs are shared and only the listed outputs are summed; the other channels of both models are kept (those of sys1 first).

parallelcoords.description: A parallel coordinates plot; returns the lines.

parallelplot.description: One line per row across parallel coordinate axes.

pareto.description: Bars in decreasing order with a line of the cumulative share.

parfeval.description: Evaluates fcn(in1, ...) for nout outputs and returns a future that holds the result. mylab has no background workers: the function runs at once, and the future is finished when parfeval returns. fetchOutputs(f) returns the outputs, or raises the error the function raised. Properties: State ('finished'), Error, OutputArguments, InputArguments, Function, NumOutputArguments, Diary (what the function printed), Read and ID.

parfevalOnAll.description: Like parfeval: with no background workers the function runs once, in this session.

parpool.description: Accepted for compatibility. mylab runs code in a single process, so no workers are started; the returned struct describes a pool with NumWorkers 1, and delete(pool) does nothing.

parse.description: Checks the given arguments against the declarations of the inputParser p and fills p.Results, p.Unmatched and p.UsingDefaults. Raises an error that names the argument when a required argument is missing, a validator rejects a value or a parameter name is unknown. Example: p = inputParser; addRequired(p, 'n'); addParameter(p, 'Tol', 1e-3); parse(p, varargin{:}); p.Results

partfrac.description: Partial fraction decomposition of a rational expression in x.

partialcorr.description: Partial correlation: the correlation between pairs of variables after removing the linear effect of the others (or of the variables in Z). Options: 'Type' ('Pearson' or 'Spearman'), 'Rows' and 'Tail'.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output] = particleswarm(fun, nvars, lb, ub, options)
particleswarm.description: Minimise a function with a swarm of candidate points that move toward the best positions found so far. Works best with bounds on every variable.

partition.description: Divides the files of a datastore into n parts of nearly equal size and returns the k-th one, or returns a datastore with the single file k (or the file with that name). Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.partition(...).

parula.description: n-by-3 matrix of RGB colours (default 256) running from dark blue through green to yellow. mylab uses matplotlib's perceptually uniform 'viridis' map for parula, also the default colormap. Use with colormap, e.g. colormap(parula(16)).

parzenwin.description: Parzen (de la Vallee Poussin) window: a piecewise cubic bell. The result is a column vector.

pascal.description: Pascal matrix: P(i, j) is the binomial coefficient (i+j-2 choose j-1), a symmetric positive definite matrix of integers. pascal(n, 1) is a lower-triangular factor with alternating column signs that is its own inverse.

patch.description: Adds filled polygons to the current axes without clearing them. Polygons are given by corner coordinates, or by a vertex list V (one row per point, 2 or 3 columns) and a face list F whose rows hold vertex numbers. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, FaceVertexCData (one number or RGB row per face).

path.description: Current search path as one char vector with folders separated by the system path separator.

pathsep.description: The character that separates folders in a search path: ':' (';' on Windows).

pattern.description: A pattern that matches the given text literally. With a string array or a cell array of character vectors it matches any one of the texts. Other patterns are built with functions such as digitsPattern, lettersPattern and wildcardPattern. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output] = patternsearch(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
patternsearch.description: Minimise a function by polling points on a mesh around the current point, shrinking the mesh when no better point is found. Needs no derivatives.

pause.description: Waits n seconds (at most an hour). pause with no argument, or with text such as 'on', returns immediately instead of waiting for a key press. With a figure open it also refreshes the plot; where there is no live window it records an animation frame like drawnow and waits only briefly.

pbaspect.description: Sets the relative lengths of the sides of the plot box; pbaspect([1 1 1]) makes it square and pbaspect([2 1 1]) twice as wide as high.

pburg.description: Power spectral density from an autoregressive model fitted by Burg's method (see arburg).

usage: [coeff, score, latent, tsquared, explained, mu] = pca(X, 'Name', value, ...)
pca.description: Principal component analysis of the rows of X. coeff holds the component directions (the largest entry of each column is positive), score the data in those coordinates, latent the component variances, tsquared Hotelling's statistic of each row, explained the percentage of variance and mu the column means. Options: 'Algorithm' ('svd' or 'eig'), 'Centered', 'Economy', 'NumComponents', 'Rows' ('complete', 'pairwise', 'all'), 'Weights', 'VariableWeights'.

pcacov.description: Principal components from a covariance (or correlation) matrix.

pcares.description: Residuals of the data after keeping ndim principal components, and the reconstruction.

usage: x = pcg(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
pcg.description: Solves A*x = b for a symmetric positive definite A with the preconditioned conjugate gradient method. A is a square matrix (sparse or full) or a function handle that returns A*x. tol is the relative residual to reach (default 1e-6) and maxit the iteration limit. M1 and M2 are optional preconditioner factors (the method works with inv(M1*M2)*A); either may be a function handle that returns M\x. x0 is the starting guess. flag is 0 when the tolerance was met and 1 when the iterations ran out, relres is norm(b-A*x)/norm(b), iter the iteration count and resvec the residual history. With a single output a one-line convergence report is printed. maxit defaults to min(n, 20).

pchip.description: Shape-preserving piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation: no overshoot between data points, and monotone data stay monotone. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial for ppval.

pcolor.description: Draws the matrix C as a flat grid of coloured cells. Each cell takes the colour of its lower-left corner, so the last row and column of C are not shown; shading interp blends the colours. The y-axis points up (unlike imagesc).

pcov.description: Power spectral density from an autoregressive model fitted by the covariance method (see arcov).

usage: sol = pdepe(m, pdefun, icfun, bcfun, xmesh, tspan)
sol = pdepe(m, pdefun, icfun, bcfun, xmesh, tspan, options)
pdepe.description: Solves systems of parabolic and elliptic PDEs in one space variable, c*du/dt = x^(-m)*d/dx(x^m*f) + s, with m = 0 (slab), 1 (cylinder) or 2 (sphere). [c, f, s] = pdefun(x, t, u, dudx); u0 = icfun(x); [pl, ql, pr, qr] = bcfun(xl, ul, xr, ur, t) states p + q*f = 0 at each end. sol(i, j, k) is component k at time tspan(i) and point xmesh(j). The space discretisation is second order; time integration uses ode15s with the RelTol, AbsTol, InitialStep and MaxStep options.

pdeval.description: Interpolates one component of a pdepe solution at one time, ui = sol(j, :, k), to the points xout, and returns its space derivative.

usage: y = pdf(name, x, A, B, C)
pdf.description: Probability density of the distribution called name (for example 'Normal', 'Weibull', 'bino') with parameters A, B, C at the points x, or of a probability distribution object pd made by makedist or fitdist.

pdist.description: Pairwise distances between the rows of X as a row vector (use squareform for the matrix). distance is 'euclidean', 'squaredeuclidean', 'seuclidean', 'mahalanobis', 'cityblock', 'minkowski', 'chebychev', 'cosine', 'correlation', 'spearman', 'hamming', 'jaccard' or a function handle.

pdist2.description: Distances between every row of X and every row of Y. distance is 'euclidean', 'squaredeuclidean', 'seuclidean', 'mahalanobis', 'cityblock', 'minkowski', 'chebychev', 'cosine', 'correlation', 'spearman', 'hamming', 'jaccard' or a function handle. 'Smallest' or 'Largest' keeps the k extreme distances in each column with their row numbers.

peak2peak.description: Difference between the largest and smallest value along the first dimension that is not one, or along dim.

peak2rms.description: Ratio of the largest magnitude to the root-mean-square value (the crest factor).

peaks.description: A smooth test surface with several hills and dips, given by a sum of Gaussian bumps. The default grid is 49-by-49 points on [-3, 3]; peaks(n) uses n points, a vector v builds the grid from v, and X, Y give the points directly. Without outputs it draws the surface.

usage: [X, Y, T, AUC, OPTROCPT] = perfcurve(labels, scores, posclass, 'Name', value, ...)
perfcurve.description: Receiver operating characteristic (or another performance curve) for scores of the positive class. X and Y default to the false and true positive rates; T holds the thresholds, AUC the area under the curve and OPTROCPT the optimal operating point. Options: 'XCrit', 'YCrit', 'NegClass', 'Cost', 'Weights', 'ProcessNaN'.

perimeter.description: Total length of all boundaries of p (holes included), or of the boundaries I. For an array of polyshapes, one value per element. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.perimeter(...).

periodogram.description: Power spectral density from one windowed FFT of the signal. window is a vector, a length (a Hamming window of that length) or [] for the default. nfft may be replaced by a vector of frequencies. Without fs the frequencies are in rad/sample and the density is per rad/sample. A trailing 'onesided', 'twosided' or 'centered' picks the frequency range; real signals give one-sided results by default. 'power' returns the power in each bin instead of a density. Columns of a matrix are separate signals. Without outputs the estimate is plotted in dB.

perms.description: Every ordering of the elements of v, one per row, n! rows in total, starting with the reverse of v. Also works on cell arrays. Limited to 11 elements. Example: perms([1 2]) is [2 1; 1 2].

permute.description: Rearranges the dimensions of A in the given order, a permutation of 1..n. permute(A, [2 1]) is the same as transposing a matrix without conjugation.

phantom.description: Head phantom made of ellipses, used to test tomography: 'Modified Shepp-Logan' (default, better contrast) or 'Shepp-Logan', n-by-n pixels (default 256). A matrix with one row [value a b x0 y0 phi] per ellipse defines another phantom.

phasez.description: Unwrapped phase response of a digital filter in radians. The inputs are those of freqz.

pi.description: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, 3.14159..., in double precision.

usage: C = pid(Kp, Ki, Kd, Tf, Ts)
pid.description: PID controller in parallel form, Kp + Ki/s + Kd*s/(Tf*s + 1). Omitted gains are 0, so pid(2, 1) is a PI controller. With a sample time Ts the integrators use the formulas IFormula and DFormula: 'ForwardEuler' (default), 'BackwardEuler' or 'Trapezoidal'. pid(sys) converts a transfer function that has PID structure. Properties: Kp, Ki, Kd, Tf, IFormula, DFormula, Ts. Sums of PID controllers and products with a number stay pid objects; other combinations give a tf, zpk or ss model, e.g. feedback(C*G, 1).

pidTuner.description: PID tuning app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

piddata.description: Gains of a controller in parallel form. sys may be a pid or pidstd object or a transfer function with PID structure.

usage: C = pidstd(Kp, Ti, Td, N, Ts)
pidstd.description: PID controller in standard form, Kp*(1 + 1/(Ti*s) + Td*s/(Td/N*s + 1)). Ti = Inf turns the integral action off and N = Inf removes the derivative filter. pidstd(sys) converts a pid object or a transfer function with PID structure. Properties: Kp, Ti, Td, N, IFormula, DFormula, Ts.

pidstddata.description: Parameters of a controller in standard form: gain, integral time, derivative time and filter divisor. An error is raised if the controller has no proportional gain.

pidtool.description: PID tuning app (older name of pidTuner). This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

pidtune.description: Tunes a PID controller for the SISO plant sys in a unity-feedback loop. type is 'P', 'I', 'PI', 'PD', 'PDF', 'PID' or 'PIDF' (F adds a filter on the derivative); a pid or pidstd object C0 gives the type, form and discrete formulas instead. The controller is designed in the frequency domain: at the crossover frequency wc the loop gain is 1 and the phase margin equals the target (60 degrees unless pidtuneOptions says otherwise). When wc is not given it is chosen to give the largest integral gain (the fastest disturbance rejection) among the designs that are stable and keep the target margin; for plants where that has no limit, a crossover of twice the slowest plant pole is used. If the margin cannot be reached at a requested wc the best achievable design is returned. info reports Stable, CrossoverFrequency and PhaseMargin. Two-degree-of-freedom types are not supported.

pidtuneOptions.description: Options for pidtune: PhaseMargin in degrees (default 60), DesignFocus ('balanced', 'reference-tracking' for weaker integral action and less overshoot, or 'disturbance-rejection' for stronger integral action), CrossoverFrequency and NumUnstablePoles.

pie.description: Pie chart of the values in x, each slice proportional to its share of the total. Without labels each slice shows its percentage; labels is a cell or string array of text.

pie3.description: A pie chart drawn as a 3-D disc.

usage: p = piecewise(cond1, val1, cond2, val2, ..., otherwise)
piecewise.description: An expression defined by cases: val1 where cond1 holds, else val2 where cond2 holds, and so on. The optional last value is used when no condition holds (otherwise NaN).

piechart.description: A pie chart object with labelled slices; set properties such as Labels, ExplodedWedges and StartAngle on the result.

pink.description: n-by-3 colormap of pastel pinks, from dark to white.

pinv.description: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, computed from the singular value decomposition. Works for rectangular and singular matrices. A tolerance argument is not supported.

usage: P = pivot(T, Columns=colvars, Rows=rowvars, DataVariable=var, Method=method)
pivot.description: A pivot table: one row for every value of the Rows variables and one variable for every value of the Columns variables. Each cell counts the matching rows of T, or with a DataVariable summarizes it with Method ('sum' by default; 'count', 'mean', 'median', 'min', 'max', 'mode', 'std', 'var', 'range', 'numunique', 'nummissing', 'percentage', 'none' or a function handle). Other options: IncludeTotals, IncludeMissingGroups, RowsBinMethod, ColumnsBinMethod.

pkg.description: GNU Octave's package command, accepted so that code written for Octave runs. The functions of the Octave Forge packages mylab covers (control, signal, statistics, optim, symbolic, image, io and others) are built in, so pkg load and pkg unload do nothing for them; another package name is an error. pkg('list') returns the names accepted.

place.description: State-feedback gain that puts the eigenvalues of A - B*K at the values in p. A pole may not be repeated more often than B has independent columns. prec estimates how many digits of the requested poles were achieved. For an observer gain use L = place(A', C', p)'.

planerot.description: Plane (Givens) rotation for a two-element column vector x: G is orthogonal, y = G*x and y(2) is zero.

plot.description: Draws 2-D lines. With one input, y is plotted against its index (complex y plots real against imaginary part). A matrix y, or a vector x with a matrix y, draws one line per column. linespec combines a colour (r g b c m y k w), a marker (o + * . x s d ^ v < > p h) and a line style (- -- : -.) in any order, e.g. 'r--o'. Name/Value options: LineWidth, Color, MarkerSize, Marker, LineStyle, DisplayName, MarkerFaceColor, MarkerEdgeColor, Visible. Replaces the current plot unless hold is on; an axes handle as first input draws there. h is a Line handle, or a column array of them when several lines are drawn, so h.LineWidth = 2 restyles the line afterwards. Example: plot(0:0.1:1, (0:0.1:1).^2, 'b-').

plot3.description: Draws a line through 3-D points on 3-D axes (matrices draw one line per column). Accepts the same line options as plot and returns Line handles in the same way.

plotbrowser.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

plotmatrix.description: Scatter plots of every pair of columns; histograms on the diagonal.

plottools.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

plotyy.description: Plots y1 against the left y-axis and y2 against a second y-axis on the right. fun names the plotting function ('plot', 'semilogy', 'stem', ...). Returns the two axes and the two plotted objects. yyaxis is the newer way to do this.

usage: [XL, YL, XS, YS, BETA, PCTVAR, MSE, stats] = plsregress(X, Y, ncomp, ...)
plsregress.description: Partial least squares regression with ncomp components (SIMPLS). BETA holds the regression coefficients with the constant first; PCTVAR the fraction of variance explained in X and Y; MSE the mean squared errors for 0 to ncomp components ('CV' cross-validates).

pmcov.description: Power spectral density from an autoregressive model fitted by the modified covariance method (see armcov).

pmtm.description: Thomson multitaper power spectral density using 2 nw - 1 Slepian tapers (nw defaults to 4). The method is 'adapt' (adaptive weights, the default), 'unity' or 'eigen'.

pointLocation.description: The triangle (tetrahedron) that contains each query point, NaN outside the triangulation, and the barycentric coordinates in it. Not for 3-D surface triangulations. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.pointLocation(...).

poisscdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the Poisson distribution with mean lambda: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

poissfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of the mean of the Poisson distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

poissinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the Poisson distribution with mean lambda: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

poisspdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the Poisson distribution with mean lambda, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

poissrnd.description: Random numbers from the Poisson distribution with mean lambda. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

poisstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the Poisson distribution with mean lambda.

pol2cart.description: Converts polar (or cylindrical) coordinates, angle in radians, to Cartesian.

polar.description: A line in polar coordinates (the older form of polarplot).

polaraxes.description: Create polar axes in the current figure (or make polar axes current).

polarbubblechart.description: A bubble chart in polar coordinates.

polarhistogram.description: A histogram of angles (in radians) drawn in polar axes.

polarplot.description: Plots points given by angle theta (radians) and radius rho on polar axes.

pole.description: Poles of a model as a column vector: the roots of the denominator of a transfer function, or the eigenvalues of A for a state-space model. Delays are not counted.

poly.description: Polynomial coefficients from a vector of roots r, or the characteristic polynomial of a square matrix A. Example: poly([1 2]) is [1 -3 2].

poly2mask.description: m-by-n binary mask that is true for the pixels whose centres lie inside the polygon with corner coordinates x (columns) and y (rows). Pixels exactly on the edge may be classified differently from other implementations.

poly2rc.description: Reflection coefficients of the prediction polynomial a (the step-down recursion). r0 is the zero-lag autocorrelation that goes with the final prediction error efinal.

poly2sym.description: Symbolic polynomial from a coefficient vector (highest power first), in x or the given variable.

polyarea.description: Area of the polygon with corners (x, y). For matrices, each column is one polygon.

polybuffer.description: Grows p by the distance d (shrinks it for negative d), or makes the region within d of a polyline or of points. Round joints follow circular arcs drawn with 64 points per circle. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.polybuffer(...).

polyconf.description: Evaluate a polynomial and, with the structure S from polyfit, the half-width delta of the prediction interval. Options: 'alpha', 'mu', 'predopt' ('observation' or 'curve') and 'simopt'.

polyder.description: Coefficients of the derivative of a polynomial. The product and quotient forms with two inputs are not supported.

polyeig.description: Polynomial eigenvalue problem: finds lambda and x with (A0 + lambda*A1 + ... + lambda^p*Ap)*x = 0. X has one eigenvector per column and s holds condition numbers of the eigenvalues.

polyfit.description: Least-squares polynomial of degree n through the points (x, y), highest power first. S holds the triangular factor R, the degrees of freedom df, the residual norm normr and rsquared, for error estimates with polyval. With mu, x is first centred and scaled: the fit uses (x - mu(1)) / mu(2), where mu = [mean(x); std(x)]; this helps with large or badly scaled x.

polyint.description: Coefficients of the antiderivative of a polynomial, with constant of integration k (default 0).

polyshape.description: A 2-D polygon that may have several regions and holes. Vertices come as x and y vectors, an N-by-2 matrix or cell arrays with one boundary per cell; NaN rows separate boundaries. By default the polygon is simplified: repeated vertices, crossings and overlapping boundaries are repaired (with the warning MATLAB:polyshape:repairedBySimplify), collinear vertices are dropped unless KeepCollinearPoints is true, and solid boundaries are stored clockwise with holes counterclockwise. A point is filled when an odd number of the given boundaries enclose it ('auto'), or by orientation with 'cw' / 'ccw'. Properties: Vertices (boundaries separated by NaN rows), NumRegions, NumHoles. Polyshapes form arrays: [p1 p2], p(k), p(k) = q. The methods area, union, intersect, xor, convhull, simplify, triangulation, plot and isequal also accept polyshapes; intersect(p, L) with an N-by-2 polyline returns the parts inside and outside.

polyval.description: Evaluates the polynomial p (highest power first) at each element of x. With mu from polyfit, x is centred and scaled first. With S from polyfit, delta is an error estimate such that y +/- delta covers new observations about 68% of the time for normal errors.

polyvalm.description: Evaluates a polynomial at a square matrix, with matrix powers: p(1)*X^n + ... + p(n)*X + p(n+1)*eye(size(X)).

posixtime.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC for each datetime. Values without a time zone are taken as UTC.

postpad.description: Makes x have length n along its first non-singleton dimension (or dim) by adding the value c (default 0) at the end, or by removing elements from the end when x is longer. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

pow2.description: pow2(x) is 2.^x. pow2(f, e) is f .* 2.^e, the inverse of [f, e] = log2(x).

pow2db.description: Converts power ratio to decibels: 10*log10(p). Negative values are an error.

usage: [bw, flo, fhi, power] = powerbw(x, fs, freqrange, r)
powerbw.description: Width of the band around the spectral peak in which the power stays within r dB (default 3.01, the half-power bandwidth) of the peak.

ppval.description: Evaluates a piecewise polynomial (from spline, pchip, makima or mkpp) at xq. Points outside the breaks use the first or last piece.

prctile.description: Percentiles of the data for percentages p (0..100), along the first dimension whose size is not 1 or along dim; NaN values are ignored. Sorted values are treated as sitting at percentages 100*(i-0.5)/n with linear interpolation between them. Example: prctile([1 2 3 4], 50) is 2.5.

predecessors.description: Nodes with an edge that enters the given node of a digraph.

usage: ci = predint(f, x, level, intopt, simopt)
predint.description: Prediction bounds at x (n-by-2): intopt 'observation' (default, for a new observation) or 'functional' (for the fitted curve); simopt 'off' (default, nonsimultaneous) or 'on' (simultaneous). y is the fit at x. f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.predint(...).

prepad.description: Makes x have length n along its first non-singleton dimension (or dim) by adding the value c (default 0) at the start, or by removing elements from the start when x is longer. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

prepareCurveData.description: Data as column vectors for fit, with the points that have NaN or Inf removed (with a warning).

usage: [x, y, z, w] = prepareSurfaceData(x, y, z, w)
prepareSurfaceData.description: Surface data as column vectors for fit, without NaN or Inf points. A row x, a column y and a matrix z with size [numel(y) numel(x)] are expanded to a grid first.

pretty.description: Prints a symbolic expression in a two-dimensional text layout.

preview.description: The first block of a datastore (the first image of an image datastore, the first eight rows of a tabular text datastore), whatever the read position. With a file name and import options it reads the first eight rows of the file. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.preview(...).

primes.description: Row vector of all prime numbers less than or equal to n. Example: primes(10) is [2 3 5 7].

print.description: Saves the current figure (or figure fig, a handle or number, or -fN) to a file. A -d option such as -dpng, -djpeg, -dpdf, -dsvg or -depsc picks the format when the file name has no extension; PNG is the default. -rN sets the resolution in dots per inch (default 150). Renderer options such as -painters are ignored. The .fig format is not supported.

print_usage.description: Stops with an error that says the running function was called in a wrong way. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

printf.description: Writes formatted text to the command window, like fprintf(format, ...). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

probnames.description: Column cell array of the problem parameter names. Works on fittype, cfit and sfit objects.

probplot.description: Probability plot of the data against a distribution: 'normal' (default), 'exponential', 'extreme value', 'lognormal', 'rayleigh', 'weibull', 'logistic', 'loglogistic' or 'half normal'. Censored observations and frequencies are supported.

probvalues.description: Row vector of the problem parameter values of a fit. f is a cfit or sfit object made by fit. Also callable as f.probvalues(...).

usage: [d, Z, transform] = procrustes(X, Y, 'scaling', tf, 'reflection', tf)
procrustes.description: Fit Y to X by translation, rotation and scaling. d is the standardised sum of squared errors, Z the transformed Y and transform holds T, b and c with Z = b*Y*T + c.

prod.description: Product of elements, working along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. 'omitnan' skips NaN values. prod([]) is 1.

profile.description: Measures where a program spends its time. Between profile on and profile off every statement of scripts and functions is timed (built-in functions count towards the statement that calls them). profile('info') returns a struct whose FunctionTable has one element per function with FunctionName, FileName, NumCalls, TotalTime (including the functions it calls), ExecutedLines (line, count, time), Children and Parents; profile viewer prints a summary table instead of opening a window. profile resume continues without clearing, profile clear discards the measurements, profile('status') tells whether the profiler is on. Programs run slower while it is on.

profsave.description: Writes the profiler's summary table to profile.txt in the folder (profile_results by default). mylab writes plain text, not the HTML pages MATLAB produces.

progress.description: The fraction of a datastore that has been read, from 0 to 1. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.progress(...).

projective2d.description: Projective transformation with the 3-by-3 matrix T used as [x y w] = [u v 1] * T, followed by division by w.

projtform2d.description: Projective transformation with the 3-by-3 matrix A used as [x; y; w] = A * [u; v; 1].

properties.description: Lists the public properties of an object or class; with an output, returns them as a cell column. Built-in classes list their documented properties (a datetime has Format, TimeZone, Year, ..., a table its variable names, Properties and its two dimension names); a class without public properties gives an empty list.

propertyeditor.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

psi.description: Digamma function, the derivative of gammaln. psi(k, x) gives the k-th derivative of digamma (polygamma), for non-negative integer k.

psnr.description: Peak signal-to-noise ratio in decibels, 10*log10(peak^2 / MSE). peak defaults to the range of the image class (255 for uint8, 1 for double). snr is the signal-to-noise ratio.

pspectrum.description: Power spectrum of a signal on 4096 frequencies, using a Kaiser window. 'Leakage' (0 to 1, default 0.5) trades resolution against sidelobes, 'FrequencyLimits' restricts the range, 'FrequencyResolution' sets the resolution bandwidth and 'TwoSided' asks for negative frequencies too. A sine wave of amplitude A shows a peak of A^2/2. The 'spectrogram' and 'persistence' types are not supported.

usage: y = pulstran(t, d, p, fs, method)
pulstran.description: Pulse train: the sum of copies of a pulse delayed by the values in d. The pulse is a function such as @rectpuls (extra inputs are passed to it) or a sampled pulse p at rate fs. A two-column d gives a delay and an amplitude for each copy.

puts.description: Writes text to the command window exactly as given: no format codes are interpreted and no newline is added. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

pwd.description: Current working folder as a char vector.

usage: [pxx, f] = pwelch(x, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
pwelch.description: Welch's power spectral density: the average of the periodograms of overlapping windowed segments. By default the signal is cut into eight Hamming-windowed segments that overlap by half. window is a vector, a length (a Hamming window of that length) or [] for the default. nfft may be replaced by a vector of frequencies. Without fs the frequencies are in rad/sample and the density is per rad/sample. A trailing 'onesided', 'twosided' or 'centered' picks the frequency range; real signals give one-sided results by default. 'power' returns power instead of density; 'maxhold' and 'minhold' keep the largest or smallest value over the segments instead of the mean.

py.*.description: Calls Python from MATLAB code: py. followed by a built-in name (py.list, py.len, py.dict) or a module and a name in it (py.math.sqrt, py.os.path.join, py.numpy.linalg.norm). Arguments are converted: numeric scalars to float, int (integer classes), bool or complex; text to str; a real row vector to an array.array; other arrays to NumPy arrays; a cell vector to a tuple; a scalar struct or containers.Map to a dict; a function handle to a callable; keyword arguments come from pyargs. Results that are float, complex or bool become double, complex double or logical, int becomes int64, and everything else stays a Python object (its class shows as py.list, py.str, py.numpy.ndarray, ...). Convert such an object with double, single, an integer class, logical, char, string, cell (elements keep their Python type unless they are numbers) or struct (for a dict); numel and length give len(obj). obj.name reads an attribute or calls a method, obj{k} takes element k (counting from 1) or a dict entry, and obj(args) calls a callable object. A Python exception becomes a MATLAB error whose message starts with 'Python Error:'. What Python prints appears in the command window. Python calls can be switched off by the program that hosts mylab (the interpreter's python_enabled setting, or the environment variable MYLAB_PYTHON=0); they then stop with an error.

pyargs.description: Keyword arguments for a Python call: py.sorted(x, pyargs('reverse', true)) calls sorted(x, reverse=True). Put it after the positional arguments.

pyenv.description: Describes the Python that Python calls use: Version, Executable, Library, Home, Status ('Loaded') and ExecutionMode ('InProcess'). It is the Python that mylab itself runs on and cannot be changed with pyenv; to use another Python, start mylab with it. Python calls can be switched off by the program that hosts mylab (the interpreter's python_enabled setting, or the environment variable MYLAB_PYTHON=0); they then stop with an error.

pyrun.description: Runs Python statements (a string, or a string array with one line each) and returns the variables named in outvar. name=value pairs create Python variables first. Variables stay defined from one pyrun call to the next, so a later call can use what an earlier one computed. Results are converted as described under py.*. Python calls can be switched off by the program that hosts mylab (the interpreter's python_enabled setting, or the environment variable MYLAB_PYTHON=0); they then stop with an error.

usage: out = pyrunfile("script.py arg1 arg2", outvar, name=value)
pyrunfile.description: Runs a Python script file, with the words after the file name as its command-line arguments (sys.argv) and the name=value pairs as variables, and returns the variables named in outvar. Each run starts with fresh variables. Python calls can be switched off by the program that hosts mylab (the interpreter's python_enabled setting, or the environment variable MYLAB_PYTHON=0); they then stop with an error.

pyulear.description: Power spectral density from an autoregressive model fitted with the Yule-Walker equations (see aryule). nfft defaults to 256.

pzmap.description: Poles and zeros of a model. Without outputs they are plotted in the complex plane, poles as x and zeros as o, with the unit circle for a discrete-time model.

pzplot.description: Draws the pole-zero map; same as pzmap without outputs.

qmf.description: Quadrature mirror filter: x reversed with the sign of every second element changed (the even positions when p is even, the odd ones otherwise).

usage: x = qmr(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
qmr.description: Solves A*x = b with the quasi-minimal residual method. A function handle is called as afun(x, 'notransp') for A*x and afun(x, 'transp') for A'*x.

qqplot.description: Quantile-quantile plot: quantiles of x against standard normal quantiles, against the quantiles of a second sample y, or against a probability distribution object, with a reference line through the quartiles.

qr.description: QR factorization A = Q*R with Q orthogonal and R upper triangular. Any second argument (such as 0 or 'econ') gives the economy-size version. Column pivoting is not supported.

qrdelete.description: QR factorization of the matrix obtained from A = Q*R by removing column j, or ('row') row j.

qrinsert.description: QR factorization of the matrix obtained from A = Q*R by inserting the column x before column j, or ('row') the row x before row j.

qrupdate.description: QR factorization of A + u*v', computed from the factorization A = Q*R without starting again. u and v are column vectors.

usage: [q, fcnt] = quad(f, a, b, tol, trace)
quad.description: Adaptive Simpson quadrature of a vectorised function over a finite interval, to an absolute tolerance (default 1e-6). fcnt is the number of function evaluations.

usage: q = quad2d(f, a, b, c, d)
[q, errbnd] = quad2d(f, a, b, c, d, 'AbsTol', at, 'RelTol', rt)
quad2d.description: Double integral of f(x, y) over a <= x <= b, c(x) <= y <= d(x) by adaptive tiling. Options: AbsTol (1e-5), RelTol, MaxFunEvals (2000) and Singular (true: use a change of variable that weakens boundary singularities).

usage: [q, errbnd] = quadgk(f, a, b, 'RelTol', rt, 'AbsTol', at)
q = quadgk(f, a, b, 'Waypoints', w, 'MaxIntervalCount', n)
quadgk.description: Adaptive Gauss-Kronrod (7, 15) quadrature of a vectorised function, with infinite limits, end-point singularities and complex contours. errbnd is an estimate of the absolute error.

usage: [q, fcnt] = quadl(f, a, b, tol, trace)
quadl.description: Adaptive Gauss-Lobatto quadrature of a vectorised function over a finite interval, to an absolute tolerance (default 1e-6).

usage: x = quadprog(H, f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = quadprog(H, f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, x0)
quadprog.description: Quadratic programming: minimizes 0.5*x'*H*x + f'*x subject to linear constraints and bounds. Without constraints and with H positive definite the minimum is solved directly; otherwise a sequential quadratic programming method is used, which finds a local minimum. Options are ignored.

quadv.description: Adaptive Simpson quadrature of an array-valued function f(x) of a scalar x.

quantile.description: Quantiles for probabilities p (0..1), computed the same way as prctile.

quarter.description: Quarter of the year (1-4) of each element of a datetime array.

quat2eul.description: Euler angles of a quaternion. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first. seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors.

quat2rotm.description: Rotation matrix of a quaternion; the quaternion is normalized first. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first.

quat2tform.description: 4-by-4 transform with the rotation of a quaternion and no translation. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first.

usage: answer = questdlg(question, title, btn1, btn2, default)
answer = questdlg(question, title, btn1, btn2, btn3, default)
questdlg.description: Asks a question with up to three choices ('Yes', 'No', 'Cancel' unless others are given) and returns the chosen text. In a terminal or notebook the question is asked as text; when nobody can answer (for example in a batch run) the default is used and a note is printed. Type the number or the name of a choice; an empty reply picks the default.

quit.description: Ends the mylab session, optionally with a numeric exit status for the operating system.

quiver.description: Draws arrows with components (U, V) starting at the points (X, Y), or on a grid of indices. Arrows are scaled automatically to fit between grid points; scale multiplies that factor and 0 turns scaling off ('AutoScale', 'off' does the same).

usage: quiver3(X, Y, Z, U, V, W)
quiver3.description: Draws 3-D arrows with components (U, V, W) at the points (X, Y, Z). Arrow lengths are scaled to fit; scale stretches them, and 0 or 'AutoScale', 'off' draws them at true length.

usage: [AA, BB, Q, Z, V, W] = qz(A, B)
qz.description: Generalized Schur (QZ) factorization of two square matrices: Q*A*Z = AA and Q*B*Z = BB, with Q and Z unitary. By default the result is complex with triangular AA and BB; 'real' keeps real matrices real, with AA quasi-triangular. V and W hold the right and left generalized eigenvectors.

rad2deg.description: Converts angles from radians to degrees (multiplies by 180/pi).

radon.description: Radon transform: each column of R holds the sums of the image along parallel lines for one angle (degrees, 0:179 by default). xp gives the distance of each row from the centre pixel.

rand.description: Uniformly distributed random numbers between 0 and 1. The class is double, or single when asked for by name or through a 'like' prototype. After rng(seed) the numbers are the ones MATLAB's default generator (the Mersenne Twister) returns for that seed, and arrays are filled column by column from the same stream. The old generator syntaxes are accepted too: s = rand('state') and s = rand('twister') return the whole generator state (625 values; double for 'state', uint32 for 'twister'), s = rand('seed') returns a scalar seed (the stream restarts from it), and rand(word, s) with any of the three words puts that state or seed back, so the same numbers follow. A scalar s seeds the generator as rng(s) does. rand and randn share the one generator rng controls, and the numbers are not those of MATLAB's retired 'state' and 'seed' generators.

randg.description: Gamma-distributed random numbers with shape A and scale 1. A can be a scalar or an array the size of the result; A = 0 gives 0 and a negative or NaN shape gives NaN. Multiply by b for scale b. The numbers come from the same generator as rand and randn (see rng), so they are reproducible after rng(seed), but they are not the same numbers MATLAB draws.

randi.description: Uniformly distributed random integers from 1 to imax, or from imin to imax. The result is double unless a numeric class name is given. After rng(seed) the numbers are the ones MATLAB's default generator (the Mersenne Twister) returns for that seed, and arrays are filled column by column from the same stream.

randn.description: Normally distributed random numbers with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. After rng(seed) the numbers are the ones MATLAB's default generator (the Mersenne Twister) returns for that seed, and arrays are filled column by column from the same stream. The old generator syntaxes are accepted too: s = randn('state') and s = randn('twister') return the whole generator state (625 values; double for 'state', uint32 for 'twister'), s = randn('seed') returns a scalar seed (the stream restarts from it), and randn(word, s) with any of the three words puts that state or seed back, so the same numbers follow. A scalar s seeds the generator as rng(s) does. rand and randn share the one generator rng controls, and the numbers are not those of MATLAB's retired 'state' and 'seed' generators.

usage: r = random(name, a, b, m, n)
random.description: Random numbers from the distribution with that name, e.g. random('Normal', 0, 1, 3, 2) or random('Poisson', 4). Names: Normal, Uniform, Exponential, Poisson, Binomial, Gamma, Beta, Chisquare, T, F, Lognormal, Weibull, Rayleigh, Geometric, Negative Binomial, Discrete Uniform. The parameters and size arguments are those of the matching function (normrnd, unifrnd, ...).

randperm.description: A random permutation of 1:n, or k different numbers drawn from it. The permutation of all n numbers is the one MATLAB returns for the same seed.

randsample.description: Random sample of k values from 1..n or from the elements of a population vector, without replacement unless replace is true. Weights w make the draw weighted (and with replacement unless replace is given as false). Uses the generator controlled by rng.

range.description: max minus min along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

rangefilt.description: Difference between the largest and smallest value in the neighbourhood of each pixel (3-by-3 by default).

rangesearch.description: For each row of Y, the rows of X within distance r (as cell arrays, nearest first).

rank.description: Number of linearly independent rows or columns, estimated from the singular values. A tolerance argument is not supported.

usage: [p, h, stats] = ranksum(x, y, Name, Value)
ranksum.description: Wilcoxon rank sum test (equivalent to the Mann-Whitney U test), a non-parametric test that two samples have equal medians. Two-sided only. Uses the exact distribution for small samples without ties and a normal approximation otherwise ('method' 'exact' or 'approximate' overrides). 'alpha' sets the level for h.
