rat.description: Rational approximation by continued fractions: n./d is close to x, within tol (default 1e-6*norm(x(:), 1)). With one output it returns the continued fraction as text, for example rat(pi) is '3 + 1/(7 + 1/16)'.

rats.description: Text with each element of x written as a ratio of small integers that approximates it, for example rats(0.75) shows 3/4 and rats(pi) shows 355/113. len is the room given to each element (13 by default); a larger len allows closer approximations. A value too small to show next to the others is shown as an asterisk. See rat for the numerator and denominator as numbers.

raylcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the Rayleigh distribution with scale b (default 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

raylfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of the scale of the Rayleigh distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05).

raylinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the Rayleigh distribution with scale b (default 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

raylpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the Rayleigh distribution with scale b (default 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

raylrnd.description: Random numbers from the Rayleigh distribution with scale b (default 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

raylstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the Rayleigh distribution with scale b (default 1).

rc2poly.description: Prediction polynomial from reflection coefficients (the step-up recursion).

rceps.description: Real cepstrum: the inverse FFT of the logarithm of the magnitude spectrum. ym is the minimum-phase signal with the same magnitude spectrum.

rcond.description: Estimate of the reciprocal condition number of the square matrix A in the 1-norm. Near 1 means well conditioned; near 0 (about eps or less) means A is singular to working precision.

rdivide.description: Same as A ./ B (element-wise right division).

read.description: Reads the next block of a datastore and moves its read position on: one image (or a column cell array of ReadSize images) for an image datastore, the next rows as a table for a tabular text datastore. info describes what was read (Filename, FileSize and, for images, Label). Reading past the end is an error; check hasdata first or call reset. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.read(...).

readFrame.description: The next frame of a VideoReader object as a uint8 image; see VideoReader. It is an error when no frame is left, so test hasFrame(v) first.

readall.description: Reads all the data of a datastore without moving its read position: a column cell array of images for an image datastore, one table for a tabular text datastore. For transformed and combined datastores, tables and cell arrays from each read are stacked vertically and other values are collected in a column cell array. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.readall(...).

readcell.description: Reads a delimited text file (or a spreadsheet) into a cell array with one cell per field: numbers as numbers, dates and times as datetime and duration values, other text as character vectors (strings with 'TextType', 'string'), and empty fields as missing. Options (name-value pairs): 'Delimiter' (a character, a name such as 'tab' or 'comma', or a cell array), 'NumHeaderLines', 'Range' (a corner 'B2', a block 'A2:C5', rows '2:5' or [row1 col1 row2 col2]), 'DecimalSeparator', 'ThousandsSeparator', 'TreatAsMissing', 'TrimNonNumeric', 'CommentStyle', 'Encoding', 'LineEnding', 'EmptyLineRule', 'ConsecutiveDelimitersRule', 'LeadingDelimitersRule', 'TrailingDelimitersRule', 'ExtraColumnsRule', 'ExpectedNumVariables', 'DataLines' and 'VariableNamesLine'. An unknown option is an error. Without 'Delimiter' the delimiter is found by trying comma, tab, semicolon, bar and white space; lines above the table that do not have its number of fields are skipped. 'DatetimeType' and 'DurationType' set to 'text' keep dates and times as text.

readimage.description: Reads the k-th file of an image datastore with its ReadFcn, without moving the read position. info is a struct with Filename, FileSize (bytes) and Label (empty when the datastore has no labels). Also callable as ds.readimage(k).

readlines.description: Reads a text file into a string column, one element per line (a final line break does not add an empty line).

readmatrix.description: Reads a delimited text file (or a spreadsheet) into a numeric matrix. Text lines at the top are skipped, and fields that are empty or not numbers become NaN. Options (name-value pairs): 'Delimiter' (a character, a name such as 'tab' or 'comma', or a cell array), 'NumHeaderLines', 'Range' (a corner 'B2', a block 'A2:C5', rows '2:5' or [row1 col1 row2 col2]), 'DecimalSeparator', 'ThousandsSeparator', 'TreatAsMissing', 'TrimNonNumeric', 'CommentStyle', 'Encoding', 'LineEnding', 'EmptyLineRule', 'ConsecutiveDelimitersRule', 'LeadingDelimitersRule', 'TrailingDelimitersRule', 'ExtraColumnsRule', 'ExpectedNumVariables', 'DataLines' and 'VariableNamesLine'. An unknown option is an error. Without 'Delimiter' the delimiter is found by trying comma, tab, semicolon, bar and white space; lines above the table that do not have its number of fields are skipped. 'OutputType' returns another class instead of double: 'single', an integer class, 'string', 'char' (a cell array), 'datetime', 'duration' or 'categorical'.

readstruct.description: Reads an XML or JSON file into a structure. In XML, child elements become fields, repeated elements become arrays (struct arrays, numeric rows or string arrays), attributes become fields whose name ends in 'Attribute' (or the given suffix), and the text of an element that also has attributes or children is its field Text. Text that is a number or true/false is converted; other text is returned as strings. A JSON file must hold an object; its text also becomes strings. The file type follows the extension unless 'FileType' is given.

readtable.description: Reads a delimited text file (or a spreadsheet, see the Sheet and Range options there) into a table. A first line of text gives the variable names, made into valid names unless 'VariableNamingRule' is 'preserve'. Each column becomes numbers, datetime, duration or text, whichever fits all its fields; empty fields are NaN, NaT or ''. Options (name-value pairs): 'Delimiter' (a character, a name such as 'tab' or 'comma', or a cell array), 'NumHeaderLines', 'Range' (a corner 'B2', a block 'A2:C5', rows '2:5' or [row1 col1 row2 col2]), 'DecimalSeparator', 'ThousandsSeparator', 'TreatAsMissing', 'TrimNonNumeric', 'CommentStyle', 'Encoding', 'LineEnding', 'EmptyLineRule', 'ConsecutiveDelimitersRule', 'LeadingDelimitersRule', 'TrailingDelimitersRule', 'ExtraColumnsRule', 'ExpectedNumVariables', 'DataLines' and 'VariableNamesLine'. An unknown option is an error. Without 'Delimiter' the delimiter is found by trying comma, tab, semicolon, bar and white space; lines above the table that do not have its number of fields are skipped. Further options: 'ReadVariableNames', 'ReadRowNames', 'TextType' ('char' or 'string'), 'DatetimeType' and 'DurationType' ('text' to keep them as text), 'MissingRule' and 'ImportErrorRule' ('fill', 'error', 'omitrow', 'omitvar'), and 'Format' with one conversion per column (%f, %d, %s, %q, %D, %C, %T, %*s to skip). opts is an object from detectImportOptions.

reallog.description: Natural logarithm that raises an error for negative input instead of returning a complex number.

realmax.description: Largest finite double-precision number, about 1.7977e308. realmax('single') is the largest single, about 3.4028e38.

realmin.description: Smallest positive normalized double-precision number, about 2.2251e-308. realmin('single') is the single-precision one, about 1.1755e-38.

realpow.description: Element-wise power x.^y that raises an error when the result would be complex.

realsqrt.description: Square root of each element. Unlike sqrt, it raises an error when an element is negative instead of returning a complex number.

rectangle.description: Adds a rectangle with lower-left corner (x, y), width w and height h to the current axes. Curvature rounds the corners: 0 is square, [1 1] gives an ellipse (a circle when w equals h). Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, LineWidth, LineStyle. Example: rectangle('Position', [0 0 2 2], 'Curvature', [1 1], 'FaceColor', 'r'); axis equal

rectint.description: Overlap area of rectangles given as rows [x y width height]. A(i, j) is the area shared by R1(i, :) and R2(j, :).

rectpuls.description: Rectangular pulse of width w (default 1) centred on 0: one for -w/2 <= t < w/2, else zero.

rectwin.description: Rectangular window: a column of n ones.

reducepatch.description: A mesh with fewer faces (a fraction r of them, or about r faces if r > 1).

refresh.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. Options such as limitrate are accepted. Where there is no live window (browser app, Jupyter, MCP, --no-plots) each call records a snapshot of the current figure, and the snapshots of a run are returned as an animated GIF. shg and refresh do the same.

refreshdata.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. Update a plot by setting XData and YData on its handle.

usage: rsys = reg(sys, K, L, sensors, known, controls)
reg.description: Regulator made of a state-feedback gain K and an estimator gain L (u = -K*xhat). rsys maps the measurements to the control inputs and is meant to be connected with positive feedback: feedback(sys, rsys, +1).

usage: [st, en, te, mat, tok, nm, sp] = regexp(s, expr)
regexp.description: Regular-expression search. Keywords 'match', 'tokens', 'names', 'start', 'end' and 'split' choose which results are returned, in the order given; without them the outputs are start indices, end indices, token extents (always empty in mylab), matches, tokens, named tokens and split pieces. 'once' returns only the first match, not wrapped in a cell. Named groups are written (?<name>...); 'names' gives a 1-by-N struct array with one element per match (a scalar struct with 'once'). Matching uses Python's regex engine, so rare constructs may differ. A cell array s gives a cell of results.

regexpPattern.description: A pattern that matches the regular expression expr. Options: 'IgnoreCase', 'DotExceptNewline', 'MultilineAnchors' and 'FreeSpacing' (true or false). Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

regexpi.description: Case-insensitive form of regexp: the same outputs and options, but letters match regardless of case.

regexprep.description: Replaces every match of a regular expression. In the replacement, $1, $2, ... insert captured groups and $0 the whole match. 'once' replaces only the first match. s may be a cell array or string array. Example: regexprep('abc', '(b)', '[$1]') is 'a[b]c'.

regexptranslate.description: Rewrites text for use in a regular expression. 'escape' puts a backslash before every special character so that the text is matched literally. 'wildcard' turns the wildcards * and ? into .* and . and escapes dots. 'flexible' replaces every character that is not a letter, digit or underscore by expr.

regionprops.description: Measures the regions of a binary image (8-connected groups), a label matrix or a bwconncomp struct and returns a struct array with one element per region, or with 'table' as first input a table with one row per region. Properties: Area, Centroid ([x y]), BoundingBox ([left top width height], measured from pixel edges), MajorAxisLength, MinorAxisLength, Eccentricity, Orientation (of the ellipse with the same second moments), EquivDiameter, Extent, Perimeter, Circularity, Image, FilledImage, FilledArea, EulerNumber, ConvexHull ([x y] corners), ConvexImage, ConvexArea, Solidity (Area / ConvexArea), Extrema, PixelIdxList, PixelList and SubarrayIdx; with a grayscale image I also MeanIntensity, MinIntensity, MaxIntensity, PixelValues and WeightedCentroid. The default is 'basic' (Area, Centroid, BoundingBox); 'all' gives everything listed. Perimeter is estimated from the chain of boundary pixels (with the usual correction for diagonal steps and corners) and can differ a little from other implementations.

regionprops3.description: Measurements of the objects in a volume, returned as a table with one row per object: 'Volume', 'Centroid', 'BoundingBox', 'EquivDiameter', 'Extent', 'VoxelIdxList', 'VoxelList', 'Image', and with an intensity volume 'MeanIntensity', 'MinIntensity', 'MaxIntensity' and 'VoxelValues'.

regions.description: The regions of p as a column of polyshapes, each a solid boundary with the holes inside it. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.regions(...).

registerApp.description: Part of the code App Designer exports: notes that fig is the window of the app object. mylab runs exported app classes (classdef MyApp < matlab.apps.AppBase).

usage: [b, bint, r, rint, stats] = regress(y, X)
regress.description: Multiple linear regression by least squares: finds b so that X*b best fits y. Include a column of ones in X to fit an intercept. bint gives 100*(1-alpha)% confidence intervals for b, r the residuals, rint residual intervals and stats = [R^2, F, p-value, error variance]. Rows containing NaN are ignored. Example: b = regress(y, [ones(size(x)) x]) fits a line.

relieff.description: ReliefF (classification) or RReliefF (regression) predictor importance from k nearest neighbours; ranks lists the predictors from most to least important.

rem.description: Remainder after division, defined as a - fix(a./b).*b, so a nonzero result has the sign of a. rem(a, 0) is NaN. Example: rem(-1, 3) is -1.

remove.description: Removes a key (or a cell array of keys) and its value from the containers.Map m.

removecats.description: Removes categories: the unused ones, or the named ones (their elements become <undefined>).

removetarget.description: Remove a graphics object from a property link made by linkprop.

removevars.description: Removes the named (or numbered) variables from a table.

renamecats.description: Renames categories of a categorical array.

reordercats.description: Changes the order of the categories (alphabetical by default). The elements keep their names.

reordernodes.description: Renumbers the nodes so that node order(k) becomes node k. idx maps the edges of H to the edges of G.

repelem.description: Repeats elements. For a vector v, each element is repeated n times (n may be a vector with one count per element). For a matrix, each row is repeated r times and each column c times. Example: repelem([1 2], [2 3]) is [1 1 2 2 2].

replace.description: Replaces every occurrence of the literal text old with new (no regular expressions). old may list several patterns, with new either one replacement for all or one per pattern; longer patterns win where they overlap. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

replaceBetween.description: Replaces the text between a start and an end marker by newText. Markers are text or patterns (every occurrence is replaced, the markers stay) or character positions (the characters at the positions are replaced too). 'Boundaries' is 'inclusive' or 'exclusive' and overrides that default.

repmat.description: Tiles A m times vertically and n times horizontally (n times both ways for a single n); further counts repeat it along higher dimensions. Works with numeric, logical, char, cell and struct arrays. Example: repmat([1 2], 2, 2) is [1 2 1 2; 1 2 1 2].

usage: y = resample(x, p, q, n, beta)
resample.description: Changes the sample rate by the factor p/q with a lowpass FIR filter and removes its delay; the result has ceil(length(x) p/q) samples. The filter uses n (default 10) samples on each side and a Kaiser window with parameter beta (default 5), or the coefficients b. n = 0 picks the nearest sample. With sample times tx the signal is first interpolated onto a uniform grid at fs ('linear', 'pchip' or 'spline').

rescale.description: Linearly maps the smallest element of x to l (default 0) and the largest to u (default 1), using all elements. InputMin and InputMax set the source range, clipping values outside it. Constant data maps to l.

reset.description: Moves the read position of a datastore back to the start. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.reset(...).

resetoptions.description: Put one or more settings of an optimoptions object back to their default values.

reshape.description: Rearranges the elements of A into an array of the given size, reading and writing in column-major order. One size may be given as [] and is computed from the element count, which must not change. Works on cells and structs too. Example: reshape(1:6, 2, 3) is [1 3 5; 2 4 6].

residue.description: Partial fraction expansion of b(s)/a(s): residues r, poles p and direct (polynomial) term k. For a pole repeated m times the residues are those of 1/(s-p), 1/(s-p)^2, ... in that order. With three inputs it converts back to the two polynomials.

residuez.description: Partial fraction expansion of a ratio of polynomials in z^-1 (a discrete-time transfer function): b(z)/a(z) = sum of r(i)/(1 - p(i)*z^-1) plus k(1) + k(2)*z^-1 + ... With three inputs it converts back.

rethrow.description: Throws again an error caught with try/catch; err is a struct with message and identifier fields, such as the variable from catch err.

retime.description: Moves the data of a timetable to new row times. newTimeStep is 'yearly', 'quarterly', 'monthly', 'weekly', 'daily', 'hourly', 'minutely' or 'secondly'; newTimes is a datetime or duration vector. Methods: 'fillwithmissing' (default: a value only where an old row time equals the new one), 'fillwithconstant' (with 'Constant', value), 'previous', 'next', 'nearest', the interpolations 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip', 'makima' (which extrapolate beyond the data unless 'EndValues' gives a constant), and the aggregations 'sum', 'mean', 'prod', 'min', 'max', 'count', 'firstvalue', 'lastvalue' or a function handle. For an aggregation each new row time starts a bin that ends at the next one; the last bin of a time step such as 'daily' is a whole step, while the last of a list of times holds only the data at exactly that time.

reverse.description: Reverses the order of the characters. Example: reverse('abc') is 'cba'.

rewrite.description: Rewrites an expression in terms of another function. Targets include 'exp', 'sin', 'cos', 'tan', 'log', 'sincos', 'sqrt' and 'heaviside'.

rgb2gray.description: Grayscale version of an RGB image, the weighted sum 0.2989 R + 0.5870 G + 0.1140 B, in the class of the input. A colormap is converted to a gray colormap. im2gray is the same but also accepts images that are already grayscale.

rgb2hsv.description: Converts colours from red-green-blue to hue-saturation-value. The result is double with all three components between 0 and 1; integer images are rescaled first.

rgb2ind.description: Converts an RGB image to an indexed image. With a number, at most n colours are chosen (exactly, when the picture has no more than n; otherwise by median-cut quantization); with a colormap every pixel gets the nearest colour in it. X is zero-based uint8 for up to 256 colours. No dithering is applied.

rgb2lab.description: Converts RGB colours to CIE 1976 L*a*b*: L from 0 to 100, a (green to red) and b (blue to yellow). Integer images are scaled to 0..1 first. The input is an M-by-3 list of colours or an M-by-N-by-3 image; the result has the same shape. 'WhitePoint' names the reference white ('d65' by default; also 'd50', 'd55', 'a', 'c', 'e', 'icc', 'f2', 'f7', 'f11' or [X Y Z]) and 'ColorSpace' the kind of RGB ('srgb', 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb').

rgb2ntsc.description: Converts RGB to the NTSC colour space: luminance Y and the two chrominance values I and Q. The result is double.

rgb2xyz.description: Converts RGB colours to CIE 1931 XYZ (Y = 1 for white). The input is an M-by-3 list of colours or an M-by-N-by-3 image; the result has the same shape. 'WhitePoint' names the reference white ('d65' by default; also 'd50', 'd55', 'a', 'c', 'e', 'icc', 'f2', 'f7', 'f11' or [X Y Z]) and 'ColorSpace' the kind of RGB ('srgb', 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb').

rgb2ycbcr.description: Converts RGB to the YCbCr colour space of digital video (ITU-R BT.601): luma from 16 to 235 and chroma from 16 to 240 on the uint8 scale, or the same divided by 255 for double images. The result has the class of the input.

rgbplot.description: Plot the red, green and blue columns of a colormap.

rhs.description: Right side of a symbolic equation or inequality.

ribbon.description: Draws each column of Y as a flat strip in 3-D, side by side, against x (default 1, 2, ...). width (default 0.75) is the strip width.

ridge.description: Ridge regression for each ridge parameter in k. With scaled = 1 (default) the coefficients refer to centred predictors scaled to unit standard deviation; with scaled = 0 they are on the original scale with the constant term first.

rigidtform2d.description: Rotation by an angle in degrees (or a rotation matrix R) followed by a translation. Properties: RotationAngle, Translation, R and A.

rindex.description: Position of the last occurrence of the text t in s, or 0. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

risetime.description: Time each rising edge of a two-level waveform takes to go from the lower to the upper reference level (10% and 90% of the way between the two state levels by default). lt and ut are the crossing times, ll and ul the levels. 'StateLevels' gives the low and high levels instead of estimating them.

rlim.description: Set or return the radius limits of polar axes.

rlocus.description: Root locus: the closed-loop poles of the unity negative feedback loop around k*sys as the gain k goes from 0 to infinity. r has one row per branch and one column per gain. Without k the gains are chosen so that the branches are smooth and the points where branches meet are included.

rlocusplot.description: Draws the root locus; same arguments as rlocus.

rltool.description: Root-locus design app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

rmappdata.description: Removes the value stored under name on h; an error if it is missing.

rmboundary.description: p without the boundaries I. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.rmboundary(...).

rmdir.description: Removes an empty folder, or with 's' the folder and everything in it. With outputs, failure is reported through status and msg instead of an error.

rmedge.description: Removes the edges between the node pairs (s, t), or the edges with the given indices.

rmfield.description: Returns a copy of the struct without the named field(s). Naming a missing field is an error.

rmholes.description: p without its holes. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.rmholes(...).

rmmissing.description: Removes missing entries: NaN in numeric data, empty char vectors in cell arrays, <missing> strings. A vector loses the missing elements, a matrix or table the rows (or columns, with dim 2) that contain at least n missing values (default 1). TF marks what was removed.

rmnode.description: Removes nodes and every edge that touches them. The remaining nodes are renumbered.

rmoutliers.description: Removes outliers from a vector, or the rows (dim 1) or columns (dim 2) of a matrix that contain outliers. The detection options are those of isoutlier.

rmpath.description: Removes folders from the search path.

rmpref.description: Removes a preference group or one preference from it.

rms.description: Root mean square: sqrt(mean(abs(x).^2)) along the first non-singleton dimension, a chosen dimension, several dimensions or all elements.

rmslivers.description: Removes thin spikes and slits: vertices closer than tol to the line through their neighbours are dropped, and boundaries narrower than tol vanish. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.rmslivers(...).

rng.description: Seeds the random number generator. rng(seed) and rng('default') (seed 0) make rand, randn, randi and randperm repeat the same numbers, and they are the numbers MATLAB gives for that seed with its default generator, the Mersenne Twister. A new session starts as after rng('default'). rng('shuffle') seeds from the clock. s = rng returns the settings (Type, Seed, State) and rng(s) restores them. Other generator names are accepted and recorded, but the numbers always come from the Mersenne Twister.

usage: [b, stats] = robustfit(X, y, wfun, tune, const)
robustfit.description: Robust linear regression by iteratively reweighted least squares (a constant term is added unless const is 'off'). wfun is 'bisquare' (default), 'andrews', 'cauchy', 'fair', 'huber', 'logistic', 'ols', 'talwar' or 'welsch'. stats has the scale estimates, se, t, p, the final weights w and the residuals.

roots.description: Roots of the polynomial with coefficients p, as a column vector (possibly complex).

rose.description: An angle histogram; with outputs, [tout, rout] trace its outline for polar.

rosser.description: The 8-by-8 Rosser matrix, a classic symmetric test matrix for eigenvalue algorithms (a double eigenvalue, three nearly equal ones and a zero eigenvalue).

rot90.description: Rotates a matrix by 90 degrees counter-clockwise, k times (negative k rotates clockwise). Example: rot90([1 2; 3 4]) is [2 4; 1 3].

rotate.description: p turned counterclockwise by theta degrees about the origin or the given point. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.rotate(...).

rotate3d.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab. Use view(az, el) to turn a 3-D plot.

rotm2axang.description: Axis and angle [x y z angle] of a rotation matrix; the angle is between 0 and pi. For no rotation the axis is [0 0 1].

rotm2eul.description: Euler angles of a 3-by-3 rotation matrix, as a row. seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors. At the singular orientation the first angle is set to 0.

rotm2quat.description: Quaternion of a 3-by-3 rotation matrix, with a scalar part that is not negative. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first.

rotm2tform.description: Puts a 3-by-3 rotation matrix into a 4-by-4 transform with no translation. A transform is a 4-by-4 matrix [R t; 0 0 0 1].

rotx.description: 3-by-3 matrix for a rotation by deg degrees about the x axis.

roty.description: 3-by-3 matrix for a rotation by deg degrees about the y axis.

rotz.description: 3-by-3 matrix for a rotation by deg degrees about the z axis.

round.description: Rounds to the nearest integer, with halves going away from zero (round(2.5) is 3, round(-2.5) is -3). With n, rounds to n digits after the decimal point; negative n rounds to tens, hundreds and so on. With 'significant', n counts significant digits instead (round(1234, 2, 'significant') is 1200). 'TieBreaker' says where a value exactly halfway between two candidates goes: 'fromzero' (the default), 'tozero', 'even', 'odd', 'plusinf' (up) or 'minusinf' (down); round(2.5, 'TieBreaker', 'even') is 2. Integer-class input keeps its class and is unchanged unless n is negative. Complex values are rounded part by part.

rowfun.description: Calls func once for every row of the table A, with the variables as separate inputs, and collects the results in a table. Options: 'InputVariables', 'GroupingVariables' (func is then called once per group, with the rows of the group), 'OutputVariableNames', 'NumOutputs', 'SeparateInputs' (false passes one row vector), 'ExtractCellContents', 'OutputFormat' ('table', 'uniform', 'cell') and 'ErrorHandler'. Variables are selected by name, by number, with a logical vector, with vartype(...) or with a function handle such as @isnumeric.

rows.description: Number of rows of a, the same as size(a, 1). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

rows2vars.description: Transposes a numeric table: each original row becomes a variable, and a first variable OriginalVariableNames lists the old column names.

rref.description: Reduced row echelon form of a symbolic matrix.

rssq.description: Square root of the sum of squared magnitudes.

rtickangle.description: Set or return the rotation of the radius tick labels, in degrees.

rtickformat.description: Set or return the number format of the radius tick labels, for example '%.1f' or 'usd'.

rticklabels.description: Set or return the labels of the radius ticks of polar axes.

rticks.description: Set or return where the radius tick marks of polar axes are.

ruler2num.description: Convert dates, durations or categories to the plain numbers an axis uses for them.

run.description: Runs a script file (with or without the .m extension) in the current workspace, so its variables stay available afterwards. The script's folder is added to the search path.

runStartupFcn.description: Part of the code App Designer exports: calls the app's startup method.

runstest.description: Runs test for randomness: counts runs of values above and below v (default the mean), or runs up and down with v = 'ud'. Exact for 50 or fewer values. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

runtests.description: Runs tests and returns an array of TestResult objects (Name, Passed, Failed, Incomplete, Duration, Details; table(results) gives a table). tests is the name of a test file, test class, folder or package, 'File/testName' for one test, or a cell array of these; with no input every test file in the current folder runs. A test file is function-based (its main function returns functiontests(localfunctions)), class-based (a classdef derived from matlab.unittest.TestCase) or script-based (sections started by %%). Selection options: 'Name', 'ProcedureName', 'Tag', 'ParameterProperty', 'ParameterName', 'BaseFolder', 'Superclass' (wildcards * and ? allowed) and 'IncludeSubfolders'. 'OutputDetail' (0 to 4 or None/Terse/Concise/Detailed/Verbose) sets how much is printed and 'LoggingLevel' which log(testCase, ...) messages are shown. Progress is printed as 'Running Name', one dot per test and 'Done Name'; a failing test prints its diagnostics with the actual and expected values.

sampsizepwr.description: Sample size, power or detectable alternative for the tests 'z', 't', 't2', 'var', 'p' and 'p2'. For the mean tests p0 is [mean, standard deviation]. Options: 'Alpha', 'Tail' and 'Ratio' (two-sample tests).

save.description: Saves variables of the workspace to a MAT-file (matlab.mat when no name is given; .mat is added to a name without extension). Names may contain * and ? wildcards, and -regexp is followed by regular expressions. -struct saves the fields of a scalar struct as separate variables. -append adds to an existing file, replacing variables of the same name. Formats: -v7 (the default, compressed), -v6 and -nocompression (uncompressed), -v4, -v7.3 (an HDF5 file in MATLAB's layout, written with h5py) and -ascii (text with 8 digits, or 16 with -double, tab-separated with -tabs; numeric and char arrays only). All numeric classes, logical, char, complex and sparse arrays, cells, structs and struct arrays are stored in the standard way, so MATLAB and Octave read them. String arrays, tables and timetables (with their properties), datetime, duration, calendarDuration, categorical, containers.Map, dictionaries, MException, function handles and classdef objects are stored as structs marked with the field mylab_class_: mylab restores them on load, other programs see the struct. An object is stored with its class name and the values of its properties other than Transient, Dependent and Constant ones (or what saveobj returns, when the class defines it), its dynamic properties and, for a class derived from a built-in type, its built-in value. A handle object met more than once in one save call, in one variable or several, is stored once, so it is one object again after load. A value that cannot be stored (a figure handle, for example) is an error that names the variable; nothing is skipped.

save_system.description: Writes a model to name.mlb.json, a readable JSON file, in the current folder (or back to the file it was loaded from). With a second name the model is renamed and saved under that name. mylab does not write .slx files.

saveas.description: Saves a figure, given as a handle (e.g. gcf) or a figure number, as an image file at 150 dpi. The type comes from the file extension (png, pdf, svg, jpg, eps, tif) or from format when the name has no extension. The .fig format is not supported and gives an error.

savefig.description: The .fig figure format is not supported; this raises an error. Save figures with saveas, print or exportgraphics as .png, .pdf or .svg instead.

sawtooth.description: Sawtooth wave with period 2*pi running between -1 and 1. width (0..1, default 1) sets where in the period the peak is; 0.5 gives a triangle wave.

scale.description: p stretched by the factor s (or sx and sy) about the origin or the given point. A negative factor mirrors the shape. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.scale(...).

scatter.description: Draws a marker at each point (x, y). sz is the marker area (default 36), scalar or per point; c is a colour name, an RGB triplet or one value per point mapped through the colormap. Markers are hollow unless 'filled' is given. Options: DisplayName, MarkerFaceColor, MarkerEdgeColor, LineWidth, MarkerFaceAlpha. s is a Scatter handle with properties such as XData, YData, SizeData and CData.

scatter3.description: Draws a marker at each 3-D point (x, y, z) on 3-D axes.

scatteredInterpolant.description: Builds an interpolating function from scattered samples; call it like a function: vq = F(xq, yq) or F(Pq). method is 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'natural' (treated as linear). extrapolation is 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'none' (NaN outside the samples). Linear extrapolation extends the plane of the nearest triangle, which approximates MATLAB's result. Properties Points, Values, Method and ExtrapolationMethod can be read and changed.

usage: scatterhistogram(tbl, xvar, yvar) or scatterhistogram(x, y)
scatterhistogram.description: A scatter plot with marginal histograms.

schur.description: Schur form of a square matrix: A = U*T*U' with U unitary. For a real A the default is the real form, where T is quasi-triangular (2-by-2 blocks for complex eigenvalue pairs); 'complex' gives a triangular T with the eigenvalues on its diagonal.

secd.description: Secant of an angle in degrees.

second.description: Seconds, including any fraction, of each element of a datetime array.

seconds.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many seconds. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of seconds.

semilogx.description: Like plot, but with a logarithmic x axis.

semilogy.description: Like plot, but with a logarithmic y axis.

sequentialfs.description: Sequential feature selection: columns of X are added (or removed with 'direction', 'backward') while the cross-validated criterion fun(XTRAIN, ytrain, XTEST, ytest) improves. Options: 'cv', 'nfeatures', 'keepin', 'keepout'.

series.description: Series connection: the outputs of sys1 drive the inputs of sys2, which is sys2*sys1. The index vectors connect only the listed outputs of sys1 to the listed inputs of sys2.

set.description: Changes properties of graphics handles, e.g. set(h, 'LineWidth', 2, 'Color', 'r'). If h holds several handles each one is changed. A struct s of property values is also accepted. set(0, 'DefaultLineLineWidth', w) and a few other root defaults change later plots. Dot assignment, e.g. h.LineWidth = 2, does the same for one property; on an array of handles it changes all of them, and reading a property from an array gives a cell array.

set_param.description: Changes parameters of a block, or settings of a model. Block values are text holding a MATLAB expression that is evaluated when the model runs; numbers are converted to text. Besides its own parameters every block has Name, Position ([left top right bottom]) and Orientation. Model settings: StartTime, StopTime, Solver, MaxStep, RelTol, AbsTol, FixedStep, ZeroCrossings. An unknown parameter name is an error that lists the names the block has.

setabstime.description: Sets the times of a timeseries from dates (text or datetime, one per sample, in increasing order): the first date becomes TimeInfo.StartDate.

setappdata.description: Stores a value under a name on the graphics object h (a figure, axes, ... or 0 for the root). Read it back with getappdata.

setcats.description: Sets the categories of c to the given list. Elements whose category is not in the list become <undefined>.

setdiff.description: Values in a that are not in b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given; c = a(ia). Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored.

setenv.description: Sets an environment variable for this session and for commands started with system. Without a value the variable is set to ''.

setfield.description: Returns a copy of the struct with a field set, the same as s.name = value. Several names reach into nested structs, creating them as needed, and cell arrays of subscripts index the value before them.

setinterpmethod.description: Sets the interpolation method of a timeseries: straight lines between samples, a zero-order hold, a function fh(newTimes, times, data) or a tsdata.interpolation object.

setoptions.description: Attach a fitoptions object to a fittype; fit then starts from these options.

setpixelposition.description: Set the position of a figure or axes in pixels.

setpref.description: Stores a preference value under a group name. In mylab preferences live in memory only and are forgotten when the session ends. addpref is the same.

setuniformtime.description: Replaces the times of a timeseries with evenly spaced ones; the data is unchanged.

setxor.description: Values found in exactly one of a and b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given. Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored.

sfdr.description: Spurious-free dynamic range: the ratio in dB of the fundamental to the largest other peak.

sfit.description: Surface fit object (fit with [x, y] data returns sfit objects). f(x, y) or f([x, y]) evaluates it; it has the cfit methods except integrate, and differentiate returns [fx, fy, fxx, fxy, fyy].

sgolay.description: Savitzky-Golay smoothing filters: row k of b gives the fitted value at position k of a frame of framelen samples from a least-squares polynomial of the given order; the middle row is the filter used away from the ends. Column n+1 of g gives the n-th derivative of the fit at the middle of the frame (to be scaled by n! and the sample spacing).

sgolayfilt.description: Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter: fits a polynomial of the given order to each window of framelen samples (odd, larger than order). Weights are not supported.

sgrid.description: Adds lines of constant damping ratio and circles of constant natural frequency to a pole-zero map or root locus in the s-plane.

sgtitle.description: Sets one title for the whole figure, above all subplots. suptitle does the same.

shading.description: Sets how surfaces are drawn: 'faceted' (the default) outlines each patch, 'flat' and 'interp' hide the grid lines. Applies to the surfaces in the current axes and to later surf calls. mylab draws 'interp' like 'flat' with smoothing.

sheetnames.description: Returns the worksheet names of an Excel file as a string array.

shg.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. Options such as limitrate are accepted. Where there is no live window (browser app, Jupyter, MCP, --no-plots) each call records a snapshot of the current figure, and the snapshots of a run are returned as an animated GIF. shg and refresh do the same.

shiftdim.description: Shifts the dimensions of an array. A positive n rotates them to the left (the first n move to the end); a negative n adds leading dimensions of length 1. With one input, leading dimensions of length 1 are removed and nshifts says how many.

shortestpath.description: Shortest path between two nodes: the nodes on it, its length and its edges. d is Inf and P is empty when t cannot be reached. Method is 'auto', 'unweighted', 'positive' (Dijkstra), 'mixed' (Bellman-Ford) or 'acyclic'.

shortestpathtree.description: Shortest paths from one node to all others (or to the nodes t; s may be 'all' with a single t). OutputForm 'tree' gives a digraph of the tree edges, 'cell' the paths as a cell array, 'vector' the predecessor of each node. D holds the distances and E marks the tree edges.

shuffle.description: A copy of a datastore with its files in random order (the global random number generator, rng, decides it), starting from the beginning. A combined datastore can be shuffled when it is made of image datastores with the same number of files; they keep their files paired. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.shuffle(...).

sigma.description: Singular values of the frequency response, one column per frequency, largest first. type 1 uses the inverse of the response, 2 uses I + response and 3 uses I + inverse (square models only). The optional second argument is a vector of frequencies in rad per time unit, or a range {wmin, wmax}; without it the frequencies are chosen from the poles and zeros (up to the Nyquist frequency pi/Ts for a discrete-time model).

sigmaplot.description: Draws the singular-value plot; same arguments as sigma.

sign.description: -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign of each element. For complex x, returns x./abs(x) (0 where x is 0).

signrank.description: Wilcoxon signed rank test of zero median for x (or for x - y). The exact distribution is used for 15 or fewer non-zero differences, a normal approximation otherwise ('Method'). stats has signedrank and, for the approximation, zval. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

signtest.description: Sign test of zero median for x (or for the differences x - y; y may be a scalar). The exact binomial distribution is used for fewer than 100 non-zero differences ('Method'). Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

silhouette.description: Silhouette value of each point: how much closer it is to its own cluster than to the nearest other one (between -1 and 1). The default distance is 'sqEuclidean'. Asking for the second output (or none) draws the silhouette plot.

sim.description: Simulates a block-diagram model over time. out.tout holds the times of the solver's steps and out.yout the signals of the top-level Out blocks, one column per element. Each To Workspace block adds a field named after its variable: a struct with Time and Data (or a plain array, depending on the block's format). out.scopes has one such struct per Scope, out.logsout one per logged line. Settings given as name, value pairs (or a struct, or options from simset) apply to this run only: StartTime, StopTime, Solver, MaxStep, RelTol, AbsTol, FixedStep, ZeroCrossings, ExternalInput ([t u1 u2 ...] for the top-level In blocks). Variable-step solvers: ode45 (default), ode23, ode113, ode15s and ode23s for stiff models. Fixed-step: ode1 (Euler), ode2, ode3, ode4 (Runge-Kutta), ode5. Block parameters are looked up in the base workspace, then in the workspace of the function that calls sim. Called without an output, sim stores out, tout, yout and the To Workspace variables in the workspace. Errors name the block they come from.

simget.description: The simulation settings stored in a model, as a struct of text values, or one of them.

simplify.description: Rewrites a symbolic expression in a simpler form, for example sin(x)^2 + cos(x)^2 becomes 1. Works on each element of a matrix and on both sides of an equation. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

simplifyFraction.description: Writes a symbolic expression as one fraction and cancels common factors.

simset.description: Makes an options struct for sim(model, tspan, options). The fields are the settings sim accepts.

simsizes.description: For level-1 S-functions used in block diagrams. Without an input: a struct with the fields NumContStates, NumDiscStates, NumOutputs, NumInputs, DirFeedthrough and NumSampleTimes, all 0, to fill in. With that struct: the vector the S-function returns for flag 0.

simtform2d.description: Similarity transformation: scaling, rotation by an angle in degrees and translation. Properties: Scale, RotationAngle, Translation, R and A.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output] = simulannealbnd(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
simulannealbnd.description: Minimise a function by simulated annealing: random steps that are sometimes accepted even when worse, less often as the 'temperature' falls.

sin.description: Sine of each element, with x in radians.

sinad.description: Ratio in dB of the fundamental to everything else except the mean (noise and distortion).

sinc.description: Normalized sinc function sin(pi*x)./(pi*x), with sinc(0) = 1.

sind.description: Sine of angles given in degrees. Multiples of 180 give exactly 0.

single.description: Converts to single precision (32-bit floating point).

sinhint.description: Hyperbolic sine integral: the integral of sinh(t)/t from 0 to x.

sinint.description: Sine integral: the integral of sin(t)/t from 0 to x.

sinpi.description: sin(pi*x), exact for integers and half-integers (sinpi(1) is 0, not 1.2e-16).

sisotool.description: SISO design app. This interactive app is not available; the function only reports that and points to the command-line functions that do the same work.

size.description: Dimensions of A. With one output, a row vector holding the length of every dimension; size(A, dim) gives one length (1 for a dimension beyond ndims(A)) and a vector of dims gives several. With several outputs, the last output absorbs all remaining dimensions (their product), so [r, c] = size(A) puts the product of dimensions 2 and up in c. Example: size(ones(2, 5, 3)) is [2 5 3].

skewness.description: Sample skewness, a measure of asymmetry (0 for symmetric data). flag 1 (default) gives the plain moment estimate, flag 0 the bias-corrected one. NaN values are ignored.

usage: slice(V, xslice, yslice, zslice) or slice(X, Y, Z, V, ...)

sminreal.description: Removes the states of a state-space model that are not connected to any input or output through nonzero matrix entries. Only the pattern of zeros matters, so no cancellation by rounding can occur.

smoothdata.description: Smooths noisy data along the first dimension whose size is not 1. method is 'movmean' (default), 'movmedian', 'gaussian' or 'sgolay' (Savitzky-Golay with polynomial degree d, default 2); the lowess/loess methods are not supported. Without a window, about a tenth of the data length is used, which may differ from other implementations. NaN values are ignored by default.

snr.description: Signal-to-noise ratio in dB. With two inputs x is the signal and y the noise. With one signal the largest spectral peak is taken as the signal and the noise is what remains after the first n (default 6) harmonics and the mean are removed, estimated from a Kaiser-windowed periodogram.

solve.description: Solves equations symbolically. An expression without == is set equal to zero. One unknown gives a column vector of solutions. A system gives one output per unknown, or with a single output a struct with one field per unknown. 'Real' keeps real solutions only. 'ReturnConditions' also returns parameters and conditions (always empty and true here: periodic solution families are not listed). Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

sort.description: Sorts in ascending order (or 'descend') along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. idx holds the original positions. Equal values keep their order; NaN goes last when ascending and first when descending; complex values sort by magnitude. Cell arrays of char vectors and string arrays are sorted alphabetically (by character code). Example: sort([3 1 2]) is [1 2 3].

sortboundaries.description: Reorders the boundaries by 'area', 'perimeter', 'numsides' or 'centroid' (distance of the boundary centroid from the reference point, the origin by default), 'ascend' or 'descend'. I gives the old positions. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.sortboundaries(...).

sortrows.description: Sorts the rows of a matrix, char array or cell array. Rows are compared by the listed columns in turn (by default all columns, left to right); a negative column number sorts that column in descending order. Cell array columns must hold text or numeric scalars. Ties keep their original order. idx is the row permutation. Example: sortrows([3 1; 1 2; 3 0], [1 -2]) is [1 2; 3 1; 3 0].

sortx.description: Sort the columns of a heatmap by the values in a row (ascending by default); sortx(h, row, 'descend') and similar forms choose the row and direction.

sorty.description: Sort the rows of a heatmap by the values in a column.

sos2tf.description: Multiplies out second-order sections into one numerator and denominator; g is an overall gain.

sos2zp.description: Zeros, poles and gain of a filter given as second-order sections.

sosfilt.description: Filters x through a cascade of second-order sections, along the first dimension that is not one or along dim.

sound.description: Checks its arguments and plays nothing: mylab has no audio device. A note is printed the first time. Use audiowrite to save the sound as a WAV file.

soundsc.description: Like sound: checks its arguments and plays nothing, because mylab has no audio device.

spalloc.description: An all-zero m-by-n sparse matrix. The third input, the expected number of nonzeros, is accepted and ignored: storage grows as needed.

usage: S = sparse(i, j, v, m, n)
sparse.description: Creates a sparse matrix, which stores only its nonzero elements. sparse(A) converts a full matrix, sparse(m, n) is an all-zero m-by-n matrix, and sparse(i, j, v) puts v(k) at row i(k), column j(k); values that land on the same position are added, which is the usual way to assemble finite-element matrices. m and n fix the size (otherwise it is max(i) by max(j)). A sparse matrix has class double (or logical); use issparse to tell it from a full one. Operators, indexing, \ and most matrix functions work on it directly; functions without a sparse version receive the full matrix.

spconvert.description: Builds a sparse matrix from a table of triplets: each row of D is [row column value], or [row column real imag] for complex values.

spdiags.description: Builds a sparse matrix from diagonals or extracts diagonals. spdiags(B, d, m, n) puts the columns of B on the diagonals numbered d (0 is the main diagonal, positive above, negative below) of an m-by-n matrix; with m >= n the element in column j of the matrix comes from row j of B. spdiags(B, d, A) replaces those diagonals of A. spdiags(A, d) returns the requested diagonals as columns, and spdiags(A) returns all nonzero diagonals and their numbers.

spectralcluster.description: Spectral clustering on a nearest-neighbour (or 'epsilon') similarity graph: k-means on the first k eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian.

usage: [S, F, T, P] = spectrogram(x, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
spectrogram.description: Short-time Fourier transform of the signal x. window is a window vector or a length (a Hamming window; default: 8 segments), noverlap the number of shared samples (default half the window), nfft the FFT length and fs the sample rate in Hz. S holds one spectrum per column, F the frequencies, T the centre time of each segment and P the power spectral density. Without outputs the result is drawn in decibels; 'yaxis' puts frequency on the vertical axis.

speye.description: Sparse identity matrix: ones on the main diagonal and nothing stored elsewhere.

spfun.description: Applies the function f to the nonzero elements of S only, keeping the zeros. For example spfun(@exp, S) leaves the zeros alone where exp(S) would turn them into ones.

sph2cart.description: Converts spherical coordinates (azimuth, elevation in radians, radius) to Cartesian.

sphere.description: Coordinates of a unit sphere as three (n+1)-by-(n+1) matrices (n = 20 by default), for surf(X, Y, Z). Without outputs it draws the sphere.

spline.description: Cubic spline through the points (x, y) with not-a-knot end conditions; if y has two more values than x, the first and last give the end slopes. With xq, returns the values there; otherwise returns a piecewise polynomial for ppval. If y is a matrix, each row is a component of a vector-valued spline.

split.description: Splits text at whitespace, or at a delimiter (a cell or string array lists several). Runs of delimiters count as one break unless 'CollapseDelimiters' is false. One input text gives a column of pieces (a cell of char vectors, or a string array for string input); a cell array whose elements all split into the same number of pieces gives a matrix. Example: split("a,b", ",") is ["a"; "b"].

splitEachLabel.description: Splits the files of a labelled image datastore label by label. Proportions (each below 1, adding up to at most 1) give the share of each label's files that goes into each output, rounded to the nearest whole file; whole numbers give a count of files per label instead. The last output gets the files that are left. Without 'randomized' the first files of each label are taken and the outputs keep the original order; 'randomized' picks the files at random with the global random number generator (rng). 'Include' keeps only the listed labels and 'Exclude' leaves out the listed ones. Also callable as ds.splitEachLabel(...).

splitapply.description: Splits the data into groups given by the group numbers G (from findgroups), calls f on each group and stacks the results, one row per group. Matrices are split by rows. f must return the same size for each group; return a cell such as @(x) {x} for anything else. Example: splitapply(@sum, [1 2 3], [1 2 1]) is [4 2].

splitlines.description: Splits text at line breaks (\n, \r\n or \r). A string gives a string column; a char vector gives a cell column of char vectors.

splitvars.description: Splits variables that have several columns, or that are nested tables, into separate variables. The columns of X are called X_1, X_2, ... unless names are given; the variables of a nested table keep their names.

spones.description: A sparse matrix with the same nonzero pattern as S and every nonzero replaced by 1.

sprand.description: Random sparse matrix with uniformly distributed nonzeros in (0, 1). About density*m*n elements are nonzero; sprand(S) keeps the pattern of S.

sprandn.description: Random sparse matrix with normally distributed nonzeros. About density*m*n elements are nonzero; sprandn(S) keeps the pattern of S.

sprandsym.description: Random symmetric sparse matrix with normally distributed nonzeros, either n-by-n with roughly the given density or with the pattern of the lower triangle of S.

sprank.description: Structural rank: the largest rank any matrix with the nonzero pattern of A could have.

spring.description: n-by-3 colormap from magenta to yellow.

sprintf.description: Formats data into text using % conversions (%d, %i, %u, %f, %e, %g, %x, %o, %c, %s, %%) with optional flags, width and precision (a * takes them from the data). Escapes such as \n and \t are expanded. Array arguments are taken element by element and the format is reused until all data is consumed. A non-integer given to %d is shown in %e style; an integer given to %s is taken as a character code, so sprintf('%s', 65) is 'A'. Returns a char vector, or a string if fmt is a string. Example: sprintf('%d-%d', 1, 2) is '1-2'.

spy.description: Plots the nonzero pattern of a matrix: one marker per nonzero, with row 1 at the top, and the number of nonzeros under the axes.

sqrt.description: Square root of each element. Negative inputs give complex results, e.g. sqrt(-4) is 0 + 2i. Integer inputs are converted to double first.

sqrtm.description: Matrix square root: Y*Y equals A. Not the same as the element-wise sqrt.

square.description: Square wave with period 2*pi taking the values +1 and -1; duty is the percentage of each period spent at +1 (default 50).

squareform.description: Converts between the vector of pairwise distances returned by pdist and the full symmetric distance matrix with zeros on the diagonal.

squeeze.description: Removes dimensions of length 1 from A. The result always keeps at least two dimensions, so 2-D inputs, including row vectors, are returned unchanged. Example: squeeze(ones(1, 1, 3)) is a 3-by-1 column.

usage: sys = ss(A, B, C, D, Ts)
ss.description: State-space model dx/dt = A x + B u, y = C x + D u (x[k+1] = A x[k] + B u[k] with a sample time Ts). D = 0 stands for a zero matrix of the right size. ss(othersys) builds a realization of a tf, zpk or pid model: controller canonical form for one input and one output, one block per column (or row) otherwise; 'minimal' also removes states that cannot be reached or observed. Properties: A, B, C, D, StateName, Ts, InputDelay, OutputDelay, InputName, OutputName. Models are value objects. Arithmetic (+ - * / \ ^), [a, b] and [a; b] concatenation, sys(i, j) indexing and the functions series, parallel, feedback, append, connect and lft combine them; a result takes the type with the highest precedence: frd, then ss, zpk, tf and pid. Numbers act as static gains. Properties are read and written with dot syntax or get/set, e.g. sys.Ts, sys.InputDelay, sys.InputName, sys.OutputName, sys.Name; names are not case sensitive and may be shortened.

usage: sos = ss2sos(A, B, C, D, iu)
ss2sos.description: Second-order sections of a state-space model (input iu when there are several).

ss2ss.description: Change of state coordinates xnew = T*x: the model with T*A/T, T*B and C/T.

usage: [b, a] = ss2tf(A, B, C, D, iu)
ss2tf.description: Transfer function of a state-space model from input iu (default 1); b has one row per output.

usage: [z, p, k] = ss2zp(A, B, C, D)
[z, p, k] = ss2zp(A, B, C, D, iu)
ss2zp.description: Zeros, poles and gain of a state-space model from input iu (default 1).

sscanf.description: Reads values from text according to a format, the reverse of sprintf. Supports %d, %i, %u, %o, %x, %f, %e, %g, %s, %c and %[...] with optional field width and * to skip a field; the format repeats until the text is used up or does not match. Numbers come back as a column; if everything read is text the result is a char row. sz (n, Inf or [m n]) shapes the output, filling columns first. count is the number of fields read; next is always one past the end. Example: sscanf('3 4 5', '%d') is [3; 4; 5].

ssdata.description: State-space matrices of a model. A tf, zpk or pid model is first converted with ss(sys).

ssim.description: Structural similarity index of two grayscale images (1 means identical), using a Gaussian window with standard deviation 1.5 and the usual constants (0.01 and 0.03 times the dynamic range, squared). map holds the value at every pixel.

stabsep.description: Splits a model into a stable part Gs and an unstable part Gu with sys = Gs + Gu. Poles on the stability boundary go to Gu; the direct feedthrough goes to Gs.

stack.description: Turns several variables of a wide table into one variable of a tall table. Every row of U gives one row of S per stacked variable; the other variables are repeated. S gets an indicator variable (categorical, named after the data variable with _Indicator) that tells which variable each value came from. Options: 'NewDataVariableName', 'IndexVariableName', 'ConstantVariables'. iu gives the row of U for each row of S.

stackedplot.description: The variables as line plots stacked above a shared x-axis.

stairs.description: Draws y as a staircase that holds each value until the next x. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

standardizeMissing.description: Replaces the values of A that equal one of the indicators with the standard missing value: NaN for numbers, '' in a cell array of char vectors, <missing> for strings.

start.description: Starts the timer t: runs StartFcn, then TimerFcn (see timer for how mylab emulates timers).

startsWith.description: True if s begins with pattern (or any pattern in a cell array). Works element-wise on a cell array s.

statelevels.description: Low and high levels of a two-level waveform, taken as the most frequent values in the lower and upper halves of a histogram with nbins (default 100) bins.

statset.description: Options structure for the iterative statistics functions (for example MaxIter, TolFun, TolX and Display). Fields that are not set are empty.

std.description: Standard deviation along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. w = 0 (the default, also used when w is []) divides by N-1; w = 1 divides by N. A single value gives 0. 'omitnan' ignores NaN. Example: std([2 4 4 4 5 5 7 9], 1) is 2.

std2.description: Standard deviation of all elements of an array (normalised by n-1).

stderr.description: The file identifier of the error output, 2. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

stdfilt.description: Standard deviation of the neighbourhood of each pixel (3-by-3 by default); the image is mirrored at its edges. The result is double.

stdout.description: The file identifier of the command window output, 1. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

stem.description: Plots each value as a vertical stem from zero topped with a marker, as for discrete signals. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

stem3.description: Draws 3-D stems: a vertical line from the xy-plane to each point, with a marker on top.

step.description: For a System object, runs one step: calls the object's stepImpl method (and setupImpl before the first step). For a control-system model (tf, zpk, ss, pid), computes the unit step response: y has one row per time, one column per output and one page per input, t is a column of times and x holds the states of a state-space model. The time argument is a final time or an evenly spaced vector; without it the duration is chosen so that the transient is shown until it has settled. Without outputs the response is plotted, and several models can be given, each with a line style. stepDataOptions sets the step size.

stepDataOptions.description: Options for step: the size of the step and the input level before it. With an offset the response starts from the steady state that belongs to u0. Pass the result as last argument: step(sys, opt).

stepinfo.description: Step-response characteristics as a struct: RiseTime (10 % to 90 % of the change), TransientTime, SettlingTime (the response stays within 2 % of the final value), SettlingMin, SettlingMax, Overshoot and Undershoot in percent, Peak and PeakTime. For a model the final value is its DC gain and the crossing times are located on the exact response, not read off a grid; for data they are interpolated between samples. An unstable model gives NaN (and an infinite peak). A model with several inputs or outputs gives a struct array.

usage: [b, se, pval, inmodel, stats, nextstep, history] = stepwisefit(X, y, ...)
stepwisefit.description: Stepwise regression on the columns of X: columns enter when their p-value is below 'PEnter' (0.05) and leave when it exceeds 'PRemove' (0.10). inmodel flags the chosen columns.

stepwiselm.description: Stepwise linear regression: starting from modelspec (default 'constant'), terms are added while their F-test p-value is below 'PEnter' (0.05) and removed when it exceeds 'PRemove' (0.10), within the bounds 'Lower' and 'Upper' (default 'interactions').

stepz.description: Step response of a digital filter; the inputs are those of impz.

usage: [s, f, t] = stft(x, fs, Name, Value)
stft.description: Short-time Fourier transform: one column of s per windowed segment. The options are 'Window' (default a periodic Hann window of 128 samples), 'OverlapLength' (default 75% of the window), 'FFTLength' and 'FrequencyRange' ('centered', the default, 'twosided' or 'onesided'). f and t are column vectors; t marks the middle of each segment. With an even FFT length the centred range ends at the positive Nyquist frequency.

stop.description: Stops the timer t and runs its StopFcn.

str2double.description: Converts text to a double. Returns NaN when the text is not a number. Cell arrays and string arrays are converted element by element (a <missing> string gives NaN); a numeric input gives NaN. Example: str2double(["1.5" "x"]) is [1.5 NaN].

str2func.description: Makes a function handle from a name such as 'sin' or from anonymous-function text such as '@(x) x + 1'.

str2num.description: Evaluates text as a bracketed expression, so '1 2 3' gives [1 2 3] and '[1;2]' a column. On failure returns [] and ok is false. Because the text is executed, prefer str2double for untrusted input.

str2sym.description: Turns text into a symbolic expression. Numbers stay exact and names become symbolic variables. A single = sign is read as an equation. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

strcat.description: Concatenates texts horizontally. Trailing whitespace of char inputs is removed first; strings keep theirs. If any input is a cell array the result is a cell array, joined element by element. Example: strcat('a ', 'b') is 'ab'.

strcmp.description: True if two texts are identical (case-sensitive). Either input may be a cell array or string array, giving an element-wise logical array. Non-text inputs give false rather than an error.

strcmpi.description: Like strcmp but ignores upper/lower case.

usage: XY = stream2(X, Y, U, V, startx, starty)
stream2.description: Streamlines of a 2-D vector field, a cell array of [x y].

usage: XYZ = stream3(X, Y, Z, U, V, W, startx, starty, startz)
streamline(X, Y, U, V, startx, starty)
streamline.description: Draw streamlines of a vector field from starting points.

usage: streamtube(X, Y, Z, U, V, W, sx, sy, sz)
streamtube.description: Streamlines drawn as tubes; narrow where the flow converges.

strel.description: Structuring element for imdilate, imerode, imopen, imclose and the other morphology functions. The result is an object: se.Neighborhood is the logical matrix of the shape and se.Dimensionality its number of dimensions; getnhood(se), reflect(se) and translate(se, v) are available. A 'disk' of radius 3 or more is built from line segments in n directions (n = 4 by default, or 6 or 8), which makes it 2r-1 pixels wide; n = 0 gives the exact disk of pixels within distance r of the centre. The radius of an 'octagon' must be a multiple of 3. 'cuboid', 'pair' and 'periodicline' shapes are also accepted.

stretchlim.description: Limits [low; high] (0..1) that leave the fraction tol of pixels saturated at each end (1% by default); one column per colour channel. Meant for imadjust.

strfind.description: Starting indices of every occurrence of pattern in s, overlapping ones included, as a row vector ([] if none). For a cell array, returns a cell of index vectors. Example: strfind('abcabc', 'bc') is [2 5].

string.description: Converts to string. A char row becomes a string scalar; a char matrix gives one string per row; a cell array of text gives a string array of the same size; numbers are converted element by element to their short text form, with NaN becoming <missing>. string() is the empty string "". Example: string([1 2]) is ["1" "2"]. For a datetime array, string(t, fmt, locale) writes the dates in format fmt with month and day names in the language of locale.

strings.description: Creates a string array of the given size filled with empty strings "". strings(1, 1) is the empty string scalar.

strip.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace, or the single character ch. side is 'both' (default), 'left' or 'right'. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

strjoin.description: Joins the texts in a cell array or string array into one piece of text, separated by delimiter (a space by default). Escapes such as '\n' in the delimiter are expanded. Returns a char vector for cell input and a string for string input.

strjust.description: Moves the text in each row of a char matrix to the 'right' (default), 'left' or 'center', keeping the width. Only char arrays are accepted; strings and cell arrays are an error.

strlength.description: Number of characters in a char vector or string scalar. For a string array or cell array of text, an array of lengths of the same size (NaN for <missing>).

strmatch.description: Rows of a char matrix, or elements of a cell array of text, that begin with str; a column of indices. With 'exact' the whole entry must equal str (trailing padding of char-matrix rows is ignored). An old function; strcmp, strncmp and startsWith are preferred.

strncmp.description: True if the first n characters of two texts match (case-sensitive). Texts shorter than n never match. Cell arrays compare element by element.

strncmpi.description: Like strncmp but ignores upper/lower case.

strread.description: Reads formatted data from text, like textread does from a file: one output per conversion in the format. An old function; textscan and sscanf are preferred.

strrep.description: Replaces every occurrence of old in s with new. s may be a cell array or string array. Example: strrep('a-b-c', '-', '+') is 'a+b+c'.

strsplit.description: Splits text at a delimiter (default: whitespace) or at any of a cell array of delimiters, which may contain escapes such as '\t'. Runs of consecutive delimiters count as one unless 'CollapseDelimiters' is false. A string input gives a string row; a char input gives a cell row. matches holds the delimiter text that was found. Example: strsplit('a,,b', ',') is {'a', 'b'}; with 'CollapseDelimiters', false it is {'a', '', 'b'}.

strtok.description: First token of the text: leading delimiter characters (default: whitespace) are skipped and the token runs up to the next delimiter. rest is the remainder, starting at that delimiter. Works elementwise on cell and string arrays. Example: [t, r] = strtok('  red green') gives t = 'red' and r = ' green'.

strtrim.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace (and null characters). Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cell arrays of text.

struct.description: Creates a struct from field name/value pairs. A value that is a cell array creates a struct array the size of that cell, one element per cell; wrap a cell in another cell, e.g. {{1, 2}}, to store it as a single field value. Example: s = struct('x', 1, 'y', 'hi').

struct2cell.description: Column cell array holding the field values of a scalar struct, in field order.

struct2table.description: Converts a struct array (one row per element) or a scalar struct of column vectors into a table whose variables are the struct fields.

structfun.description: Calls f on the value of each field of a scalar struct. By default the scalar results form a column vector; with 'UniformOutput' false the results are returned as a struct with the same field names.

strvcat.description: Stacks texts as rows of a char matrix padded with spaces. Empty inputs are skipped.

sub2ind.description: Converts subscripts into linear indices for an array of size sz (column-major numbering). Subscript arrays must have matching sizes; scalars are expanded. With fewer subscripts than dimensions the last one spans the remaining dimensions. Out-of-range subscripts are an error. Example: sub2ind([3 4], 2, 3) is 8.

subgraph.description: The graph formed by the listed nodes (numbers, names or a logical mask) and the edges between them.

subplot.description: Splits the figure into an m-by-n grid of axes and makes axes p current, counting along rows from the top left. A vector p makes one axes spanning those cells. subplot(221) is shorthand for subplot(2, 2, 1). Asking again for the same cell reuses its axes. ax is an Axes handle; subplot(ax) makes it current. See also tiledlayout.

subs.description: Replaces variables (or subexpressions) with new values. Several replacements are made at the same time. A vector or matrix value expands the result to that size. With one argument, variables are replaced by the workspace variables of the same name. The result is still symbolic: use double to get a number. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

subsasgn.description: Returns A after the assignment described by S (from substruct); for example subsasgn(A, substruct('.', 'x'), 5) is A.x = 5. Classes cannot overload it.

subset.description: A datastore with only the files at the given indices (a vector of file numbers or a logical vector with one element per file), in that order, with their labels. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.subset(...).

subspace.description: Angle in radians between the column spaces of A and B: the largest principal angle. It is 0 when one space contains the other and pi/2 when they are orthogonal.

subsref.description: Applies the indexing described by S (from substruct) to A; for example subsref(A, substruct('()', {1, ':'})) is A(1, :). Classes cannot overload it.

substr.description: The part of s that starts at position offset and is len characters long (to the end of s by default). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

substruct.description: Builds the subscript description used by subsref and subsasgn: a struct array with fields type ('()', '{}' or '.') and subs (a cell array of subscripts, or a field name).

subtitle.description: Adds a smaller second line of text under the title of the current axes. title(txt, subtxt) sets both at once.

subtract.description: The part of p1 outside p2. shapeID tells for each row of q.Vertices which input it comes from (0 for a new intersection point) and vertexID its row there. Also union, intersect and xor for polyshapes. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.subtract(...).

successors.description: Nodes reached by an edge leaving the given node of a digraph.

sum.description: Sum of elements. For a vector, the total; for a matrix, a row of column sums. dim = 1 sums down columns, dim = 2 across rows, and 'all' sums everything. 'omitnan' skips NaN values. sum([]) is 0. Integer inputs keep their class and saturate. Example: sum([1 2; 3 4]) is [4 6].

sumblk.description: Summing junction for connect: a static-gain model whose output and inputs carry the signal names of the formula, with gains +1 or -1. A second argument n makes every signal a vector of n channels.

summary.description: Prints a short description of each table variable: its size and type, plus the minimum, median and maximum of numeric variables.

summer.description: n-by-3 colormap from green to yellow.

sumsq.description: Sum of the squared magnitudes of the elements, sum(abs(x).^2, dim). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

superclasses.description: Lists the names of all superclasses of a class, nearest first, including built-in bases such as handle. With an output it returns a cell column of names; without one it prints them.

superiorto.description: Called in the constructor of a class kept in an @folder: when an operator or function is given objects of this class and of one of the named classes, the method of this class runs. In classdef files use the InferiorClasses attribute instead.

suptitle.description: Sets one title for the whole figure, above all subplots. suptitle does the same.

surf.description: Draws a coloured 3-D surface with heights Z over the grid X, Y (vectors are expanded to a grid; without them the indices are used), coloured with the current colormap. It replaces the current axes (other subplots are kept) unless hold is on. Edges follow the shading setting; options EdgeColor, FaceColor and FaceAlpha are honoured. s is a Surface handle. surfc currently draws the same plot without the contour lines underneath.

surf2patch.description: The faces, vertices and colours of a surface, for patch.

surface.description: Adds a surface to the current axes without clearing what is already drawn (surf starts a new plot unless hold is on). Accepts 'XData', 'YData', 'ZData' name-value pairs.

surfc.description: Draws a coloured 3-D surface with heights Z over the grid X, Y (vectors are expanded to a grid; without them the indices are used), coloured with the current colormap. It replaces the current axes (other subplots are kept) unless hold is on. Edges follow the shading setting; options EdgeColor, FaceColor and FaceAlpha are honoured. s is a Surface handle. surfc currently draws the same plot without the contour lines underneath.

surfl.description: Surface plot shaded as if lit from the side. Light direction arguments are ignored.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output] = surrogateopt(fun, lb, ub, options)
surrogateopt.description: Minimise an expensive function inside bounds by fitting a cheap model to the points tried so far and sampling where the model looks best.

svd.description: Singular value decomposition A = U*S*V'. With one output, the singular values as a column in decreasing order. Passing any second argument (such as 'econ' or 0) gives the economy-size factors.

svds.description: A few singular values of a large matrix: the k largest (default 6) in decreasing order, or the smallest ones with 'smallest'. With three outputs A is approximated by U*S*V'.

swapbytes.description: Reverses the byte order of every element, converting between little- and big-endian data. Example: swapbytes(uint16(1)) is 256.

swarmchart.description: A scatter plot for grouped data: points with the same x are spread sideways so they do not hide each other, which shows the shape of each group's distribution.

swarmchart3.description: A 3-D swarm chart: points are spread in x and y around their group position.

sym.description: Creates a symbolic variable, or converts numbers to exact symbolic values. Doubles that are close to a simple fraction, a multiple of pi or a square root become that exact value, so sym(1/3) is 1/3. sym(x, 'd') keeps a decimal number and sym(x, 'f') keeps the exact binary value.
