Text that is not a name is read as a number or an expression. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

sym2poly.description: Numeric coefficient vector of a symbolic polynomial in one variable, highest power first.

symamd.description: Minimum-degree style ordering for a symmetric matrix (same as amd here).

symfun.description: Creates a symbolic function with the given argument order, so that f(1, 2) substitutes values. The short form is f(x, y) = x^2 + y. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

usage: x = symmlq(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
symmlq.description: Solves A*x = b for a symmetric (possibly indefinite) A with the symmetric LQ method. A preconditioner must be symmetric positive definite.

symprod.description: Product of the symbolic expression f for k from a to b. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

symrcm.description: Reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering: a permutation p such that A(p, p) has its nonzeros close to the diagonal.

syms.description: Creates symbolic variables in the workspace. A word such as real, positive, integer or rational after the names sets an assumption. 'syms f(t)' creates a symbolic function f and its variable t. A size in brackets creates a vector or matrix of numbered variables (a1, a2, ... or A1_1, A1_2, ...). Without arguments it lists the symbolic variables. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

symsum.description: Sum of the symbolic expression f for k from a to b. b may be Inf for a series. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

symvar.description: The symbolic variables in an expression, in alphabetical order. With n, the n variables closest to x in the alphabet (the ones functions such as diff pick by default).

synchronize.description: Combines timetables into one with common row times. newTimeBasis is 'union' (default), 'intersection', 'commonrange', 'first' or 'last'; a time step or a vector of times works as in retime. Variables with the same name get the names of the input timetables appended. Methods: 'fillwithmissing' (default: a value only where an old row time equals the new one), 'fillwithconstant' (with 'Constant', value), 'previous', 'next', 'nearest', the interpolations 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip', 'makima' (which extrapolate beyond the data unless 'EndValues' gives a constant), and the aggregations 'sum', 'mean', 'prod', 'min', 'max', 'count', 'firstvalue', 'lastvalue' or a function handle. For an aggregation each new row time starts a bin that ends at the next one; the last bin of a time step such as 'daily' is a whole step, while the last of a list of times holds only the data at exactly that time.

system.description: Runs an operating-system command through the shell and waits for it. status is its exit code (0 normally means success). With one output the command's output is shown in the command window; with two it is captured as text instead, unless '-echo' asks for both. Not available when mylab runs in the browser.

table.description: Creates a table: columns (variables) of equal height that may hold numbers, logicals, text in cells or strings. Variables are named after the input variables, or Var1, Var2, ... Rows can be named with 'RowNames' (or later through T.Properties.RowNames) and then indexed by name, as in T('row2', :). Access a variable with T.name, a sub-table with T(rows, vars) and the contents with T{rows, vars}, which can also be assigned.

table2array.description: Concatenates all table variables side by side into one array. The variables must have compatible types.

table2cell.description: Cell array with one cell per table entry: numbers as numeric values, text as char vectors or strings.

table2struct.description: Converts a table into an n-by-1 struct array, one element per row.

table2timetable.description: Makes a timetable from a table. The row times are the first datetime or duration variable of T (which is removed from the variables), a given vector or variable, or regular times.

tabularTextDatastore.description: A collection of delimited text files that have the same columns, read a block of rows at a time. location is a file, a folder, a pattern with * or a cell array of these. read returns the next ReadSize rows (20000 by default, or 'file' for one file at a time) as a table, hasdata tells whether rows are left, reset starts again, readall returns everything and preview the first eight rows. Properties: Files, ReadSize, VariableNames, SelectedVariableNames, SelectedFormats, Delimiter, NumHeaderLines, ReadVariableNames, TextType and DatetimeType. Options: those of readtable plus 'FileExtensions', 'IncludeSubfolders', 'ReadSize', 'SelectedVariableNames' and 'SelectedFormats'. Also available: partition(ds, n, k), subset(ds, indices), shuffle(ds), numpartitions(ds), progress(ds), transform(ds, @fcn) and combine(ds1, ds2).

tabulate.description: Frequency table of the values in x with columns Value, Count and Percent. For positive integers every value from 1 to max(x) is listed; text in a cell array gives a cell result. Without an output the table is printed.

tail.description: Last k rows of a table or array (default 8).

tan.description: Tangent of each element, with x in radians.

tand.description: Tangent of angles given in degrees; 0 and multiples of 180 give exactly 0.

tar.description: Creates a tar archive from files, folders or wildcard patterns. A name ending in .tgz or .gz is compressed as well.

taylor.description: Taylor polynomial of f around a (default 0). 'Order' n keeps the terms below degree n; the default 6 gives terms up to the fifth power. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

taylorwin.description: Taylor window with nbar (default 4) nearly equal sidelobes next to the main lobe at the level sll in dB (default -30). The window is not scaled to a peak of one. The result is a column vector.

tcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

tempdir.description: The system folder for temporary files, ending with a file separator.

templateDiscriminant.description: Discriminant analysis learner template for fitcecoc.

templateNaiveBayes.description: Naive Bayes learner template for fitcecoc.

templateTree.description: Tree learner template for fitcensemble, fitrensemble and fitcecoc.

tempname.description: A unique name for a temporary file or folder (nothing is created).

tensorprod.description: Tensor product of two arrays. With no dimensions it is the outer product, of size [size(A) size(B)]. Listed dimensions of A and B are multiplied and summed over (contracted); 'all' contracts every dimension and returns a scalar.

terminal_size.description: The [rows columns] of the command window that the display of wide matrices is laid out for. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

testsuite.description: Collects tests into a suite (an array of matlab.unittest.Test objects) without running them. Takes the same inputs and selection options as runtests. Run the suite with results = run(suite), narrow it with selectIf(suite, ...), and join suites with [suite1, suite2].

tetramesh.description: The tetrahedra with corner numbers T (m-by-4) and points X (n-by-3).

text.description: Writes text on the current axes starting at data point (x, y), vertically centred on it. Vector x, y with a cell array of strings write several labels. Options: FontSize, Color, FontWeight, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, Rotation. Returns Text handle(s) on request.

textBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: the start or the end of the text. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

textread.description: Reads a whole text file with a textscan-style format, returning one output per conversion: numeric columns for %f and %d, cell arrays of text for %s. n limits how many times the format is used. Without a format the file is read as a numeric matrix. New code should prefer textscan or readmatrix.

textscan.description: Reads formatted text from an open file or from a character vector into a cell array with one cell per conversion. The format is applied again and again, N times at most. Conversions: %f and %n (double; %f32 single), %d and %u (int32 and uint32, or with 8, 16, 32, 64 appended), %s (a word, or a whole field when a delimiter is set), %q (text that may be in double quotes), %c (characters, %5c for five), %[abc] and %[^abc] (characters in or not in a set), %D and %{format}D (datetime), %T (duration) and %C (categorical). A number after % limits the field width, %*f reads and discards, and other text in the format must match the input. Options: 'Delimiter' (one or a cell array; without it fields are separated by white space, including line ends), 'EndOfLine', 'Whitespace', 'HeaderLines', 'CommentStyle' (a marker, or {open, close}), 'MultipleDelimsAsOne', 'EmptyValue' (for empty numeric fields; NaN by default), 'TreatAsEmpty', 'CollectOutput', 'TextType' and 'ReturnOnError' (false: stop with an error where the text does not fit the format, instead of returning what was read). With a delimiter, a line that ends early gives empty values for its remaining fields. Reading from a file leaves it positioned after the text that was used; position is that place.

tf.description: Transfer function model. num and den are coefficient vectors in descending powers of s (or z); for several inputs and outputs they are cell arrays with one vector per output/input pair, and a single den is shared by all pairs. Ts is the sample time (0 or omitted: continuous time, -1: unspecified). tf('s') is the Laplace variable, so G = 1/(s^2 + 2*s + 1) builds a model with ordinary algebra, and exp(-tau*s) adds a time delay. tf(othersys) converts a zpk, ss or pid model. Properties: Numerator and Denominator (also num, den; cell arrays), Variable ('s', 'p', 'z', 'q', 'z^-1', 'q^-1'), Ts, InputDelay, OutputDelay, IODelay, InputName, OutputName, Name. Models are value objects. Arithmetic (+ - * / \ ^), [a, b] and [a; b] concatenation, sys(i, j) indexing and the functions series, parallel, feedback, append, connect and lft combine them; a result takes the type with the highest precedence: frd, then ss, zpk, tf and pid. Numbers act as static gains. Properties are read and written with dot syntax or get/set, e.g. sys.Ts, sys.InputDelay, sys.InputName, sys.OutputName, sys.Name; names are not case sensitive and may be shortened. Delays are in the time unit of the model for continuous time and in sample periods for discrete time.

tf2latc.description: Lattice coefficients of an FIR filter b, of the all-pole filter 1/a, or lattice (k) and ladder (v) coefficients of the filter b/a.

tf2sos.description: Second-order sections of the digital filter b/a: each row is [b0 b1 b2 1 a1 a2]. Poles are paired with the zeros nearest to them and the sections are ordered with the poles nearest the unit circle last ('up', the default) or first ('down'). Without g the gain is put into the first section.

tf2ss.description: State-space model of the transfer function b/a in controller canonical form.

tf2zp.description: Zeros, poles and gain of a transfer function in descending powers of s. Each row of a matrix b is one output; its zeros fill a column of z, padded with Inf.

tf2zpk.description: Zeros, poles and gain of a digital filter whose coefficients multiply 1, z^-1, z^-2, ...; the shorter vector is padded with zeros at the end.

tfdata.description: Numerator and denominator coefficients of a model (converted to a transfer function if necessary). The outputs are cell arrays with one row vector per output/input pair; with 'v' and a SISO model they are plain row vectors. Both vectors of a pair have the same length (the shorter one is padded with leading zeros), which is the form the Transfer Fcn block and filter functions expect.

usage: [txy, f] = tfestimate(x, y, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
tfestimate.description: Transfer function estimate from the input x to the output y: Pxy ./ Pxx ('H1', the default) or Pyy ./ Pyx ('H2'). The inputs are those of pwelch.

tform2eul.description: Euler angles of the rotation part of a 4-by-4 transform. seq is the axis order 'ZYX' (default), 'ZYZ' or 'XYZ'; the angles are in radians and listed in that order. Rotation matrices multiply column vectors.

tform2quat.description: Quaternion of the rotation part of a 4-by-4 transform. A quaternion is a row [w x y z] with the scalar part first.

tform2rotm.description: The 3-by-3 rotation part of a 4-by-4 transform. A transform is a 4-by-4 matrix [R t; 0 0 0 1].

tform2trvec.description: The translation [x y z] of a 4-by-4 transform, as a row. A transform is a 4-by-4 matrix [R t; 0 0 0 1].

tformfwd.description: Applies a transformation (a maketform struct or a transformation object) to points.

tforminv.description: Applies the inverse of a transformation to points.

usage: x = tfqmr(A, b, tol, maxit, M1, M2, x0)
tfqmr.description: Solves A*x = b with the transpose-free quasi-minimal residual method.

thd.description: Total harmonic distortion in dB relative to the fundamental: the power of harmonics 2 to n (default 6) over the power of the fundamental. harmpow and harmfreq list the fundamental and the harmonics.

thetalim.description: Set or return the angle limits of polar axes, in degrees.

thetatickformat.description: Set or return the format of the angle tick labels, for example 'degrees'.

thetaticklabels.description: Set or return the labels of the angle ticks of polar axes.

thetaticks.description: Set or return where the angle tick marks of polar axes are, in degrees.

throw.description: Throws the error described by ME, a struct with message and identifier fields such as one made by MException.

throwAsCaller.description: Raises the caught error err again; the same as rethrow(err).

thselect.description: Threshold for denoising data with unit noise: 'sqtwolog' (the universal threshold sqrt(2 log n)), 'rigrsure' (minimises Stein's unbiased risk estimate), 'heursure' (a mix of the two) or 'minimaxi' (minimax).

tic.description: Starts a stopwatch. With an output, also returns a start-time value that can be passed to toc.

tiedrank.description: Ranks of the values, with tied values given their average rank (each column of a matrix is ranked separately). tieadj is the tie adjustment used by rank tests.

tiledlayout.description: Starts a grid of axes in the current figure (clearing it). An m-by-n layout has fixed tiles; 'flow' grows and rearranges the grid as tiles are added ('vertical' and 'horizontal' stack them). Use nexttile to create each axes. title(t, txt), xlabel(t, txt) and ylabel(t, txt) label the whole layout. TileSpacing and Padding accept 'loose', 'compact', 'tight' or 'none'.

tilenum.description: Tile number of an axes in its tiled layout, or of a row and column of a layout.

tilerowcol.description: Row and column of an axes (or of tile numbers) in a tiled layout.

time.description: The time part of a calendarDuration array as a duration. The other parts are read with calyears, calquarters, calmonths, calweeks, caldays or split.

timeit.description: Measures how long the function handle f (taking no inputs) takes to run: calls it several times and returns the median time in seconds. numOutputs is the number of outputs to request on each call (default 0).

timeofday.description: Time elapsed since midnight for each element of a datetime array, as a duration.

timer.description: Creates a timer object. Properties: TimerFcn, StartFcn, StopFcn, ErrorFcn (function handles called as fcn(t, event), text to evaluate, or a cell {fcn, extra...}), ExecutionMode ('singleShot', 'fixedRate', 'fixedDelay', 'fixedSpacing'), Period, StartDelay, TasksToExecute, TasksExecuted, Running, Name, Tag, UserData. mylab has no background thread: start(t) runs the callbacks at once, one after the other, without waiting for Period or StartDelay. A timer with a limited TasksToExecute (or 'singleShot') finishes inside start. An endless timer runs once in start and keeps running inside wait(t) until a callback calls stop(t).

timerange.description: A subscript that selects the rows of a timetable whose times lie between start and stop: TT(S, :). The interval includes start and excludes stop ('openright') unless intervalType is 'closed', 'open', 'openleft' or 'closedleft'. With a unit ('years', 'months', 'days', ...) the interval runs from the start of the unit of start to the end of the unit of stop. start and stop are datetimes, durations or date text; -Inf and Inf leave a side open.

timerfind.description: Returns an empty array: mylab keeps no list of timers.

timerfindall.description: Returns an empty array: mylab keeps no list of timers.

timeseries.description: A set of data samples, each tied to a time. Without times the samples are 0, 1, 2, ... seconds apart; the samples are sorted by time. For a vector or matrix, each row is one sample (IsTimeFirst is true); with three or more dimensions, or when only the columns of a matrix match the times, the last dimension runs along time. Times given as date text or datetime values set TimeInfo.StartDate and count days from it. Properties: Data, Time, Name, Length, Quality (int8 codes, one per sample or per value), QualityInfo, IsTimeFirst, Events, TreatNaNasMissing, UserData, TimeInfo (Units, Start, End, Increment, Length, StartDate, Format) and DataInfo (Units, Interpolation). Property names may be written in any case (ts.data). Methods: resample, synchronize, append, addsample, delsample, getsamples, getdatasamples, getsampleusingtime, setinterpmethod, getinterpmethod, addevent, delevent, detrend, filter, idealfilter, plot, get, set, and the statistics mean, median, max, min, std, var, sum and iqr (with 'MissingData', 'Quality' and 'Weighting' options). Arithmetic works between timeseries with the same times and between a timeseries and numbers. length(ts) is the number of samples and size(ts) is [length 1]. A timeseries can be saved to and loaded from MAT-files.

timeseries2timetable.description: Makes a timetable with one variable per timeseries. The row times are durations in the timeseries' time units, or datetimes when TimeInfo.StartDate is set. Each variable is named after its timeseries; unnamed ones become Data (or Data_1, Data_2, ...). All the timeseries must have the same times; quality codes are dropped with a warning.

timetable.description: A table whose rows are labelled with times: a datetime or duration vector, or regular times made from a sample rate or a time step. TT.Time (or the name of the times variable) gives the row times and TT.Properties has RowTimes, StartTime, SampleRate and TimeStep. Rows are selected by number, by time (a datetime, date text, timerange, withtol) or with a logical vector. See retime, synchronize, lag, isregular, table2timetable, timetable2table.

timetable2table.description: Makes a table from a timetable. The row times become the first variable unless 'ConvertRowTimes' is false.

timetable2timeseries.description: Makes timeseries from the numeric variables of a timetable, one per output and named after the variable (with a single output and several variables, one timeseries holds them side by side). Duration row times become times in their display units; datetime row times become seconds from a StartDate.

timezones.description: A table of the time zone names that datetime accepts for 'TimeZone', with their area, their standard offset from UTC and their daylight saving shift in hours. area is 'Africa', 'America', 'Asia', 'Europe', ... or 'All'. The list comes from the time zone database of the system (or the tzdata package).

tinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

title.description: Sets the title of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle). A cell array or multi-row char array gives several lines, and subtxt adds a subtitle. Options: FontSize, FontWeight, Color, FontName, Interpreter (remembered only). t is a Text handle whose String, FontSize, Color, ... can be changed.

toc.description: Seconds since the last tic (or since tic returned t). Without an output it prints 'Elapsed time is ... seconds.'

today.description: The current local date as a whole serial date number.

toeplitz.description: Toeplitz matrix, constant along each diagonal, with first column c and first row r. With one input the matrix is symmetric. Example: toeplitz([1 2 3]) is [1 2 3; 2 1 2; 3 2 1].

tolower.description: Same as lower: converts text to lower case.

topkrows.description: The first k rows of X after sorting its rows in descending order (by all columns, or by the listed ones; a negative column number sorts that column ascending). direction is 'descend', 'ascend' or one per column. I holds the row numbers. Also works on tables.

toposort.description: Topological order of a directed acyclic graph: every edge goes from an earlier to a later node. 'stable' gives the smallest possible node numbers first. H is the graph with its nodes in that order.

totaldelay.description: Matrix of the total delay between each input and output: input delay + output delay + I/O delay.

toupper.description: Same as upper: converts text to upper case.

tpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

trace.description: Sum of the main diagonal of a square matrix.

transclosure.description: Transitive closure of a digraph: an edge from i to j whenever j can be reached from i.

transform.description: A datastore that passes every read of ds through fcn: read(tds) returns fcn(read(ds)). With 'IncludeInfo', true the function takes the data and the info struct and returns both. The datastore is copied and starts from the beginning; readall applies the function to every block. The result can be transformed or combined again. Works on image datastores, tabular text datastores and the datastores that transform and combine return. Also callable as ds.transform(...).

translate.description: p shifted by (dx, dy). p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.translate(...).

transltform2d.description: Translation by [tx ty]. Properties: Translation and A.

transpose.description: Same as A.' : swaps rows and columns without conjugating. Works on arrays of every type, arrays of graphics objects included.

transreduction.description: Transitive reduction of a digraph: a graph with the fewest edges that has the same reachability.

trapz.description: Approximate integral of sampled data by the trapezoid rule, with unit spacing or the points in x. Works along the first dimension whose size is not 1; a dim argument is not supported. Example: trapz([1 2 3]) is 4.

treelayout.description: Coordinates for drawing a tree given by its parent vector (0 marks a root). h is the height of the tree and s the largest number of children.

treeplot.description: Draws the tree given by a parent vector (0 marks a root).

triang.description: Triangular window of length n whose end points are not zero. The result is a column vector.

triangulation.description: Triangulation object from a connectivity list T (m-by-3 triangles or m-by-4 tetrahedra, rows of vertex IDs) and points P (n-by-2 or n-by-3). The read-only properties Points and ConnectivityList hold the data; TR(i, j) indexes the connectivity list and size(TR) is its size. Methods: edges, freeBoundary, neighbors, vertexAttachments, edgeAttachments, faceNormal, vertexNormal, incenter, circumcenter, barycentricToCartesian, cartesianToBarycentric, nearestNeighbor, pointLocation, isConnected, featureEdges, size. triplot, trisurf and trimesh accept TR directly.

tril.description: Lower triangular part of A: entries above the k-th diagonal are set to zero.

usage: [x, u, y, dx] = trim(model, x0, u0)
trim.description: Finds a steady state of a model: states x and inputs u for which the derivatives dx are zero, starting the search (least squares) from the guess x0, u0. y holds the outputs there. Check dx: when no steady state exists near the guess, the result is only the closest point found.

trimesh.description: Draws the triangles listed in T (from delaunay) as a mesh through the points (x, y, z).

trimmean.description: Mean after discarding the highest and lowest percent/2 of the values. flag is 'round' (default), 'floor' or 'weighted'.

usage: q = triplequad(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax)
q = triplequad(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax, tol, method)
triplequad.description: Triple integral over a box. f(x, y, z) is called with a vector x and scalar y and z.

triplot.description: Draws the edges of the 2-D triangulation T (from delaunay).

tripuls.description: Triangular pulse of width w (default 1) centred on 0. The skew s (-1 to 1) moves the peak to t = s w/2.

usage: h = trisurf(T, x, y, z, 'FaceAlpha', a)
trisurf.description: Draws the triangles listed in T (from delaunay) as a coloured surface through the points (x, y, z).

triu.description: Upper triangular part of A: entries below the k-th diagonal are set to zero (k = 0 is the main diagonal).

trnd.description: Random numbers from the Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

true.description: Logical 1, or a logical array of ones. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array.

trvec2tform.description: 4-by-4 transform that only shifts by the vector t = [x y z]. A transform is a 4-by-4 matrix [R t; 0 0 0 1].

tsdata.event.description: An event: a named moment in time that can be attached to a timeseries with addevent. Properties: Name, Time, Units, StartDate and EventData.

tsdata.interpolation.description: An interpolation method for a timeseries (ts.DataInfo.Interpolation): straight lines between samples, zero-order hold (each value lasts until the next sample), or a function fh(newTimes, times, data). Properties: Name and Fhandle.

tsne.description: t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding of the rows of X (exact gradient). Options: 'NumDimensions', 'Perplexity', 'Exaggeration', 'LearnRate', 'Distance', 'Standardize', 'NumPCAComponents', 'InitialY', 'Options' (MaxIter).

tstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom.

usage: [h, p, ci, stats] = ttest(..., Name, Value)
ttest.description: One-sample t-test that the data have mean m (default 0), or paired t-test on x - y when y has the same size. h = 1 rejects the hypothesis at the significance level 'Alpha' (default 0.05). 'Tail' is 'both' (default), 'right' or 'left'; 'Dim' picks the dimension. ci is the confidence interval for the mean and stats holds tstat, df and sd. NaN values are ignored.

usage: [h, p, ci, stats] = ttest2(x, y, Name, Value)
ttest2.description: Two-sample t-test that x and y come from populations with equal means. Assumes equal variances unless 'Vartype' is 'unequal' (Welch's test). 'Alpha', 'Tail' and 'Dim' work as in ttest; ci is the interval for the difference of means.

tukeywin.description: Tapered cosine window: flat in the middle with cosine tapers that take up the fraction r (default 0.5) of the length. r = 0 is a rectangular window and r = 1 a Hann window. The result is a column vector.

turbo.description: n-by-3 rainbow colormap with smoother brightness than jet.

turningdist.description: Distance between the turning functions (tangent angle against normalized arc length) of two single-boundary polyshapes, minimized over the start point and rotation: 0 for similar shapes. For arrays, a matrix of all pairs. p is a polyshape. Also callable as p.turningdist(...).

type.description: Prints the contents of a text file. If the file is not found as given, name.m and the search path are tried.

typecast.description: Reinterprets the bytes of a real numeric scalar or vector as another numeric type ('double', 'single' or an integer class) without changing the bits, using little-endian byte order. The total byte count must divide evenly into the new type. The result is a row, or a column for column input. Example: typecast(single(1), 'uint32') is 1065353216.

types.description: The class names of the keys and of the values of the dictionary d, as strings.

tzero.description: Invariant zeros of a state-space model: the values of s where the matrix [A - s*I, B; C, D] loses rank. nrank is the normal rank of the transfer matrix. For a non-square system the zeros are the ones common to two random square combinations of its channels.

tzoffset.description: The offset of a datetime array from UTC in its time zone, as a duration (NaN for datetimes without a time zone). dst is the part of the offset that is due to daylight saving time.

uialert.description: Shows a message box in front of an app window. The code continues at once; CloseFcn runs when the user closes the box. Icon is 'error' (default), 'warning', 'info' or 'success'.

uiaxes.description: An axes inside an app window. Pass it as the first input of the plotting functions: plot(ax, x, y), title(ax, 'Signal'), xlabel(ax, 't'), hold(ax, 'on'), cla(ax), imagesc(ax, C). It has the usual axes properties (XLim, YLim, Title, ...) plus Position, Layout, Visible and Tag. The front end shows the drawing as an image that is refreshed after every callback.

uibutton.description: A push button, or a state button (uibutton(parent, 'state')) that stays pressed. Properties: Text, Icon (an image file), ButtonPushedFcn (push button), Value and ValueChangedFcn (state button). Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uibutton(fig, 'Text', 'Run', 'ButtonPushedFcn', @(src, event) disp('pressed'))

uibuttongroup.description: A panel whose radio buttons and toggle buttons exclude each other. Properties: Title, SelectedObject (the selected button), Buttons, SelectionChangedFcn (event.OldValue and event.NewValue are the buttons). Works with uiradiobutton, uitogglebutton and with uicontrol('Style', 'radiobutton').

uicheckbox.description: A check box. Properties: Text, Value (true or false), ValueChangedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uicheckbox(fig, 'Text', 'Show grid', 'Value', true)

uiconfirm.description: Asks a question with buttons. Run with the mylab command, the answer is the button the user presses. In the web app and other places that cannot wait for a click, the call with an output returns DefaultOption at once and prints a note; use the CloseFcn form there: the dialog is shown and fcn(src, event) runs later with event.SelectedOption and event.SelectedOptionIndex.

uicontextmenu.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uicontrol.description: A classic control in a figure window (or panel). Style is 'pushbutton' (default), 'togglebutton', 'checkbox', 'radiobutton', 'edit', 'text', 'slider', 'popupmenu' or 'listbox'. Properties: String (the text; the list of items as a cell array or 'a|b|c' for pop-up menus and list boxes), Value (the slider value, the item number, or Max/Min for check boxes and toggles), Min, Max, SliderStep, Callback, Position, Units ('pixels', 'normalized', 'characters', ...), FontSize, ForegroundColor, BackgroundColor, Enable, Visible, Tag, UserData, TooltipString. Read and change them with get and set or with a dot. Callback is a function handle called with (source, eventdata), a cell array {@fcn, extra, ...} or text to evaluate. Without a parent the control goes into the current figure. Example: uicontrol('Style', 'pushbutton', 'String', 'OK', 'Position', [20 20 80 30], 'Callback', @(src, ~) disp('OK'))

uidatepicker.description: A field for choosing a date. Properties: Value (a datetime, NaT when empty), ValueChangedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: d = uidatepicker(fig); d.Value = datetime(2024, 5, 17);

uidropdown.description: A list that drops down to choose one item. Properties: Items (cell array of text), ItemsData (optional values that stand for the items), Value (the chosen item, or its ItemsData element), ValueIndex, Editable (the user may type a new value), ValueChangedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: d = uidropdown(fig, 'Items', {'Red', 'Green'}, 'ValueChangedFcn', @(s, e) disp(e.Value))

uieditfield.description: A box for one line of text, or for a number (uieditfield(parent, 'numeric')). Properties: Value (text, or a number), Placeholder, Editable, ValueChangedFcn (runs after Enter or when the field loses the focus; event.Value and event.PreviousValue), ValueChangingFcn (while typing); numeric fields also have Limits, RoundFractionalValues and ValueDisplayFormat. A number outside Limits is not accepted. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: f = uieditfield(fig, 'numeric', 'Limits', [0 100], 'Value', 5)

uifigure.description: Creates an app window and returns its handle. Put a uigridlayout in it, or place components with Position. Properties: Name (the window title), Position, Color, Visible, Resize, CloseRequestFcn (runs when the window's close button is pressed; without it the window is deleted), SizeChangedFcn, UserData, Tag. The window is shown by the mylab web app (App panel), or in your browser when the file is run with the mylab command. Example: fig = uifigure('Name', 'Demo'); uibutton(fig, 'Text', 'Hello');

uigauge.description: A gauge that shows a number in a range (read-only). Properties: Value, Limits. The styles 'circular', 'linear', 'ninetydegree' and 'semicircular' are all shown as a bar with the value next to it. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: g = uigauge(fig); g.Value = 40;

uigetdir.description: Asks for a folder (typed as a path) and returns it, or 0 after a cancel. An empty reply, or nobody to answer, gives the start folder (the current folder when none is given).

uigetfile.description: Asks for an existing file by having its path typed, and returns the file name and its folder (ending with a file separator); join them with fullfile. Both are 0 after a cancel (an empty reply), so test isequal(file, 0). When nobody can answer, the default name is used if that file exists, otherwise the result is a cancel. With MultiSelect, several paths separated by semicolons return a cell array of names.

uigridlayout.description: A layout that arranges components in rows and columns and fills its parent. New components take the next free cell, row by row; move one with h.Layout.Row = 2 and h.Layout.Column = [1 3] (a range spans several cells). RowHeight and ColumnWidth are cell arrays with one entry per row or column: a number of pixels, 'fit' (as large as the content) or a weight such as '1x' or '2x' (a share of the space that is left). Other properties: Padding ([left bottom right top]), RowSpacing, ColumnSpacing, Scrollable. Example: g = uigridlayout(fig, [2 2]); g.RowHeight = {'fit', '1x'};

uihtml.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uihyperlink.description: A link that opens a web address. Properties: Text, URL, HyperlinkClickedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uihyperlink(fig, 'Text', 'Docs', 'URL', 'https://example.org')

uiimage.description: A picture. Properties: ImageSource (a file name such as 'logo.png', or an m-by-n-by-3 array), ScaleMethod ('fit', 'fill', 'none', 'stretch'), ImageClickedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uiimage(fig, 'ImageSource', 'logo.png')

uiknob.description: A knob for a number in a range. mylab shows it as a slider. Properties: Value, Limits, ValueChangedFcn, ValueChangingFcn. uiknob(parent, 'discrete') chooses one of Items instead and is shown as a drop-down list. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uiknob(fig, 'Limits', [0 11])

uilabel.description: A line of text (a cell array or string array gives several lines). Properties: Text, HorizontalAlignment ('left', 'center', 'right'), VerticalAlignment, WordWrap. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uilabel(fig, 'Text', 'Name:')

uilamp.description: A small colored light. Properties: Color (a color name, hex code or [r g b]). Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: lamp = uilamp(fig); lamp.Color = 'red';

uilistbox.description: A list that shows several items at once. Properties: Items, ItemsData, Value, Multiselect ('on' lets the user pick several; Value is then a cell array), ValueChangedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uilistbox(fig, 'Items', {'a', 'b', 'c'}, 'Value', 'b')

uimenu.description: A menu in the menu bar of a window, or an item of a menu. Properties: Text (classic name: Label), MenuSelectedFcn (classic name: Callback), Checked, Separator, Enable.

uint16.description: Converts to the uint16 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..65535, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint16(2.5) is 3.

uint32.description: Converts to the uint32 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..4294967295, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint32(2.5) is 3.

uint64.description: Converts to the uint64 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..about 1.8e19, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint64(2.5) is 3.

uint8.description: Converts to the uint8 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..255, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint8(2.5) is 3.

uipanel.description: A box with an optional Title that holds other components. Components inside it are placed relative to the panel. In a classic figure the default Units are 'normalized' and the default parent is the current figure; BorderType 'none' hides the border.

uiprogressdlg.description: A progress box in front of an app window. Set d.Value (0 to 1) and d.Message as the work goes on, read d.CancelRequested, and finish with close(d). The front end only redraws after a callback returns, so a box that is opened and closed inside one callback is never seen.

uipushtool.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uiputfile.description: Asks for the name of a file to save to (typed as a path) and returns the name and folder, or 0 and 0 after a cancel. When nobody can answer, the default name is used if one was given.

uiradiobutton.description: A radio button inside a uibuttongroup; only one button of the group is selected. Properties: Text, Value. React to the choice with the group's SelectionChangedFcn.

uirangeslider.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uislider.description: A slider for a number in a range. Properties: Value, Limits ([low high]), Orientation ('horizontal' or 'vertical'), ValueChangedFcn (when the handle is released), ValueChangingFcn (while it is dragged; read event.Value). A Value outside Limits is moved to the nearest limit. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uislider(fig, 'Limits', [0 10], 'ValueChangedFcn', @(s, e) disp(e.Value))

uispinner.description: A number field with up and down arrows. Properties: Value, Limits, Step, RoundFractionalValues, ValueChangedFcn, ValueChangingFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uispinner(fig, 'Limits', [1 10], 'Step', 1, 'Value', 3)

uistack.description: Moves the graphics objects h in the drawing order of their axes: position is 'up' (default) or 'down' by n steps (1 by default), or 'top' or 'bottom'.

uistyle.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uiswitch.description: An on/off switch. Properties: Items (two texts, {'Off', 'On'}), ItemsData, Value (one of the items), ValueChangedFcn. The styles 'slider', 'rocker' and 'toggle' look the same in mylab. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: s = uiswitch(fig); s.Value = 'On';

uitab.description: One page of a tab group. It holds components like a panel does. Example: tg = uitabgroup(fig); t = uitab(tg, 'Title', 'Data'); uitable(t);

uitabgroup.description: A set of tabs. Add pages with uitab(tg, 'Title', text). SelectedTab is the page that is shown (set it to switch pages); SelectionChangedFcn runs when the user switches, with event.OldValue and event.NewValue.

uitable.description: A table of values. Data is a numeric or logical matrix, a cell array, a string array or a table. Other properties: ColumnName (cell array of headings), RowName, ColumnEditable (true or false, or one value per column), ColumnFormat, CellEditCallback (runs after the user changes a cell: event.Indices is [row column], event.PreviousData, event.NewData and event.EditData the typed text), CellSelectionCallback and SelectionChangedFcn. Logical columns are shown as check boxes. An edit is stored in Data before the callback runs. Example: uitable(fig, 'Data', magic(3), 'ColumnEditable', true)

uitextarea.description: A box for several lines of text. Properties: Value (a cell array with one line per cell), Editable, Placeholder, ValueChangedFcn. Every component also has Position ([left bottom width height] in pixels), Visible, Enable, Tooltip, Tag, UserData, FontSize, FontWeight, FontColor and BackgroundColor, and Layout.Row / Layout.Column inside a grid layout. See docs/APPS.md. Example: uitextarea(fig, 'Value', {'first line'; 'second line'})

uitogglebutton.description: A button inside a uibuttongroup that stays pressed while it is the selected one. Properties: Text, Value.

uitoggletool.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uitoolbar.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uitree.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uitreenode.description: Not available in mylab's app windows; calling it raises an error.

uiwait.description: Waits until uiresume(fig) is called or the window is closed. This works when the app is run with the mylab command, where the window stays open while the script waits. In the web app, in notebooks and when there is no window, it returns at once: write the rest of the work in callbacks instead.

undershoot.description: Undershoot of each transition as a percentage of the difference between the state levels: how far the signal swings back towards the level it came from just after the transition.

undo_string_escapes.description: Replaces special characters in s (newline, tab, backslash, double quote ...) by their escape sequences. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

unicode2native.description: Converts text to bytes (uint8) in the given character encoding (default UTF-8).

unidcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the discrete uniform distribution with values 1, 2, ..., n: the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

unidinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the discrete uniform distribution with values 1, 2, ..., n: the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

unidpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the discrete uniform distribution with values 1, 2, ..., n, evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

unidrnd.description: Random numbers from the discrete uniform distribution with values 1, 2, ..., n. Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

unidstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the discrete uniform distribution with values 1, 2, ..., n.

unifcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the continuous uniform distribution with lower limit a and upper limit b (defaults 0 and 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

unifinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the continuous uniform distribution with lower limit a and upper limit b (defaults 0 and 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

unifit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimates of the limits of a continuous uniform distribution (the smallest and largest observation) with confidence intervals.

unifpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the continuous uniform distribution with lower limit a and upper limit b (defaults 0 and 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

unifrnd.description: Random numbers from the continuous uniform distribution with lower limit a and upper limit b (defaults 0 and 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

unifstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the continuous uniform distribution with lower limit a and upper limit b (defaults 0 and 1).

union.description: Values found in a or b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given. The result is a row unless a is a column. Also accepts cell arrays of text. In mylab ia and ib list the position in a (and in b) of each result value found there. The 'rows' option is ignored.

unique.description: The distinct values of x, sorted unless 'stable' is given (first-appearance order). The result is a row if x is a row, otherwise a column. ia and ic are index columns with u = x(ia) and x = u(ic); 'last' makes ia point to last occurrences. 'rows' finds distinct rows. Also works on cell arrays of char vectors and on string arrays. Example: unique([3 1 3 2]) is [1 2 3].

uniquetol.description: Unique values of A where values closer than tol*max(abs(A(:))) count as equal (tol is 1e-12 for double and 1e-6 for single by default).

unix.description: Same as system on Linux and macOS; on Windows it does nothing and returns status 0.

unmkpp.description: Takes a piecewise polynomial apart: its breaks, coefficient matrix, number of pieces l, order k and number of components d.

usage: U = unstack(S, vars, ivar, Name, Value)
unstack.description: The opposite of stack: the values of the variable vars are spread over one new variable per value of the indicator variable ivar. Rows that agree in the remaining (grouping) variables become one row. Several values in one place are summed, or combined with 'AggregationFunction'; empty places are filled with missing values. Other options: 'GroupingVariables', 'ConstantVariables', 'NewDataVariableNames', 'VariableNamingRule'.

untar.description: Extracts a tar archive, compressed or not, from a file or an http(s) address.

unwrap.description: Removes jumps larger than tol (default pi) from phase angles in radians by adding multiples of 2*pi, giving a continuous phase curve.

unzip.description: Extracts a zip archive (a file or an http(s) address) into the current folder or outputfolder, and returns the names of the extracted files.

usage: y = upcoef(type, x, wname, n, len)
upcoef.description: Rebuilds n levels upwards from coefficients x taken as approximation ('a') or detail ('d') coefficients; len keeps the central part of the result.

upfirdn.description: Inserts p-1 zeros between samples, filters with the FIR filter h and keeps every q-th sample. Columns of a matrix are processed separately.

upper.description: Converts text to upper case, character by character, so the length never changes (a letter whose upper-case form is longer, such as the German sharp s, is kept). Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cells.

upsample.description: Inserts n-1 zeros after each sample of x (each row of a matrix).

urlread.description: Older form of webread that always returns text. With two outputs a failure gives '' and status false instead of an error.

urlwrite.description: Older form of websave: downloads a web address into a file.

usage.description: Stops with an error whose message starts with 'usage: '. This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

usejava.description: Always false: mylab has no Java virtual machine or Java-based desktop.

usage: validateattributes(A, classes, attributes, funcname, varname, argindex)
validateattributes.description: Checks an input and throws a descriptive error if it fails. classes is a cell array of allowed class names (or {} for any; 'numeric', 'float' and 'integer' work as groups). attributes is a cell array of tests such as 'scalar', 'vector', 'row', 'column', '2d', 'square', 'nonempty', 'real', 'finite', 'nonnan', 'integer', 'positive', 'nonnegative', 'nonzero', 'binary', 'even', 'odd', 'increasing', 'nondecreasing', or pairs like '>', 0 / 'numel', 3 / 'size', [NaN 2] (NaN = any). funcname, varname and argindex are optional and only shape the message.

validatecolor.description: RGB triplets (one per row) for colour names, short names, hex codes or RGB values.

validatestring.description: Matches str against a list of allowed texts, ignoring case and accepting an unambiguous leading part, and returns the full matching option. No match or an ambiguous match is an error. Example: validatestring('lin', {'linear', 'cubic'}) is 'linear'.

values.description: Returns the values of the containers.Map m as a cell array, in the order of its sorted keys, or the values for the given cell array of keys.

vander.description: Vandermonde matrix: column j holds v raised to the power n-j, so the last column is all ones.

var.description: Variance, the square of std. w = 0 (default) divides by N-1 and w = 1 divides by N. Works along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given.

varfun.description: Applies the function f to each table variable. Result variables are named like mean_Height. With 'GroupingVariables', f is applied to each group of rows separately and the result has one row per group, with the group values and a GroupCount column. 'OutputFormat' 'uniform' returns a numeric row and 'cell' a cell row instead of a table.

vartest.description: Chi-square test of the hypothesis that normal data have variance v. ci is the confidence interval for the variance; stats has chisqstat and df. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

vartest2.description: F-test of equal variances of two normal samples. ci is the interval for the variance ratio; stats has fstat, df1 and df2. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

vartestn.description: Test of equal variances across several groups (columns of x, or groups given by a grouping variable). 'TestType' is 'Bartlett' (default), 'LeveneQuadratic', 'LeveneAbsolute', 'BrownForsythe' or 'OBrien'. The summary table is printed unless 'Display' is 'off'.

vartype.description: A subscript that selects the variables of a table by type, e.g. T(:, vartype('numeric')). type is a class name or 'numeric', 'float', 'integer', 'cellstr'.

vco.description: Voltage-controlled oscillator: a cosine whose frequency follows x (between -1 and 1), from 0 to 2 fc, or from fmin to fmax. fs defaults to 2 and fc to fs/4.

vec.description: All elements of x as one column, the same as x(:). This is an Octave function that mylab accepts so that Octave scripts run; MATLAB does not have it.

vecnorm.description: p-norm (default 2, the Euclidean length) of each column of A, or of each vector along dim; a vector input gives a single norm. p = Inf gives the largest magnitude. Example: vecnorm([3 0; 4 1]) is [5 1].

ver.description: Prints mylab's own version and the product versions it reports to programs. With an output it returns a struct array with fields Name, Version, Release and Date for MATLAB and for the toolboxes mylab covers in part (Image Processing, Signal Processing, Statistics and Machine Learning, Optimization); ver('signal') selects one, and an unknown product gives an empty struct array.

verLessThan.description: True if the installed version of a product is older than the given version text, e.g. verLessThan('matlab', '9.4'). mylab compares against the versions listed by ver (MATLAB 9.14 and the matching 'images', 'signal', 'stats' and 'optim' versions). Any other toolbox is not available and counts as older than every version, so the result is true rather than an error.

verifyClass.description: Checks that the class of actual is exactly className. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyClass(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyEmpty.description: Checks that actual has no elements. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyEmpty(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyEqual.description: Checks that actual equals expected in class, size and value (NaN equals NaN; cell arrays and structs are compared element by element). 'AbsTol', t and 'RelTol', t allow numeric differences up to t, or t times the expected value. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyError.description: Checks that calling the function raises an error with that identifier, for example testCase.verifyError(@() myFun(-1), 'myFun:negative'). ?MException accepts any error. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyError(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyFail.description: Fails unconditionally, for code paths that must not be reached. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyFail(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyFalse.description: Checks that actual is the logical scalar false. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyFalse(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyGreaterThan.description: Checks that every element of actual is greater than bound. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyGreaterThan(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Checks that every element of actual is at least bound. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyGreaterThanOrEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyInstanceOf.description: Checks that isa(actual, className) is true (subclasses count). A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyInstanceOf(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyLength.description: Checks that length(actual) equals expectedLength. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyLength(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyLessThan.description: Checks that every element of actual is less than bound. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyLessThan(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyLessThanOrEqual.description: Checks that every element of actual is at most bound. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyLessThanOrEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyMatches.description: Checks that the text actual matches the regular expression. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyMatches(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyNotEmpty.description: Checks that actual has at least one element. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyNotEmpty(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyNotEqual.description: Checks that the two values differ. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyNotEqual(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyNotSameHandle.description: Checks that the two are different handle objects. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyNotSameHandle(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyNumElements.description: Checks that numel(actual) equals expectedCount. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyNumElements(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyReturnsTrue.description: Checks that the function returns the logical scalar true. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyReturnsTrue(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifySameHandle.description: Checks that both are the same handle object. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifySameHandle(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifySize.description: Checks that size(actual) equals expectedSize. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifySize(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifySubstring.description: Checks that the text actual contains substring. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifySubstring(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyThat.description: Checks actual against a constraint object from matlab.unittest.constraints, for example IsEqualTo(5, 'Within', AbsoluteTolerance(0.1)) or IsGreaterThan(3) & IsLessThan(9). A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyThat(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyTrue.description: Checks that actual is the logical scalar true. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyTrue(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyWarning.description: Checks that calling the function issues a warning with that identifier. The function's outputs are returned. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyWarning(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

verifyWarningFree.description: Checks that calling the function issues no warning. The function's outputs are returned. A failure is recorded and the test goes on (the test ends as Failed). A method of the test case, also written testCase.verifyWarningFree(...). The optional diagnostic (text, or a function handle to run) is shown on failure together with the actual and expected values.

version.description: Version text. So that programs checking for a recent MATLAB take their modern code path, mylab answers as MATLAB 9.14 (R2023a): version returns '9.14.0 (R2023a) mylab x.y.z', '-release' gives '2023a', '-date' (and the second output) the date of that release, and '-description' mylab's own version.

vertcat.description: Stacks arrays on top of each other, the same as [A; B; ...]. They must have the same number of columns.

vertexAttachments.description: Column cell array: C{i} is a row vector of the IDs of the triangles (tetrahedra) that use vertex i (or VID(i)). TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.vertexAttachments(...).

vertexNormal.description: Unit normals at the vertices of a 3-D surface triangulation: the area-weighted average of the normals of the attached triangles. TR is a triangulation or delaunayTriangulation. Also callable as TR.vertexNormal(...).

view.description: Sets or returns the direction the current axes are seen from: azimuth az (degrees, measured counterclockwise from the negative y-axis) and elevation el (degrees above the x-y plane). view([x y z]) looks at the origin from the point [x y z]. view(2) is the 2-D view from above (az = 0, el = 90) and view(3) the default 3-D view (az = -37.5, el = 30). A 2-D plot seen from elsewhere becomes a 3-D view of the same objects at z = 0 (lines, patches, scatter, text, images; their handles stay valid), and view(2) brings it back to a 2-D axes while nothing 3-D has been added. [az, el] = view returns the current angles; a 2-D axes reports 0 and 90.

violinplot.description: The distribution of each group as a density outline.

voronoi.description: The Voronoi diagram of points; [vx, vy] = voronoi(x, y) returns the edges.

voronoiDiagram.description: Voronoi diagram of an unconstrained delaunayTriangulation. V holds the Voronoi vertices (the circumcenters of the triangles, after a first row of Inf for the vertex at infinity); r{i} lists the indices into V of the region of point i, in adjacent order in 2-D, starting with 1 for unbounded regions. Also DT.voronoiDiagram().

voronoin.description: The Voronoi diagram of the points in the rows of X (two or more dimensions). V lists the Voronoi vertices, the first row being Inf for the point at infinity; C{k} lists the rows of V around the cell of point k, with 1 where the cell is unbounded. Computed with Qhull.

vpa.description: Evaluates the numbers in a symbolic expression to d significant digits (default: the digits setting, 32). Variables stay symbolic. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

vpasolve.description: Solves equations numerically to the precision set by digits. A polynomial equation returns all roots; other equations return one solution near the start value x0 or inside [a b]. Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".

wait.description: Blocks until the timer t has stopped. For an endless timer this is where the remaining TimerFcn calls happen; it gives up with a warning after 100000 calls.

waitbar.description: Shows progress x between 0 and 1. In a terminal a single text progress bar is redrawn in place; elsewhere nothing is printed. Update the bar by passing its handle h (or nothing, for the most recent bar), and finish with close(h) or delete(h). Example: h = waitbar(0, 'Working'); for k = 1:10, waitbar(k/10, h); end; close(h)

waitfor.description: waitfor(h) behaves like uiwait(h). With a property name it returns at once.

waitforbuttonpress.description: Waits for a mouse click (0) or key press (1) in a plot window. Without a live window it returns 0 at once.

warndlg.description: Prints the message with the label 'Warning' (there is no pop-up window) and returns a handle that close and delete accept. The message can be text or a cell array of lines.

warning.description: Prints a warning and records it for lastwarn, or controls which warnings are shown. warning('off', id) hides one warning and warning('off', 'all') all of them; 'on' shows them again; 'error' makes warning(id, ...) raise an error instead. Each of these returns the previous state as a struct with the fields identifier and state (a struct array for 'all'), and warning(s) puts that state back, which is the usual way to silence a warning for a few lines only. warning('query', id) returns the current state, and warning with no input returns or lists all states. 'backtrace' and 'verbose' are accepted as modes.

waterfall.description: Draws each row of Z as a separate line in 3-D, like a mesh without the lines across rows.

watershed.description: Watershed transform: A is flooded from its regional minima and each catchment basin gets a label. Pixels where basins meet are 0. conn is 4 or 8 (the default) for images and 6, 18 or 26 for volumes, or a 3-by-3 matrix of neighbours.

wavedec.description: Wavelet decomposition of a vector to level n: the transform is applied n times to the approximation. c holds the coarsest approximation followed by the details from coarse to fine, and l the length of each of those pieces followed by the length of the signal. The signal is extended at its ends with the current extension mode (see dwtmode); 'mode', m overrides it for one call.

wavedec2.description: Wavelet decomposition of a matrix to level n. C is a row vector holding the coarsest approximation followed by the horizontal, vertical and diagonal details of each level from coarse to fine (each stored column by column); S lists the size of the approximation, of the details at each level, and of the image.

waverec.description: Rebuilds a signal from the decomposition made by wavedec.

waverec2.description: Rebuilds a matrix from the decomposition made by wavedec2.

wavread.description: Older form of audioread for WAV files.

wavwrite.description: Older form of audiowrite for WAV files (default 8000 Hz, 16 bits).

wblcdf.description: Cumulative distribution function of the Weibull distribution with scale a and shape b (defaults 1 and 1): the probability of a value less than or equal to x. With 'upper' it returns the upper tail probability, computed without cancellation.

wblfit.description: Maximum-likelihood estimate of [scale, shape] of the Weibull distribution from the data x, with 100(1-alpha)% confidence intervals in pci (one column per parameter, lower limit in row 1; alpha defaults to 0.05). censoring marks right-censored observations with 1 and freq gives the count of each observation.

wblinv.description: Inverse cumulative distribution function (quantile) of the Weibull distribution with scale a and shape b (defaults 1 and 1): the value x whose cumulative probability is p. p outside [0, 1] gives NaN.

wbllike.description: Negative log-likelihood of the Weibull distribution with the given parameter vector for the data. The second output is the asymptotic covariance matrix of the parameter estimates (the inverse of the observed information), which is meaningful when params are the maximum-likelihood estimates.

wblpdf.description: Probability density (or probability mass) of the Weibull distribution with scale a and shape b (defaults 1 and 1), evaluated at each element of x. Scalar arguments expand to the size of the others; invalid parameters give NaN.

wblrnd.description: Random numbers from the Weibull distribution with scale a and shape b (defaults 1 and 1). Without sizes the result has the size of the parameters. The generator is the one seeded by rng.

wblstat.description: Mean m and variance v of the Weibull distribution with scale a and shape b (defaults 1 and 1).

usage: xd = wden(x, rule, sorh, scal, n, wname)
wden.description: Denoises a signal by thresholding the details of a level-n decomposition. rule is a thselect rule, sorh is 's' or 'h', and scal says how the noise level is found: 'one' (noise of unit variance), 'sln' (from the first level) or 'mln' (separately at each level).

usage: xc = wdencmp('gbl', x, wname, n, thr, sorh, keepapp)
xc = wdencmp('lvd', x, wname, n, thr, sorh)
wdencmp.description: Denoises or compresses a signal or image by thresholding its wavelet coefficients, with one threshold for all levels ('gbl') or one per level ('lvd'; for images a 3-by-n matrix). perf0 is the percentage of coefficients set to zero and perfl2 the percentage of energy kept.

wdenoise.description: Denoises a signal (or each column of a matrix) in the wavelet domain. The defaults are the 'sym4' wavelet, as many levels as the length allows, and the empirical Bayes method with the posterior median. Options: 'Wavelet', 'DenoisingMethod' ('Bayes', 'UniversalThreshold', 'SURE' or 'Minimax'), 'ThresholdRule' ('Median', 'Mean', 'Soft' or 'Hard' with 'Bayes'; 'Soft' or 'Hard' otherwise) and 'NoiseEstimate' ('LevelIndependent' or 'LevelDependent').

web.description: Does not open a browser. Prints a short note with the address, or returns status 0 when an output is requested.

weboptions.description: Options for webread and websave as a struct. Only Timeout (seconds) has an effect.

webread.description: Downloads the content of a web address. Text is returned as a char vector, JSON is decoded when jsondecode is available, and pictures are returned as image arrays. Name-value pairs are added to the address as query parameters. Needs network access: it raises a clear error when the address cannot be reached, and is unavailable when mylab runs in the browser.

websave.description: Downloads a web address into a file and returns the file's full path. Needs network access, like webread.

week.description: Week number within the year (the week containing January 1 is week 1 and weeks start on Sunday), or within the month.

weekday.description: Day of the week as a number, 1 for Sunday through 7 for Saturday, for a datetime array, serial date numbers or date text. The second output is the short day name ('Mon'), or the full name with 'long'.

wenergy.description: Percentage of the energy of a wavedec decomposition held by the approximation (ea) and by the details of each level (ed).

usage: y = wextend('1D', mode, x, n, loc)
wextend.description: Extends a vector or matrix by n samples with one of the modes listed under dwtmode. loc is 'l' (left or top), 'r' (right or bottom) or 'b' (both, the default).

wfilters.description: The four filters of an orthogonal wavelet: low- and high-pass filters for decomposition (LoD, HiD) and for reconstruction (LoR, HiR). type picks a pair: 'd' decomposition, 'r' reconstruction, 'l' the two low-pass and 'h' the two high-pass filters. The wavelet is 'haar', 'dbN' (Daubechies, N vanishing moments), 'symN' (symlets) or 'coifN' (coiflets, N = 1..5); two filter vectors may be given instead of a name.

what.description: Lists the MATLAB files in a folder (the current one by default). With an output it returns a struct with the folder's path and cell arrays m, mat, mlx, classes and packages.

which.description: Tells what a name refers to: 'variable' for a workspace variable, the full path of the .m file for a file function or script, the path of a data file found on the search path, or 'built-in (mylab/name)' for a function built into mylab. Returns '' (and prints a message when used as a command) for an unknown name. '-all' returns every match in a cell array.

whitepoint.description: XYZ coordinates (Y = 1) of a standard illuminant: 'd65', 'd50', 'd55', 'a', 'c', 'e', 'f2', 'f7', 'f11' or 'icc' (the default).

whitespaceBoundary.description: A pattern that matches a position, not characters: a place where whitespace meets another character. The type is 'start', 'end' or 'either' (the default). Put ~ in front of the pattern to match the places where it does not hold. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

whitespacePattern.description: A pattern that matches whitespace characters (space, tab, line breaks). With no argument it matches one or more of them, with N exactly N, and with (min, max) between min and max (max may be Inf). Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind.

who.description: Lists the variables of the workspace, of the global workspace, or of a MAT-file, optionally only those that match the names, wildcards or regular expressions. With an output it returns the names as a cell column.

whos.description: Like who, with the size, bytes and class of each variable and whether it is global, sparse or complex. With an output it returns a struct array with the fields name, size, bytes, class, global, sparse, complex, nesting and persistent instead of printing. Bytes are counted for the data as MATLAB counts them (two bytes per character, 16 per complex double) and are approximate for cells, structs and objects.

width.description: Number of variables (columns) of a table.

wiener2.description: Adaptive noise removal: smooths strongly where the local variance is close to the noise power and little near edges. The noise power is estimated as the average local variance when not given.

wildcardPattern.description: A pattern that matches any characters, as few as possible: zero or more by default, exactly N, or between min and max. With 'Except' the matched characters must not start a match of pat2. Patterns are combined with + (one after the other) and | (either one) and can be given to contains, matches, startsWith, endsWith, count, extract, extractBefore, extractAfter, extractBetween, replace, erase, insertBefore, insertAfter, replaceBetween, eraseBetween, split, strip and strfind. Example: "<" + wildcardPattern + ">" matches one tag.

wilkinson.description: Wilkinson's eigenvalue test matrix: symmetric and tridiagonal, with ones next to the diagonal and abs(-(n-1)/2 : (n-1)/2) on it. Its largest eigenvalues come in close pairs.

window.description: Calls a window function by handle, for example window(@hamming, 64) or window(@kaiser, 64, 5). Extra inputs are passed on.

winter.description: n-by-3 colormap from blue to green.

wishrnd.description: A random matrix from the Wishart distribution with covariance Sigma and df degrees of freedom. D is the Cholesky factor of Sigma, which can be passed back to save time.
