withtol.description: A subscript that selects the rows of a timetable whose times are within the duration tol of one of the given times: TT(withtol(t, seconds(1)), :).

wkeep.description: Keeps n elements from the middle of a vector, or from the left ('l'), the right ('r') or starting at a given index. For a matrix the central part of the given size is kept.

wmaxlev.description: Largest sensible decomposition level for a signal of the given length: the deepest level at which at least one coefficient is free of end effects.

wnoisest.description: Noise standard deviation estimated from the detail coefficients of the given levels (default level 1): the median absolute value divided by 0.6745.

usage: wordcloud(words, sizes), wordcloud(tbl, wordVar, sizeVar) or wordcloud(categorical)

workspace.description: Accepted so that scripts written for the MATLAB desktop keep running; it does nothing in mylab.

wrapTo180.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [-180, 180]; values already in range are kept.

wrapTo2Pi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [0, 2*pi]; positive multiples of 2*pi map to 2*pi.

wrapTo360.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [0, 360]; positive multiples of 360 map to 360.

wrapToPi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [-pi, pi]; values already in range are kept.

usage: x = wrcoef(type, c, l, wname, n)
wrcoef.description: Rebuilds the part of the signal carried by one branch of a wavedec decomposition: the approximation ('a') or the details ('d') at level n. The approximation at the coarsest level plus the details of all levels give back the signal.

writeVideo.description: Appends to the open VideoWriter v: a frame or array of frames from getframe, an image (height-by-width or height-by-width-by-3, uint8 or doubles from 0 to 1), or a 4-D stack of images. Later frames are resized to the size of the first one.

writecell.description: Writes a cell array of numbers and text to a delimited text file, one row of the cell array per line. A file name ending in .xlsx (or .ods) writes an Excel workbook (or an OpenDocument spreadsheet).

writelines.description: Writes text (a string array, cell array or char vector) to a file, one element per line, each followed by a line break.

writematrix.description: Writes a matrix to a delimited text file with full precision, one row per line. The delimiter may be 'comma' (default; tab for .tsv files), 'tab', 'space', 'semi', 'bar' or any single character. Cell arrays, strings and char arrays are written as text, quoted when they contain the delimiter. A file name ending in .xlsx (or .ods) writes an Excel workbook (or an OpenDocument spreadsheet); 'Sheet' and 'Range' choose where.

writestruct.description: Writes a structure to an XML or JSON file, the reverse of readstruct. In XML the root element is named 'struct' unless StructNodeName says otherwise, each field becomes an element, the elements of an array become repeated elements, fields ending in 'Attribute' become attributes, and nested structures become nested elements.

writetable.description: Writes a table to a delimited text file with a header row of variable names. A file name ending in .xlsx writes an Excel workbook and one ending in .ods an OpenDocument spreadsheet; 'Sheet' and 'Range' choose where.

wthresh.description: Thresholding with the threshold t: 's' (soft) shrinks every value towards zero by t, 'h' (hard) sets values of magnitude t or less to zero and keeps the rest.

x2fx.description: Design matrix for the predictors X: model is 'linear' (default, a constant column and X), 'interaction', 'quadratic', 'purequadratic' or a terms matrix.

xcorr.description: Cross-correlation r(m) = sum of x(n+m) conj(y(n)) for lags -(N-1) to N-1, or the autocorrelation of x. A shorter signal is padded with zeros. maxlag limits the lags; scaleopt is 'none', 'biased' (divide by N), 'unbiased' (divide by N-|m|) or 'normalized'/'coeff' (one at zero lag for an autocorrelation). For a matrix with N columns the result has N^2 columns: column (i-1)N+j correlates column i with column j. lags is a row vector.

xcorr2.description: Two-dimensional cross-correlation of matrices a and b (the autocorrelation with one input); the result has size(a) + size(b) - 1 elements each way.

xcov.description: Cross-covariance: the cross-correlation of the signals after their means are removed. The options are those of xcorr.

xlabel.description: Labels the x axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

xlim.description: Sets or returns the x-axis limits of the current axes. An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. xlim([0 Inf]).

xline.description: Draws a vertical line across the current axes at x (several lines for a vector). Options: a line style such as '--r', a label, 'Color', 'LineWidth', 'LineStyle', 'Alpha'.

xlsfinfo.description: Returns a description and the worksheet names (cell array) of an Excel file.

xlsread.description: Reads a worksheet of an Excel file. num is the block of numbers (NaN where a cell holds text or nothing; header rows and columns are dropped), txt a cell array with the text cells and raw a cell array with everything. sheet is a name or number, range is like 'B2:D10'. Works with .xlsx workbooks. With the openpyxl package installed (pip install mylab[excel]) it is used for reading and writing; otherwise a built-in reader and writer handles numbers, text and logical values without formatting. OpenDocument spreadsheets (.ods) are read and written the same way, and Excel 97-2003 workbooks (.xls) are read (cell values, including the stored results of formulas; the xlrd package is used when it is installed). Dates are read as Excel serial numbers. Binary .xlsb workbooks are not supported.

xlswrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix or a cell array of numbers and text to a worksheet of an Excel file, starting at cell A1 or at the first cell of range. Other sheets of an existing file are kept. Works with .xlsx workbooks. With the openpyxl package installed (pip install mylab[excel]) it is used for reading and writing; otherwise a built-in reader and writer handles numbers, text and logical values without formatting. OpenDocument spreadsheets (.ods) are read and written the same way, and Excel 97-2003 workbooks (.xls) are read (cell values, including the stored results of formulas; the xlrd package is used when it is installed). Dates are read as Excel serial numbers. Binary .xlsb workbooks are not supported.

xmlread.description: Reads an XML file and returns its document node. Nodes answer to the usual DOM method names: getNodeName, getNodeValue, getNodeType, getParentNode, getChildNodes, getFirstChild, getLastChild, getNextSibling, getPreviousSibling, hasChildNodes, getAttributes, hasAttributes, getTextContent, setTextContent, appendChild, removeChild, insertBefore, replaceChild and cloneNode; elements add getTagName, getAttribute, setAttribute, hasAttribute, removeAttribute and getElementsByTagName; the document adds getDocumentElement, createElement, createTextNode, createComment and createCDATASection; text nodes add getData, setData and getLength. Node lists and attribute lists have getLength and item(k), where k counts from 0 and an index past the end gives []. A method without arguments may be written without parentheses. Text comes back as character vectors (in MATLAB as Java strings, so char(...) around it works in both), counts as numbers and tests as logicals. As in MATLAB, white space between elements is kept as text nodes. The constants ELEMENT_NODE, TEXT_NODE and so on are properties of every node.

xmlwrite.description: Writes a document or element node (from xmlread or built with createElement) as indented XML text, to a file or, with one argument, as the returned character vector.

xor.description: Element-wise exclusive OR: true where exactly one of A and B is nonzero.

xperm.description: Reorders the states of a state-space model in the order given by P.

xregion.description: Shade the vertical band between two x values across the full height of the axes.

xsecondarylabel.description: Set the small extra label drawn at the end of the x-axis (the place where an exponent or a date is normally shown).

xtickangle.description: Rotates the x-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

xtickformat.description: Set or return the format of the x-axis tick labels: a number format such as '%.2f', 'usd', 'percentage', or a date or duration format.

xticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

xticks.description: Puts the x-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

xyz2lab.description: Converts CIE XYZ colours to L*a*b* for the given reference white (default 'd65').

xyz2rgb.description: Converts CIE XYZ colours to RGB; 'OutputType' may be 'double', 'single', 'uint8' or 'uint16'. 'WhitePoint' names the reference white ('d65' by default; also 'd50', 'd55', 'a', 'c', 'e', 'icc', 'f2', 'f7', 'f11' or [X Y Z]) and 'ColorSpace' the kind of RGB ('srgb', 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb').

ycbcr2rgb.description: Converts YCbCr colours back to RGB. The result has the class of the input.

year.description: Year numbers of a datetime array (serial date numbers and date text are also accepted).

years.description: With numbers, creates a duration array of that many years of 365.2425 days. With a duration array, converts it to a plain number of years of 365.2425 days.

ylabel.description: Labels the y axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

ylim.description: Sets or returns the y-axis limits of the current axes (the active side with yyaxis). An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. ylim([0 Inf]).

yline.description: Draws a horizontal line across the current axes at y (several lines for a vector). Options: a line style such as '--r', a label, 'Color', 'LineWidth', 'LineStyle', 'Alpha'.

ymd.description: Year, month and day numbers of a datetime array as three numeric arrays.

yregion.description: Shade the horizontal band between two y values across the full width of the axes.

ysecondarylabel.description: Set the small extra label drawn at the end of the y-axis.

ytickangle.description: Rotates the y-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

ytickformat.description: Set or return the format of the y-axis tick labels: a number format such as '%.2f', 'usd', 'percentage', or a date or duration format.

yticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

yticks.description: Puts the y-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

yyaxis.description: Gives the current axes a second y axis on the right. Later plots, labels and limits apply to the chosen side; each side has its own colour.

yyyymmdd.description: Each date as one number whose digits are the year, month and day, such as 20240315.

zero.description: Zeros of a model: the numerator roots for one input and one output (gain is the zero-pole-gain factor), and the transmission zeros for a model with several inputs or outputs.

zeros.description: An array of zeros. The class is double unless a class name ('single', 'int8', ..., 'logical') is given; 'like', p takes the class and complexity from the value p.

zgrid.description: Adds the unit circle and curves of constant damping ratio and natural frequency (in rad per sample) to a pole-zero map or root locus in the z-plane.

zip.description: Creates a zip archive from a file, folder, wildcard pattern or cell array of those. Names in the archive are relative to rootfolder (the current folder by default). '.zip' is added to the archive name if it has no extension.

zlabel.description: Labels the z axis of the current 3-D axes; ignored on 2-D axes.

zlim.description: Sets or returns the z-axis limits of the current 3-D axes; an infinite end keeps the current limit on that side.

zoom.description: Accepted so that scripts written for a desktop plot window keep running; it has no visible effect in mylab.

zp2sos.description: Second-order sections from zeros, poles and gain; see tf2sos for the layout and ordering.

usage: [A, B, C, D] = zp2ss(z, p, k)
zp2ss.description: State-space model from zeros, poles and gain.

zp2tf.description: Numerator and denominator from zeros, poles and gain. Columns of z with one gain each give one numerator row per output.

zpk.description: Zero-pole-gain model k*(s - z1)(s - z2).../((s - p1)(s - p2)...). z and p are vectors ([] for none); for several inputs and outputs they are cell arrays and k is a matrix. zpk(othersys) converts a tf, ss or pid model by computing its zeros and poles. Properties: Z, P (cell arrays of column vectors), K, DisplayFormat ('roots', 'frequency' or 'time constant'), Variable, Ts and the delay and name properties. Models are value objects. Arithmetic (+ - * / \ ^), [a, b] and [a; b] concatenation, sys(i, j) indexing and the functions series, parallel, feedback, append, connect and lft combine them; a result takes the type with the highest precedence: frd, then ss, zpk, tf and pid. Numbers act as static gains. Properties are read and written with dot syntax or get/set, e.g. sys.Ts, sys.InputDelay, sys.InputName, sys.OutputName, sys.Name; names are not case sensitive and may be shortened.

zpkdata.description: Zeros, poles and gain of a model. z and p are cell arrays of column vectors, one per output/input pair, and k is a matrix; with 'v' and a SISO model z and p are column vectors.

zplane.description: Plots zeros (o) and poles (x) with the unit circle. Column vectors are zeros and poles, row vectors numerator and denominator coefficients.

zscore.description: Standardizes data: subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation (N-1 normalization, or N with flag 1) along the first dimension whose size is not 1. Constant data gives zeros.

zsecondarylabel.description: Set the small extra label drawn at the end of the z-axis.

usage: [h, p, ci, zval] = ztest(x, m, sigma, ...)
ztest.description: z-test of the hypothesis that the data come from a normal distribution with mean m, when the standard deviation sigma is known. h is 1 when the hypothesis is rejected. Options by name: 'Alpha' (default 0.05) and 'Tail' ('both', 'right' or 'left').

ztickangle.description: Set or return the rotation of the z-axis tick labels, in degrees.

ztickformat.description: Set or return the format of the z-axis tick labels.

zticklabels.description: Set or return the labels of the z-axis ticks.

zticks.description: Sets or returns the z-axis tick positions of 3-D axes.

ztrans.description: Z-transform of the sequence f(n): the sum of f(n)/z^n for n = 0, 1, 2, ... Needs SymPy: pip install "mylab-lang[symbolic]".
